2. The primary applicant should be the Project Leader.
3. The applicant has to be incubated in an incubator (Incubator could be located anywhere in the country and may/may not be supported by BIRAC). At the time of applicationRs. the applicant is expected to have identified a preferred incubator. LoI/MoU with the incubator is required for final approval.
4. If the applicant is formally employed (or registered as a student) with an academic or research organizationRs. then
the applicant has to produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the competent authority of the organization indicating that the organization has policies in place to allow the applicant while in service/ on sabbatical/on Extraordinary Leave:
accept funding support (if successful) as an individualRs.
manage the funds through a separate no-lien account in individual capacity
undertake the BIG project in an incubator
to create an enterprise.
AlternativelyRs. the applicant needs to provide an undertaking that he/she plans to terminate his/her association with the current employer and take up the project full-time in the event of grant approval. A resignation/ relieving/ retirement letter will be needed as a supporting document before final approval and release of the grant.
5. If the applicant is formally employed with a for-profit company/LLPRs.
the applicant needs to provide an undertaking that he/she plans to terminate his/her association with the current employer and take up the project full-time in the event of grant approval (A resignation/ relieving/retirement letter will be needed as supporting document before final approval and release of the grant.)Rs. orRs.
AlternativelyRs. the application should be submitted under the Company/LLP category.
6. An individual who is a promoter shareholder of a Biotech company or one of the partners in a Biotech LLP will not be allowed to apply as an individualRs. irrespective of the percentage of shareholding of the applicant in the company. (In such a caseRs. the application can be submitted through the company/LLP routeRs. in case the company/LLP meets the required eligibility criteria as detailed below).
> **Eligibility criteria for Company/ LLP:**


1. The Company/LLP should be registered under the Indian Companies ActRs. 1956/2013.
1. The incorporation date of the Company/LLP should not be earlier than 5 years from the date of closing of a particular BIG call.
1. A company is considered as 'owned by resident Indian citizen(s) if minimum 51% of the capital is beneficially owned by resident Indian citizen(s) and/or Indian companiesRs. which are ultimately owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens.
1. Company/LLPs application should be represented by a Project Leader.
1. The Company/LLP must have its own in-house R&D facility that is functional and adequate to execute the project. If the Company/LLP does not have a functional and adequate laboratory of its own then it should be incubated at an incubator (This shall be verified and confirmed by BIG Partner )Rs.
1. If an applicant companyRs. in which any promoter holding more than or equal to 20% of the sharesRs. is a co-promoter of another ineligible company or a partner in another ineligible LLPRs. then the applicant will not be eligible. The only exception to this shall be a situation wherein the latter ineligible company/LLP is operating in a non-biotech domain. In case the applicant is an LLP: An applicant LLPRs. in which any of the partners is also a partner in another ineligible LLP or is a co-promoter in another ineligible companyRs. then the applicant will not be eligible. The only exception to this shall be a situation wherein the latter ineligible LLP/company is operating in a non-biotech domain.

**Note 01:** Every proposal must clearly identify a Project Leader who will take responsibility for the technical and managerial aspects of the project execution.
**Note 02:** The Project Leader must be technically qualified to undertake the project. The Project Leader must have completed basic undergraduate training in any discipline.
**Note 03:** In the event that the proposal is shortlisted for presentation in front of the Selection Committee(s)Rs. the Project Leader will be required to present the case for support. In the event that a proposal is shortlisted for funding supportRs. the Project Leader will be required to sign the project agreement.
**Note 04:** The project Leader must be a shareholder in the applicant company.
**Note 05:** The proposed objectives and deliverables should not have received funding support from any other agency.
**Note 06:** BIG support can be provided only once to any individual/startup.
**Note 07:** Biotech Start-ups and Individual Entrepreneurs with innovative ideas having potential for commercialization are eligible to apply.
**Note 08:** ScientistsRs. FacultyRs. Research ScholarsRs. and Graduates in any discipline incubating/ intend to incubate at a Bio Incubator.

name: PM POSHAN - Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme For Holistic Nourishment
brief_description:
PM POSHAN is a centrally sponsored scheme by the Department of School Education & LiteracyRs. Ministry of Education. Under this schemeRs. one hot cooked meal will be provided to the children studying in Government and Government aided schools. The Scheme is implemented across the country covering all the eligible children without any discrimination of gender and social class. > **Objective:** The main objectives of the PM POSHAN Abhiyaan are to address two of the pressing problems for the majority of children in IndiaRs. viz. hunger and education by improving the nutritional status of eligible children in Government and Government-aided schools as well as encouraging poor childrenRs. belonging to disadvantaged sectionsRs. to attend school more regularly and help them concentrate on classroom activities.
POSHAN Abhiyaan is one of the many schemes under the umbrella scheme "Integrated Child Development Services Scheme (ICDS)". ICDS also includes Anganwadi Services SchemeRs. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana YojanaRs. and Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
benefits:
**Nutrition norm per child per day:** 1. Primary: Calorie 450; Protein - 12 gms 1. Upper Primary: Calorie 700; Protein - 20 gms **Food norms per child per day:** 1. Primary: Food grains - 100 gms; Pulses - 20 gms; Vegetables - 50 gms; Oil & fat - 5 gmsRs. Salt & condiments - As per need. 1. Upper Primary: Food grains - 150 gms; Pulses - 30 gms; Vegetables - 75 gms; Oil & fat 7.5 gmsRs. Salt & condiments - As per need.
Under the SchemeRs. there is the provision of hot cooked meals to children of pre-schools or Bal Vatika (before class I) in primary schools also in addition to the 11.80 crore children of classes I to VIII studying in 11.20 lakh schools.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a citizen of India.
1. The applicant must be studying in a Primary or Upper Primary class (Class 1st to Class 8th) in a Government or a Government-aided school.

name: Jute Diversification Scheme
brief_description: The scheme "Jute Diversification Scheme" was launched by the National Jute BoardRs. Ministry of TextilesRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to spread jute diversification programsRs. provide trainingRs. and create sustained employment by setting up Jute Resource-cum-Production Centres across the country. The scheme provides basicRs. advancedRs. and design training in jute diversified products manufacturingRs. financial incentives for collaborating agenciesRs. and subsidies for procuring machinery. The applicant must be a registered agency or entrepreneur with at least three years of experience in product identificationRs. bulk productionRs. skill trainingRs. and marketing of jute diversified products. The scheme is implemented by the National Jute Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through the official websiteRs. followed by a hard copy submission.
benefits: ##### ***Financial Assistance for Activities*** - The scheme provides an estimated cost of 12Rs./- for organizing 5 cycles of basicRs. advanceRs. and design training for 24 beneficiaries per cycle. - Incentive for Collaborating Agencies: The agency receives 2Rs./- (calculated as 20% of the activity cost) for organizing the activities and maintaining the infrastructure. ##### ***Infrastructure Support*** The scheme provides 12Rs./- for the installation of a biometric machineRs. internet connectivityRs. and maintenance. ##### ***Machinery Subsidy*** The scheme offers 9Rs./- per year per centre to procure 72 machines (at 50% subsidy or a maximum ceiling of 12Rs./- per machineRs. whichever is less) for successful beneficiaries engaged in production. ##### ***Disbursal*** - 50% of the activities cost is released as an advance along with the approval of the action plan. - The remaining 50% of the activities costRs. the cost of the biometric machineRs. and the incentive are released upon successful completion of the activities and submission of final claims and reports. - The machine subsidy is released in two installmentsRs. where 50% is released within one month of installationRs. and the remaining 50% is released after six months upon inspection certifying that the beneficiaries are engaged in manufacturing and sales. - The payments of such incentives are paid strictly through Direct Bank Transfer. ##### ***Conditions*** - The collaborating agency must ensure the engagement of at least 50% of the trainees in jute diversification activities post-training. - In the case of self-employmentRs. the beneficiary must achieve sales of at least 5Rs./- per month or 15Rs./- per quarter. - The agency must maintain a separate bank account for all advances and limit cash transactions to a maximum of 5Rs./- per activity. - The installation of an Aadhaar linked biometric attendance machine and a webcam is mandatory at the training site.
eligibility:
- The applicant must be a bonafide Indian agency or an Indian citizen. - The applicant must be a reputed registered jute entrepreneurRs. manufacturerRs. exporterRs. merchant traderRs. non-governmental organizationRs. cooperative societyRs. federationRs. public sector undertakingRs. or organization. - The applicant must be engaged in the product identificationRs. bulk productionRs. skill trainingsRs. and marketing of jute diversified products for at least the last three years. - The applicant should possess recognized experience in the trainingRs. promotionRs. and development of Women Self Help Groups in the field of production and marketing of jute diversified productsRs. handloomsRs. or handicrafts. - The applicant must have their own office of at least 250 sq.ft. equipped with a telephone or mobile connectionRs. a computer or laptopRs. and email facilities. - The applicant must have at least 500 sq.ft. of space available for setting up the Jute Resource-Cum-Production Centre. - The applicant must obtain a minimum of 50 marks in the evaluation criteria to be eligible for consideration for selection.
##### ***Preference*** Preference is given to recognized agencies with at least three years of experience in trainingRs. promotionRs. and development of Women Self Help Groups in the handloomRs. handicraftsRs. and textiles sector. ##### ***Earmarking/Reservation*** At least 70% of the training beneficiaries must be individual women or women belonging to Women Self Help Groups. ##### ***Relaxation*** If an entrepreneur collaborates with the purpose of converting the centre into a full-fledged manufacturing unit by employing at least 50% of its traineesRs. the condition of training over 70% women will not be applicable. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Jute Board. - The applicant must submit an annual action plan supported by a list of confirmed bonafide trainees. - The applicant must submit a bank guarantee equivalent to 50% of the activities cost of the approved cycles. - The applicant must set up the centre by procuring and installing new branded machineries within one month from the date of the in-principle approval.

name: Micro Finance Scheme of NMDFC
brief_description: Under this Scheme of NMDFCRs. credit is extended to the members of the Self Help Groups (SHGs)Rs. predominantly comprising of the minority women scattered in remote villages and urban slumsRs. who are not able to take advantage of the formal banking credit. Under the schemeRs. an amount of 1Rs./- under credit Line-1 & upto 1Rs./- under Credit Line-2 is extended to each member of SHG at interest rate of 7% & 10% respectively. Concession of 2% is extended to women beneficiaries under Credit Line-2.
benefits: - Concessional Credit to the beneficiaries among minority communities.
eligibility:
a) The scheme is implemented through Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Thrift and Credit Groups (TCGs) comprising members of minority communities. b) At least 75% of the members of each SHG/TCG must belong to notified minority communities. The remaining up to 25% may belong to weaker sectionsRs. including Scheduled CastesRs. Scheduled TribesRs. Other Backward ClassesRs. or Persons with Disabilities.
In exceptional casesRs. groups with minimum 60% minority members may also be considered. c) The annual family income of each beneficiary must not exceed: Rs. 3.00 lakh under Credit Line1. Rs. 8.00 lakh under Credit Line2. d) The SHG should have a satisfactory record of thrift and credit activity for at least six months. e) The beneficiaries should not be defaulters under any other loan scheme. f) Loans shall be used for income-generating activities such as petty tradeRs. handicraftsRs. food processingRs. and service enterprises. g) Preference shall be given to women SHGs and groups operating in rural and minority-concentrated areas.

name: Production Linked Incentive Support on JDPs
brief_description: The scheme "Production Linked Incentive Support on JDPs" was launched by the National Jute BoardRs. Ministry of Textiles. The scheme aims to make Indian Jute Diversified Products cost-competitive globallyRs. increase market shareRs. attract more entrepreneursRs. and increase export values to 16Rs./- by 2026. The scheme provides a financial incentive by reimbursing five percent of the cost of jute raw material used in manufacturing exported Jute Diversified ProductsRs. limited to three percent of the sales valueRs. subject to a maximum of 12Rs./- per unit per annum. The applicant must be a Jute Mill Company or MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium Enterprise unit set up within India engaged in manufacturing and exporting Jute Diversified Products. The scheme is implemented by the National Jute Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted online.
benefits: - Financial incentive reimbursing 5% of the cost of Jute Raw Material used in manufacturing exported Jute Diversified Products. - The reimbursement is limited to 3% of the sales value of Jute Diversified Products exportsRs. whichever is less. - The maximum financial support provided is 12Rs./- per unit per annum. ##### ***Disbursement*** - Payment for all Jute Material purchased and receipt of export proceeds must be made only through electronic means or banks. No cash transactions will be considered for the incentive. - Claims are paid on a quarterly basis within two months of submissionRs. provided the claims are complete in all respects with the required documentation. - If a claimant misses a quarterRs. they can submit it with the immediate next quarter's claims along with a written explanation. ##### ***Conditions*** The beneficiaries under the scheme must be Aadhaar-seeded. - The claimants must give an undertaking to the National Jute Board that they have not availed nor will they avail of any other incentive on the Jute Diversified Products production and exports on which this incentive has been claimed. - Claimants must update their documents and data at the beginning of every financial year. - Any unit availing the benefits is liable to return the amount of subsidy with interest (at prevailing bank interest rates for commercial loans) if found to have claimed benefits using false or fraudulent documents.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a Jute Mill Company or a MicroRs. Small and Medium Enterprise unit set up within the geographical boundary of India. - The applicant must be actively engaged in the manufacturing and export of Jute Diversified Products. - The applicant must ensure the manufactured products contain more than 50% jute content by weightRs. or more than 33% by weight in the case of multifibres where jute is the dominant fibre.

name: Term Loan Scheme of NMDFC
brief_description: Under this scheme of NMDFCRs. credit is extended for financing economically viable income generation ventures. Loan of upto 20Rs./- under Credit Line-1 and upto 30Rs./- under Credit line -2 is extended to beneficiaries at 6% p.a. & 8% p.a. respectively. FurtherRs. concession of 2% is extended to women beneficiaries under Credit Line-2.
benefits: - Concessional Credit to the beneficiaries among minority communities.
eligibility: a) The applicant must be Indian and belong to one of the six notified minority communities: MuslimRs. ChristianRs. SikhRs. BuddhistRs. ParsiRs. or Jain. b) The annual family income should not exceed: Rs. 3.00 lakh per annum under Credit Line1. Rs. 8.00 lakh per annum under Credit Line2. c) The applicant must be 18 years or above and capable of undertaking self-employment activity. d) The applicant should not have any outstanding loan or default under any Central/State Government financing scheme. e) The project proposal should be economically viable and technically feasible. f) The applicant must have a valid Aadhaar-linked bank accountRs. residence proofRs. income certificateRs. and minority community certificate issued by a competent authority. g) Preference shall be given to womenRs. youthRs. and occupational groups belonging to the minority communities. h) Insurance of the borrower and assets financed is mandatory under NMDFC guidelines.

name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
brief_description: The scheme "Pre-Matric Scholarships to the Students Belonging to Scheduled Castes & Others with Component 1: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students" has been launched by the Department of Social Justice & EmpowermentRs. Ministry of Social Justice & EmpowermentRs. Government of IndiaRs. and aims to support parents of Scheduled Caste children through financial assistance for education at the pre-matric stageRs. improve participation in educationRs. minimise dropoutsRs. particularly during transition stagesRs. and enhance opportunities for progression to post-matric education. Through this schemeRs. consolidated academic allowances are provided to Scheduled Caste students studying in Classes IX and X. The scheme is implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory AdministrationsRs. which award scholarships to eligible domiciled students. Scholarships are available for studies in India in Government schools and recognised private schools having a valid UDISE code. The scholarship amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary through Direct Benefit Transfer. The scheme also provides additional support to Divyang students through an extra allowance. > **Objective:** - To supportRs. through financial assistanceRs. parents of children belonging to Scheduled Castes for the education of their wards at the pre-matric stage. - To improve the participation of Scheduled Caste students in education. - To minimise the incidence of dropoutsRs. especially during transition from primary to higher levels and from elementary to secondary education. - To improve academic performance and increase opportunities for progression to post-matric education.
benefits: 1. **Day Scholar**: 3500 Per Annum1. **Hosteller:** 7000 for Hostellers. **Additional benefits for Person with Disability (PwD)** studying in private unaided Schools - 1. Divyang (Disabled) students are eligible for an additional allowance equal to 10% of the applicable academic allowance. 1. Disability should be certified under the provisions of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities ActRs. 2016 by the designated competent authority.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should pursue studies in India. 1. The applicant should be studying in a Government school or a recognized private school having a valid UDISE code. 1. The applicant should not hold another educational scholarship for studying in Classes I to X. If awarded another scholarshipRs. the applicant may avail only one scholarship and should inform the concerned authorities about the option chosen. 1. The applicant should maintain satisfactory academic performance and at least 75% attendance in every academic year for continuation of the scholarship. 1. The applicant should be promoted to the next class for automatic renewal of the scholarship. 1. The applicant repeating the same class is not eligible to receive the scholarship for that class for a second or subsequent year.

name: National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme
brief_description: The National Savings (Monthly Income Account) SchemeRs. 2019Rs. popularly known as the Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS)Rs. is a government-backed small savings scheme administered by the Ministry of Finance. The scheme provides a fixed monthly income to investors through periodic interest payments on a one-time deposit made at the time of account opening. The scheme is designed for individuals seeking a secure investment option with regular monthly returns. Accounts can be opened individuallyRs. jointly by up to three adultsRs. or on behalf of eligible minors. > **Key Features** - Government-backed savings scheme with assured returns. - Single deposit account with no recurring contributions. - Monthly interest payout to the account holder. - Account tenure of 5 years. - Joint accounts permitted with up to three adults. - Nomination facility available as per applicable rules. - Transfer of an account from one post office to another is permitted. - Multiple accounts may be opened subject to the prescribed deposit limits.
benefits: > **Deposit Limits** - Minimum Deposit: 1Rs. and thereafter in multiples of 1Rs.. - Maximum Deposit in Single Account: 4Rs.. - Maximum Deposit in Minor Account/Account opened by Guardian: 4Rs.. - Maximum Deposit in Joint Account: 9Rs.. > **Interest** - Interest Rate: 7.6% per annum (as specified in the 2019 notification; subject to revision by the Government from time to time). - Interest is payable monthly from the date of deposit. - Unclaimed monthly interest does not earn additional interest. > **Maturity** - The account matures after 5 years from the date of opening. - On maturityRs. the deposited amount along with eligible interest is payable to the account holder upon submission of the prescribed application. > **Premature Closure** - Premature closure is allowed after completion of one year from the date of account opening: - Closure before completion of 3 years: Deduction of 2% of the principal deposit. - Closure after 3 years but before maturity: Deduction of 1% of the principal deposit. > **Death of Account Holder** - In the event of the account holder's death before maturityRs. the account may be closed and the deposit refunded along with interest up to the month preceding the month of refundRs. as per applicable rules.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a citizen of India. 1. The applicant must be residing in India. 1. The account may be opened by a single adult. 1. The account may be opened jointly by up to three adults. 1. A minor who has attained the age of 10 years may open and operate the account in his/her own name. 1. A guardian may open the account on behalf of a minor or a person of unsound mind.

Government of IndiaRs. aiming to create a national database of Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) and issue a Unique Disability Identity Card to each individual to ensure transparencyRs. efficiencyRs. and ease in delivering government benefits. benefits: The Unique Disability Identity (UDID) cardRs. also known as the Swavlamban CardRs. is a mandatory document for persons with disabilities (PwDs) in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu to access various central and state government welfare schemes. The applicant should have secured admission through the All India Entrance Examination (AIEE) conducted for ICAR admissions. 1. name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
brief_description:
NPS Vatsalya Scheme was announced by the Honble Finance Minister in the Union Budget for FY 2024-25. It is designed exclusively for minors below 18 years of ageRs. with the objective of nurturing a culture of savings from an early ageRs. promoting financial literacyRs. and building a secure financial future for children. The scheme is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) under the PFRDA ActRs. 2013. Under this schemeRs. parents or guardians can open an NPS Vatsalya account for their children and contribute until the child reaches 18 years. The minimum contribution is 250 per yearRs. and there is no limit on the maximum contribution. NPS Vatsalya fosters early financial planningRs. disciplined savingRs. and professional investment of funds dedicated to a child's future financial securityRs. with regulatory safeguards.
**The NPS Vatsalya Scheme offers the following:**
**Modes of opening an NPS Vatsalya account:** - **Physical mode**: By visiting any registered PoP - **Online facility** provided by PoPs- **eNPS platform** of NPS Trust - Any other electronic mode approved by PFRDA
**Contribution:** - Account Opening contribution: Min. 250/- and Max no limit. - Subsequent contribution: Min. 250/- p.a. and Max no limit.
**Gift Contribution:** In addition to Parents/guardiansRs. relatives and friends can gift contributions to the NPS Vatsalya account.
**Investment** To manage investments of the contributions to the accountRs. parents/guardians can choose any one pension fund (PF) registered with the PFRDA .
**Upon Attainment of the age of 18 Years:** - Upon attainment of 18 years of ageRs. the subscriber shall continue under NPS Vatsalya for a period of up to three years (till 21 years)Rs. unless the subscriber opts to exit or shift to NPS All Citizen Model or any other applicable model. - Upon attainment of 18 years of ageRs. the subscriber shall be required to complete fresh KYCRs. furnish nominee(s) details and any other stipulated details
**Exit and withdrawal from the account:** - For the purpose of education of subscriberRs. treatment of specified illnessesRs. disability more than 75%Rs. or the reasons as may be specified by PFRDA in the interest of the minor subscriberRs. the guardian shall be allowed to partially withdraw up to 25% of subscribers contribution excluding returns thereon after minimum 3 years from the date of opening of account. Subscribers/Guardians may take up to 2 partial withdrawals until the subscriber attains 18 years of age. After the subscriber turns 18Rs. upon completion of the prescribed KYC requirementsRs. two additional partial withdrawals are allowed during the period between 18 and 21 years of age. Such a facility shall be made available on a declaration basis. - In the case of the death of the minor subscriberRs. the entire accumulated corpus is to be paid to the guardian or nominee(s) or legal heir(s)Rs. as the case may be. The recipient shall also have the option to transfer the proceeds to their individual NPS account. - In case of the death of the guardian registered under the accountRs. another guardian is to be registered on behalf of the minor subscriber by submitting the KYC documents as specified by the PFRDA from time to time. - In case of the death of both parentsRs. the legally appointed guardian may continue the account with or without making contributions to the accountRs. and upon attainment of 18 years of age by the subscriberRs. the subscriber shall have an option to continue or exit from the scheme. - The subscriber shall be allowed to exit only upon attainment of age of 18 years. Upon such exitRs. up to 80% of the accumulated corpus can be withdrawn as lump sumRs. and the balance is to be utilised for purchase of an annuity. In case the accumulated corpus is less than 8 LakhRs. the subscriber shall have the option to withdraw the entire accumulated corpus. - If no option of either exit or shift to NPS is chosen by the age 21Rs. the account automatically shifts to NPS in a higher-equity scheme under Multiple Scheme FrameworkRs. under the same Pension Fund and thereafter terms and conditions of NPS shall apply. Withdrawals will only be allowed after KYC is completed. - The exits and withdrawals under the scheme shall be governed by the provisions of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pensions System) RegulationsRs. 2015 and amendments thereof.
benefits: 1. **Power of compounding along with financial security** - Starting early allows money to grow significantly over time through compounding creating a financial cushion for the future.1. **Financial discipline**: SmallRs. regular investments build a strong habit of saving and planning.1. **Empower your child:** Early exposure to saving builds responsible financial behaviour for life.1. **Tax Efficient** - Attractive tax benefits under the Income Tax ActRs. 1961.1. **Optimum Returns** - Provides market-linked returns based on pension funds performance.1. **Transparent** - 24/7 online access to the accountRs. with mandatory public disclosures ensuring transparency.
eligibility: 1. The scheme is available to all Indian citizens who are aged below 18Rs. including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) 1. The account should be opened by parents/guardian in the minor's nameRs. as they will operate the account exclusively for the benefit of the minor. 1. If the guardian is court-appointedRs. they must submit a copy of the court order confirming the guardianship and KYC documents. 1. The guardian must comply with KYC norms as per the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) requirements.

name: National Food Security Mission NFSM
brief_description: The core objective of the Mission is to bridge the yield gap in respect of these crops through dissemination of improved technologies and farm management practices. Under the programmeRs. various incentives like production and distribution of seedsRs. supply of seed mini kitsRs. Front Line/Cluster DemonstrationsRs. improved farm implementsRs. bio-pesticidesRs. micronutrientsRs. bio-fertilizers etc. are provided to the farmers.
benefits: The scheme targets to provide following benefits: 1) Enhance production and productivity of crops 2) Promotion and extension of improved technologies and seed varieties through Cluster DemonstrationRs. Cluster Frontline DemonstrationRs. and Frontline Demonstration 3) Assistance for quality / certified seeds production and distribution 4) Support for nutrient management and pest management 5) Provision of flexi component for Interventions covering farm implements/ machinesRs. capacity building of farmersRs. water carrying pipesRs. post-harvest technologies like Dal Mill/de-stoning/ gradingRs. etc. S. No.ComponentBenefit1DemonstrationThe incentives for demonstration in one ha area for sole crop (excluding coarse cereals) will Rs 9000/- and 15000/- for a cropping-system based demonstration.For coarse cerealsRs. the incentive for demonstration in one ha area will be 6000/-2Seed DistributionAssistance for purchase of seeds will be available to selected farmers for the area not exceeding 2 ha each in a crop season as per provisions in the DBT. States will be allowed to make allocation to SC/ST farmers proportionate to their population in the States/districts. 2) At least 33% allocation of the fund is to be made for small and marginal farmers. 3) At least 30% allocation of the fund is to be made for women farmers. 4) All the farmers are entitled to avail the assistance for various components of the Mission limited to 5 hectares in a season. **Criteria for selection of districts:** 1) Districts with area more than 50Rs. ha and yield below State average yield under NFSM-Rice and NFSM-Wheat have been selected. 2) All districts of north-eastern states (except Assam) with at least 5000 ha area under rice have been selected. 3) Districts with at least 15000 ha area under rice or wheat in hill states of Himachal PradeshRs. Jammu & Kashmir and Uttarakhand have been selected. 4) All districts of 29 states have been included under NFSM pulses. 5) In case of coarse cereals (Maize and Barley)Rs. the districts covering 70% of the total coarse cereals area of the state have been selected. 6) All States growing JowarRs. BajraRs. Ragi and Small Millets will be covered under the programme of NFSM-Nutri-Cereals (JowarRs. BajraRs. Ragi and Small Millets). For a Cluster Front Line Demonstration (CFLD) organised by ICARRs. each cluster must be atleast 25 ha For a Front Line Demonstration (FLD) organised by ICARRs. each cluster must be atleast 1 ha For a Demonstration organised by state governmentRs. each cluster must be atleast 100 ha (25 ha for Hilly and North East states)

name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)
brief_description: The scheme Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) was launched by the Department of PharmaceuticalsRs. Ministry of Chemicals & FertilizersRs. in November 2008. Branded medicines are sold at significantly higher prices than their unbranded generic equivalentsRs. though both are identical in therapeutic value. Given the widespread poverty across the countryRs. making reasonably priced quality generic medicines available in the market benefits all sections of society. **Objectives:** To make quality generic medicines available at affordable prices to allRs. PMBJP was launched by the Government of India in November 2008. Under the schemeRs. dedicated outlets known as Janaushadhi Kendras are opened to provide generic medicines at affordable prices. As of March 2026Rs. more than 19Rs. Kendras are functional across the country. The product basket comprises 2Rs. medicines and 300 surgical items. The scheme is implemented by the Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) [erstwhile BPPI]Rs. registered under the Societies Registration Act. **Objectives include:** - Ensuring access to quality medicines for allRs. especially the poor and deprived. - Creating awareness about generic medicines through education and publicity to counter the perception that quality is linked only to high prices. - Generating employment by engaging entrepreneurs in opening Kendras.
benefits: > **The scheme is operated by government agencies as well as private entrepreneurs.** **1**. **Normal Incentive:** - PMBJKs run by entrepreneurs/Pharmacists/Trusts/Societies & Charitable Organizations linked with PMBI headquarters through PoS software receive incentives. - Incentive @ 20% of monthly purchase from PMBIRs. subject to a ceiling of Rs. 20Rs. per month. - Disbursed on a 50:50 basis: - 10% incentive on purchase (up to Rs. 10Rs.). - 10% incentive for maintaining stock of 200 medicines (up to Rs. 10Rs.). **2**. **Special Incentive:** - One-time grant of Rs. 2 lakh for women entrepreneursRs. SC/STRs. DivyangjanRs. ex-servicemenRs. and entrepreneurs in aspirational districtsRs. HimalayanRs. islandRs. and North-Eastern regions. - 1.5 lakh reimbursement for furniture/fixtures. - 0.5 lakh reimbursement for computerRs. internetRs. printerRs. etc. **3**. **Affordable Medicines:** - Prices of Janaushadhi medicines are 50%80% lower than branded medicines. **4.** **Quality Assurance:** - Medicines procured only from WHO-GMP certified suppliers. **5**. **Testing:** - Each batch is tested at NABL-accredited laboratories. **6**. **Margin:** - Operating agencies receive a 20% margin on MRP (excluding taxes) of each drug. > **Janaushadhi Suvidha Sanitary Napkin:** Launched on 27 August 2019Rs. Janaushadhi Suvidha Oxo-biodegradable sanitary napkins are available at Rs. 1 per pad. - Distributed through all Kendras nationwide. - Cumulative sales crossed 100 crore pads by March 2026.
eligibility: **Individuals:** - The applicant must hold D. Pharma/B. Pharma degree or employ qualified pharmacists. **Organizations/NGOs:** - The applicant must employ B. Pharma/D. Pharma degree holders. **Government hospital premises (including medical colleges):** - Preference to reputed NGOs/charitable organizations though individuals are also eligible.

name: Pre Matric Scholarship For Students With Disabilities
brief_description: The scheme "Pre-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities" by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)Rs. Ministry of Social Justice & EmpowermentRs. Government of India aims to support students with disabilities to continue their studiesRs. minimize drop-out rates during the transition from elementary education to higher educationRs. and improve participation of students with disabilities in Classes IX and X at the pre-matric stage of education. Through this schemeRs. maintenance allowanceRs. book grantRs. and disability allowance are provided to students with disabilities studying in Classes IX and X. The scheme is implemented through the National Scholarship PortalRs. and the scholarship amount is transferred to the bank accounts of beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). > **Objectives:** - To support students with disabilities for further studies and help them prepare to earn their livelihood and live with dignity. - To minimise the incidence of drop-outRs. especially during the transition from elementary education to higher education. - To improve the participation of students with disabilities in Classes IX and X and at the pre-matric stage of education.
benefits: 1. **Maintenance Allowance** * ( per Month): Day Scholars: 500Rs. Hostellers: 800.1. **Book Grant**: 1000/- per annum.1. **Disability Allowances** ( per Annum): - Visually Impaired: 4Rs.. - Hearing Impaired: 2Rs.. - Physically Disabled (OH): 2Rs.. - Intellectual Disabilities: 4Rs.. - Other disabilities not covered above: 2Rs.. > **[NOTE: (*) means for 12 months in an academic year]**
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be an Indian national. 1. The applicant should be a student with a benchmark disability and should have a valid disability certificate issued by the competent authority. 1. The applicant should be a regularRs. full-time student studying in Classes IX and X in: - A Government school; or - A school recognised by the Government; or - A school recognised by the Central/State Board of Secondary Education. 1. The applicants parents/guardians income from all sources should not exceed 2Rs./- per annum. 1. Not more than 2 children with disabilities of the same parents will be eligible for benefits under the scheme. In case the second child is a twinRs. the scholarship will be admissible to both twins. 1. Preference/Priority/Reservation/Relaxation 1. 50% of the total scholarships available each year are reserved for female candidates. If adequate eligible female candidates are not availableRs. remaining slots may be utilised for suitable male candidates.

name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
brief_description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan" was launched by the Ministry of Labour and EmploymentRs. Government of IndiaRs. and the scheme aims to ensure old age protection for unorganised workers. The scheme provides a minimum assured pension of 3Rs./- per month after attaining the age of 60 yearsRs. matching government contributionsRs. and a family pension amounting to 50% of the pension for the spouse. The applicant must be an unorganised worker in the entry age group of 18 to 40 years with a monthly income of 15Rs./- or lessRs. and must make regular age-specific monthly contributions. The scheme is implemented by the Life Insurance Corporation of India and Common Services Centres.
benefits:
- A **minimum assured pension of 3Rs./- per month** is provided to the subscriber after attaining the age of 60 years.- A matching contribution is provided by the Central Government on a 50:50 basisRs. where an equal amount to the subscriber's age-specific contribution (ranging from 55/- to 200/-) is credited to the pension account.
**** During the receipt of the pensionRs. if the subscriber dies:*** The spouse of the beneficiary shall be entitled to receive a family pension equal to 50% of the pension received by the beneficiary. **** If a beneficiary has given regular contributions and died due to any cause before the age of 60 years:*** _Their spouse will be entitled to join and continue the scheme subsequently by the payment of regular contributions._ **** If a beneficiary has given regular contributions and died due to any cause before the age of 60 yearsRs. and the spouse decides to exit:*** _The beneficiary's contribution along with accumulated interest as actually earned by the fund or at the savings bank interest rate (whichever is higher) will be returned._ **** If the subscriber exits the scheme within a period of less than 10 years:*** _The beneficiary's share of contribution only will be returned to them with the savings bank interest rate._ **** If the subscriber exits after a period of 10 years or more but before the superannuation age of 60 years:*** _The beneficiary's share of contribution along with accumulated interest as actually earned by the fund or at the savings bank interest rateRs. whichever is higherRs. will be returned._
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be an unorganised worker. 1. The applicant must have an entry age between 18 and 40 years. 1. The applicant must have a monthly income of 15Rs./- or less. 1. The applicant must possess a Savings Bank Account or Jan Dhan account number with an Indian Financial System Code. 1. The applicant must possess a mobile phone.

name: Kisan Credit Card
brief_description:
The KCC Scheme was introduced with the objective of providing adequate and timely credit to the farmers for their agricultural operations. The Government of India provides interest subvention of 2% and Prompt Repayment Incentive of 3% to the farmersRs. thus making the credit available at a very subsidized rate of 4% per annum. The scheme was further extended for the investment credit requirement of farmers viz. allied and non-farm activities in the year 2004 and further revisited in 2012 by a working Group under the Chairmanship of Shri T. M. BhasinRs. CMDRs. Indian Bank with a view to simplify the scheme and facilitate issue of Electronic Kisan Credit Cards. The scheme provides broad guidelines to banks for operationalizing the KCC scheme. Implementing banks will have the discretion to adopt the same to suit institution/location-specific requirements. **Objective / Purpose** The Kisan Credit Card scheme aims at providing adequate and timely credit support from the banking system under a single window with the flexible and simplified procedures to the farmers for their cultivation and other needs as indicated below : 1. To meet the short term credit requirements for the cultivation of crops; 1. Post-harvest expenses; 1. Produce marketing loan; 1. Consumption requirements of farmer household; 1. Working capital for maintenance of farm assets and activities allied to agriculture; 1. Investment credit requirement for agriculture and allied activities **Type of Card** - A magnetic stripe card with PIN (Personal Identification Number) with an ISO IIN (International Standards Organization International Identification Number) to enable access to all banks ATMs and micro ATMs - In cases where the Banks would want to utilize the centralized biometric authentication infrastructure of the UIDAI (Aadhaar authentication)Rs. debit cards with magnetic stripe and PIN with ISO IIN with biometric authentication of UIDAI can be provided. - Debit Cards with magnetic stripes and only biometric authentication can also be provided depending on the customer base of the bank. Till such timeRs. UIDAI becomes widespreadRs. if the banks want to get started without inter-operability using their existing centralized bio metric infrastructureRs. banks may do so. - Banks may choose to issue EMV (EuropayRs. MasterCard and VISARs. a global standard for the interoperation of integrated circuit cards) and RUPAY compliant chip cards with magnetic stripe and pin with ISO IIN. - FurtherRs. biometric authentication and smart cards may follow the common open standards prescribed by IDRBT and IBA. This will enable them to transact seamlessly with input dealers and also enable them to have the sales proceeds credited to their accounts when they sell their output at mandiesRs. procurement centresRs. etc
**Delivery Channels :** The following delivery channels shall be put in place to start with so that the Kisan Credit Card is used by the farmers to effectively transact their operations in their KCC account. 1. Withdrawal through ATMs / Micro ATM 1. Withdrawal through BCs using smart cards. 1. PoS machine through input dealers 1. Mobile Banking with IMPS capabilities / IVR 1. Aadhaar enabled Cards
benefits:
**Fixation of credit limit/Loan amount**

1. **The short-term limit to arrive for the first year: For farmers raising a single crop in a year:** Scale of finance for the crop (as decided by District Level Technical Committee) x Extent of area cultivated + 10% of limit towards post-harvest / household/consumption requirements + 20% of limit towards repairs and maintenance expenses of farm assets + crop insuranceRs. PAIS & asset insurance.1. **Limit for second & subsequent year**: First-year limit for crop cultivation purposes arrived at as above plus 10% of the limit towards cost escalation/increase in the scale of finance for every successive year ( 2ndRs. 3rdRs. 4th and 5th year) and estimated Term loan component for the tenure of Kisan Credit CardRs. i.e.Rs. five years.1. **For farmers raising more than one crop** in a yearRs. the limit is to be fixed as above depending upon the crops cultivated as per the proposed cropping pattern for the first year and an additional 10% of the limit towards cost escalation/increase in the scale of finance for every successive year (2ndRs. 3rdRs. 4th and 5th year). It is assumed that the farmer adopts the same cropping pattern for the remaining four years also. In case the cropping pattern adopted by the farmer is changed in the subsequent yearRs. the limit may be reworked. 1. **Term loans for investments** towards land developmentRs. minor irrigationRs. purchase of farm equipment and allied agricultural activities. The banks may fix the quantum of credit for the term and working capital limit for agricultural and allied activitiesRs. etc.Rs. based on the unit cost of the asset/s proposed to be acquired by the farmerRs. the allied activities already being undertaken on the farmRs. the banks judgment on repayment capacity vis-a-vis total loan burden devolving on the farmerRs. including existing loan obligations.1. **The long-term loan limit** is based on the proposed investments during the five-year period and the banks perception of the repaying capacity of the farmer 1. **Maximum Permissible Limit**: The short-term loan limit arrived for the 5th year plus the estimated long-term loan requirement will be the Maximum Permissible Limit (MPL) and treated as the Kisan Credit Card Limit.1. **Fixation of Sub-limits for other than Marginal Farmers:**


- **Short-term** loans and term loans are governed by different interest rates. BesidesRs. at presentRs. short-term crop loans are covered under Interest Subvention Scheme/ Prompt Repayment Incentive scheme. FurtherRs. repayment schedules and norms are different for short-term and term loans. HenceRs. in order to have operational and accounting convenienceRs. the card limit is to be bifurcated into separate sub-limits for short-term cash credit limit cum savings account and term loans. - **The drawing limit** for short-term cash credit should be fixed based on the cropping pattern and the amounts for crop productionRs. repairs and maintenance of farm assets and consumption may be allowed to be drawn at the convenience of the farmer. In case the revision of the scale of finance for any year by the district-level committee exceeds the notional hike of 10% contemplated while fixing the five-year limitRs. a revised drawable limit may be fixed and the farmer is advised about the same. In case such revisions require the card limit itself to be enhanced (4th or 5th year)Rs. the same may be done and the farmer be so advised. For term loansRs. instalments may be allowed to be withdrawn based on the nature of the investment and the repayment schedule drawn as per the economic life of the proposed investments. It is to be ensured that at any point in timeRs. the total liability should be within the drawing limit of the concerned year. - Wherever the card limit/liability so arrived warrants additional securityRs. the banks may take suitable collateral as per their policy.

name: Annapurna Yojana
brief_description: The scheme Annapurna Yojana implemented by the Women and Child Development and Social Welfare DepartmentRs. Government of West Bengal aims to provide assured monthly financial assistance to eligible women residing in the state for their empowerment and socio-economic upliftment. Under the schemeRs. eligible women receive 3Rs./- per month through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The financial assistance is credited directly into the Aadhaar-linked bank account of the beneficiary. Existing beneficiaries of the "Lakshmir Bhandar" Scheme are migrated to the "Annapurna Yojana" subject to prescribed conditions. Online application facilities for new applicants are available through the Annapurna Yojana Portal from 1st JuneRs. 2026.
benefits: - **Monthly Financial Assistance:** Eligible women receive 3Rs./- per month. > **Note:** - **Mode of Disbursement:** The financial assistance is transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). - **Bank Account Requirement:** The amount is credited to the Aadhaar-linked bank account of the beneficiary.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a woman. - The applicant must be aged between 25 to 60 yearsRs. - The applicant must not be in any permanent government employment getting regular salary/ pension under the union or this state governmentRs. any statutory bodyRs. government undertakingRs. panchayatRs. municipal bodyRs. local body; teaching or non-teaching employment under this state government's aided educational institutionRs. etc. - The applicant must not be paying any Income Tax. > **Notes:** - All the existing beneficiaries of the "Lakshmir Bhandar" Scheme shall be migrated to the "Annapurna Yojana" except deadRs. shiftedRs. deletedRs. and absentee electors identified during SIR-2026Rs. deletion in the 2TM list after publication of draft listRs. deleted after adjudicationRs. ASDD found during voter slip distribution. - Beneficiaries who have filed an appeal before the SIR Tribunal/applications under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act shall get financial assistance under the New Scheme till disposal of their applications. LikewiseRs. names of dead and shifted beneficiaries will be deleted in the future on a regular basis.

name: NBCFDC General Loan Scheme
brief_description: The scheme "General Loan" has been launched by the National Backwards Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC)Rs. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and aims to provide loan assistance for various income-generating activities such as agriculture and allied activitiesRs. small businessRs. artisan and traditional occupationsRs. transport sector activitiesRs. service sector activitiesRs. and technical and professional trades/courses. Through this schemeRs. financial assistance is provided to eligible members of Backwards Classes for undertaking income-generating activities. The scheme is implemented by the National Backwards Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) through its Channel Partners. NBCFDC finances up to 85% of the project costRs. while the remaining 15% is contributed by the Channel Partner and/or beneficiary. The applicable rate of interest varies according to the loan amount. The loan is repayable in quarterly instalments over a maximum period of 8 yearsRs. including a moratorium period of 6 months on recovery of the principal amount.
benefits: 1. Loan assistance of up to 15Rs./- for income-generating activities such as agriculture and allied activitiesRs. small businessRs. artisan and traditional occupationsRs. transport sectorRs. service sectorRs. and technical/professional trades or courses. 1. NBCFDC finances 85% of the project costRs. while 15% is contributed by the Channel Partner and/or beneficiary. 1. Concessional interest rates ranging from 6% to 8% per annumRs. depending on the loan amount. 1. Repayment in quarterly instalments over a maximum period of 8 yearsRs. including a 6-month moratorium on recovery of the principal amount.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be an Entrepreneur 1. The applicant should be a member of the Backwards ClassesRs. as notified by the Central Government or the State Government from time to time. 1. The applicant's annual family income should be up to 3Rs./-.

name: Scheme for Dronacharya Award for Outstanding Coaches in Sports and Games
brief_description: "Scheme for Dronacharya Award for Outstanding Coaches in Sports and Games" has been launched by the Department of SportsRs. Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. The award is conferred upon coaches who have made exceptional contributions to sports coaching and athlete development. **Objectives:** - To honour coaches who have consistently produced outstanding international-level sportspersons. - To motivate coaches to dedicate themselves to improving sports performance standards and bringing glory to India through international achievements. **Sports Disciplines Covered:** The award is given to coaches associated with: - Olympic sports disciplines. - Non-Olympic sports disciplines recognized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. - Indigenous sports recognized by the Government of India. **Award Categories:** - Dronacharya Award (Regular) - Dronacharya Award (Lifetime Contribution) **Number of Awards:** - OrdinarilyRs. not more than 5 awards are given in a calendar year. - Out of theseRs. 2 awards are reserved for Lifetime Contribution in Coaching.
benefits: > **Selected awardees receive:** **Dronacharya Award (Regular)** - Statuette - Certificate - Ceremonial Dress - Cash Prize of 10Rs. **Dronacharya Award (Lifetime Contribution)** - Statuette - Certificate - Ceremonial Dress - Cash Prize of 15Rs. **Additional Information** - The awards are ordinarily conferred by the President of India on 29th August (National Sports Day). - No individual can receive the award more than once. - The award may be conferred posthumously.
eligibility: **Eligibility for Regular Dronacharya Award** 1. The applicant must be a coach at the GrassrootRs. DevelopmentRs. or Elite level. 1. The applicant must have produced outstanding sporting achievements during the four years immediately preceding the award year. 1. Submit details of the athletes coached and the coaching period claimed for the achievements. **Eligibility for Lifetime Contribution Category** 1. The applicant must have contributed to coaching and athlete development for 20 years or more. 1. In the case of Grassroot/Development coachesRs. they have been associated with an athlete for at least 5 years during the 20-year period.

name: Labour Welfare Scheme (Health)
brief_description: The scheme "Labour Welfare Scheme (Health)" was launched by the Ministry of Labour and EmploymentRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to provide comprehensive health care facilities and medical financial assistance to unorganised sector workers. The scheme provides outpatient dispensary servicesRs. hospital careRs. and monetary reimbursements up to 7Rs./- for critical illnesses such as cancerRs. heart diseasesRs. and kidney transplantationRs. alongside subsistence allowances and maternity benefits. The applicant must be a registered beediRs. cineRs. or specified non-coal mine worker or their dependant.
benefits:
##### ***General Healthcare*** - Healthcare facilities are provided to workers and their dependants through a network of 10 hospitals and 285 dispensaries. - Financial assistance of 300/- is provided for the purchase of spectacles. ##### ***Heart Diseases*** Reimbursement of expenditure up to 1Rs./- is provided for the treatment of heart diseases. ##### ***Kidney Diseases*** Reimbursement of expenditure up to 2Rs./- is provided for kidney transplantation. ##### ***Cancer*** - Reimbursement of actual expenses on treatmentRs. medicinesRs. and diet chargesRs. up to 7Rs./-Rs. is provided for cancer. - Travel allowance for a cancer patient and one attendant is payable at 50/- per day per person. ##### ***Minor Surgeries*** Reimbursement of expenditure up to 30Rs./- is provided for minor surgeries like herniaRs. appendectomyRs. ulcerRs. gynaecological diseasesRs. and prostate diseases. ##### ***Maternity and Family Welfare*** - Grant of 1Rs./- per delivery is provided to female workers as a maternity benefit. - Monetary incentive of 500/- per head is provided for undergoing sterilization under the family welfare initiative. ##### ***Tuberculosis*** - Subsistence allowance of 750/- to 1Rs./- per month is granted for tuberculosis patients. - Maintenance allowance of 600/- to 750/- per month and medicine cost of 50/- per month are payable for domiciliary treatment of tuberculosis. - Daily food allowance of 15/- or a yearly grant of 20Rs./- is provided per tuberculosis patient. ##### ***Leprosy*** - Financial assistance of 30/- per patient per day for indoor treatment and 6/- to 60/- per patient per day for outdoor treatment is provided for leprosy. - Subsistence allowance of 300/- per month with dependants and 200/- per month without dependants is provided for leprosy patients. ##### ***Mental Diseases*** - Maintenance allowance of 180/- per month for state beds and 900/- per month for independent beds for six months is provided for mental diseases. - Maintenance allowance for dependants of mental disease patients is provided at 600/- to 750/- per month for nine months.
##### ***Conditions for Availment*** _* Prior approval of the concerned Welfare Commissioner is necessary before beginning treatments for heart ailmentsRs. kidney treatmentRs. and cancer._ _* The ophthalmic benefit for purchasing spectacles is given only to the worker and not to their dependants._ _* The maternity benefit is limited strictly to the first two deliveries._
eligibility:
- The applicant must be a registered beedi workerRs. cine workerRs. or an ironRs. manganeseRs. chromeRs. limestoneRs. dolomiteRs. or mica mine worker. - The applicant must be a dependant of an eligible worker to claim dependant-specific medical benefits. - The applicant must possess a valid identity card indicating their status as a recognized unorganised worker.
***Post-Selection Conditions / Special Cases*** - _The applicant must be a female worker undergoing her first or second delivery to avail the maternity benefit._ - _The applicant must have exactly two children to avail the family planning operation scheme benefit._

name: Scheme For Adolescent Girls
brief_description: The scheme "Scheme for Adolescent Girls" has been launched by the Ministry of Women and Child DevelopmentRs. Government of IndiaRs. and aims to provide a structured support system for adolescent girls through a life cycle approach. The scheme is implemented under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 through the concerned States/Union Territories. The scheme covers adolescent girls in the age group of 14-18 years in identified areasRs. including Aspirational Districts of States and North-Eastern States. The services are delivered through the existing Anganwadi Centres and other linked platforms for reaching the beneficiaries. > **Objectives:** - To improve the nutritional and health status and self-development of girls in the age group of 14-18 years. - To provide the adolescent girl with the required linkage with educationRs. life skillsRs. literacy and numeracy skills through the non-formal stream of educationRs. to stimulate a desire for more social exposure and knowledgeRs. and to help them improve their decision-making capabilities. - To train and equip the adolescent girl to improve/upgrade other life skills. - To promote awareness of healthRs. hygieneRs. nutrition and family welfareRs. home management and child care and to take all measuresRs. so as to facilitate their marrying only after attaining the age of 18 years and if possibleRs. even later. - To enable a better understanding of environment-related social issues and their impact on the lives of adolescent girls. - To encourage adolescent girls to initiate various activities so that they may become productive and useful members of society.
benefits: > **Nutritional Benefits:** 1. The applicant receives supplementary nutrition containing 600 caloriesRs. 18-20 grams of protein and micronutrients. 1. The supplementary nutrition is provided in the form of Take Home Ration (THR). 1. The benefit is provided for 300 days in a year. 1. The Take Home Ration is prepared with fortified micronutrients as per nutritional standards. 1. Age-specific processed food mixtures are labelled to ensure consumption by the targeted beneficiaries. 1. Last-mile tracking of services is undertaken through Poshan Tracker. > **Non-Nutrition Benefits:** 1. Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation is provided. 1. Health Check-up and Referral Services are provided. 1. Nutrition & Health Education (NHE) is provided. 1. Promotion of menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls is ensured. 1. Participation of adolescent girls is encouraged through the Peer Educator Programme for addressing adolescent issues and awareness about available services. 1. Skill training is provided to generate livelihood opportunities for adolescent girls trained under the scheme.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be an adolescent girl in the age group of 14-18 years. 1. The applicant should be identified by the concerned State Government. 1. The applicant should belong to the covered areas under the schemeRs. including Aspirational Districts of StatesRs. including Assam and North-Eastern States. 1. The applicant should have an Aadhaar number to avail benefits under the scheme.

name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom:Small Cardamom Irrigation Land Development : Rain water harvesting structure (nos)
brief_description: The Rain Water Harvesting Structure Scheme implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and IndustryRs. Government of IndiaRs. and as per the Modalities and Scheme Guidelines approved by the Competent Authority for the implementation of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion and Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (202122 to 202526)Rs. financial assistance is provided to motivate growers to bring more area under irrigation and land development through the construction of rain water harvesting structures. The scheme aims to increase productivity and improve the quality of small cardamom.
benefits: 1. 33.33 % of cost of construction subject to a maximum of 18Rs. per structure for General and 75% subject to maximum of 40Rs. /- per structure for SC/ST. 1. The above assistance will be for a structure of 200 cu. Mt. capacity lined with silpauline sheet. For lesser capacity the assistance will be limited proportionate to the water holding capacity. 1. Devices can be for harvesting water from direct rainfall as well as surface run off without blocking the natural flow of water including streams. 1. Registered cardamom growers having land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a registered small cardamom grower eligible under the scheme guidelines of the Spices Board. 1. The rain water harvesting structure should not block the natural flow of waterRs. streamsRs. or drainage channelsRs. and should not create objections from the local community or concerned authorities. 1. The constructed structure must be inspected by the designated officialsRs. and assistance will be recommended only for eligible cases as per the approved delegation. 1. The Inspecting Officer must ensure that all scheme conditions are complied with before recommending the case for sanction. 1. Random checking of the approved structures may be conducted by the respective controlling officers.

name: Investment Promotion Scheme (IPS) 2022- for Thrust Sectors: Scheme For Vaccine Manufacturing Units
brief_description: The scheme Scheme For Vaccine Manufacturing Units is a sub scheme under the Investment Promotion Scheme (IPS)- 2022 for Thrust Sectors. It was launched on 07th May 2022 for a period of five years by the Dept. of IndustriesRs. U.T. Administration Of Dadra & Nagar Haveli And Daman & Diu. > **Objective of the "Investment Promotion Scheme (IPS)- 2022:** - The scheme envisages to provide incentives and assistance to the MSME Sector in order to nurture them and protect them from market vagaries thereby making them vibrant and successful. - The Scheme intends to provide impetus for the identified Thrust sectors such as FurnitureRs. MarbleRs. IT & ITeS Rs. Electric Vehicles & Spare PartsRs. Toys and Semi-Conductor Industries SectorRs. Medical Equipment and AccessoriesRs. Medical diagnostics and AYUSH ProductsRs. Vaccine Manufacturing unitsRs. Food ProcessingRs. Marine Products thereby making the U.T as a hub of manufacturing of these Products. - To double the value of Export of the Processed Products as well as to make the U.TRs. a center for these identified export products. - To incentivize industry to take up environment protection measures for judicious use of scarce resources and as well as to ensure inter generational equity. - To reduce unemployment among the local residents and incentivize the industries to employ resident laborers. - To maximize Women participation in the business sector by providing incentives. - To encourage first generation Entrepreneurs and support them in their entrepreneurial endeavor. - To hone the Entrepreneurship skills of the youth of the Territory and create a skillful workforce. - To provide further fillip to the specialized Textile sector such as Technical textilesRs. FabricsRs. CarpetsRs. GarmentsRs. Apparels and Industries Manufacturing Textile MachineryRs. Medical FabricsRs. therefore making the U.T. a Special Hub for Technical Textiles. - To promote innovation in Industrial sector by encouraging industry to involve themselves in Research & Development (R&D) works and to obtain Patents bothRs. National and International Level. **Objective of the " Scheme For Vaccine Manufacturing Units" Sub-scheme:** Under this schemeRs. Credit-Linked Interest Subsidy and Capital Subsidy shall be provided to Vaccine Manufacturing Units.
benefits: Credit Linked Interest Subsidy for Vaccine Manufacturing Units @ 70% of interest charged by Bank with upper ceiling up to Rs.60 Lakhs per annum for 5 years OR for the period of repayment of loan whichever is earlier and Capital investment Subsidy @ 15% of the investment upto a maximum of 10 crores.
eligibility: 1. The Scheme is applicable to New Enterprises and Existing Enterprises who had started commercial production during the operative period of the Scheme. 1. Only Gross Fixed Capital Investment (GFCI) made in New BuildingRs. New Plant & Machinery / Equipment and Machineries excluding land will be eligible for incentives for manufacturing. 1. Enterprise shall have to furnish information regarding productionRs. salesRs. turnoverRs. and employment etc. annually to concerned DIC before end of September each year. 1. Enterprise will have to observe pollution Control measures as prescribed by PCC or other competent authority. 1. Enterprise will have to remain in production for 5 years from the date of commercial production and if it fails to continue production for 5 yearsRs. the amount of Capital Investment Subsidy disbursed will be recovered as arrears of land revenue. 1. Out of Diversification and ExpansionRs. only one activity once will be eligible for subsidy during the policy period. 1. Existing or New Enterprise carrying out an activity of Expansion or Diversification with an investment more than 50% (out of which minimum 60% investment should be in Plant & machinery) of GFCI will be eligible. 1. The Enterprise shall furnish Chartered Accountant certified bills. 1. Loan Sanctioned by Bank or Financial Institution as per RBI guidelines for the industry located in U.T. will be eligible for subsidy under this Scheme. 1. The Enterprise will not be eligible for Interest Subsidy under this Scheme ifRs. term loan is sanctioned after one year from the date of commencement of commercial production. 1. Enterprise shall have to apply at online portal within one year from the date of first disbursement of loan or on or before the date of commencement of commercial productionRs. whichever is later. 1. Interest subsidy will be eligible either from the date of first disbursement of loan or from the date of commencement of commercial production whichever is later. 1. Reimbursement of interest subsidy will be made only after commencement of commercial production of the enterprise. 1. If the Enterprise becomes defaulter in payment of interest or instalment of term loan to Bank/Financial institution as per guidelines of RBI and as mentioned in certificate of Bank/Financial institution such default period will be deducted. 1. The interest subsidy will be available only on interest levied by the financial institution/banks. 1. Interest Subsidy will not be available for penal interest or any other bank charges. 1. The eligible Enterprise shall have to bear a minimum of 2% interest levied on term loan by any Bank / Financial institution. The Enterprise shall submit details and undertaking in this regard. 1. The interest subsidy will be directly credited to Bank / Financial institution.

name: Atal Pension Yojana
brief_description:
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is an old age income security scheme for a savings account holder in the age group of **18-40 years who is not an income tax-payee. The scheme helps in addressing** the longevity risks among the workers in the unorganized sector and encourages the workers to voluntarily save for their retirement.
#### Focus of APY
The scheme is mainly targeted **at the poorRs. the under-privileged and workers in** the unorganized sector.
#### APY Subscriber Contribution Chart -
[ https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/nsdl/scheme-details/APY_Subscribers_Contribution_Chart_1.pdf](https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/nsdl/scheme-details/APY_Subscribers_Contribution_Chart_1.pdf)
#### **Charges and fees and overdue interest under APY:**
The charges and fees and the overdue interest for non-payment or delayed payment of prescribed contribution amount shall be levied on the subscribers of APY. These charges and their method of application shall be prescribed by PFRDA from time to timeRs. in consultation with the Central Government.
##### **Raising Grievance Under APY**
A subscriber can raise grievance anytime free of cost from anywhere by visiting: [www.npscra.nsdl.co.in](https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/)
>>Home >> select: NPS-Lite or through CGMS Subscriber raising the grievance will be allotted a token number against the grievance raised. Subscriber may check the status of the grievance under Check the status of Grievance / Enquiry already registered.
benefits:
#### Upon exit on attaining 60 years
The subscriber shall receive the following three benefits on attaining the age of 60:
**(i) Guaranteed minimum pension amount:** Each subscriber under APY shall receive a guaranteed minimum pension of Rs. 1000/- per month or Rs. 2000/- per month or Rs. 3000/- per month or Rs. 4000/- per month or Rs. 5000/- per monthRs. after the age of 60 years until death.
**(ii) Guaranteed minimum pension amount to the spouse:** After the subscribers demiseRs. the spouse of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriberRs.until death.
**(iii) Return of the pension wealth to the nominee of the subscriber:** After the demise of both the subscriber and the spouseRs. the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealthRs. as accumulated till the subscriber's age of 60 years.
Contributions to the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) are eligible for tax benefits similar to the National Pension System (NPS) under section 80CCD(1).
#### Voluntary exit (Exit before 60 Years of age):
The subscriber shall be refunded only the contributions made by him to APY alongwith the net actual accrued income earned on his contributions (after deducting the account maintenance charges).
HoweverRs. in case of subscribers who joined the scheme before 31st March 2016 and have received the Government Co-ContributionRs. shall not receive the same including the accrued income earned thereon.
#### For death before 60 years
**Option 1:** In case of death of the subscriber before 60 yearsRs. option will be available to the spouse of the subscriber to continue contribution in the APY account of the subscriberRs. which can be maintained in the spouses nameRs. for the remaining vesting periodRs. till the original subscriber would have attained the age of 60 years. The spouse of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the same pension amount as the subscriber until death of the spouse. Such APY account and pension amount would be in addition even if the spouse has his/her APY account and pension amount in own name.
**Option 2:** The entire accumulated pension corpus till date under APY will be returned to the spouse / nominee.
eligibility:
#### Age of joining and contribution period

1. The minimum age of joining APY is 18 years and maximum is 40 years.
1. The age of exit and start of pension is 60 years.
1. Subscriber contribution to APY shall be made through the facility of auto-debit of the prescribed contribution amount from the savings bank account of the subscriber on monthlyRs. quarterly or half-yearly basis.
1. The subscribers are required to contribute the prescribed contribution amount from the age of joining APY till the age of 60 years.

name: Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Diploma)
brief_description:
A scholarship scheme by AICTERs. MoE for Girl Students admitted in 1st or 2nd Year of the technical diploma course in an AICTE approved institution. A maximum of two girl children per family are eligible to avail of the benefits. The benefits are provided for a period of maximum of 3 years for first-year admitted students and a maximum of 2 years for second-year admitted students through lateral entry.
This scheme is an attempt to give young women the opportunity to further their education and prepare for a successful future by empowering Women through knowledgeRs. skillRs. and self-confidence.
benefits: ** 50Rs./-** per annum for every year of studyRs. i.e. maximum 3 years for first-year admitted students and maximum 2 years for second-year admitted studentsRs. through lateral entry as lump sum amount towards payment of **college feeRs. purchase of computerRs. stationeriesRs. booksRs. equipmentRs. softwareRs. etc.** No other additional grant will be payable instead of hostel charges medical chargesRs. etc.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a **Girl Student.**1. The applicant must be pursuing either **the First year of the Diploma course** OR **the** **Second year of the Diploma course through lateral entry.**1. The **annual income of the family** (from all sources) must not be more than ** 8Rs. per annum** during the current financial year.1. **All eligible girls** (who submit an online scholarship form) **from the following 13 Union Territories and North Eastern States** i.e.Rs. Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UT)Rs. Jammu and Kashmir (UT)Rs. Ladakh (UT)Rs. Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu (UT)Rs. Lakshadweep (UT)Rs. Arunachal PradeshRs. AssamRs. ManipurRs. MeghalayaRs. MizoramRs. NagalandRs. SikkimRs. & Tripura will be given a scholarship by AICTE.

name: National Youth Corps
brief_description:
A volunteership scheme by Ministry of Youth Affairs And Sports to tap the potential of the disciplined and dedicated youth In the age group of 18 to 29 years who have the inclination and spirit to engage in nation building exercisesRs. to serve up to two years in Nation Building activities for which they would receive a monthly honorarium of Rs- 5000/- .
Each NYV is required to be IT Savvy. Further NYVs should have the capability of preparing report/documentation of youth program and upload online. NYC should also know about preparing reports for media/news statement. Each NYV should know the using of required mobile Apps (for example DigidhanRs. Digital India etc).
The NYC Scheme is being implemented by Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS).
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be between 18 - 29 years of age.
1. The applicant must have passed Class 10th.

name: SVAMITVA Yojana (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas)
brief_description:
SVAMITVARs. a Central Sector scheme of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj provides a Record of Rights to village household owners with the issuance of legal ownership cards (Property cards/Title deeds) to the property owners by mapping land parcels using drone technology.
> **Objectives**


- Creation of accurate land records for rural planning and reducing property-related disputes.
- To bring financial stability to the citizens in rural India by enabling them to use their property as a financial asset for taking loans and other financial benefits.
- Determination of property taxRs. which would accrue to the GPs directly in States where it is devolved or elseRs. add to the State exchequer.
- Creation of survey infrastructure and GIS maps that can be leveraged by any department for their use.
- To support in the preparation of a better-quality Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) by making use of GIS maps

The scheme is a reformative step towards the establishment of clear ownership of property in rural inhabited (Abadi) areasRs. by mapping of land parcels using drone technology and providing Record of Rights to village household owners with the issuance of legal ownership cards (Property cards/Title deeds) to the property owners.
There are about 6.62 lakh villages in the country which will be eventually covered in this scheme. The entire work is likely to be spread for five years.
benefits:
- Drone Digitally Maps All the Land Parcels of the Inhabited Area of the Village.
- Creation of Property Cards on the Exact Area of Each Property in the Village.
- Proprietary Rights to the Village Household Owner.
- Property as a Financial Asset for Taking Loans and Other Financial Benefits.
- Reduce Property Disputes and Legal Cases.
- Determination of Property Tax.
- Creation of Accurate Land Records for Rural Planning.
- Better Gpdp - Leveraging Gis Database/ Maps Created for Better Planning and Execution of Plans.
eligibility: The applicant should have a property in rural inhabited (Abadi) area.

name: Health Ministers Discretionary Grant
