TechnologyRs. Engineering and Mathematics (STEM). The scheme supports women researchers holding regular or long-term positions in academiaRs. research institutesRs. or industry. It is implemented by the Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC) under the Department of Science & Technology (DST)Rs. Government of IndiaRs. and the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)Rs. Government of Germany. The scheme encourages networkingRs. gender inclusionRs. research collaborationRs. and leadership opportunities for women in bilateral research projects. > **Tenure:** The tenure of the grant is for 3 years or till completion of the project whichever is earlier and will cover one visit per year for a short stay up to 1 month.
benefits: The grant will cover basic project assistance (including research staff for the Indian awardeeRs. consumablesRs. and contingency) for the awardee in the parent country and a one-month research stay in the host country (single round-trip airfareRs. visa feeRs. medical insuranceRs. per diem for the stay). > **Indian Awardee:** 1. Travel (including visa fee and insurance) approximately 1Rs./-. 1. Project cost up to 12Rs./- per year (including research staffRs. consumablesRs. contingencyRs. and per diem @ 2300/month in Germany). > **German Awardee:** 1. Travel (including visa fee and insurance) approximately 1500. 1. Project cost up to 14500/year (including consumablesRs. contingencyRs. and per diem @ 2300/month in India).
eligibility: - The applicant must be working either in India or Germany. - Through this schemeRs. women researchers/entrepreneurs holding regular positions in academic/research institutions/industrial research organizations in India/Germany may apply to be a part of an ongoing R&D project of interest with acceptance from the host team. - The programme is open to all areas of STEM. - The programme has no age-limit (Preference to Early/Mid-career researchers). **Note 01:** The applicant must define her role in the projectRs. and provide details of the objectiveRs. execution strategyRs. and expected outcome. **Note 02:** The applicant shall specify the value addition to the project in the host country. **Note 03:** Choice and acceptance from the host is the sole responsibility of the applicant. The applicant should ensure an endorsement/consent letter from the host at the time of the application. **Note 04:** The applicant shall submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC)/Endorsement letter from the head of the institution (present organization). **Note 05:** The awardee shall commence her visit within 12 months from the date of the award letter. **Note 06:** The awardee will abide by the conductRs. rules & regulations of the host and the host country. IGSTC will not be responsible for the violation of any Rules and regulations by the awardee. **Note 07:** The awardee and host must intimate IGSTC through email/letter in case of discontinuation by the awardee. **Note 08:** The awardee must recognize and acknowledge IGSTC in all online/print documentsRs. communicationsRs. reportsRs. publicationsRs. conferencesRs. thesesRs. etc. on work emanating from the grant.

name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
brief_description: The "Craftsmen Training Scheme" was launched by the Directorate General of TrainingRs. Ministry of Skill Development and EntrepreneurshipRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to ensure a steady flow of skilled workers in different trades for the domestic industryRs. to raise quantitatively and qualitatively the industrial production by systematic trainingRs. to reduce unemployment among the educated youth by providing them with employable skillsRs. and to cultivate and nurture a technical and industrial attitude in the minds of the younger generation. The scheme provides systematic vocational training through a network of Industrial Training Institutes and National Skill Training Institutes located all over the countryRs. offering comprehensive skill development programs in various trades and conducting All India Trade Tests for certification.
benefits: ##### ***Vocational Training and Skill Development*** - **Training Duration:** Varies from 6 months to 2 yearsRs. depending on the trade.- **Trade Certification:** National Council for Vocational Training certificate upon successful completion.- **Skill Development:** Hands-on practical training in various industrial trades.- **Employment Opportunities:** Enhanced employability in domestic and international markets. ##### ***Training Infrastructure and Facilities*** - **Training Network:** Access to 15Rs. Industrial Training Institutes and 33 National Skill Training Institutes.- **Modern Equipment:** Training on the latest industrial equipment and technology.- **Expert Instruction:** Training by qualified instructors and industry experts.- **Workshop Facilities:** Well-equipped workshops for practical training. ##### ***Assessment and Certification*** - **All India Trade Tests:** Conducted by the Directorate General of Training under the aegis of the National Council for Vocational Training at the end of training.- **National Recognition:** Certificates recognized across India for employment.- **Industry Standards:** Training aligned with current industry requirements and standards. ##### ***Conditions*** - Minimum 80% attendance is required to appear in the Final Trade Test. - Regular participation in practical training sessions and workshops. - Compliance with the institute rules and regulations. - Successful completion of periodic assessments and tests.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be an Indian citizen. 1. The applicant must meet the age requirements as specified for different trades (generally between 14 to 40 years). 1. The applicant must have completed the minimum educational qualifications as prescribed for specific trades (ranging from 8th standard to 12th standard). 1. The applicant must be able to read and write in the local language / Hindi / English. 1. The applicant must be physically and medically fit to undergo the specific trade training. 1. The applicant must not have any physical disabilities that would prevent them from performing the trade activities. 1. The applicant must meet specific requirements for certain trades (such as colour vision for electrical trades). 1. The applicant must demonstrate basic aptitude for the chosen trade.

name: Internship Scheme Of The Department Of Economic Affairs
brief_description: The scheme "Internship Scheme Of The Department Of Economic Affairs" has been implemented by the Department of Economic AffairsRs. Ministry of FinanceRs. Government of IndiaRs. aiming to familiarize selected candidates with the overall process of formulation of economic policies at the macro level and provide an opportunity to carry out brief research investigations into key economic issues/problems faced by the country and offer solutions for the same. Through this schemeRs. internship opportunities along with token remuneration are provided to outstanding Post Graduate and PhD students in EconomicsRs. LawRs. FinanceRs. and Management from reputed institutions. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)Rs. Ministry of Finance. Under the schemeRs. interns are attached to Joint SecretariesRs. DirectorsRs. or the Office of the Chief/Principal Economic Adviser for research and policy-related assignments. The internship covers areas such as capital marketsRs. economic reformsRs. exchange managementRs. foreign investmentRs. monetary policyRs. fiscal policyRs. inflation managementRs. debt managementRs. bilateral investment treatiesRs. and infrastructure financing. Interns are expected to prepare reports/papersRs. present their findings before concerned divisionsRs. and provide feedback on completion of the internship. The scheme also provides office spaceRs. computer facilitiesRs. and internet support to selected interns. > **Objective:** - To familiarise selected candidates with the overall process of formulation of economic policies of the Government at the macro level. - To provide an opportunity to carry out brief research investigations into key and specific economic issues/problems faced by the country. - To encourage interns to offer solutions for identified economic issues/problems.
benefits: > **Internship Exposure:** 1. Exposure to macro-economic policy formulation and economic research. 1. Opportunity to work on issues related to capital marketsRs. economic reformsRs. foreign investmentRs. fiscal policyRs. debt managementRs. infrastructure financingRs. and related sectors. > **Token Remuneration:** 1. 10Rs./- per month for Post Graduate interns. 1. 20Rs./- per month for PhD interns. 1. Remuneration is payable after satisfactory completion of the internship and submission of the Report/Paper. > **Office and Academic Support:** 1. Office spaceRs. computer facilitiesRs. and internet access are provided. 1. Interns are attached to Joint SecretariesRs. DirectorsRs. or the Office of the Chief/Principal Economic Adviser. > **Certificate:** Certificate of Internship is issued after successful completion of the internship and submission of the Report/Paper. > Validity: Internship duration is between 3 months and 5 months.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be an outstanding candidate pursuing or having completed Post Graduation or Ph.D in EconomicsRs. LawRs. FinanceRs. or Management. 1. The applicant should belong to Universities/Institutions within the top 25 ranks as per the National Institutional Ranking FrameworkRs. Ministry of Human Resource DevelopmentRs. or International Institutes of repute. 1. The applicant should be working on specific issues relating to: - Macro-economic issues - Management - Capital markets - Infrastructure policy - Climate finance - Financial and investment laws > **Research Proposal Requirements:** 1. The applicant should apply against specific research study opportunities. 1. The applicant should indicate research interests and topics during the application process. > **Duration Requirements:** 1. The applicant should be available for an internship period of 3 months to 5 months. 1. Preference may be given to applicants willing to stay for at least 4 months. > **Preference / Priority** 1. Preference may be given to candidates whose research proposals and competencies significantly match DEA requirements. 1. Preference may be given to candidates willing to stay for at least 4 months. > **Other Conditions:** - The applicant should sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement before commencing work. - The applicant should take the internship seriously and invest sufficient effort. - The applicant may be relieved prematurely in case of insufficient effort or lack of interest. - The applicant may be required to work from home due to seating restrictions. - The applicant should follow COVID-19 precautions and protocols issued by the Department of Personnel and Training and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

name: Establishment Of Small Scale Dairy Unit (SSDU)
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
brief_description: The "Small Scale Dairy Unit (SSDU)" has been launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary ServicesRs. U.T. Administration of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. It aims to promote dairy development by supporting the establishment of a small-scale dairy unit with indigenous Gir cows. Through this schemeRs. financial assistance in the form of capital subsidy and back-ended subsidy is provided to beneficiaries for the purchase of milch cowsRs. construction of cattle shedsRs. and procurement of feedRs. equipmentRs. and insurance coverage.
benefits:
**Assistance for 10 Cows:**

eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a resident of the Union Territory of Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. 1. The applicant should establish a small-scale dairy unit with 10 milch cows. 1. The applicant should procure indigenous Gir breed cows only. 1. The applicant should avail a bank loan for implementation of the project. 1. name: Mass Communication Internship Programme
brief_description:
The "Mass Communication Internship Programme" was launched by the Department of Water ResourcesRs. River DevelopmentRs. and Ganga RejuvenationRs. Ministry of Jal Shakti. The internship programme is short-term exposure designed to engage students in undergraduateRs. graduateRs. and postgraduate studies in the field of mass communication. The internship offers hands-on experience in media and social media activitiesRs. aiming to create awareness about the importance of water resources conservation and management.
> **Framework of internship:** - **First month of internship:** Learn about the department's IEC activitiesRs. Create social media content (FacebookRs. InstagramRs. TwitterRs. LinkedInRs. YouTube)Rs. Plan social media strategyRs. and set targets. - **Second month of internship:** Promote services and raise awarenessRs. Engage and build relationships with the audienceRs. Drive traffic and establish KPIsRs. Draft press releases for Department events. - **Third month of internship:** Interact and research target audienceRs. Analyze social media resultsRs. Publicize National Water Awards to attract applicantsRs. and Draft speeches for senior officials on Department achievements. > **Duration of internship:** The internship duration is a minimum of three monthsRs. extendable up to six months on a monthly basis.
> **Number of students for internship:** A maximum of three interns are selected for each internship duration.
> **Terms & Conditions for the Intern:** - Pursue the program with dedication and maintain discipline. - Maintain 90% attendance. - Attend a full-time internship physically in the main secretariat. - Arrange your own accommodation. - Work hours: 9:00 AM to 5:30 PMRs. unless otherwise permitted. - Follow Department rules and regulations. - Internship is not a job or employment assurance. - Adhere to Department advice on external representations. - Poor performance may result in discontinuation of the internship. - Provide prior notice if disengaging from the internship. - Library use is for reference only; borrowing is not allowed. - Maintain confidentiality and do not disclose Department information.
benefits: - **Honorarium****:**An honorarium of 15Rs./- per month will be paid to each intern. - **Certificate:** A certificate will be received upon successful completion of the internship. - **Facilities:** The department provides working spaceRs. internet facilityRs. and other necessities as deemed fit by the Heads. - **Placement:** Each selected intern will be posted with a Deputy SecretaryRs. DirectorRs. Joint SecretaryRs. or the office of the Secretary (WRRs. RD & GR) and will work closely with the IEC Section.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a bonafide student of a recognised University or Institution in India. 1. The applicant should be pursuing a postgraduate course or research programme in Mass CommunicationRs. JournalismRs. Public RelationsRs. MBA (Marketing)Rs. or related fields. 1. The applicant may also be a student who has completed a degree/diploma in the above-mentioned courses from a recognised college or university. 1. The applicant must have secured at least 55% marks or equivalent grade in Graduation. 1. The applicant should possess skills and interest relevant to the internship programmeRs. including writingRs. communicationRs. time managementRs. organisationRs. traditional and digital marketingRs. customer serviceRs. relationship buildingRs. strategic and analytical thinkingRs. and creativity.

name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of Lakadong turmeric (Ha)
brief_description: The scheme Promotion of Exportable Surplus of Identified Spices in the North East: Cultivation of Lakadong Turmeric (Ha) under the Spices BoardRs. IndiaRs. Ministry of Commerce and IndustryRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to promote the cultivation of Lakadong turmeric for exports by providing 50% of the cost of planting materialRs. subject to a maximum of 30Rs. per HaRs. to turmeric growers of the North East having land holdings of 0.10 Ha to 8 HaRs. as per the modalities and scheme guidelines approved by the Competent Authority for implementation of the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (202122 to 202526)Rs. under the component Export Oriented Production.
benefits: 1. 50% of cost of planting material subject to maximum of 30Rs. per Ha 1. Turmeric growers of NE having land holding size of 0.10 Ha to 8 Ha
eligibility: 1. The applicable to turmeric growers in SikkimRs. Darjeeling & Kalimpong district of West BengalRs. and other North Eastern States. 1. Eligible cases will be finalized based on inspection and recommendation by designated officials.

name: Nyaya Mitra Scheme
brief_description: The scheme "Nyaya Mitra Scheme" was launched by the Department of JusticeRs. Ministry of Law and JusticeRs. in April 2017Rs. and the scheme aims to facilitate the expeditious disposal of ten to fifteen-year-old pending cases in High Courts and Subordinate Courts. The scheme provides assistance to litigants suffering due to delayed trials by actively identifying casesRs. offering legal adviceRs. and referring marginalized applicants to Lok Adalats for priority resolution. The applicant must be a retired judicial or executive officer with legal experience who acts as a Nyaya Mitra to support affected individuals. The scheme is implemented by the Department of JusticeRs. and the applications for this scheme are accepted and managed at District Facilitation Centres housed within Common Service Centers.
benefits: - Expeditious disposal of ten to fifteen-year-old pending cases in High Courts and Subordinate CourtsRs. including matrimonial casesRs. accident claimsRs. and criminal cases. - Active identification of delayed cases through the National Judicial Data Grid. - Provision of legal advice and connection of litigants to the District Legal Services AuthorityRs. Common Service Centers Tele LawRs. other government agenciesRs. and civil society organisations. - Referral of marginalized applicants to Lok Adalats for prioritized dispute resolution. - Assistance towards prison reforms within the district in coordination with the district judiciary and other stakeholders. - Critical analysis of pending cases to assist Registrar Generals and district judges in understanding bottlenecks and finding solutions. - Coordination with state and district authorities to enable witnesses to arrive on time or within a stipulated time frame for the early disposal of cases. - Execution of follow-up actions such as issuing noticesRs. summonsRs. staysRs. injunctionsRs. and letters to lower courts for summoning records pursuant to court orders.
eligibility: ##### ***For Nyaya Mitras*** - The applicant must be a retired judicial officer or a retired executive officer. - The applicant must possess legal experience or an educational background in law. ##### ***For Beneficiaries (Litigants)*** - The applicant must be a litigant whose case has been languishing in the subordinate courts for more than ten years. - The applicant must be an individual for whom quality legal aid is not available due to social and economic barriers. - The applicant must be suffering due to a delay in investigations or trial.

name: Prime Ministers Scholarship Scheme for the Wards of Central Armed Police Forces & Assam Rifles
brief_description: The Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS) for the wards of Central Armed Police Forces / Assam Rifles personnel has been introduced by the Ministry of Home AffairsRs. Government of IndiaRs. and aims to encourage higher technical and professional education for the dependent wards and widows of Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles personnel who are martyred during Terror/Naxal attacks. Through this schemeRs. a monthly scholarship for girls and boys is provided to the eligible dependent wards/widows pursuing first professional degree programmes. The scheme is implemented by the Welfare and Rehabilitation Board (WARB) under the Ministry of Home AffairsRs. under the aegis of the National Defence FundRs. through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) version 2.0.
benefits: 1. The applicant who is a girlRs. shall receive 3Rs./- per monthRs. totalling 36Rs./- per year. 1. The applicant who is a boyRs. shall receive 2Rs./- per monthRs. totalling 30Rs./- per year. 1. The amount is paid annually after selection. 1. All applicants selected under the fresh category will be given personal letters from the Hon'ble Prime Minister in the appropriate language. > **Number of Scholarships:** 1. A total of 2Rs. new scholarships are granted each academic year (in addition to renewal cases of the previous year)Rs. equally distributed between boys and girls (1Rs. each). 1. The quota of 1Rs. each fixed for boys and girls is not interchangeable. > **Duration of Scholarship:****** Up to 5 years (depending upon the duration of the course being pursued by the applicant and as approved by the respective regulatory body).
eligibility: 1. Wards/widows of deceased Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles (ARs) personnel who died in harness/election dutyRs. wards of personnel disabled due to causes attributable to Government serviceRs. and Wards of Ex CAPFs & AR personnel in receipt of Gallantry Awards. 1. Wards/widows of retired and serving CAPFs & AR Personnel. (Personnel below Officer Rank) 1. Pursuing first professional degree programme in the field of EngineeringRs. MedicineRs. DentalRs. VeterinaryRs. BBARs. BCARs. B. PharmaRs. B.SC (NursingRs. AgricultureRs. etc.)Rs. MBA and MCARs. etc. in accordance with the [guidelines](https://scholarships.gov.in/public/schemeGuidelines/warb/G_1197_3001.pdf) as mentioned in Para- 8 (B). 1. Having a minimum of 60% marks in Minimum Entry Qualification (MEQ) i.e. 10+2/Diploma/Graduation or equivalent in case of a new applicant. (OR) For applicants applying under the renewal categoryRs. it is mandatory to pass each subsequent academic year of the professional courses being pursued by them with a minimum of 50% marks. 1. A grace period of one year only for casesRs. where there is a delay on the part of the candidate for submission of the application for renewal of scholarship may be entertained. > **Order of Preference:** Applications received from the eligible applicants under the Fresh category will be shortlisted on the basis of an order of preference as mentioned below and the percentage of marks obtained by them in MEQ:- **Sl. No.****Category****Details**1Category-A Wards/Widows of CAPFs & AR personnel killed in action.2Category-BWards of Ex-CAPFs & AR personnel disabled in action.3Category-CWards/Widows of deceased CAPFs & AR personnel died for causes attributable to Government service including casualties during conduct of Election.4Category-DWards of Ex-CAPFs & AR personnel disabled while in service with disability attributable to Government Service5Category-EWards of Ex-CAPFs & AR personnel in receipt of Gallantry Awards.6Category-FWards of Ex- CAPFs & AR personnel (PBOR).7Category-GWards of serving CAPFs & AR personnel (PBOR) subject to availability of scholarship.**Note 01:** Wards of deceased CAPF/AR personnel will be considered for scholarship under Categories A to F as per their priorityRs. even on compassionate appointment of spouse/NOKs in CAPFs. **Note 02:** The Wards of Assistant CommandantRs. holding Local Rank of CAPFs & AR (who are not entailing the pay benefits of Assistant Commandant and drawing the Salary of Inspectors) are eligible for granting PMS under category F & G also. **Note 03:** This scholarship is admissible for only two Children per family and should be ensured by the beneficiaries as well as by the respective CAPF & AR. **Note 04:** The applicants irrespective of his /her marital status are eligible for PMSS. **Minimum Entry Qualification (MEQ):** For being eligible for the Scholarship under PMSSRs. an applicant should have secured a minimum of 60% marks in MEQRs. i.e. 10+2 / Diploma / Graduation as the case may be. name: Agri-Clinics And Agri-Business Centres Scheme
brief_description: The "Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Scheme" (ACABC) is being implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' WelfareRs. Government of IndiaRs. in association with NABARD & MANAGE. SericultureRs. Veterinary SciencesRs. ForestryRs. DairyRs. Poultry FarmingRs. FisheriesRs. etc. Those completing the training can apply for special start-up loans for ventures.

Extension consultancy services 1. Soil and water quality cum inputs testing laboratories (with Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometers) 1. Pest surveillanceRs. diagnostic and control services 1. MaintenanceRs. repairsRs. and custom hiring of agricultural implements and machinery including micro-irrigation systems (sprinkler and drip) 1. Provision of Extension Consultancy Services 1. Hatcheries and production of fish fingerlings for aquaculture 1. Provision of livestock health coverRs. setting up veterinary dispensaries & services including frozen semen banks and liquid nitrogen supply 1. Setting up of Information Technology Kiosks in rural areas for access to various agriculture-related portals 1. Feed Processing and testing units 1. Value Addition Centres 1. name: Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0): Construction and Redevelopment Incentives
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
brief_description: The scheme Scheme for Promotion of Affordable Rental Smart Housing (SPARSH 2.0) implemented through verticals "Incentivising the development or redevelopment of housing complexes and residential spaces for urban poor as SPARSH 2.0 housing complexes by relaxing construction norms for such complexes" by the Labour & Employment DepartmentRs. UT Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu aims to encourage development and redevelopment of affordable rental housing infrastructure. Housing complexes registered under the scheme become eligible for further scheme incentives and benefits. The registration process also ensures annual monitoring and compliance verification. SPARSH 2.0 is applicable across DamanRs. Dadra and Nagar HaveliRs. and Diu for the period from 2022 to 2027. > **Objectives:** - To address the vision of Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan by creating a sustainable ecosystem of affordable rental housing solutions for workers in industriesRs. construction sitesRs. and other weaker sections. - To achieve the objective of Housing for All by promoting affordable rental housing for workers and laborers. - To create a conducive environment by incentivising public and private entities to invest in affordable rental housing stock. - To increase the productivity of industries by improving the health and well-being of workers. - To reduce the financial burden on workers due to treatment costs and wage loss. - To increase the happiness and quality of life of workers. - To harmonise the Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHC) Scheme guidelines with the SPARSH Scheme.
benefits: For any housing complex to apply under the SPARSH 2.0 schemeRs. the proposed construction should either be registered under the ARHC scheme orRs. in the alternativeRs. should fulfil all conditions as mentioned in the first vertical except condition (g) and shall also have other valid permissions as may be required in law. Concerned authoritiesRs. whether the Planning and Development Authority or MunicipalitiesRs. entrusted with the responsibility of giving construction permission or an occupancy certificateRs. shall provide the following benefits/relaxation to the construction permission. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to an additional 50% of the applicable FSI. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to an additional 20% of the ground coverage. 1. Each such housing complex under the SPARSH 2.0 scheme shall be entitled to such relaxations in setbacks or abutting road size as the concerned Authority may determine by rules/bye-laws made in this behalf. 1. The concerned Authority shall regularise the existing housing complexes if they fall within the relaxed guidelines as prescribed under this Scheme. Concerned Revenue Departments shall prioritise any application for NA for the construction of such housing complexes.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should belong to Dadra And Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant should be the owner or authorised representative of the housing complex. 1. The housing complex should fulfil SPARSH 2.0 infrastructure norms. 1. The housing complex should possess a valid construction permission and/or occupancy certificate. 1. The applicant should agree to reserve at least 66% dwelling units for Economically Weaker Section beneficiaries. 1. The applicant should agree to maintain the housing complex and waste management systems.

name: Mission Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, DNH & DD

brief_description: The scheme Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 by the Ministry of Women and Child DevelopmentRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to provide nutritional supportRs. improve nutritional outcomesRs. strengthen Early Childhood Care and EducationRs. and address malnutrition among childrenRs. pregnant womenRs. lactating mothersRs. and adolescent girls. Through this schemeRs. supplementary nutritionRs. pre-school non-formal educationRs. nutrition and health educationRs. immunisationRs. health check-upRs. referral servicesRs. and nutritional support are provided to children below 6 years of ageRs. Pregnant Women and Lactating Mothers (PW&LM)Rs. and Adolescent Girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and all districts of the North East Region. The scheme is implemented by the Central Government through policy and planning supportRs. while the State Governments are responsible for day-to-day programme implementation. > **Types of Malnutrition:** - **Wasting:** Low weight for height - **Stunting:** Low height for age - **Underweight:** Low weight for age - **Overweight/Obesity:** Excess fat due to diet/lifestyle > **Major Causes of Malnutrition:** - Maternal Malnutrition (Underage/Underweight/Low birth weight baby) - Inappropriate birth spacing (Multiple pregnancies) - Lack of diet diversityRs. the diet lacks adequate nutrition - The gap between two mealsRs. meal frequency among children and having only 2-3 meals per day - Lack of complementary feeding as per age criteria - The mother goes to work at a factory/farmRs. and exclusive breastfeeding is compromised - Lack of hygiene practice - Inappropriate method of cooking and eating habits > **Awareness and Education:** - Poshan ke 5 Sutra: Crucial for brain development and long-term health. - First 1000 golden days - Nutrition-rich diet - Anemia management - Diarrhoea prevention - Sanitation **1. Anganwadi Centres (AWCs):** - Total 300 AWCs in DNHRs. 50 in Daman & 29 in Diu. - Timing 9:30 AM to 1:30 PM - Children aged 3- 6 years come to AWCs - Early learning through a play-based curriculum. - Hygiene practices like handwashingRs. bathingRs. brushing teethRs. and wearing clean clothes. - Apart from meals provided at the Anganwadi CentreRs. the child should be fed 3 to 4 nutritious meals at home every day. - Supplementary Nutrition: Take-Home Ration (THR): For children <3 years and pregnant/lactating mothers. - Healthy Environment: Provide a safeRs. lovingRs. and stimulating atmosphere that supports the childs physical growth and mental development. - Educate mothers and caregivers on foodRs. hygieneRs. and breastfeeding. - Immunization: Support ASHA and ANM in ensuring child vaccination. - Growth Monitoring: Monthly tracking of height and weight. - Health Check-ups and Referrals for each child under the Anganwadi Health Programme. **2. Pregnant Women:** - Registration at AWCs/Health Centre. - MCP Card: Follow the schedule and monitor progress. - ANCS: At least 3 with BPRs. bloodRs. urine checksRs./ Anaemia. - IFA tabletsRs. immunisations (Tetanus)Rs. and weight gain tracking. - RestRs. avoid heavy workRs. and maintain hygiene. - Use of iodised salt. - Weight gain during pregnancy. Weight should increase by at least 10-12 kg during Pregnancy. In the last 6 months of pregnancyRs. there is an increase of at least 1 kg per month. - Timely Immunisation of Tetanus Toxoid and deworming - Diet: Variety of nutritious foodRs. such as locally available fresh green leafy vegetables (MethiRs. palakRs. Vada BhajiRs. Moringa leavesRs. CucumberRs. Bitter gourdRs. bottle gourdRs. etc.)Rs. fruits (BananaRs. GuavaRs. PapayaRs. MangoRs. ChickooRs. Jack fruitRs. AmlaRs. LemonRs. etc.). milk and milk productsRs. pulsesRs. cerealsRs. milletsRs. etc. Households that are non-vegetarian need to consume a source of high-quality proteinRs. Vitamin A and Vitamin D. To consume at least 4 meals a day - Promotion of institutional delivery. > **Activity:** - Recipe demo using locally available resources at Anganwadi Centre. - Nutri-garden promotion at Anganwadi Centres/Households as per availability of space. - Community-based events like God Bharai and Suposhan Diwas. **3. Lactating Mothers:** - Early breastfeeding (first within two hours of birth)/ Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months. - Complementary Feeding post 6 months. - Start with softRs. well- cooked and mashed foods like Semi-solid khichdiRs. DalRs. MilletsRs. Rab. - Mashed green and yellow orange vegetables and fruits - Maintain hygieneRs. continue breastfeeding - Growth monitoring of the child every month at the Anganwadi centre/Immunisation as per the MCP Card - In case of any health-related issues with the childRs. communicate with the nearest Health centre/Anganwadi worker - Maintain hygiene at home - Encourage hand washing before cooking mealsRs. before feeding a child Washing vegetables and fruits before consumption. - Take-home ration (THR) given to the mother and child should be consumed by the beneficiary only. > **Activity:** - Complementary food preparation and feeding demo - Annaprashan Divas celebration; Suposhan Divas; Poshan Mein Sudhar.
benefits: 1. Under the schemeRs. Pregnant womenRs. lactating mothersRs. and children in the age group of 0 to 3 years receive Take Home Ration (THR) in the form of ready-to-eat nutritious ladoos on a monthly basis. AdditionallyRs. children aged 3 to 6 years are provided with hot cooked meals at the Anganwadi Centres.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a child below 6 years of age. 1. The applicant should be a Pregnant Woman. 1. The applicant should be a Lactating Mother. 1. The applicant should be an Adolescent Girl aged 14-18 years.

name: Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer-DNH&DD
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
brief_description: The scheme Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer has been implemented by the Agriculture DepartmentRs. UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. It aims to encourage the use of fertilizers so as to improve productivity. Through this schemeRs. manure and fertilizers are provided to Scheduled Castes (SC)Rs. Scheduled Tribes (ST)Rs. and non-SC/ST small and marginal farmers having land holdings up to 2 hectares on subsidy-cum-loan basis. The scheme is implemented by the Agriculture Department through field-level functionaries. Manures and fertilisers are provided to eligible cultivators on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. The assistance is given in kind and not in cash. The quantity of fertilizers is limited as per the prescribed crop-wise rates. The scheme focuses on supporting small and marginal farmers to enhance agricultural output.
benefits: 1. **Provision of Manure and Fertilizers** - Manures and fertilizers will be provided to eligible cultivators. - Assistance is given in kind and not in cash. 1. **Subsidy and Loan Component** - Assistance is provided on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. 1. **Crop-wise Fertilizer Quantity (in Nutrients)** - Paddy: Nitrogen 110Rs. Phosphorus 60Rs. Potash 60 - Maize: Nitrogen 100Rs. Phosphorus 50 - Groundnut: Nitrogen 25Rs. Phosphorus 50 - Castor: Nitrogen 20Rs. Phosphorus 20 - Wheat: Nitrogen 100Rs. Phosphorus 50Rs. Potash 50 - Sugarcane: Nitrogen 250Rs. Phosphorus 125Rs. Potash 125 1. **Green Manuring Support** - 40 kg of seeds per hectare will be supplied for green manuring. 1. **Loan Recovery Provision** - The loan amount shall be recovered in one instalment after completion of the season. 1. **Season-wise Recovery Period** - Kharif (June to July): Recovery from December to February - Rabi (October to November): Recovery from March to May - Hot Weather (January to February): Recovery from June to July 1. **Interest and Penalty Condition** - Interest rate will be as prescribed by the Government of India from time to time. - In case of defaultRs. penal interest at 212% will be charged. - Recovery will be made as arrears of land revenue.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a cultivator or farmer. 1. The applicant should belong to categories such as Scheduled Castes (SC)Rs. Scheduled Tribes (ST)Rs. or original farmers (as mentioned). 1. The applicant should have a land holding of up to 2 hectares. 1. The applicant should be engaged in agricultural activities requiring fertilisers or manure.

name: INAE Travel Grant Scheme for Engineering Students from IITs/NITs/Govt. Approved Engineering Colleges/Institutions other than AICTE
brief_description: An "INAE Travel Grant Scheme for Engineering Students from IITs/NITs/Govt. Approved Engineering Colleges/Institutions other than AICTE" scheme by the Ministry of EducationRs. All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE). The scheme aims at enhancing the quality of engineering education in the country and inculcating a culture of research amongst the students. The scheme aims to provide partial travel assistance and registration fees to Bachelor's and Master's Level engineering students for presenting a research paper at an international scientific event (conference/seminar/symposium/workshop/exhibition etc) to encourage engineering students to engage in research.
benefits: > **Financial Support** **Financial Support for Physical Participation** - Reimbursement of 100% of the registration fee. - Reimbursement of 100% of the visa fee. - Reimbursement of 50% of the actual airfare for discounted/concessional air ticketsRs. provided the expenditure is not claimed from any other source. - Reimbursement of travel expenses from the institution to the nearest airport and backRs. limited to AC II-Class train fare. - Maximum financial assistance per student is limited to 1Rs./-. **Financial Support for Online Participation** - Reimbursement of 100% of the registration fee incurred for presenting the research paper online through video conferencing.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a pre-final or final year student of B.E./B.Tech or Integrated M.Tech; or 1. The applicant must be a first or second-year student of M.E./M.Tech; and 1. The applicant must be pursuing studies in an IITRs. NITRs. Government-approved Engineering College/Institution (other than AICTE-approved institutions)Rs. or another recognized university. 1. The applicant must have secured a minimum CGPA of 8.0 or equivalent percentage in the qualifying examination. 1. Possess a letter of acceptance for presenting a research paper at an international conferenceRs. seminarRs. symposiumRs. workshopRs. exhibitionRs. or similar scientific event held abroad. 1. The applicant has not previously received financial assistance under this scheme during the same course of study.

name: National Overseas Scholarship For Students With Disabilities
brief_description: The "National Overseas Scholarship For Students With Disabilities" scheme has been launched by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment for regularRs. full-time students with disabilities to obtain higher education viz.Rs. a Master's degreeRs. or Ph.D. courses from foreign universitiesRs. in one of the specified fields of study. The students with the specified disabilities defined in Schedule of the "Rights of Persons with Disabilities ActRs. 2016" will be eligible under this scheme. This includes persons with visualRs. hearingRs. speechRs. loco-motorRs. mental retardationRs. and other disabilities. NOS is implemented offline by the DEPwD. At times SwDs are deprived of harnessing their latent skills and thereby miss the opportunity. This scheme aims to support SwDs to study further in order to prepare themselves to earn their livelihood and to find a dignified place for themselves in the society as they face several barriers physicalRs. financialRs. psychologicalRs. mental in pursuing studies and living with dignity.
benefits: 1. **Annual Maintenance Allowance:** For United States of America (USA) & other countries except UK: $15400 (US Dollars); For United Kingdom (UK): 9900 GBP (Great Britain Pounds)1. **Contingency Allowance:** For United States of America (USA) & other countries except UK: $1500 (US Dollars); For United Kingdom (UK): 1100 GBP (Great Britain Pounds)1. **Equipment Allowance:** 1500 INR1. **Tuition Fees:** Actual as charged1. **Visa Fees:** Actual Visa Fees in INR1. **Poll Tax:** Actual as charged1. **Medical Insurance Premium:** Actual as charged1. **Incidental Journey Allowance & Equipment Allowance:** 20 US Dollars for each or its equivalent in INR.1. **Air Passage:** Air passage grant on actual basis from India to the nearest place to the educational institution and back to IndiaRs. by economy class and shortest route in arrangements with the national carrierRs. shall be provided.1. **Local Travel:** Second or Coach Class railway fare from the port of disembarkation to the place of study and back. 1. In case of far-flung places not connected by railRs. bus fare(s) from the place of residence to the nearest railway stationRs. actual charge of crossing by ferryRs. airfare to the nearest rail-cum-air Station and/or second class railway fare by the shortest route to the port of embarkation and back will be permissible. 1. The applicant must be Admitted into (or received an unconditional offer of admission) Masters's level courses and Ph.D. courses abroad in institutions/universities accredited by the Government/authorized body of that country.

1. The applicant must be 35 years or lesser in ageRs. as on the first day of the month of advertisement of the scheme.
1. The Total Family Income of the applicant (from all sources) must not exceed 6 lakh per annum.

name: Emeritus Fellowship
brief_description: The "Emeritus Fellowship" is a scheme of the University Grants Commission (UGC)Rs. Ministry of EducationRs. aimed at providing an opportunity to highly qualified and experienced superannuated teachers to pursue advanced research in their respective fields of specialization. The fellowship enables retired teachers to continue contributing to academic research and knowledge creation in recognized higher educational institutions across India. **The fellowship may be undertaken in:** - UniversitiesRs. InstitutionsRs. and Colleges recognized under Sections 2(f) and 12(B) of the UGC ActRs. 1956. - Deemed-to-be Universities eligible to receive grants from UGC under Section 3 of the UGC ActRs. 1956. - UniversitiesRs. InstitutionsRs. and Colleges funded by the Central Government or State Governments. - Institutes of National Importance.
benefits: **The following assistance is provided under the scheme:** 1. Honorarium of 31Rs. per month for a period of two years (non-extendable). 1. Contingency Grant of 50Rs. per annum (non-lapsable) for: - Secretarial assistance. - Travel within India related to the research project. - Stationery and postage. - Consumables. - Books and journals. - Equipment required for research. 1. Permission for one foreign visit per year related to the approved research workRs. subject to prior approval of the host institution and UGCRs. with no financial liability on UGC. 1. Medical facilities and other institutional privileges available to university faculty membersRs. excluding housing facilities. 1. The fellowship is awarded for a maximum period of two years or until the fellow attains the age of 70 yearsRs. whichever is earlier. **Fellowship Slots:** **Total: 200 fellowship slots at any given time** - 100 slots for Science disciplines. - 100 slots for HumanitiesRs. Social SciencesRs. and Languages.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a superannuated teacher from a recognized universityRs. collegeRs. or institution. 1. Selection is based on the quality of research work and publications produced during the applicant's service career. 1. The applicant must submit a well-definedRs. time-bound research proposal. 1. The fellow may work under the scheme up to the age of 70 years or for two years from the date of awardRs. whichever is earlier. 1. The applicant should not be holding any other position or gainful employment at the time of joining the fellowship. 1. Target Group: Highly qualified and experienced superannuated teachers of recognized universitiesRs. collegesRs. and institutions.

name: National Mission on Natural Farming
brief_description: The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers WelfareRs. Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers WelfareRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to promote natural farming practices through capacity buildingRs. awareness creationRs. certificationRs. and financial assistance for on-farm input production infrastructure to farmers. It focuses on reducing dependence on externally purchased inputsRs. lowering cultivation costsRs. improving soil healthRs. and increasing farmers' income. The mission supports the formation of natural farming clustersRs. Farmer Field SchoolsRs. certification under the Natural Farming Recognition SystemRs. and market development initiatives for natural farming produce. It also promotes integrated agriculture-animal husbandry models based on desi cows and locally available resources.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance for On-Farm Input Production Infrastructure** - Financial assistance of 15Rs./- per hectare is provided. - Assistance is released at 5Rs./- per hectare per year for 3 years. - Assistance is provided for creating on-farm natural farming input production infrastructure. - Assistance is available only to farmers who adopt and continue natural farming practices. > **Training and Capacity Building** - Participation in Farmer Field Schools (FFS) for practical training on natural farming techniques. - Training programmes organized by Champion Farmers and Community Resource Persons. - Exposure visits to successful natural farming models and farms. > **Natural Farming Kit** - Natural Farming Kit provided to participating farmers during Farmer Field School activities. - Cost norm of 1Rs./- per farmer for the kit. > **Certification Support** - Registration and certification support under the Natural Farming Recognition System (NFRS). - Certification facilitation and verification support provided for cluster members. > **Market Development Support** - Support for marketingRs. brandingRs. exhibitionsRs. haatsRs. melasRs. and promotion of certified natural farming produce. - Promotion of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) for aggregation and marketing.
eligibility: - The scheme is applicable to all farmers in India.

name: Post Matric Scholarships to the Students Belonging to Scheduled Castes, DNH & DD
state: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
brief_description: The scheme "Post Matric Scholarships to the Students Belonging to Scheduled Castes" by the Department of Social Justice & EmpowermentRs. Ministry of Social Justice & EmpowermentRs. Government of India. It aims to appreciably increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio of Scheduled Caste students in higher educationRs. with a focus on students from the poorest households. Through this schemeRs. financial assistance in the form of reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable fees and academic allowance is provided to Scheduled Caste students pursuing post-matriculation and post-secondary education in India. The scheme is implemented by the UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. The scholarships are available for recognised post-matriculation and post-secondary courses pursued in recognised institutions. The scheme covers both fresh and renewal cases. Benefits are available for the complete duration of the approved courseRs. subject to fulfilment of prescribed conditions. Scholarship payments are made directly into the student's bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
benefits: 1. Academic allowance for Day Scholars: 2Rs. to 7Rs. per annum. 1. Academic allowance for Hostellers: 4Rs. to 13Rs. per annum. 1. Reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable feesRs. including tuition fees. 1. Additional 10% allowance for Divyang students. 1. Students pursuing CA/ICWA/CS/ICFA are treated as day scholars. 1. DiplomaRs. long-term Vocational Training CertificateRs. GraduateRs. name: Financial Assistance For Procuring Mobility Equipment To Disabled Ex-Servicemen (All Ranks)
brief_description: The scheme "Financial Assistance For Procuring Mobility Equipment To Disabled Ex-Servicemen(All Ranks)" by the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare of the Ministry of DefenceRs. provide financial assistance for the procurement of modified scooter for those Ex-Servicemen (ESM)Rs. who are disabled after their retirement from service with disability of 50% or more. After their retirementRs. most of the ESMs continue to be engaged in physically challenging activities/work. Some of them unfortunately become handicapped due to accidents etc after their retirement and need mobility equipment such as modified scootersRs. crutches and wheelchairs to carry on with their life. To procure mobility requirementsRs. the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) provides financial assistance to disabled ESMs from the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF).
benefits: - **Maximum Financial Assistance:** Financial assistance of up to 1Rs./- is provided for the purchase of eligible mobility equipment.- **Re-Application Provision:** The beneficiary may apply for new mobility equipment after the completion of 10 years from the date of purchase of the previous equipment.
eligibility: - The applicant should be an Ex-Serviceman. - The applicant should be disabled after retirement from the service. - The percentage of the disability should be 50% or more. - The applicant should not be covered under a similar scheme of the Army/Navy/Air Force. - The application of the applicant should be recommended by the respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB). - The applicant should be capable of personally utilizing the mobility equipment provided.
