It aims to provide financial assistance and practical training support to tribal law graduates who begin their legal practice. Under this schemeRs. tribal youth who have obtained their charter within two years of completing their LLB are given a monthly stipend.
benefits: > **Stipend to junior tribal advocates:** - 10Rs. per month for the first year. - 8Rs. per month for the second year. - 6Rs. per month for the third year. > **Allowance to senior advocate (mentor):** - 5Rs. per month for three years.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a Scheduled Tribe (ST) youth. 1. The applicant should have completed LLB degree. 1. The applicant should have obtained a charter within two years of graduation. 1. The applicant should begin legal practice as a junior lawyer under a senior advocate. 1. The applicant should be practicing in tribal areas of Gujarat.

name: Internship Programme Of The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (MoEFCC)
brief_description: The scheme "Internship Programme Of The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau" by the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) under the Ministry of EnvironmentRs. Forests and Climate Change aims to build capacity and awareness in wildlife crime control through providing internship opportunities to students and researchers. It offers a platform for academic learning and practical exposure in areas related to wildlife protectionRs. law enforcementRs. and conservation. The programme enables interns to work closely with experts and officials of WCCB. It also helps in developing researchRs. analyticalRs. and policy understanding in wildlife crime prevention. The nature of work**** is to collect & consolidate data on wildlife crimes or carry out any other task entrusted to them under the directions of the Head of the Department.
benefits: - **Certificate of Internship:** Upon satisfactory completion of the internshipRs. a certificate will be issued to the intern after the submission of the report.- **Duration:** The Internship Programme in Wildlife Crime Control Bureau will be conducted in two phases in a yearRs. during the summer & winter vacations of colleges. Each programme will be one month longRs. commencing on the 1st of the month and concluding at the end of the month. 1. **Summer Internships:** shall be conducted during the months of May & June.1. **Winter Internships:** shall be conducted during the months of December & January.
eligibility: - The applicant should be an Indian Citizen. - The applicant should not be in a regular jobRs. either in Public/ Private Sector. - The applicant should not be more than 30 years of age. - Students pursuing graduation/post-graduation/Diploma in any of the following subjects. 1. Any subject related to Wildlife Management/Conservation/Protection. 1. Zoology. 1. Botany. 1. Law.

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
brief_description: The scheme "Janani Suraksha Yojana" was launched in 12th April 2025 by the Ministry of Health and Family WelfareRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant womenRs. and making available medical care during pregnancyRs. deliveryRs. and post-delivery periods. The scheme provides 100% centrally sponsored cash assistance integrated with delivery and post-delivery careRs. focusing on increasing institutional and safe deliveries for Below Poverty Line familiesRs. and includes assistance for Caesarean sections or obstetric complications up to 1Rs./- per case for hiring specialists. The applicant must meet specific eligibility criteria related to the state type (Low Performing State or High Performing State)Rs. Below Poverty Line or Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe statusRs. and deliver in a government health center or an accredited private institution for institutional delivery benefits. The applications for this scheme are accepted through registration for antenatal careRs. typically facilitated by Accredited Social Health Activists or other link health workers.
benefits:
> **One-Time Cash Assistance for Institutional Delivery (Mother's Package):** - **In Low Performing States (LPS):** 1Rs./- for rural areas and 1Rs./- for urban areas.- **In High Performing States (HPS):** 700/- for rural areas and 600/- for urban areas.- **For North-Eastern States (except Assam) and Rural areas of tribal districts of other states:** 700/- (Mother's package). > ***Notes:*** - _For pregnant women delivering in a public health institutionRs. the entire cash entitlement should be disbursed to her in one installment at the health institution._ - _For women accessing an accredited private institutionRs. at least three-fourths of the cash assistance should be paid to the beneficiary in one installment at the time of delivery._ - _The money must be paid only to the beneficiary and not to any other person or relative._ - _Disbursement should preferably be done at the institution._ - _All payments made before or after seven days of delivery are considered illegitimate and subject to audit objection._ > **Cash Assistance for Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) Package:** - **Referral Transport Assistance:** 250/- (approx.) for transport to the nearest health facility; the exact amount may be decided by the state.- **Institutional Delivery Support:** Minimum 200/- per delivery for facilitating institutional delivery.- **Boarding and Lodging Cost:** The remaining amount from the total package is used for boarding and lodging during stay at the health centre.- **Total Benefit For Rural Areas:** 600/- per caseRs. including 300/- for antenatal care and 300/- for institutional delivery.- **Total Benefit For Urban Areas:** 400/- per caseRs. including 200/- for antenatal care and 200/- for institutional delivery. > **Notes:** - _The first paymentRs. covering transactional costsRs. should be made at the health center upon arrival with the expectant mother._ - _The second paymentRs. the cash incentiveRs. should be paid after the ASHA has completed her postnatal visit and the child has been immunized for Bacillus CalmetteGuerin (BCG)Rs. and this payment should be made within 7 days of delivery._ - _All payments to ASHA are made by the Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)._ - _If the ASHA fails to organize transport for the pregnant womanRs. the transport assistance money is paid directly to the pregnant woman at the institution upon arrival and registration for delivery._ - _An ASHA receives cash benefits only if she accompanies the pregnant woman to the health center. Her work is assessed based on the number of pregnant women she has motivated and escorted to deliver in a health institution._ > **Cash Assistance for Home Delivery** - 500/- per delivery for the Below Poverty Line pregnant womenRs. regardless of age and number of children. - For the beneficiary's care during delivery or to cover incidental expenses. _*The disbursement is done at the time of delivery or approximately 7 days before delivery by an Auxiliary Nurse MidwifeRs. Accredited Social Health ActivistRs. or any other link worker. All payments made before or after seven days of delivery are considered illegitimate._
> **Assistance for Caesarean Section or Management of Obstetric Complications** - Up to 1Rs./- per delivery (case)Rs. utilized by the health institution to hire services of specialists from the private sector or to pay an honorarium or transport cost to bring specialists from other government setups if they are not available in the government health institution. _*This assistance is provided to the government health institutionRs. not directly to the beneficiary. A panel of such doctors must be prepared in advance by the health institutions providing this facilityRs. and pregnant women should be informed during micro-birth planning._ > **Comprehensive Maternal and Newborn Care (aligned with Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram - JSSK objectives)** - Free and Cashless Delivery: Includes normal deliveries and Caesarean sections. - Free Drugs: Provision of necessary medicines. - Free Diagnostics: Essential diagnostic tests. - Free Provision of Blood: Availability of blood transfusions if needed. - Free Diet: Hot cooked meals in Government Hospitals and Tertiary Care Centers; two dry packs of biscuits and a milk packet in Primary Health Centres/Community Health Centres. - Free Transport: To and from the health facilityRs. including referral transport to higher centers and drop-back homeRs. for obstetric women and sick infants up to 30 days of age. > **Compensation for Sterilization** - If the mother or her husband voluntarily undergoes sterilization immediately after deliveryRs. the compensation money available under the existing Family Welfare scheme should be disbursed to the mother at the hospital itself. > **Antenatal Care (ANC) Services** - Includes identification and registration of pregnant womenRs. provision of at least three ANC check-upsRs. Tetanus Toxoid (TT) injectionsRs. and Iron Folic Acid (IFA) tablets. > **Postnatal Care (PNC) Services** - Includes a postnatal visit within 7 days of delivery to track the mothers health and facilitate careRs. counseling for the initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of delivery and its continuance for 3-6 monthsRs. and promotion of family planning. > **Newborn Immunization** - Arrangement to immunize the newbornRs. initially specified until 14 weeks of age (some sources refer to 10 weeks).
eligibility: > **For Institutional Delivery (General):** - The applicant must deliver in a government health centreRs. such as a Sub-centre (specifically approved for institutional delivery by the state)Rs. Primary Health CentreRs. Community Health CentreRs. First Referral UnitRs. or the general wards of District and State Hospitals. - The applicant may deliver in an accredited private health institution. > **Eligibility Specific to Low Performing States (LPS):** - The applicant must be a pregnant woman. - The applicant does not need any marriage or Below Poverty Line (BPL) certification if delivering in a Government or accredited private health institution. - For Above Poverty Line (APL) women in LPS: The applicant is extended benefits if availing institutional delivery care in government health centres (Sub-centreRs. Primary Health CentreRs. Community Health CentreRs. First Referral UnitRs. and general wards of District and State Hospitals). > **Eligibility Specific to High Performing States (HPS):** - The applicant must be from a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household. - The applicant must be a Scheduled Caste (SC)/Scheduled Tribe (ST) woman. > **For Accredited Private Institutions (LPS & HPS):** The applicant must be from a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household. - The applicant must be a Scheduled Caste (SC)/Scheduled Tribe (ST) woman. - The applicant must produce a proper Below Poverty Line or a Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe certificate. - The applicant should carry a referral slip from the Accredited Social Health Activist/Auxiliary Nurse Midwife/Medical Officer and the Maternal and Child Health - Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) card. > **For Home Delivery (All States/Union Territories):** - The applicant must be from a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household. - The applicant must have a Below Poverty Line certificate to access benefits.

name: Indo-French Postdoctoral Research Programme for Women in Science
brief_description:
The Indo-French Postdoctoral Research Programme for Women in Science (PROWIS-I) is dedicated to the young women scientists of both India and France. This programme will provide a platform for women candidates to engage & work with Indian/French scientific communities with an aim to accelerate their talented instincts towards carrying out advanced studies and research in the frontier areas of Science & Technology.
> **Duration of Fellowship:**

The duration of the Fellowship will be for a period of three to four months.
benefits:
> **For Indian National:**


1. Fellowship Euros 2000/- per month along with miscellaneous allowances.
1. To and Fro International travel between India and France.

> **For French National:**


1. Fellowship 90Rs./- per month along with miscellaneous allowances.
1. To and Fro International travel between France and India.
eligibility:
1. Women applicants must be Indian or French citizens (citizens residing in France) from a recognized university or research institution in India/France.
1. Indian applicants should be holding a PhD degree & sanctioned/tenured post in a scientific/academic institution and willing to undertake collaborative research projects in French institutions/universities are eligible to apply.
1. French women applicants holding a PhD degree and currently completing a postdoctoral project & willing to undertake collaborative research projects in Indian institutions/universities are eligible to apply.
1. The mobility should take place during the employment period of the applicant in the concerned institution.
1. The applicant should not have availed of any Postdoctoral fellowship in France/India during the last 5 years.
1. This fellowship cannot be availed simultaneously with any other fellowship.

**Note 01:** Preference will be given to those candidates who dont have any international exposure.
**Note 02:** Preference will be given to candidates having previous R&D experience & publications.
**Note 03:** CEFIPRA may relax the eligibility conditions in case of potential candidates.

name: Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Quality Upgradation / Certification: Supply of Baby Pulpers
brief_description: The scheme "Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Quality Upgradation / Certification: Supply of Baby Pulpers" is a Sub-Component of the Scheme "Integrated Coffee Development Project During the Medium Term Framework (MTF) Period: Development Support to Stakeholders" by the Coffee BoardRs. Department of CommerceRs. Ministry of Commerce and Industry. This scheme aims to facilitate the improvement of the quality of coffee produced by growers by encouraging them to establish infrastructure for quality enhancement and obtain certification for their coffeesRs. enabling them to earn better returns. This involves three main activities: supply of pulpersRs. construction of cement drying yardsRs. and eco-certification of coffee holdings.
benefits:
**Unit Cost:** Actual cost of the unit or 16Rs. per unitRs. whichever is less.
**Scale of Subsidy:** 75% of the Unit Cost.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a tribal grower. 1. The applicant is eligible for only one unit.

name: Women Scientist Scheme-C
brief_description: A scheme by MoST for female candidates with a break in their career interested in addressing societal challenges through viable S&T interventions. 1-year training is provided in Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs)Rs. patent searchRs. know-howRs. draftingRs. filingRs. trademarksRs. trade secretsRs. and copyrightRs. in association with various Knowledge Partners (i.e. Law firmsRs. Knowledge Processing Organizations (KPOs)Rs. CompaniesRs. Government agenciesRs. and so on). The scheme is being implemented by the Patent Facilitating Centre of Technology Information Forecasting & Assessment Council (TIFAC). Minimum essential qualifications are Master of Science; Bachelors in Engineering/Technology or equivalent. Proficiency in handling computerized databasesRs. collectionRs. collationRs. analysisRs. and report preparation is desirable.
benefits:
1. 35Rs./- per month for Ph.D. in Basic or Applied Sciences/MD or equivalent degree.
1. 30Rs./- per month for M.Phil / M.Tech / M.Pharm / M.VSc or equivalent degree.
1. 25Rs./- per month for M.Sc in Basic or Applied Sciences / MBBS / B.Tech or equivalent degree.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a female.
1. The applicant must have a break in her career.
1. The age of the applicant must be between 27 and 45 years.
1. Minimum Educational Qualification must be either Master of Science or Bachelors in Engineering / Technology or equivalent.

name: Mahila Samman Savings Certificate
brief_description: The scheme Mahila Samman Savings Certificate launched by the Department of Economic AffairsRs. Ministry of Finance aims to provide financial security and attractive investment opportunities to girls and women in India. It is available through Post Offices and eligible Public and Private Sector BanksRs. ensuring wider accessibility. The scheme offers a 2-year tenure with an interest rate of 7.5% per annum (compounded quarterly) on deposits ranging from 1Rs. to 2Rs.. It also allows partial withdrawal of up to 40% of the balance and is valid for subscription until 31st March 2025.
benefits: - **Investment Options:** Provide attractive and secure investment options for girls and women. - **Interest Rate:** Offers fixed interest of 7.5% per annumRs. compounded quarterly. - **Investment Limit:** The maximum investment ceiling is 2Rs. with flexible investment options. - **Tenure:** The scheme has a duration of 2 years. - **Interest Credit:** Interest is compounded quarterly and credited to the account. > **Note:** - The interest payable to the account holder in respect of any account opened or deposit made which is not in consonance with the provisions of this Scheme shall be payable at the rate applicable to the Post Office Savings Account.
eligibility: - The applicants must have Indian citizenship. - This scheme is only for women and girl children. - Any Individual Woman can apply under the scheme. - The minor account can also be opened by the guardian. - There is no upper age limitRs. and women of all ages can avail the benefits of this scheme. **Note:** An account opened under this Scheme shall be a single-holder type account. > **Deposits:** - An individual may open any number of accounts subject to the maximum limit for deposit and a time gap of three months shall be maintained between the existing account and the opening of other accounts. - A minimum of 1000/- and any sum in multiples of one hundred rupees may be deposited in an account and no subsequent deposit shall be allowed in that account. - A maximum limit of 2Rs./- shall be deposited in an account or accounts held by an account holder. > **Payment on maturity:** - The deposit shall mature on completion of two years from the date of the deposit and the Eligible Balance may be paid to the account holder on maturity. - In calculating the maturity valueRs. any amount in fraction of a rupee shall be rounded off to the nearest rupeeRs. and for this purpose; any amount of fifty paisa or more shall be treated as one rupeeRs. and any amount less than fifty paisa shall be ignored. > **Withdrawal from account:** - The account holder shall be eligible to withdraw a maximum of up to 40% of the Eligible Balance once after the expiry of one year from the date of opening of the account but before the maturity of the account. - In case of an account opened on behalf of a minor girlRs. the guardian may apply for the withdrawal for the benefit of the minor girl by submitting the specified certificate to the accounts office. - In calculating the withdrawal from the accountRs. any amount in fraction of a rupee shall be rounded off to the nearest rupeeRs. and for this purpose; any amount of fifty paisa or more shall be treated as one rupeeRs. and any amount less than fifty paisa shall be ignored.

name: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana 2.0
brief_description: **The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana 2.0 (PMUY)** was launched in May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide free LPG connections to women from poor households. Its main objective is to promote clean cooking fuel like LPG among rural and deprived families who traditionally rely on firewoodRs. coalRs. or cow-dung cakes. This shift helps reduce health risks for women and minimizes environmental pollution. Under PMUY 2.0Rs. the scheme was further expanded to reach more beneficiaries across India. - The target under the scheme was to release 8 Crore LPG Connections to the deprived households by March 2020. - On 7th September 2019Rs. the Honble Prime Minister of India handed over the 8th Crore LPG connection in AurangabadRs. Maharashtra. - The release of 8 Crore LPG connections under the scheme has also helped in increasing the LPG coverage from 62% on 1st May 2016 to 99.8% on 1st April 2021. - Ujjwala 2.0: Additional allocation of 1.6 Crore LPG Connections under PMUY Scheme with special facility to migrant households. The scheme was launched in MahobaRs. Uttar Pradesh by the Honble Prime Minister of IndiaRs. Shri. Narendra Modi.
benefits: Cash assistance for PMUY connections is provided by the Government of India - 1600 (for a connection 14.2kg cylinder/ 1150 for a 5 kg cylinder). The cash assistance covers: 1. Security Deposit of Cylinder 1250 for 14.2 kg cylinder/ 800 for 5 kg cylinder. 1. Pressure Regulator 150. 1. LPG Hose 100. 1. Domestic Gas Consumer Card 25. 1. Inspection/ Installation/ Demonstration charges 75. AdditionallyRs. All PMUY beneficiaries will be provided with first LPG refill and Stove (hotplate) both free of cost along with their deposit-free connection by the Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be at least 18 years old. 1. The applicants household must not have any existing LPG connection. 1. The applicant woman must belong to any one of the eligible categories. - SC Households - ST Households - Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) - Most Backward Classes - Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) - Tea and Ex-Tea Garden tribes - Forest Dwellers - People residing on Islands and River Islands - SECC Households (AHL TIN) - Poor Household as per 14-point declaration

name: Internship Programme for Women Students / Scholars / Social Activists / Teachers
brief_description: The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched the Internship Programme aims to tap the talent of the internsRs. giving them an opportunity to work for infusing further efficiency in implementation of schemes as also deliberate on its policies through different assignments. The Internship Programme would provide a common platform for meaningful interaction and space for research related to Government programs/initiatives. This Programme is expected to yield promptness in bridging possible information gaps pertaining to issues and problems of women and children in the country. The objective of the Internship Programme is to translate the Honble PMs idea of SABKA SATHRs. SABKA VIKAASRs. SABKA VISHWAASRs. SABKA PRAYAAS for building a self-reliant India.
benefits: - **Stipend:** 20Rs. per month provided as a lump sum amount. - ***Duration:*** The duration of the Internship Programme will be 2 months throughout the year. Interns can select any of the 2-month batches while submitting their applications - **Travel Reimbursement (Joining & Return):** Travel cost reimbursed by Deluxe/AC Bus or 3 Tier AC Train for joining and returning after completion. - **Travel & DA During Programme:** Travel expenses and Dearness Allowance (DA) reimbursed for official tours as per Government of India rates. - **Certification:** Certificate awarded upon successful completionRs. subject to submission/presentation of reports or papers. - **Hostzl Facility:** Shared hostel accommodation provided in Delhi during the internship period. - **Hostel Amenities:** Basic facilities include triple sharing roomRs. attached bathroomRs. bed (without mattress)Rs. tableRs. chairRs. and cupboard. - **Hostel Duration:** Available from 2 days before the start to 2 days after completion of the programme. - **Logistic Support:** Includes seating arrangementRs. internet facilityRs. and stationery items in the Ministry. - **Internship Coordinator:** Dedicated coordinator assigned for overall guidanceRs. coordinationRs. and communication. #### **Note**: Mess charges are not included as part of the accommodation and are to be borne by the intern availing the hostel facility
eligibility: - The women studentsRs. scholarsRs. social activists and teachers from non-tier-I cities and rural parts of India will be eligible for the programme. - The women studentsRs. scholarsRs. social activistsRs. teachers (herein after referred to as interns) need to be enrolled in/associated with any university/academic/non-academic institution. - The age of the applicant should be between 21 to 40 years. > **Number of Interns:** - The ministry would take up to 20 interns per batch.

name: VAANI (Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages)
brief_description: The scheme VAANI (Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages) was launched by the All India Council for Technical EducationRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to create a knowledge base by conducting conferencesRs. seminarsRs. and workshops in twenty-two Indian languages. The scheme provides a maximum funding of 2Rs./- per programme to eligible institutionsRs. along with an honorarium of up to 5Rs./- per session for subject experts. The applications for this scheme are accepted online.
benefits:
- The scheme provides financial assistance up to a maximum of 2Rs./- per programme. - The honorarium for experts is a maximum of 5Rs./- per expert and per session. - Financial assistance shall be reimbursed against actual expenses after the successful completion of the conferenceRs. seminarRs. or workshop and the submission of requisite documents. - An advance of 50% of the sanctioned amount will be released only to the Government Institutions.
##### ***Terms and Conditions*** - The approved conferenceRs. seminarRs. or workshop must be conducted within six months. - A minimum of one-third of the resource persons must be from an industry background. - One expert can give a maximum of two lectures for the conferenceRs. seminarRs. or workshop. - The coordinator must maintain a webpage for the event on the website of the institute. - The institution must post the link to the funding schemes of the All India Council for Technical Education on its website and the event webpage. - Any change in the programme scheduleRs. coordinatorRs. or venue requires prior approval from the councilRs. failing which the grant offer is automatically withdrawn. - Funds sanctioned for a particular event cannot be utilized for any other programme or conference. - If the event is cancelledRs. it must be reported immediatelyRs. and the grantee must refund the entire amount with a 10% simple interest. - Any unutilized amount must be refunded to the All India Council for Technical Education through Real-Time Gross Settlement or National Electronic Funds Transfer only. - The logo of the All India Council for Technical Education must be prominently displayed on all online and offline informationRs. stage backdropsRs. podiumsRs. and publicity materialsRs. which must be in an Indian language.
eligibility: - The applicant must be an AICTE-approved instituteRs. including institutions offering Bachelor of Business Administration or Bachelor of Computer Applications programs. - The applicant must identify a co-coordinator who must be a faculty member with at least seven years of experience in teaching and research. - The applicant must ensure the academic background of the coordinatorRs. co-coordinatorRs. resource personsRs. and paper presenters is in conformity with the theme of the proposed event. - The applicant must ensure participants are strictly faculty members of approved institutionsRs. research scholarsRs. Master of Technology scholarsRs. research fellowsRs. or working professionals from the industry. - The applicant must ensure the event is conducted in one of the twenty-two specified Indian languagesRs. such as AssameseRs. BengaliRs. BodoRs. DogriRs. GujaratiRs. HindiRs. KannadaRs. KashmiriRs. KonkaniRs. MaithiliRs. MalayalamRs. ManipuriRs. MarathiRs. NepaliRs. OdiaRs. PunjabiRs. SanskritRs. SanthaliRs. SindhiRs. TamilRs. TeluguRs. or Urdu. - The applicant must limit their application to receive the grant to once in a year.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
brief_description: The **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)** is a Centrally Sponsored flagship scheme by the Ministry of Women and Child DevelopmentRs. Government of IndiaRs. designed to support pregnant women and lactating mothers. The scheme is to provide maternity benefits to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. The maternity benefit is to be provided to a woman for the first two living children provided the second child is a girl. For the first child the maternity benefit of 5Rs./- is provided in two instalments under PMMVY and the beneficiary is also entitled to receive the cash incentive as per approved norms towards Maternity Benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an averageRs. a women gets 6Rs./-. For the second childRs. the benefit of 6Rs./- is to be provided subject to second child is a girl childRs. in one installment after the birth. Cases of miscarriage/still births are to be treated as fresh cases for providing maternity benefit under the scheme. FurtherRs. as per the new guidelines for '**Mission Shakti**Rs. applicable with effect from 01.04.2022Rs. the scheme **(PMMVY 2.0)** seeks to promote positive behavioral change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second childRs. if that is a girl child. ThusRs. for the second childRs. the benefit of 6Rs./- is to be provided in one instalment post birth. This would contribute towards improving Sex Ratio at Birth by discouraging female feticide. AlsoRs. in case of miscarriage/stillbirthRs. the beneficiary will be treated as a fresh beneficiary in the event of any future pregnancy.
benefits:
The cash incentives is provided in two instalments for the first child as per the schedule provided in
table below:

- **Scheme Condition for First Child**

**Instalment** **Conditions****Amount (in Rs.)****First Instalment**On registration of pregnancy and at least one Antenatal checkup within six months from last menstrual period date at the Anganwadi Centre or approved Health facilities may be identified by the respective administering State/UT. 3Rs./-**Second Instalment**Childbirth is registered. The child has received all due vaccines till the age of 14 weeks as admissible under the Universal Immunization Programme of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.2Rs./-
- **Scheme Condition for Second Child (if it is a girl child)**

**Single Instalment**On registration of pregnancy and at least one Ante-Natal Check-up (ANC) within six months from LMP at the Anganwadi Centre (AWC) approved Health facilities may be identified by the respective administering State/UT. The girl child birth shall be registered under this Scheme. The girl child has received all due vaccines till the girl child attains age of fourteen weeks from the date of birth as admissible under the Universal Immunization Programme of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.6Rs./-In case of miscarriage/still birthRs. the beneficiary would be treated as fresh beneficiary in event of any
future pregnancy.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be of at least 19 years old and a pregnant women.
1. The applicant should be employed and experiencing wage-loss due to the pregnancy.
1. The scheme is applicable only for the first live birth.
1. Eligible beneficiary can apply for the benefit under PMMVY scheme within 270 days from the child birth.
1. If a beneficiary delivers twins/ triplets/ quadruplets in her second pregnancyRs. with one or more children being girlRs. she will receive incentive for second girl child as per the PMMVY 2.0 norms.

**Criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society are the following:**

1. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes
1. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan)
1. Women holder of BPL Ration Card
1. Women Beneficiaries under Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (PMJAY) under Ayushman Bharat.
1. Women holding e-Shram card
1. Women farmers who are beneficiaries under Kisan Samman Nidhi
1. Women holding MGNREGA Job Card
1. Women whose net family income is less than Rs. 8 Lakh per annum
1. Pregnant and Lactating AWWs/ AWHs/ ASHAs
1. Women holding Ration Card under NFSA Act 2013.
1. Any other category as may be prescribed by the Central Government

name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Sericulture In Irrigated Area
brief_description: The "Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Sericulture In Irrigated Area" scheme launched by the Co-operationRs. Food and Consumer Protection DepartmentRs. Tamil NaduRs. aims to support farmers involved in sericulture within irrigated areas by offering loans ranging from 49Rs./- to 79Rs./- per acre. The interest rate varies between 11% to 12.75% (subject to change).
benefits: - **Access to Loan:** Loan amount between 49Rs./-to 79Rs./- per acre. - **Interest Rate:** 11% to 12.75% (subject to change).
eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
1. The beneficiary should be a farmer.
1. The beneficiary should be engaged in sericulture activities within irrigated areas.
1. The beneficiary should be interested in availing loan for sericulture activities.
1. The beneficiary should have the intention to use the loan specifically for sericulture activities.

name: Distribution of Iron Boxes at Free of Cost
brief_description: The "Distribution of Iron Boxes at Free of Cost" scheme launched by the Backward ClassesRs. Most Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare DepartmentRs. Tamil NaduRs. aims to provide complimentary iron boxes to support individuals from Backward Classes (BC)Rs. Most Backward Classes (MBC)Rs. and Denotified Communities (DNCs) engaged in washing work.
benefits: - Free provision of iron boxes to eligible individuals.
eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
1. The beneficiary should belong to Backward Classes (BC)/ Most Backward Classes (MBC)/ and Denotified Communities (DNCs).
1. The beneficiary should be engaged in washing work.
1. Annual income should not exceed 40Rs./- in rural areas and 60Rs./- in urban areas.

name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
brief_description: The National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme allows young talent to be associated with the NCCS work for mutual benefit. It will enable NCCS to interact with young scholars and to get fresh ideas and study/ research support from the field of academics. At the same timeRs. it will provide an opportunity for young scholars to contribute to the NCCS work and have an insight into the related technical work. The opportunity enables the young population to acquire knowledge in the areas like Hardware level SecurityRs. Source Code analysis (Static and dynamic analysis at HLLRs. Binary Code Analysis) Crypto algorithm implementation validation and Crypto Module validationRs. Supply chain vulnerabilitiesRs. Run time vulnerabilities in a live network (Advanced Persistent Threats)Rs. Back door entry vulnerabilitiesRs. Identification of Intentional/ Hidden Malware in Software/ Firmware of equipment. > **Slots** 1. NCCS will assess the requirement of the interns periodically. 1. The total number of interns engaged shall not exceed 20 (inclusive of Category I & II)Rs. at any point in time. > **Duration** **For Category I:** The minimum duration of the internship shall be of sixty days. **For Category II:** The minimum duration of the internship shall be of six monthsRs. extendable up to a maximum of twelve months. **NOTE:** Extension beyond six months shall be permittedRs. on the application of an intern duly recommended by the concerned Head of Division and with the approval of the Head of NCCS. > **Placement** 1. The interns would be attached to one of the officers in the Divisions of the NCCS. 1. An orientation workshop will be held for interns at the beginning of the internship. The work of interns will be monitored through periodic interaction with the interns. 1. The attendance record and the details of work supervision shall be maintained by the Divisions/Units in NCCS. > **Submission of Paper** The interns will be required to submit a Report/Paper on the work undertaken at the end of the internship to the respective Division. The Report shall be signed by the concerned Officer with whom the intern is attachedRs. as an acceptance of the successful completion of the Internship.
benefits: > **Token Remuneration** 1. Interns selected under Category I will be paid a token remuneration 7Rs./- per month on pro-rata basis. 1. Interns selected under Category II will be paid a token remuneration 15Rs./- per month on pro-rata basis. 1. The remuneration shall be paid after the completion of the month subject to satisfactory progress of work duly accepted by the concerned division from the "Professional Services" head of Accounts. > **Certificate of Internship** On successful completion of the Internship and submission of the Report duly signed and accepted by the competent authorityRs. a Certificate shall be issued by the concerned Division. > **Logistics & Support** NCCS shall provide them with working spaceRs. workplace Internet facility and other necessities as deemed fit by the concerned Head of Division. **NOTE:** Interns will be required to have their own laptops.
eligibility:
> **Eligibility for Category I** Indian students from recognized universities in India or abroadRs. studying in 3rd/ 4th year (Final or pre-final year) in Bachelor's Degree course in Electronics/ Communications/ Telecommunication /Radio/ Information Technology/ Computers / Electrical (with majors in electronics/communications/computers) Engineering or related discipline and secured minimum 60% marks. > **Eligibility for Category II** Indian students from recognized universities in India or abroadRs. who have completed Bachelor's Degree courses in Electronics/ Communications/ Telecommunication/ Radio/ Information Technology/ Computers/ Electrical (with majors in electronics/communications/computers) Engineering or related discipline course with a minimum of 60% marks. **OR** Indian students from recognized universities in India or abroadRs. who have completed Graduation or pursuing Post Graduate/Master's Degree courses in Electronics/ Communications/ Telecommunication/ Radio/ Information Technology/ Computers/ Electrical Engineering or related discipline courses with a minimum of 60% marks. > **Preference/Relaxation**
**NOTE 1:** The qualifications may be relaxed in deserving cases based on the needs of the NCCSRs. on the recommendations of Selection Committee and approval of Head of NCCS. **NOTE 2:** Possessing minimum qualifications as above shall not guarantee Internship in NCCS. Candidates having exposure in the area of intended internship with good academic background and having higher qualificationRs. based on need shall be given preference.

name: ICMR-Junior Research Fellowship
brief_description: The scheme "ICMR-Junior Research Fellowship" by the Department of Health ResearchRs. Ministry of Health & Family WelfareRs. aims to select eligible Indian candidates for research through a national-level entrance examination and provide financial support for pursuing Ph.D. programmes. It provides fellowships to candidates in Life Sciences and Social Sciences streams based on merit. A total of 150 fellowships are awardedRs. along with additional candidates for placement under ICMR-funded projects. The fellowship is granted subject to securing placement in recognized institutions such as medical collegesRs. universitiesRs. or research institutes. The validity of the fellowship is 6 monthsRs. and the result remains valid for 2 years for placement.
benefits: - **Fellowship Stipend:** 31Rs./- per month for 1st and 2nd year (JRF); 35Rs./- per month for 3rd to 5th year (SRFRs. if upgraded). - **Contingency Grant:** 20Rs./- per year for research-related expenses. - **Fellowship Duration:** JRF for 2 to 3 years; SRF for a maximum 3 years; total duration up to 5 years. - **Ph.D. Opportunity:** Eligible candidates can enroll in Ph.D. programmes in recognized universities/institutions. - **Hostel Facility:** Hostel accommodation may be provided by the instituteRs. subject to availability. - **Medical Benefits:** Provided as per the rules of the respective institution (ICMR does not bear expenses). - **Leave Benefits:** Casual leave and maternity leave as per Government rules. - Additional Opportunity: 100 additional candidates considered for JRF positions under ICMR-funded projects (subject to conditions). > **Note:** - The Fellow will not be treated as an employee of the ICMR. - The applicant should not draw any stipend or salary or be in receipt of any other type of financial assistance except leave salary during the fellowship.
eligibility: - The candidate should have a Post Graduate degree (M.Sc./MA) in basic science or a Post-Graduate degree (M.Sc./MA) in a professional course with 55% marks for General/Other Backward Class (OBC) and 50% for SC/ST/Physically Handicapped (PH)/Visually Handicapped (VH). - The students having degrees like B. Tech/M. Tech in biomedical sciencesRs. B. Pharma/M. Pharma or D. Pharma are not eligible. - The upper age limit is 28 years [upper age limit relaxable up to five years in case of candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC/PH/VH and female candidatesRs. three years in the case of OBC category].

name: Welfare Services for Disabled Persons
brief_description: The "Welfare Services for Disabled Persons" under the Mizoram Grant-in-Aid framework focuses on improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities by supporting voluntary organizations in delivering specialized services. Beneficiaries include persons with locomotorRs. visualRs. hearingRs. and mental disabilitiesRs. and multiple disabilities such as cerebral palsy and autism. The scheme supports activities like vocational trainingRs. early detectionRs. medical treatmentRs. rehabilitationRs. and the provision of assistive devices. It also promotes awareness regarding the rights of disabled persons and supports the establishment of special schools and institutions.
benefits: > **Rehabilitation & Training:** - Vocational training for self-employment. - Early detection and intervention services. > **Medical Support:** - Treatment and rehabilitation services. - HIV/AIDS care for disabled persons. > **Assistive Devices:** - ProstheticsRs. mobility aidsRs. hearing aidsRs. Braille equipment. - Education Support. - Special schools and vocational centres. > **Awareness:** - Awareness programmes on disability rights.
eligibility: > **For Individuals (Beneficiaries):** - The applicant must be a person with disability having at least 40% disabilityRs. duly certified by a competent medical authority. - The applicant must belong to any category such as locomotorRs. visualRs. hearingRs. mentalRs. or multiple disabilities. - The applicant must require support for rehabilitationRs. medical treatmentRs. educationRs. or livelihood. > **For Organizations:** - The organization must be a registered voluntary organization/NGO/institution. - The organization must have experience in implementing disability welfare programmes. - The organization must have adequate infrastructure and trained personnel to provide services. - The organization must ensure that services are provided without discrimination.

name: DPIIT Internship Scheme
brief_description: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)Rs. Ministry of Commerce & Industry has been implementing internship scheme for the students pursuing Under Graduate/Post Graduate degree or are Research Scholars enrolled in recognized University/Institution within India or abroad. The objective behind the internship scheme is to give exposure to the students to understand the working culture of Govt. of India and exposure to the schemes being run by this Department. Students can choose a period of their choice ranging from one month /two months / three months as per their requirements. The applications will be accepted online mode only.
benefits: **Stipend:** - Interns would be paid a stipend of 10Rs./- per month. The processing of payment towards the stipend amount will be initiated after the completion of the internship period. **Number of Interns:** - Maximum Number of Interns selected at a time will not be more than 20. **Period of Internship:** - The period of Internship shall be minimum one month and maximum three months. - After completing internshipRs. students will be awarded an Experience Certificate. - Those who will not satisfactorily complete the requisite period of internship will not be awarded any certificate or stipend.
eligibility:
Applicants pursuing Graduation/Post Graduation/Research in following domain are eligible to apply:-

- Engineering
- Management
- Law
- Economics
- Finance
- Computers
- Library Management

**Note 01:** Candidates from other domains can also be considered based on requirements on case to case basis.
**Note 02:** Interns shall be required to submit a brief report/paper at the end of their assignment to the concerned Divisional Head about their learning experience.

name: Scheme For Award Of Senior/Junior Fellowships To Outstanding Persons In The Fields Of Culture
brief_description: The Scheme for Award of Senior/Junior Fellowships to Outstanding Persons in the Fields of Culture was launched by the Ministry of CultureRs. Government of India to support artists in creative fields. EarlierRs. while academicians and scientists had opportunities for independent work through fellowships by institutions like the University Grants Commission and the Council of Scientific and Industrial ResearchRs. similar support was lacking in the field of creative arts. There was also a gap in schemes providing financial assistance for advanced training or independent creative workRs. especially beyond the age groups already covered. This scheme aims to fill that gap by offering financial support and a creative environmentRs. including for artists in rural and tribal areas. The fellowships are awarded for research-oriented projectsRs. and applicants must demonstrate their capability to undertake such work. HoweverRs. the fellowships are not meant for training programsRs. workshopsRs. seminarsRs. or for writing memoirsRs. autobiographiesRs. fictionRs. or similar works. **Fields/Area:** 1. Senior/Junior Fellowships in the Field of PerformingRs. Literary and Plastic Arts. Performing Arts ( Music/Dance/Theatre/Folk Traditional & Indigenous Arts including Puppetry) Literary Arts (Travelogue/History & Theory of Literature) Plastic Arts (Graphics/Sculpture/Painting including Folk Paintings and Research Work on Traditional Paintings/Creative Photography) 2. Senior/Junior Fellowships in the New Areas related to Culture: In the New Areas related to cultureRs. projects are sought in the following fields : Indology Epigraphy Sociology of Culture Cultural Economics Structural and Engineering Aspects of Monuments Numismatics Scientific and Technical aspects of Conservation Management aspects of Art and Heritage Studies relating to application of Science and technology in areas related to culture and creativity. The objective is to encourage analytical application of new research techniquesRs. technological and management principles to contemporary issues in areas related to art and culture. General and theoretical macro-studies will not be considered. The proposal should be innovative and application-oriented and preferably interdisciplinary in nature.
benefits: > The number of fellowships will be up to 400 each year. These are of two typesRs. namelyRs. senior and junior fellowships. **Senior Fellowship:** - Number of fellowships: 200 - Monthly amount: 20Rs. - Age group: Above 40 years **Junior Fellowship:** - Number of fellowships: 200 - Monthly amount: 10Rs. - Age group: 2540 years - Age is calculated as on 1st April of the given year **Publishing Grant** In additionRs. there could be a one time grant up to maximum of 20Rs./- or 50% of the cost of the publicationRs. whichever is lessRs. for publication of selected Project documents. This will be restricted to 20% of the awardees.
eligibility:
1. The age of the applicant should be above 40 years for applying under senior fellowships.
1. The age of the applicant should be between 25-40 years for applying under junior fellowships.
1. Graduation is the minimum educational qualification for applicants in the fields/areas mentioned in the scheme guideline.
1. Applicants for senior fellowship should not be the recipient of pension from the Ministry of Culture under the scheme for grant of financial assistance to artists in indigent circumstances.
1. An applicant should not have availed of the same fellowship earlier. HoweverRs. an applicant who had been awarded a Junior Fellowship can apply for a Senior FellowshipRs. provided 5 years have elapsed after the closure of the earlier project.

**Note 01:** The age of the applicant will be reckoned as of 1st April of the year.
**Note 02:** Under the Senior and Junior FellowshipsRs. the awardees will submit a six-monthly progress report. In cases where such reports are not received timelyRs. the Ministry may withhold further releases of the Fellowship amount.
**Note 03:** The selected candidates will have to undertake academic or application-oriented research work on projects for which they have been awarded the Fellowship. They will complete their Projects within two years and submit the same to the Ministry. Extension of time by a maximum of three months will be permissible without any additional financial liability to the Government.
**Note 04:** A mid-term review/assessment of performance in each case will be carried out after one year and further continuance of Fellowship will depend on such review/assessment.

name: Divyangjan Kaushal Yojana
brief_description: The scheme "Divyangjan Kaushal Yojana" was announced by the Hon'ble Finance Minister during the presentation of the Union Budget 2026-2027. The scheme is planned to be launched by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with DisabilitiesRs. Ministry of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to ensure dignified livelihood opportunities for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) by providing industry-relevant and customized training specific to each group. The scheme provides skill development in high-growth sectors such as Information TechnologyRs. AnimationRs. Visual EffectsRs. Gaming and Comics (AVGC)Rs. and hospitalityRs. focusing on task-oriented and process-driven roles. The applicant must be a Person with Disability seeking employment-oriented skill training.
benefits: - Customized and industry-relevant training specific to the needs of each 'divyang' group. - Skill development in high-growth sectorsRs. including Information TechnologyRs. AnimationRs. Visual EffectsRs. Gaming and Comics (AVGC)Rs. HospitalityRs. and Food and Beverages. - Access to task-oriented and process-driven job roles suitable for Persons with Disabilities. - Support for securing dignified livelihood opportunities. - A budgetary allocation of 2Rs./- for the fiscal year 2026-27 to support the training initiatives.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a Person with Disability (Divyangjan). - The applicant must be eligible for skill training aimed at livelihood opportunities.

name: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research
brief_description: The scheme "ICMR-Junior Research Fellowship" by the Department of Health Research (DHR)Rs. Ministry Of Health & Family WelfareRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to enhance the availability of trained health research personnel through providing short-term training fellowships and financial assistance to medical faculty and researchers. It supports training in both Indian and foreign institutions for a duration of 1-3 months. The scheme focuses on priority areas such as clinical trialsRs. genomicsRs. toxicologyRs. and biotechnology. It encourages multidisciplinary collaboration and the development of research projects addressing national and local health challenges. The fellowship also aims to build a skilled workforce in advanced medical and health research domains.
benefits: > **For Training In Indian Institutes (1-3 Months):** - **Stipend:** 40Rs./- per month (if training is at a different station); 20Rs./- per month (if training is at the same station). - **Travel Support:** Travelling expenses are provided as per Travelling Allowance rules of the parent organization. - Contingency Grant: One-time grant up to 20Rs./- for local travelRs. meetingsRs. and related expenses. > **For Training In Foreign Institutes (1-3 Months):** - **Stipend:** US $3000/- per month or equivalent in other foreign currency. - **Air Travel:** Economy class airfare by Air India via the shortest route from parent institute to host institute. - **Contingency Grant:** One-time grant up to 30Rs./- for visaRs. insuranceRs. local expensesRs. meetings; additional 20Rs./- for attending review meetings. - **Conference Grant:** US $600/- for attending conferences or institutes of interest with approval.
eligibility: - Only Indian citizens working in Indian institutes are eligible. - They should hold M.D./ M.S./ M.D.S. or MBBS/BDS/ MVSc./ M.Sc./M.Pharma/M.Tech or equivalent with Ph.D. in health/biomedical research. - Faculty having at least three years experience in the college/institute as a regular employee. - Persons up to 55 years of age as of the last date of receipt of application will be eligible. - They should not have availed any fellowship of the duration of one month or above duration from any of the agencies of Govt. of India / State Governments for the same subject of training/research project. - The fellowship is for 1-3 months. Fellowship is non-transferable.

name: Sagar Samman Award- Recognition of Outstanding Maritime Training Institutes
brief_description: The "Sagar Samman Award- Recognition of Outstanding Maritime Training Institutes" scheme has been launched by the Directorate General of ShippingRs. Ministry of PortsRs. Shipping and WaterwaysRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to recognize exceptional contributions made by maritime training institutes in advancing maritime educationRs. skill developmentRs. and human resource capacity in the maritime sector.
benefits: - Formal national-level recognition to top 3 institutes in each category. - Inter-se ranking to determine 1stRs. 2ndRs. and 3rd positions. - Public acknowledgment during National Maritime Day celebrations. - Enhanced institutional reputation and credibility.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) approved maritime training institute. 1. The applicant should have participated in the Comprehensive Inspection Programme (CIP). 1. The applicant should have demonstrated consistent and high performance in training quality and outcomes. 1. The applicant should fall under one of the following categories: - Pre-sea training institutes for Officer Cadets (Nautical & Engineering); - Pre-sea training institutes for Rating Trainees; - Post-sea training institutes conducting Competency Courses.

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for the Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribe for Studies in India
brief_description: The scheme "Post-Matric Scholarship for the Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribe for Studies in India" is implemented by the Department of Tribal Affairs (Plain)Rs. Government of Assam. The scheme aims to enable eligible Scheduled Tribe students to undertake quality education from the post-matriculation to the post-graduate level by providing them with comprehensive financial assistance. The scheme provides financial assistance covering the payment of compulsory non-refundable fees and a monthly stipendRs. alongside an additional disability allowance for specially-abled students.
benefits:
##### ***Fee Component*** - The scheme covers the payment of compulsory non-refundable fees for the recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary course pursued by the student. - There is a fee ceiling of 2Rs./- per annum per student for Engineering courses in private sector institutes. - There is a fee ceiling of 6Rs./- per annum per student for Bachelor of MedicineRs. Bachelor of SurgeryRs. Master of SurgeryRs. and Doctor of Medicine courses in private sector institutes. - There is a fee ceiling of 1Rs./- per annum per student for all other courses in private sector institutes.
##### ***Monthly Stipend (Payable For A Maximum Of 10 Months Annually)*** - For Group I (Degree and Post Graduate professional courses): Hostellers receive 1Rs./- per month (12Rs./- annually)Rs. and day scholars receive 550/- per month (5Rs./- annually). - For Group II (Non-professional Degree and Post Graduate courses): Hostellers receive 820/- per month (8Rs./- annually)Rs. and day scholars receive 530/- per month (5Rs./- annually). - For Group III (VocationalRs. Industrial Training InstituteRs. and 3-year diploma courses): Hostellers receive 570/- per month (5Rs./- annually)Rs. and day scholars receive 300/- per month (3Rs./- annually). - For Group IV (Post-matriculation non-degree courses): Hostellers receive 380/- per month (3Rs./- annually)Rs. and day scholars receive 230/- per month (2Rs./- annually).
##### ***Additional Disability Allowance*** - Specially-abled hosteller students receive an additional allowance of 800/- per month (9Rs./- annually). - Specially-abled day scholar students receive an additional allowance of 600/- per month (7Rs./- annually).
##### ***Benefit Disbursal Details*** - The scholarship amounts are disbursed exclusively through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode directly into the Aadhaar-linked bank accounts of the beneficiaries. - The stipend is payable monthlyRs. calculated from 1st April or from the month of admissionRs. whichever is laterRs. until the month in which the annual examinations are completed.
##### ***Conditions for Availment and Continuation*** - The continuous disbursement of the scholarship is strictly dependent on the satisfactory academic progressRs. good conductRs. and regularity in attendance of the enrolled scholars. - The scholarship will be immediately cancelled or withheld if the student resorts to strikes or maintains irregular attendance without formal permission from the institution authorities. - The scholarship will not be renewed if the student fails in a particular academic yearRs. and the benefits will be paused until the student clears that class and gets promoted to the next class.
eligibility:
- The applicant must belong to the Scheduled TribeRs. Other Backward ClassesRs. or More Other Backward Classes as specified in relation to the State or Union Territory to which they actually belong. - The applicant must have successfully passed the Matriculation or Higher Secondary or any higher examination of a recognized University or Board of Secondary Education. - The applicant must take admission in recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary courses pursued in governmentRs. government-aidedRs. or approved private institutions. - The applicant must possess a validRs. active bank account in a Scheduled Bank. - The applicant must link their bank account securely with their Aadhaar number and their active mobile number. - The applicant should preferably continue using the identical mobile number linked with the bank account for the entire duration of the course.
***Income Criteria*** - The applicant must belong to a family whose total gross income from all sources does not exceed 2Rs./- per annum without any exemption or deductions. - The applicant must calculate the combined income of both parents from all sources if both the father and mother are currently working. - The applicant must compute the income of only one parent if only one parent is alive and supporting the family. - The applicant must not include the income of siblings or other earning members of the family while computing the total family income. - The applicant must be fully exempt from the family income criteria if they are an orphan supported by a guardian.

name: Welfare Services for Children
brief_description: The "Welfare Services for Children" component under the Mizoram Grant-in-Aid framework is designed to ensure the well-beingRs. protectionRs. and holistic development of children in vulnerable situations. The scheme supports voluntary organisations in delivering essential services to children who are deprived of family careRs. exposed to exploitationRs. or facing socio-economic hardships. Target beneficiaries include orphansRs. street childrenRs. children affected by HIV/AIDSRs. child labourersRs. and juvenile delinquents. The scheme provides financial assistance to organizations for setting up and running institutions such as orphanagesRs. daycare centresRs. and special schools. It also supports health and nutrition programmesRs. educational initiativesRs. and rehabilitation services aimed at reintegrating children into society. Preventive measures are encouraged to reduce child labour and protect children from exploitation. Special emphasis is given to providing a safe environmentRs. access to educationRs. vocational trainingRs. and healthcare services.
benefits: > **Shelter & Care:** - Establishment of homes for orphaned and abandoned children. - Provision of foodRs. shelterRs. and basic amenities. > **Education & Training:** - Formal and non-formal education support. - Vocational training for skill development. > **Health & Nutrition:** - Nutritional support through daycare centres. - Health programmesRs. including maternal and child care. > **Child Protection Services:** - Helplines and referral services for children at risk. - Preventive measures against child labour. > **Rehabilitation Support:** - Rehabilitation of juvenile delinquents. - Reintegration of vulnerable children into society. > **Special Support:** - Services for children affected by HIV/AIDS. - CounsellingRs. careRs. and medical assistance.
eligibility: The following individual types of applicants are eligible under this scheme: - Orphans and abandoned children - Street children - Children affected by HIV/AIDS - Child labourers - Juvenile delinquents

name: Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme
brief_description: The UNNATI (Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme)Rs. 2024Rs. is a Government of India initiative to boost industrial growthRs. investmentRs. and employment in the North-Eastern Region (NER) states by offering substantial financial incentivesRs. capital subsidiesRs. and interest subventions for new and expanding manufacturing and service sector businessesRs. aiming to create a robust industrial ecosystem with simplified processes and support for innovation and skill development.
benefits: - Capital Investment Incentive (CII) - 30% of the eligible P&M in Zone A and 50% in Zone B. - Capital Interest Subvention (CIS) - 3% interest subvention in Zone A and 5% in Zone B for a period of 7 years. - Manufacturing & Services Linked Incentive (MSLI) - All eligible units of Zone A & Zone B will be granted MSLI equal to 100% of the Net payment of GSTRs. i.e. GST Paid less Input Tax CreditRs. for a maximum period of 10 years from the date of commencement of commercial production/operation or till the validity of the scheme whichever is earlier.
eligibility: > As per detailed scheme guidelines including minimum investmentRs. legal entity statusRs. fulfilling requirements viz. registered lease deadRs. GST detailsRs. various reports such as DPRRs. BAR etc.

name: Financial Assistance for Education (HPBOCWWB)
brief_description: The "Financial Assistance for Education Scheme" has been introduced by the Himachal Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HPBOCWWB) and has been providing annual financial assistance for the education of up to two children of a beneficiaryRs. covering studies from Class I to professional courses such as Medical and EngineeringRs. as well as PhD and research programs.
benefits: 1. Primary & Middle School (Class 18): 8Rs./- per year 1. Secondary & Senior Secondary (Class 912): 12Rs./- per year 1. Graduation Level: 36Rs./- per year 1. Post-Graduation Level: 60Rs./- per year 1. Diploma Courses: 48Rs./- per year 1. Polytechnic Diploma: 60Rs./- per year 1. Professional / Research Courses: 1Rs./- per year **Note:** This applies equally to both girls and boys.
eligibility: **For Registration as a Building/ Construction Worker:** 1. The applicant should be a resident of Himachal Pradesh 1. The applicant should be a Building/ Construction Worker.. 1. The applicant should be aged between 18 and 60 years. 1. The worker should have completed at least 90 days of building and other construction work in the last 12 months. 1. The registration of the applicant should have been renewed annually. **Eligibility Criteria for Scheme:** 1. The parent of the child must be engaged in building or construction work under the Himachal Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HPBOCWWB). 1. The parent of the child should be registered with the Himachal Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HPBOCWWB). 1. The parent's membership with the Himachal Pradesh Welfare Board must be active at the time of application.

name: Dr. Ambedakar Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarships for the Economically Backward Class (EBC) Students
brief_description: "Dr. Ambedakar Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarships for the Economically Backward Class (EBC) Students" is a Scholarship Scheme by the Department of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Economically Backward Class (EBC) students studying at the post-matriculation or post-secondary stage to enable them to complete their education. These scholarships shall be available for studies in India only and will be awarded by the Government of State/Union Territory to which the applicant actually belongsRs. i.e. permanently settled.
benefits: **Maintenance Allowance** > **Group A** 1. Degree and Post Graduate level courses including M.Phil.Rs. PhD and Post Doctoral research in Medicine (AllopathicRs. Indian and other recognized systems of medicines)Rs. EngineeringRs. TechnologyRs. PlanningRs. ArchitectureRs. DesignRs. Fashion TechnologyRs. AgricultureRs. Veterinary and Allied SciencesRs. ManagementRs. Business Finance/AdministrationRs. Computer Science/Applications. 1. Post Graduate Diploma courses in various branches of management & medicine. 1. C.A./ I.C.W.A./ C.S./ I.C.F.A. etc. 1. M. Phil.Rs. Ph.D. and Post-Doctoral Programmes (D.Litt.Rs. D.Sc. etc.). 1. L.L.M **Rate of Maintenance Allowance ( per month):** Hostellers: 750; Day Scholars: 350. > **Group B** 1. Graduate/Post/Graduate courses leading to DegreeRs. DiplomaRs. Certificate in areas like Pharmacy (B. Pharma)Rs. Nursing (B Nursing)Rs. LLBRs. BFSRs. other para-medial branches like rehabilitation diagnostics etc.Rs. Mass CommunicationRs. Hotel Management & CateringRs. Travel/Tourism/Hospitality ManagementRs. Interior DecorationRs. Nutrition & DieteticsRs. Commercial ArtRs. Financial Services (e.g. BankingRs. InsuranceRs. Taxation etc.) for which entrance qualification is minimum Sr. Secondary (10+2)Rs. except aviation related courses. 1. Post Graduate courses not covered under Group A e.g. MA/M.Sc./M.Com/ M.Ed./M.Pharma etc. **Rate of Maintenance Allowance ( per month):** Hostellers: 510; Day Scholars: 335. > **Group C** All other courses leading to a graduate degree not covered under Group A & B e.g. BA/B.Sc./B.Com etc. **Rate of Maintenance Allowance ( per month):** Hostellers: 400; Day Scholars: 210. > **Group D** All post-matriculation level non-degree courses for which entrance qualification is High School (Class X)Rs. e.g. senior secondary certificate (class XI and XII); both general and vocational streamRs. ITI coursesRs. 3-year diploma courses in PolytechnicsRs. etc. **Rate of Maintenance Allowance ( per month):** Hostellers: 260; Day Scholars: 160. **NOTE:** Scholars who are entitled to free boarding and/or lodging will be paid maintenance chargers at 1/3rd of the hostellers' rate. **Reader Charges for Blind Students (Blind Scholars)** The blind scholars will be given an additional amount as 'Readers Charges' as mentioned below: **Group: A & B;** Reader Allowance ( per month): 175 **Group: C;** Reader Allowance ( per month): 130 **Group: D;** Reader Allowance ( per month): 90 **Fees** Scholars will be paid enrolment/registrationRs. tuitionRs. gamesRs. unionRs. libraryRs. magazineRs. medical examination and such other fees compulsorily payable by the scholar to the institution or University/Board. Refundable deposit-like caution money and security deposit willRs. howeverRs. be excluded. **Study Tours** Study tour charges upto a maximum of 900/- per annum limited to the actual expenditure incurred by the student on transportation charges etc.Rs. will be paid to the scholars studying professional and technical coursesRs. provided that the head of the institution certifies that the study tour is essential for the scholar for completion of his/her course of study. **Thesis Typing/ Printing Charges** Thesis typing/printing charges upto a maximum of 1000/- will be paid to research scholars on the recommendation of the Head of the Institution. **Mode of Disbursal** In order to ensure timely payment of scholarship amount to the beneficiariesRs. the State Government/UT administrations are requested to avoid cash payment of scholarship amount and are required to issue instructions to all concerned that payment of scholarship should be made directly to beneficiaries through their accounts in post offices/banks with phased transition to Smart Cards. **Duration of Awards** The award once made will be tenable from the stage at which it is given to the completion of the course subject to good conduct and regularity in attendance. **Renewal of Awards** It will be renewed from year to year provided that within a courseRs. which is continuous for a number of yearsRs. the scholar secures promotion to the next higher class irrespective of the fact whether such examinations are conducted by a University or the Institution.
eligibility:
1. The scholarships will be open to Indian nationals belonging to the General Category (Other than Schedule CasteRs. Schedule Tribe and Other Backward Classes).
1. These scholarships will be given for the study of all recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary courses pursued in Government institutions.
1. Students pursuing Post-graduate courses in medicine will be eligible if they are not allowed to practice during the period of their course.
1. Students who after failing or passing the undergraduate/Post-Graduate examinations in Arts/Science/Commerce join any recognized professional or Technical certificate/diploma/degree courses will be awarded scholarships if otherwise eligible. No subsequent failure will be condoned except for courses in Group 'A' and no further change in the course will be allowed.
1. Students who pursue their studies through correspondence courses will be eligible towards reimbursement of a non-refundable fee. The term correspondence includes distant and continuing education. Besides reimbursement of non-refundable feesRs. such students will also be eligible for an annual allowance of Rs. 900/- for essential/prescribed booksRs. as applicable.
1. Only two boys of the same parents/guardians will be entitled to receive scholarships. This restriction willRs. howeverRs. not apply to girls. AccordinglyRs. scholarships availed by girls of the same parents/guardian will not adversely affect the admissibility of availing scholarships upto two boys of the same parents/guardian.
1. A scholarship holder under this Scheme will not hold any other scholarship/stipend. If awarded any other scholarship/stipendRs. the student can exercise his/her option for either of the two scholarships/stipendsRs. whichever is more beneficial to him/her and should inform the awarding authority through the Head of the Institution about the option made. No scholarship will be paid to the students under this Scheme from the date he/she accepts any other scholarships/stipend. The student canRs. howeverRs. accept free lodging or a grant or ad-hoc monetary help from the State Government or any other source for the purchase of booksRs. and equipment or for meeting the expenses on board and lodgingRs. in addition to the scholarship amount paid under this Scheme.
1. Scholarship holders who are receiving coaching in any of the pre-examination training centres with financial assistance from the Central Government/State Government will not be eligible for a stipend under the coaching schemes for the duration of the coaching programme.
1. Employed students whose income combined with the income of their parents/guardians does not exceed 1Rs. per annum shall be eligible for post-matric scholarships to the extent of reimbursement of all compulsorily payable non-refundable fees.
1. In the case of unemployed students whose parents/guardians income from all sources does not exceed 1Rs. per annum will be entitled to the scholarship under the Scheme.

name: Assistance to Voluntary Organizations Working for Welfare of OBCs
brief_description: The central sector scheme "Assistance to Voluntary Organizations Working for Welfare of OBCs" was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to involve the voluntary sector to improve the educational and socio-economic conditions of the target group i.e. OBCsRs. to upgrade skills to enable them to start income-generating activities on their own or get gainfully employed in some sector or the other. The projects can be implemented in villages under the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY). > **Types of Activities Covered** CarpentryRs. Computer EducationRs. Craft CentreRs. Dari making TrainingRs. Diesel Pump set repairingRs. Electrical trainingRs. Fruit Preservation TrainingRs. Gem cuttingRs. Welding and Fitter trainingRs. PhotographyRs. PlumbingRs. PrintingRs. composing and book bindingRs. ScooterRs. motorcycle and auto-rickshaw repairingRs. Spinning and weavingRs. Typing and shorthandRs. Tie and dye trainingRs. Leather artRs. Denting and spray paintingRs. TVRs. VCR and radio repair.
benefits: - Financial support for skill development projects aimed at improving socio-economic conditions of OBCs. - Simplified and transparent application and approval process. - Regular monitoring and evaluation to ensure effective utilization of funds. - Support for NGOs to enhance their capacity and expand their reach. - Encouragement of self-employment and gainful employment for OBCs. - Priority given to projects in backward districts and villages under SAGY. > **Extent of Assistance:** - Government may cover up to 90% of approved project expenditure. - PSUs or other organizations limited to 30% of project cost for skill development programs. - First installment up to 75% on submission of necessary documents. - Second installment on receipt of audited accounts and utilization certificates.
eligibility: > **For the Organization:** 1. Registered under the Societies Registration ActRs. 1860 (XXI of 1860) or any relevant Act of the State/Union Territory/Public trust. 1. The organization should have an appropriate administrative structure and managing/executive committee. 1. The organization should be democratically governed without external control. 1. The organization must be registered for at least three years (waivable in exceptional cases). 1. The organization should maintain a bank account in the organizations name for at least three years. 1. The organization should not be run for profit by any individual or a body of individuals. > **The following criteria would be kept in view while selecting the new VOs/NGOs:** 1. Experience of at least two years in the relevant field. 1. Projects should be in Backward Districts identified by the Planning Commission. > **For the Beneficiaries:** 1. The beneficiary must belong to the Central or state/UT OBC list. 1. The beneficiary's annual family income should not exceed 1Rs./-..

name: PM Vishwakarma
brief_description:
PM Vishwakarma is a Central Sector Scheme launched by Ministry of MicroRs. Small and Medium Enterprises to provide holistic and end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople through access to collateral free creditRs. skill trainingRs. modern toolsRs. incentive for digital transactions and market linkage support. The scheme will initially be implemented for five years up to 2027-28.
> **Objectives**


1. To enable the recognition of artisans and craftspeople as Vishwakarma making them eligible to avail all the benefits under the Scheme.
1. To provide skill upgradation to hone their skills and make relevant and suitable training opportunities available to them.
1. To provide support for better and modern tools to enhance their capabilityRs. productivityRs. and quality of products.
1. To provide the intended beneficiaries easy access to collateral-free credit and reduce the cost of credit by providing interest subvention.
1. To provide incentives for digital transactions to encourage the digital empowerment of these Vishwakarmas.
1. To provide a platform for brand promotion and market linkages to help them access new opportunities for growth.

> **Implementing Agency**


- The scheme is conjointly implemented by the following Ministries/Departments:
- Ministry of MicroRs. Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME).
- Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).
- Department of Financial Services (DFS)Rs. Ministry of Finance (MoF).
benefits: 1. **Recognition**: Recognition as Vishwakarma through Certificate and ID Card 1. **Skilling**: 1. Skill Verification followed by 5-7 days (40 hours) of Basic Training 1. Interested candidates can also enrol for 15 days (120 hours) of Advanced Training 1. Training Stipend: 500/- per day. 1. **Toolkit Incentive**: 15Rs./- grant. 1. **Credit Support**: 1. Collateral-free Enterprise Development Loans: 1Rs./- (First Tranche for 18 months repayment) & 2Rs./- (Second Tranche for 30 months repayment) 1. Concessional Rate of Interest: 5% to be charged from the beneficiary with an Interest Subvention cap of 8% to be paid by MoMSME 1. Credit Guarantee fees to be borne by GoI 1. **Incentive for Digital Transaction**: 1/- per transaction for a maximum of up to 100 transactions (monthly) 1. **Marketing Support**: The National Committee for Marketing (NCM) will provide services such as Quality CertificationRs. Branding and PromotionRs. e-commerce LinkageRs. Trade Fair AdvertisingRs. PublicityRs. and Other Marketing Activities. > **NOTE**: Notification to beneficiaries on disbursement of incentives will be done through SMS.
eligibility: - The applicant should be an artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools. - The applicant should be engaged in an unorganized sector on a self-employment basis. - The applicant should be engaged in one of the 18 family-based traditional trades mentioned in the scheme. - On the date of registration for the schemeRs. the minimum age of the applicant should be 18 years. - The applicant should be engaged in the concerned trade on the date of registration. - The applicant should not have availed loans under similar credit-based schemes of the Central Government or State Government for self-employment/ business developmentRs. e.g. PMEGPRs.
