eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a girl. 1. The applicant should be a student. 1. The applicant should be studying in class VIII(8) in Government School of the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

name: Nagar Van Yojana
brief_description: The scheme "Nagar Van Yojana" was launched by the Ministry of EnvironmentRs. Forest and Climate ChangeRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to develop 400 Nagar Vans and 200 Nagar Vatikas to create green spaces in urban areas by protecting land from degradation. The scheme provides a one-time development grant of 4Rs./- per hectare up to a maximum of 2Rs./- for 50 hectares to cover costs such as fencingRs. soil-moisture conservationRs. theme-based plantationsRs. and maintenance of tree cover. The applicant must formulate a detailed project proposalRs. include a Keyhole Markup Language map on a 1:10Rs. or larger scaleRs. ensure a commitment to bear the balance costRs. and submit the plan for the identified land. The scheme is implemented by the State Forest Department and the National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted offline through the concerned State Forest Department offices.
benefits:
- The Ministry will provide a one-time development and non-recurring grant of 4Rs./- per hectare. - The maximum financial assistance for a Nagar Van is limited to 2Rs./- for 50 hectares. - The State Forest Department is permitted to engage one technical consultant at a cost of 40Rs./- per month until the completion of the project for monitoring and other works. - The State Forest Department will receive a lump sum grant of 50Rs./- per project for monitoringRs. evaluationRs. and meeting overhead expenses. **Mode of Disbursal:** The funds will be released directly to the respective State Forest Departments from the National Fund under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority. **Frequency and Validity:** The grant is a one-time assistanceRs. released in two separate instalmentsRs. and financial assistance is provided to each Nagar Van or Nagar Vatika for the first two years only.
##### ***Components*** - Fencing of the identified area must be undertaken. - Establishment and maintenance of woodlots or tree cover with an emphasis on locally appropriate species must be carried out. - Theme-based plantations such as Smriti Van or Nakshatra Van may be established. - Plants representing floral biodiversityRs. including ornamental treesRs. medicinal plantsRs. and fruit treesRs. must be included. - Irrigation and rain water harvesting facilities must be established. - Establishment and maintenance of public conveniencesRs. drinking water facilitiesRs. benchesRs. walkwaysRs. and cycle tracks must be completed. - An Information and Extension CentreRs. including display boards and information brochuresRs. must be established and maintained.
##### ***Conditions*** - The first instalment of 70% of the sanctioned amount is released to the State Forest Department after the approval of the project by the National Authority. - The remaining second instalment of 30% is released after 60% utilization of the first instalment and on the submission of the utilisation certificate and progress report. - The State Forest Department must further release the portion of the grant meant for an implementing agency within a period of seven days. - A corpus of the entire funds received by the implementing agency must be maintained as an interest-bearing account in a government or public sector bank. - Detailed accounts of receipts and expenditures must be maintained by each implementing agency and the State Forest Department. - All funds received by the implementing agency must be subjected to an annual audit by a chartered accountant.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a Municipal CorporationRs. Municipal CouncilRs. MunicipalityRs. Urban Local BodyRs. State Forest DepartmentRs. Educational InstitutionRs. UniversityRs. Government OrganisationRs. or Non-Government Organisation. - The applicant must have possession of the proposed land. - The applicant must provide a commitment to bear the balance cost of the project beyond the provided grant. - The applicant must ensure that the proposed area is situated on forest land or other vacant non-forest public land. - The applicant must formulate a Development cum Management Plan with year-wise details of works under different components. ##### ***For Nagar Van*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Van over a minimum area of 10 hectares. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area for grant calculation to 50 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located within a 5-kilometre limit of the Municipal CorporationRs. Municipal CouncilRs. or Municipality. - The applicant must maintain a minimum of 2/3rd of the Nagar Van area under woodland or tree cover. ##### ***For Nagar Vatika*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Vatika in a minimum area of 1 hectare. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area of the Nagar Vatika to 10 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located strictly within the city limits or congested parts of the cities. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must keep all Nagar Vans and Nagar Vatikas open and accessible to the city dwellers and general publicRs. subject to suitable restrictions. - The applicant should encourage a Public-Private Partnership mode to ensure the active participation of peopleRs. studentsRs. and other stakeholders in planningRs. implementationRs. and management. - The applicant should select trees from species that are best suited for local conditions. - The applicant should place an emphasis on enriching biodiversityRs. planting fruit-bearing treesRs. and cultivating medicinal plants. - The applicant should ensure sufficient revenue generation for maintenance by levying user feesRs. receiving grants from other agenciesRs. and promoting economic activities like the sale of saplings or processed forest products from the first year. - The applicant should encourage the use of locally available materialRs. energy conservationRs. and waste recycling.

name: PRL Junior Research Fellowships
brief_description: The Physical Research Laboratory (PRL)Rs. a prestigious institution under the Department of SpaceRs. Government of IndiaRs. launched the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) Program. The JRF program aims to provide highly motivated and academically excellent candidates with an opportunity to pursue cutting-edge research in a variety of science domainsRs. such as Astronomy and astrophysicsRs. atomicRs. MolecularRs. and optical PhysicsRs. GeosciencesRs. Planetary SciencesRs. Space and Atmospheric SciencesRs. Solar PhysicsRs. and Theoretical Physics.
benefits: > **Fellowship Allowance:** Junior Research Fellow (JRF): 37Rs./- per month. Senior Research Fellow (SRFRs. after 2 years): 42Rs./- per month (based on performance review). > **Platinum Jubilee Research Fellowship (ATAL):** Selected meritorious JRFs may receive an additional ATAL fellowship of 40Rs./- per month (for 3rd to 5th year). > **Ph.D. Registration:** Fellows have the opportunity to register for a Ph.D. at an institute/university with an MoU with PRL.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be an Indian citizen.
1. The applicant should have studied at recognized Universities/Institutes in India.
1. The applicants age should be 28 years as of 01st July 2024.
1. The applicant should complete a Bachelors and Masters degree in science or engineering with at least 60% marks (or equivalent) at both levels.
1. Candidates from disciplines of any branch of PhysicsRs. ChemistryRs. Engineering PhysicsRs. PhotonicsRs. Space PhysicsRs. Atmospheric ScienceRs. Environmental ScienceRs. OceanographyRs. MeteorologyRs. GeologyRs. GeophysicsRs. Earth Science and Remote Sensing are eligible to apply.
1. The applicant should be interested in pursuing a research career in the current research areas at PRLRs. and must have qualified in any one of the following exams:



- CSIR-UGC-NET JRF/AP (2022 or later) in Physical Sciences/Chemical Sciences/EarthRs. AtmosphericRs. OceanRs. and Planetary Sciences.
- GATE (2022 or later) in relevant subjects.
- JEST (2024) in Physics.
- UGC-NET JRF/AP (2022 or later) in Environmental Sciences.

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
brief_description: The "Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)" is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Department of AgricultureRs. Cooperation and Farmers WelfareRs. Government of India under the "National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)". The scheme aims to promote organic farming through a cluster-based approach and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification. It supports farmers in converting conventional agricultural land into organic farming systems through financial assistance for certificationRs. organic inputsRs. manure managementRs. and marketing activities. The scheme is implemented over a period of 3 yearsRs. corresponding to the 36-month conversion period from conventional to organic farming. The funding pattern is 60:40 between the Central and State GovernmentsRs. 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan StatesRs. and 100% Central assistance for Union Territories.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance for Organic Farming Cluster:** - Total assistance of 14Rs./- per cluster of 20 hectares (50 acres) for 3 years. - Maximum assistance of 10Rs./- per cluster for farmer members. - Maximum assistance of 50Rs./- per farmer per hectareRs. limited to 1 hectare per farmer. > **Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) Certification:** - Assistance for mobilization of farmers and formation of Local Groups. - Support for PGS certification and quality control activities. - Assistance for online registrationRs. soil testingRs. field inspectionsRs. residue analysisRs. and certification processes. > **Conversion of Land into Organic Farming:** - Assistance for conversion of conventional land into organic farming. - Support for organic cropping systems. - Assistance for organic seed procurement and nursery raising. - Support for establishment of organic input production units. - Assistance for biological nitrogen harvesting plantations. - Support for botanical extract production units. > **Integrated Manure Management** - Assistance for production and use of liquid bio-fertilizers. - Assistance for liquid bio-pesticides. - Support for natural pest control practices. - Assistance for Phosphate Rich Organic Manure (PROM). - Support for vermicompost units. > **Custom Hiring Centre (CHC):** - Assistance for hiring agricultural implements required for organic farming operations. > **PackingRs. Labelling and Branding:** - Assistance for procurement of packing materials. - Support for PGS logo and hologram printing. - Assistance for branding and marketing of organic products. - Support for transportation of organic produce. - Assistance for participation in organic fairs.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a farmer willing to adopt organic farming practices. - The applicant must be part of a cluster or Local Group formed under the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS)-India programme. - The applicant must be a member of a cluster covering approximately 20 hectares (50 acres) in a contiguous area.

name: Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme For The Scheduled Castes
brief_description: The scheme "Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for the Scheduled Castes (SCs) (CEGSSC)" by the Department of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Ministry of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled CastesRs. support innovation and growth-oriented enterprisesRs. facilitate financial inclusionRs. generate employmentRs. and encourage economic development through credit enhancement guarantees. Through this schemeRs. credit enhancement guarantee support is provided to banks and financial institutions that extend financial assistance to eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. The scheme is implemented by IFCI Limited (Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited) as the nodal agency. Under the schemeRs. the Government of India has established a corpus fund of 200 crore to provide guarantees for working capital loansRs. term loansRs. and composite term loans extended to eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. The scheme seeks to improve access to financeRs. create wealth and employment opportunitiesRs. encourage profitable business venturesRs. and strengthen forward and backward economic linkages across communities. The scheme is operational across India on an ongoing basis. > **Objective:** 1. To promote entrepreneurship among the Scheduled Caste population across India. 1. To promote innovation and growth-oriented entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes. 1. To provide Credit Enhancement Guarantees to banks and financial institutions financing SC entrepreneurs. 1. To create wealthRs. generate employmentRs. and build confidence among Scheduled Castes. 1. To promote financial inclusion and economic development of SC entrepreneurs. 1. To enhance direct and indirect employment generation for SC communities.
benefits: The scheme provides guarantee cover for Working Capital LoansRs. Term LoansRs. and Composite Term Loans extended to eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. **Loan Amount****Guarantee Cover****Guarantee Obligation**15Rs./- to 1Rs./-100% of the sanctioned facility100% of the amount in defaultRs. subject to maximum guarantee coverAbove 1Rs./- to 2Rs./-80% of the sanctioned facility80% of the amount in defaultRs. subject to maximum guarantee coverAbove 2Rs./- to 5Rs./-70% of the sanctioned facility70% of the amount in defaultRs. subject to the maximum guarantee coverAbove 5Rs./-60% of the sanctioned facility60% of the amount in defaultRs. subject to the maximum guarantee cover> **Additional Benefit Conditions:** - The maximum guarantee cover available under the scheme is 5Rs./-. - Startup Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs are eligible for guarantee coverage. - Individual Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs are eligible for guarantee cover on loan amounts up to 1Rs./-. - Repeat credit enhancement may be extended after successful liquidation of the first facility and a satisfactory track record. - Incubation facilities may be facilitated through existing departmental schemes for loans above 2Rs./-. > **Mode of Disbursement:** - Benefits are provided in the form of Credit Enhancement Guarantees issued by IFCI to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs). - Loans are extended by Member Lending Institutions to eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. > **Expected Time of Disbursement** - The guarantee is issued after submission of the sanction letterRs. proof of disbursementRs. and the guarantee fee by the Member Lending Institution within 30 days of the first loan disbursement. > **Validity** - Initially valid for 1 year. - Renewable annually. - The maximum tenure of guarantee cover is 7 years or the repayment periodRs. whichever is earlier.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should establishRs. promoteRs. and operate an enterpriseRs. projectRs. or unit in the primaryRs. manufacturingRs. or service sector resulting in asset creation. 1. The applicant should be a Scheduled Caste entrepreneurRs. companyRs. partnership firmRs. societyRs. sole proprietorship firmRs. or individual entrepreneur as specified under the scheme. 1. The applicant should have more than 51% ownership and management control held by Scheduled Caste entrepreneursRs. promotersRs. partnersRs. or members. 1. The applicant should maintain Scheduled Caste ownership and control above 51% throughout the currency of the loan. 1. The applicant should provide documentary proof of Scheduled Caste status. 1. The applicant may operate under any Central Government or State Government subsidy or grant scheme. 1. Preference is given to Scheduled Caste-promoted companies over registered partnership firms and registered societies.

name: Janshree Bima Yojana for Khadi Artisans
brief_description: The scheme "Janshree Bima Yojana for Khadi Artisans" has been launched by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)Rs. Government of IndiaRs. and aims to provide insurance cover to Khadi artisans. Through this schemeRs. group insurance benefits are provided to Khadi artisans (spinners and weavers). The scheme is implemented by Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) in association with Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The scheme was formulated in the name of Khadi Karigar Janshree Bima Yojana (JBY) to provide insurance protection to Khadi artisans. The scheme provides assistance in cases of deathRs. permanent disabilityRs. and partial disability. A free add-on scholarship benefit is also provided for children of Khadi Karigar studying in 9th to 12th standard.
benefits: 1. **For death:** Natural causes 20Rs.; and Accident 50Rs..1. **For permanent disability** (loss of two eyes or two limbs) 50Rs..1. **For partial disability** (loss of one eye or one limb) 25Rs..1. **Free add-on benefit**: Scholarship of 300 per quarter for children of Khadi KarigarRs. studying in class 9th to 12th standardRs. subject to a maximum of 2 children per family
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a Khadi Artisan (Khadi Karigar). 1. The age of the applicant must be between 18 and 59 years. 1. The applicant must be a member of the approved vocation/occupation groups. 1. The group must have a minimum of 25 members.

name: Group Supply Of Goats And Sheep
brief_description:
In MaharashtraRs. group supply of goat and sheep refers to a collective approach taken by small-scale farmers to supply their livestock to larger markets. These farmers form groups or cooperatives to pool their resources and negotiate better prices for their goats and sheep.
Group supply is often used for the purpose of reducing costsRs. improving access to marketsRs. and promoting efficient utilization of resources. The species of goats and sheep commonly found in Maharashtra include JamunapariRs. BeetalRs. and SirohiRs. among others. Group supply of goats and sheep is an important aspect of the livestock industry in MaharashtraRs. contributing to both the economy and food security of the region.
The group supply system has several advantages for small-scale farmersRs. including reduced transportation costsRs. improved market accessRs. and increased bargaining power. By working togetherRs. farmers can also share knowledge and resourcesRs. such as veterinary services and animal feed.
OverallRs. group supply of goat and sheep is an important component of the agricultural economy in MaharashtraRs. supporting small-scale farmers and providing a valuable source of meat to consumers.
eligibility:
1. Beneficiary should belong to Scheduled Tribe.
2. Beneficiary should be below poverty line.

name: Development Of Playfield Under CMSGUY
brief_description:
The "Development of Playfield" Scheme is a Component under the Umbrella Scheme of "Chief Minister Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojna (CMSGUY)" by the Govt. of Assam. CMSGUY was launched by Hon'ble Chief Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on 5th February 2017 in Guwahati. The scheme is being implemented in a mega-mission mode across Assam. CMSGUY will be implemented through a saturation model by covering each revenue village through focused interventions in direct economic activitiesRs. logistic support including market linkagesRs. and community support.
The scheme "Development of Playfield" is an Infrastructure Development Scheme by the Assam Youth Development Mission Society (AYDMS) formed under Chief Minister Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojna (CMSGUY). AYDMS has decided to develop one playfield for the promotion of Games and Sports in the State through the Sports & Youth Welfare DepartmentRs. Govt. of Assam. It has been decided to develop 500 Football Playfields during 2017-18 in the first phase of operation of the scheme. It has been proposed to develop one football playground and playing facilities like Volleyball Courts having a dressing roomRs. store-cum-officeRs. and toilet facilities. A boundary wall will also be provided for the protection of the playground.
eligibility:
1. The SchoolsRs. CollegesRs. ClubsRs. and other Sports Organizations have playgrounds measuring a minimum of 120m in length x 90m in breadth that will be considered for development.
1. The SchoolsRs. CollegesRs. and Clubs having requisite suitable land in the area can apply in a prescribed format to take up the scheme for the up-gradation of their playgrounds.
1. The earth filling should be done with sandy and loamy soil.
1. The top surface of the playground should be made with sufficient sand filling and planting required grass.
1. The compaction of the playfield should be made with a light roller not exceeding 2 tons.
1. There must be sufficient space a minimum of 5m wide around the playfield for the movement of the playersRs. officialsRs. and spectators and for the construction of the dressing room.
1. The available playfield should be owned by either the local School/College AuthorityRs. Sports ClubRs. or Gaon Panchayat.
1. Playing facilities should be made available to the ChildrenRs. YouthRs. and Senior Citizens of the villages.

name: Scheme Of Provision Of Subsidized Rams To Sheep Breeders
brief_description:
The Department of Animal HusbandryRs. Government of Himachal Pradesh has introduced a scheme named "**Scheme of provision of subsidized Rams to Sheep Breeders**" to improve the Quality and Quantity of Wool being produced in the state. The scheme is open to all sheep breeders of the state who have a registered sheep unit. The subsidy is provided on a first-come-first-serve basisRs. and the number of rams provided under the scheme is limited. Rampur Bushari and Gaddi breeds of Himachal Pradesh are famous for indigenous carpet wool production in the Country. The total sheep population in the State is 8.05 lakh. As per normsRs. one breeding ram is required per 20-25 sheep. It is expected that a breedable population of approximately 3 lakh sheeps may require at least 12Rs. rams in the state.
**Aim of this scheme:**

1. provide High Genetic Merit breeding rams of Rambouillet and Russian Merino breeds and
1. after purchasing from Farms/progressive breeders of the state and neighboring States and
1. to provide these to sheep breeders at 60% subsidy.

**Objective of the scheme:**

1. To improve Quality and Quantity of Wool being produced in the stateRs. thereby ensuring better economic returns to the Sheep Breeders.
1. Genetic improvement of indigenous Sheep breeds and dissemination of Superior Germplasm amongst the migratory flocks of sheep in the state.
1. To resolve the problem of inbreeding amongst the migratory sheep flocks of Tribal Sheep Breeders.

**Key features:**

1. **Subsidized Rams:** The scheme provides rams of superior breeds at subsidized rates to eligible sheep breeders. 1. **Superior Breeds:** The rams provided under the scheme are of superior breeds such as MerinoRs. RambouilletRs. and Hampshire.
**Note:** This scheme is for all the sheep breeders who want to adopt modern and scientific methods of sheep breeding. By providing them with superior breed rams at subsidized ratesRs. the scheme aims to increase the productivity and profitability of sheep farming in the state.
benefits:
This Scheme of Provision of subsidized Rams to Sheep Breeders in Himachal Pradesh can benefit sheep breeders in the state by providing access to superior breed ramsRs. increasing productivity and profitabilityRs. and promoting the adoption of modern and scientific methods of sheep breeding. Under this schemeRs. Breeding Ram will be provided on 60% subsidy.
**Some of the key benefits of this scheme are:**

1. **Access to superior breed rams:** The scheme provides access to high-quality rams of superior breeds such as MerinoRs. RambouilletRs. and HampshireRs. which can improve the genetic potential of the sheep population and enhance their productivity. 1. **Affordable rates:** The rams are provided at subsidized ratesRs. which makes them more affordable for sheep breeders who may not have the financial resources to purchase them at market rates. 1. **Increased productivity:** By providing access to superior breed ramsRs. the scheme can increase the productivity of the sheep populationRs. which can lead to higher wool and meat yields. 1. **Improved profitability:** The scheme can lead to improved profitability for sheep breeders as higher productivity can result in higher revenues and reduced costs. 1. **Adoption of modern methods:** The scheme encourages sheep breeders to adopt modern and scientific methods of sheep breedingRs. which can result in more efficient and effective breeding practices. 1. **Employment generation:** The scheme can also generate employment opportunities in the sheep farming sectorRs. as increased productivity can lead to increased demand for labor in areas such as shearingRs. wool sortingRs. and meat processing.
eligibility:
The eligibility criteria for the Scheme may vary based on the specific guidelines and criteria set by the implementing agency of the scheme. HoweverRs. some of the general eligibility descriptions given as under:

1. A Sheep breeder of H.P. having a flock of at least 25 sheep will be considered for providing ram under this scheme.
1. One ram per 25 Sheep will be allotted. A maximum of two rams will be allotted to one beneficiary.
1. The beneficiary will have to sign an agreement that he will not sell and castrate the allotted ram during the breeding life of the ram.

name: Bal Sakha Yojana
brief_description:
1. The Bal Sakha Yojana is a community-based program that aims to provide support to children in need of care and protection. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Women and Child Development in collaboration with the NHM and the State Child Protection Society.
1. A network of trained volunteers called "Bal Sakhis" are deployed in villages and urban areas to identify and report cases of child abuseRs. neglectRs. and exploitation.
1. The Bal Sakhis also provide support to families in need of assistance to ensure the well-being of their children. The scheme also provides financial assistance to children in need of care and protection.
1. The scheme is targeted towards vulnerable children in the age group of 0-18 yearsRs. especially those from socially and economically disadvantaged backgrounds. The Bal Sakha Yojana aims to ensure the overall development and well-being of children by providing them with necessary support and protection.
benefits:
1. Under this schemeRs. expert care will be provided to newborn babies to ensure child health.
1. The paediatrician attends all eligible newborns at the place of birth and has to ensure their survival by providing early neonatal care including immunizations at birthRs. nutrition advice.
eligibility: - All newborns up to 30 days old belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families and Scheduled Caste categoriesRs. who do not pay income taxRs. will be eligible for benefits.

name: Breed Multiplication Farm Entrepreneurship
brief_description: It is proposed to make available a 50% capital subsidy (limited to Rs. 2.00 Crore) to the interested entrepreneur for the construction of cattle shedsRs. equipmentRs. procurement of elite bull mothers etc. The entrepreneur will establish a breed multiplication farm (BMF) and produce elite heifers using sexed semen or IVF technology. Disease-free heifers (free from at least TBRs. JD & Brucella) produced at the BMF will be sold to interested farmers and HGM bulls born at BMF will be procured by semen stations for semen productionRs. subject to qualifying Minimum Standards for production of frozen semen. BMF will also act as the training centre to conduct training for farmers and entrepreneurs. There is no system available in the country for producing disease-free elite animals of indigenous breeds of cattle and buffalo or exotic breeds of cattle. Therefore it is proposed to establish breed multiplication farms through an entrepreneurship model to make available disease-free high-yielding heifers/pregnant heifers /cows preferably of indigenous breeds of cattle/buffaloes in the country.
eligibility:
1. The applicant shall be an entrepreneur-aggregator /private individualRs. SHGs/FPOs/FCOs/ JLGs and Section 8 companies who have their registered offices in India.
1. Entrepreneur/applicant shall have appropriate experience in breeding or rearing dairy animals
1. The entrepreneur/applicant will be responsible for arranging land of suitable size and location. At least having ownership/lease deed of 5 acres of land.
1. The entrepreneur/applicant will make its own arrangement for the procurement of feed and fodder as per the requirement of the farm
1. The entrepreneur will establish a breed multiplication farm of at least 200 milch cows/buffalo and use the latest breeding technology to continuously upgrade the stock.

name: Bihar Startup Policy
brief_description: The government of Bihar is making continuous efforts to improve the economy. In this processRs. the Bihar government has started the Bihar Startup Policy. This policy is to boost entrepreneurship in the state of Bihar. The primary objective of this startup policy is to accelerate the growth of the MSMEs sector in Bihar.
benefits:
1. Bihars startup policy was launched in Bihar in the month August 2022 to boost entrepreneurship in the state.
1. Young Bihar entrepreneurs would get a loan of 10 lacks without interest for ten years. This sum will be allocated as seed money under the Bihar Startup Policy.
1. Enhanced incentives of 5 per cent for female entrepreneursRs. in addition to a grant of 3 lakh rupees for businesses that participate in rigorous training for product improvement and finance.
1. In addition to shared office spaceRs. there are financial incentives and other amenities available.
1. Created a startup platform for young business people in the state of Bihar who is interested in taking advantage of the policies and programs available to them.
eligibility:
1. Up to a period of ten years from the date of incorporation/ registrationRs. if it is incorporated as a private limited company (as defined in the Companies ActRs. 2013) or registered as a partnership firm (registered under section 59 of the Partnership ActRs. 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership ActRs. 2008).
1. Turnover of the entity for any of the financial years since incorporation/ registration has not exceeded one hundred crore rupees.
1. The entity is working towards innovationRs. development or improvement of products or processes or servicesRs. or it is a scalable business model with a high potential for employment generation or wealth creation.
1. Provided that an entity formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business shall not be considered a Start-up.
1. Provided Start-up must be incorporated or registered in Bihar and have an office in Bihar.
1. Provided further applicable taxes from the operations of the company are payable in Bihar.

name: Financial Assistance To Institutions/Societies Belonging To Scheduled Castes/Backward Classes
brief_description:
The scheme Financial Assistance to Institutions/Societies Belonging to Scheduled Castes/Backward Classes was launched by the Department of Welfare of Scheduled Castes & Backward ClassesRs. Government of Haryana. The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the institutions/societies of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes to enable them to construct/complete/repair/renovate buildings that can be used for community social or educational purposes etc. of Scheduled Castes / Backward Classes and provide basic facilities and equipment in these buildings.
**Definitions:**

- Financial Assistance means the amount sanctioned /released out of Government funds to supplement public efforts for development.
- Competent Authority means the DirectorRs. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes DepartmentRs. Haryana.

**Purpose of Financial Assistance:** In addition to the purposes mentioned in the objectRs. the Financial Assistance may also be sanctioned for any one of the following purposes:-

- For completionRs. repairRs. or construction of community building/institutions which used or are to be used for educational and social purposes.
- For the construction of recreation centers/halls in the above-said buildings institutional for setting up of libraries in the institutions.
- For purchase of T.V./listening setsRs. educational equipmentRs. etc. for use in the institutions.
- Priority for grant of funds will be given for completion/ repair/new construction in that order.
benefits:
1. Financial Assistance up to 2.00 lakhs may be sanctioned by the Minister in chargeRs. Welfare of Scheduled Castes/Backward Classes.
1. The Chief Minister may sanction grants exceeding 2.00 lakhs in genuine cases.
1. In deserving casesRs. additional funds can also be sanctioned later on for construction/completion/ repair/ renovation of the infrastructure or for providing basic amenities in the buildingRs. or for any other purpose.

**Note 01:** Financial Assistance will be sanctioned only for the work to be executed within Haryana State.
**Note 02:** The grant will be utilized for the purpose for which it is sanctioned and not for any other purpose within one year of the date of receipt of the grant. Unspent balanceRs. if anyRs. should have to be returned to the competent authority. In case of defaultRs. the amount will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
**Note 03:** The institutions shall incur the expenditure out of this grant in the most economical manner.
**Note 04:** Any institution/society found guilty of non-fulfillment of the conditions shall be debarred from being considered for release of Government grant for a minimum period of three years or more as may be decided by the competent authority.
eligibility:
1. Only those institutions/ societies of Scheduled Castes/ Backward classes registered under the Societies Registration ActRs. 1860Rs. or the Indian Trust Act would be eligible for grant-in-aid.
1. The society/ institution should have at least 100 sq yards of its own land or allotted /donated to it by the Govt./ Panchayat/ Local Body/ any individual etc.
1. Second-time grants to the same institution will be given after only five years if all the UCs for the grants released earlier have been submitted to the District Welfare officer.

**Note 01:** The institution/ society will maintain separate accounts for the grant which shall be open for inspection by the DirectorRs. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes DepartmentRs. Haryana/concerned District Welfare OfficerRs. or any other officer deputed by the competent authority.
**Note 02:** Utilization certificate duly signed by the Head of the institution/ society dully verified by the Chartered Accountant will be furnished to the District Welfare OfficerRs. who after spot inspection will forward the same to the DirectorRs. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward ClassesRs. Haryana with his comments for record.
**Note 03:** The guarantee will have to furnish an indemnity bond in the prescribed format (ANNEXURE B) to the Govt. binding itself to fulfill all the conditions attached to the grant and to refund the amount of the grant already paid in the event of non-fulfillment of the aim to abide by the decision of the authority releasing grant-in-aid.

name: Sastraposhini Scheme
brief_description:
Sastraposhini is a programme envisaged by the Kerala State Council for ScienceRs. Technology and Environment (KSCSTE) for strengthening science education in schools of Kerala. Under the programmeRs. model science laboratories are established in selected Government high schools of the State to provide a better learning environment. The programme was launched by KSCSTE in association with the Department of EducationRs. Government of Kerala in the year 2003. So farRs. KSCSTE has successfully established more than 200 science laboratories throughout Kerala. PresentlyRs. KSCSTE has decided to implement the scheme only in government high schools of Kerala.
**The objectives of the Programme are:**

- To stimulate interest in science at the school level by the performance of experiments in PhysicsRs. Chemistry and Biology by students.
- To provide hands-on experiments to students for observationRs. inferenceRs. interaction and self-designing of experiments.
- To organize training programmes for the teachers to demonstrate scientific experiments.
- To evolve a low-cost laboratory kit based on readily available material for the performing of a range of experiments.
benefits:
1. A total of 8 lakhs is spent to establish Sastraposhini laboratories (PhysicsRs. ChemistryRs. and Biology) in one school with a fair share from KSCSTE.
1. Training will be provided to selected teachers from Sastraposhini schools by eminent scholars/ academicians from different disciplines.
1. Laboratory manuals and visual experimental aids and models will be provided to the selected schools.
1. Training programme for teachers:


- Two teachers each in PhysicsRs. ChemistryRs. and Biology from Sastraposhini schools are invited to participate in a training programme. The trained teachers will be in charge of each laboratory.
- Scientists/academicians offer classes on creating science awarenessRs. good laboratory practicesRs. setting up of laboratoriesRs. and practical demonstrations. Based on the training receivedRs. the teachers will be encouraged to carry out innovative projects in science for children utilizing the facilities of Sastraposhini laboratories.
eligibility:
1. Only government high schools in the State with sufficient facilities (three rooms to establish PhysicsRs. ChemistryRs. and Biology laboratories)Rs. and qualified faculty in science are eligible.
1. The schools applying for the scheme shall have the following basic requirements:


- Sufficient space to establish Sastraposhini laboratories (separate rooms for physicsRs. chemistryRs. and biology laboratories).
- Qualified teachers in three subject areas (physicsRs. chemistryRs. and biology).
- Sufficient number of students in the high school section.
- Extend of administrative support from the Headmaster/Principal/Management for the smooth implementation of the scheme.

name: Industry Linked Biotechnology Research Scheme
brief_description:
The Scheme Industry Linked Biotechnology Research Scheme (IBRS) facilitates Academia-Industry interaction by undertaking projects in collaboration with an industrial partner which should result in commercializing the product or process or service. Kerala Biotechnology Commission (KBC) under the Kerala State Council for ScienceRs. Technology and Environment (KSCSTE) provides project mode support to facilitate Academia-Industry interaction. The project proposals should be result-oriented with an eye on commercializing the product or process or service that would result from it.
The scheme is to provide financial assistance in the form of grants to Scientists and Technologists of R&D Centers/academic Institutions/Organizations actively involved in biotechnological research with emphasis on areas relating to marineRs. agricultureRs. healthRs. and environment. The proposals need to be submitted with active collaboration with an industry in which the industrial partner is willing to share 25% of the KBC allocated funds additionally.
benefits:
1. Financial assistance in the form of a grant of 40 lakhs excluding overhead cost and industry share (25%) for a period of three years shall be provided to Scientists and Technologists of R&D Centers/academic Institutions/Organizations actively involved in biotechnological research with emphasis on areas relating to marineRs. agricultureRs. health and environment.
1. In additionRs. the host institution will be eligible for an overhead @ 10% of total expenditure subject to a ceiling of 2 lakh.

**Note:** Under the schemeRs. the industrial collaborator who is willing to share 25% of funds additionallyRs. a clear statement needs to be submitted along with an endorsement from the Head of the organization and should clearly mention the extent of financial support and break-up of the budget.
eligibility:
1. The applicants should be the Scientists and Technologists of R&D Centers/Academic Institutions/Organizations actively involved in biotechnological research with emphasis on areas relating to marineRs. agricultureRs. healthRs. and environment.
1. The proposals need to be submitted in active collaboration with an industry in which the industrial partner is willing to share 25% of the Kerala Biotechnology Commission allocated funds additionally.

name: Scheme to Provide Special Financial Assistance for Organizing Cultural Events
brief_description:
"Scheme to Provide Special Financial Assistance for Organizing Cultural Events" is a Grant-In-Aid to the NGOs designed to provide financial support to institutionsRs. cultural groups and individuals to organize/conduct various types of Cultural Events/Programmes/ Exhibitions/Festivals/Workshops. This scheme intends to give opportunity to young Goan artists to develop their talentsRs. so also to give opportunity to the artists as well as the general public to witness various standard cultural performances/Events/Exhibitions/Festivals/ Workshops.
> **Objectives** 1. To encourage Cultural Events/Programmes/Exhibitions/Festivals/Camps/Workshops. 1. To give financial support to cultural groups or individuals to organize cultural events. 1. To give opportunity to young Goan artists to develop their talent.
benefits:
1. Financial grant maximum upto ** 5Rs. or 80% of the expenditure** incurred for organizing the cultural eventsRs. whichever is lessRs. based on the nature of the cultural events. 1. HoweverRs. in the case where the Directorate of Art & Culture suo-moto identifies any institution or group or individual person to organize any Cultural Event/Programme/Exhibition/Festival/Camp & Workshop for the Department of Art & Culture then the grant a maximum upto ** 5Rs. or 100% of the expenditure** incurred for organizing the eventRs. whichever is less shall be granted for this purpose.
[**NOTE:** The applicant shall get the financial grant to the extent decided by the Department of Art & Culture/ Government based on the nature and scope of the proposed cultural event and the reputationRs. standing and eligibility of the applicant.]
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be an individual or a cultural group/organization/institutionRs. registered or unregistered. 1. The applicant should have experience organizing cultural events/programmes/ exhibitions/festivals. 1. The applicant should not be a defaulter of the Directorate of Art & Culture for non-submission of utilization certificate or statement of accounts for any other grant received by the applicant. **NOTE:** The Directorate of Art & CultureRs. may also suo-moto identify any institution/cultural group or individual person to organize any Cultural Event/Programme/Exhibitions/Festival/Camp/Workshop for the Department of Art & Culture.
> **Reservation / Preference / Priority** Preference will be given to registered institutions/organizations.

name: Scheme to Provide Grant in Aid to Cultural Organization (Maintenance/ Regular Grants)
brief_description:
"Scheme to Provide Grant in Aid to Cultural Organization (Maintenance/ Regular Grants)" by the Directorate of Art and CultureRs. Government of GoaRs. aims to provide financial support to voluntary Cultural Organizations in order to promote cultural activities and to create and develop cultural talent in the State of Goa.
> **Objectives** 1. To create and develop cultural talent. 1. To provide financial support to cultural organizations. 1. To create and develop a cultural environment in the State of Goa. 1. To purchase musical equipment.
benefits:
**Grant-In-Aid in the form of reimbursement to the extent of 80% of the expenditure** incurred by the institution for the last financial yearRs. subject to the maximum ceiling given below -
- 10Rs./- for Group HRs. - 20Rs./- for Group G - 35Rs./- for Group F - 50Rs./- for Group E - 75Rs./- for Group D - 1Rs. for Group C - 2Rs. for Group B - 3Rs. for Group A
**NOTE 1:** The institution shall bourne all the expenditure and conduct its activities from its own funds for the first year. **NOTE 2:** The applicant shall get the financial grant to the extent decided by the Department of Art & Culture based on the nature and scope of the cultural activities conducted by the institution.
eligibility:
Any Goan institution registered under the Societys Registration ActRs. 1860 or under the Indian Trust Act.
> **Reservation / Preference / Priority** Preference will be given to the institutions involved in Cultural Education i.e. imparting training in musicRs. danceRs. dramaRs. fine art etc.

name: Scheme for Interest Subvention to Nano Household Enterprises
brief_description:
The scheme Scheme for Interest Subvention to Nano Household Enterprises has been introduced to promote the Nano and household enterprises in the state. The scheme intends to provide financial assistance in the form of interest subvention to Nano and household enterprises on a reimbursement basis for the term loan availed by the unit. The units engaged in manufacturingRs. services as well and job work can apply under the scheme.
> **Objectives:**


1. To generate employment opportunities in households through new self-employment projects (Nano/Household units)
1. To aggregate household/Nano units 85 increase the extent of potential employment.
1. To provide continuous and sustainable employment and increase the wage earning capacity of unorganized /household/units.
1. To address specific issues not covered under similar schemes of the Government of India/Government of Kerala.
1. The new scheme for providing financial assistance to Nano and household units is to support units with a capital investment of 10 Lakhs or less for manufacturing units engaged in job work and units engaged in service sector activities having any type of value addition in physical form by using machinery or equipment. The assistance is by way of interest subvention on the term loan availed for a period of three years on a reimbursement basis.
1. The assistance is provided for the first three years after the units are set up. In the first year assistance is given without considering prompt repayment. During the 2nd and 3rd year interest subvention is accorded if the loan is not classified by the bank as NPA. Thus it is a big relief in the early stages of business.
1. The unit will be monitored for financial health and symptoms of sickness can be found out well on time.
1. The units engaged in job work were hitherto not eligible for any sort of financial assistance other than under PMEGP.

> **Indicative List of Service Activities**: The list which is given below is indicative; not exhaustive. Similar activities in the service sector having any type of value addition which is recommended by the District Level Committee will be also eligible.


1. ProcessingRs. Preserving & packaging of Meat & Fish.
1. Processing and preserving of fruits and vegetables.
1. Embroidery work and other ornamental trimmings.
1. Metal-working service activities & repair of fabricated metal products.
1. Repair & Services of Computers & peripheral equipmentRs. projectorsRs. Mobile phonesRs. TVsRs. A/CRs. Video CamerasRs. Watches. ClocksRs. other electronic equipment & other household equipment.
1. Electrical Welding & Soldering
1. Laundry Services / Dry cleaning.
1. Photo copying
1. Repair and servicing and alteration of Motor Vehicles and related parts and accessories.
1. Tyre re-treading
1. Upholstery work
1. Repair & maintenance of boatsRs. fishing boatsRs. vessels and other floating structures.
1. Repair & maintenance of structural products
1. Repair & maintenance of pipes & pipelines
1. Repair & maintenance of metal tanksRs. reservoirs etc.
1. Repair of machinery enginesRs. pumps and related equipment.
1. Treatment & disposal of waste of all kinds.
1. Other information service activities
1. Recycling
1. Workshop

> **Negative List:**

Photo Studios and Colour Processing CentresRs. Breweries and Distilleries of all typesRs. SawmillsRs. Soap Grade Sodium SilicateRs. Asbestos processing except units in which the quantum of asbestos used in the production process is less than 25% and environmental and occupational health hazards have been taken care of the satisfaction of authorities concernedRs. Metal Crushers including Granite Manufacturing unitsRs. All types of Steel Re-rolling MillsRs. Units manufacturing iron ingotsRs. Calcium CarbideRs. Cement manufacturing except units manufacturing cement from fly ashRs. Potassium ChlorateRs. Cashew industrial unitsRs. Power intensive units based on electro-thermal/electrochemical processor units where total power requirement exceeds 5000 KVA of contract load or where the cost of power is more than 33% of cost of production of the items manufacture except where the units generate their power requirement in excess of 5000 KVA of contract load by own captive power.
benefits:
1. The unit will be eligible for interest subvention to an extent of 6% per annum for the term loan availed by the unit on a reimbursement basis for three years.
2. For women and SC/ST enterprisesRs. the interest subvention will be 8% for three years.
3. The assistance shall be limited to the fixed percentage of the composite investment upon
(a) plant & machineryRs.
(b) other fixed assets including essential office equipment and
(c) Electrification cost of Land and Building shall not be included in the Fixed Capital Investment under this scheme.
**Note:** In the event of default on repayment of the loan with interest at the end of 1st yearRs. the subvention will not be passed. The same is applicable for 2nd and 3rd years.
eligibility:
A unit/enterprise which satisfies the following conditions is eligible for the scheme:
1. The fixed capital investment is 10 lakh or less.
2. Engaged in manufacturingRs. servicesRs. or job work.
3. In the white and the green category as per pollution control norms.
4. Connected load is 5 HP or less.
> **Obligations of the applicant entrepreneurs:**

1. The applicant shall provide all required details and declare such information as to be true.
2. The applicant shall provide clarifications of further details sought by the recommending/sanctioning authority.
3. The applicant shall allow inspection or verification of any details mentioned in the application including plant and machinery and all other assets if so required by recommending/sanctioning authority.
4. The applicant shall produce originals of any important documents if so required by the Recommending/ sanctioning Authority for verification.

name: Revival and Rehabilitation Scheme for Defunct MSMEs and Cashew Processing Units
brief_description:
Introduction:
The trend in increasing number of defunct units is a challenge to the secondary sector. The MSMEs which have become defunct due to genuine issues in the value chain and have potential needs to be revived and rehabilitated considering the role of these units play in the state economyRs. the Government of Kerala launched a new scheme for defunct MSMEs including cashew processing units during 2020-21.
Besides the lack of improved technologyRs. MSME units become defunct due to constraints on marketingRs. competition from MNCs and global challenges etc. In the field of cashew units the processing cost is comparatively higher in the state and competition from other countries is badly high. Most of the cashew units are in financial crunches. Process mechanization is the only way to revive the units.
> **Objective:**

The scheme envisages supporting defunct MSMEs in the manufacturing sector including cashew processing units through assistance in the form of capital grants and working capital incentives.
> **Definitions:**

**Defunct MSMEs:** MSMEs which are non-operational for 6 months or more but can be revivable. In the case of units which become defunct due to the plastic ban and those who wish for diversificationRs. the above time limit is not applicable.
**Defunct Cashew Processing Units:** The Cashew Processing Units which were defunct at least for six months/no matter whether they have received any Government assistance or bank loan within six months and are in the process of revival.
benefits:
1. Entitlement in the scheme shall be limited to 15 Lakhs per applicant unit and it can avail only once.
2. Financial Assistance under the scheme provided for the following components-
a) Building Renovation - 25% of the total revival project cost limited to 2 lakh:
i) Building Renovation includes maintenance and repair of existing factory buildingsRs. construction of fresh
roofing in the factory shedRs. infrastructure for Waste Disposal / Treatment facilities etc.
b) Plant & Machinery and Electrification - 40% of the total revival project cot limited to 8 lakh:
i) It will be available for the purchase of new machineryRs. Repair and Maintenance of Existing machinesRs.
industrial electrification etc.
c) Working Capital (Margin) - 50% margin of working Capital loan approved by financial institution subject to
i) Assistance is limited to 2 lakhs for defunct MSMEs.
ii) Assistance is limited to 5 lakhs for Cashew Units.
d) Maximum Limit 12 lakhs for defunct MSMEs per unit.
e) Maximum Limit 15 lakhs for defunct cashew processing per unit.
**Note 01:** Bank Sanction of fresh working capital loan is mandatory for availing Working Capital (Margin) AssistanceRs. but a bank loan is not mandatory for assistance for building renovationRs. plant and machineryRs. electrification etc.
**Note 02:** The assistance under the scheme shall be released to the eligible entrepreneur by the bank on a pro-rata basis.
eligibility:
1. All MSMEs in the manufacturing sector which are defunct for at least 6 months due to genuine issues including cashew processing enterprises that have the potential to be revived and rehabilitatedRs. are eligible for assistance under the scheme.

> **Obligations of the Applicant Entrepreneurs:**


1. The applicant shall provide all required details and declare such information as to be true.
1. The applicant shall provide clarifications or further details sought by the recommending/ sanctioning authority.
1. The applicant shall allow inspection or verification of any details mentioned in the application including plant and machinery and all other assets if so required by recommending/ sanctioning authority.
1. The applicant shall produce originals of any important documents if so required by the recommending/ sanctioning authority for verification.
1. The applicant shall execute the requisite legal agreement on Stamp paper worth 200 as and when the proposal is approved for implementation and furnishes the signed hard copy to General ManagerRs. District Industries Centre.
1. The applicant shall utilize the amount received only in the manner agreed upon as per the revival project submitted.
1. The applicant shall operate the unit as stipulated in the agreement in which the quantum of support receivedRs. failing which the assistance shall be resumed by restoring the provisions of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act.

name: Kerala Stressed MSMEs Revival & Rehabilitation Scheme
brief_description:
The Kerala Stressed MSMEs Revival & Rehabilitation Scheme intends to provide financial and other handholding support to the MSMEs which show signs of stress and to convert their non-productive assets into productive assets. This scheme aims to revive microRs. small and medium manufacturing enterprises in Kerala that suffer due to stressed assets. The maximum assistance admissible for each unitRs. all reliefs and assistances put togetherRs. under the scheme will be limited to 5 Lakh.
> **Stressed MSME:** As per the Notification of the Reserve Bank of IndiaRs. an MSME can be treated as stressed if:-

a) Principal or interest payment not overdue for more than 30 days but account showing signs of incipient stress.
b) Principal or interest payment overdue between 31 - 60 days.
c) Principal or Interest payment overdue between 61 -91 days
**Note:** The above condition may vary in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India from time to time.
> **Sick Unit:** An MSME should be considered sick if-

a) Any of the borrower accounts of the unit remains substandard for more than six months i.e. principal or interest in respect of any of its borrower accounts has remained overdue for a period exceeding one year or more. The requirement of an overdue period of one year or more will remain unchanged even if the period for classification of an account as sub-standardRs. is reduced in due course; Or
b) There is erosion in the net worth of the unitRs. which is to the extent of 50% of its net worth due to accumulated cash losses during the previous accounting year; And
c) The unit has been in commercial production for at least two years for closed units and one year for working units.
> **Closed Unit:**

An MSME is referred to as a closed unitRs. if the unit has been in commercial production for at least two years before its closureRs. and it has remained closed continuously for a period of 6 months. This must be supported with ample proof such as electricity disconnection due to closure or the prescribed return of commercial tax for this period has been nil or any other reason as the expert committee may deem fit.
> **Potentially Viable sick unit:**

A sick unit can be considered as Potentially Viable if it is in a positionRs. after implementing a relief package spread over a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of the package from banksRs. financial institutionsRs. Government (Central/State) and other agencies concernedRs. as may be necessaryRs. to continue to service its repayment obligations as agreed upon including those forming part of the package without the help of concessions after the aforesaid period.
> **Negative List:** List of units which are ineligible for any financial assistance/loan/exemption/subsidy from the state Government.

1. Photo Studios and Colour Processing Centres
2. Breweries and Distilleries of all types
3. Sawmills
4. Soap Grade Sodium Silicate
5. Asbestos processing except for units in respect of which the quantum of asbestos used in the production process is less than 25% and environmental and occupational health hazards have been taken care of to the satisfaction of authorities concerned.
6. Metal Crushers including Granite Manufacturing units.
7. All types of Steel Re-rolling mills and units manufacturing iron ingots.
8. Calcium Carbide
9. Cement manufacturing except units manufacturing cement from fly ash
10. Potassium Chlorate
11. Cashew industrial units
12. Power-intensive units based on electrothermal/electrochemical Processor units where total power requirement exceeds 5000 KVA of contract load or where the cost of power is more than 33% of the cost of production of the items manufactured except where the units generate their power requirement in excess of 5000 KVA of contract load by own captive power.
**Note:** The Negative list may be amended from time to time.
benefits:
1. Entitlement in the scheme shall be limited to an amount of 5 lakhs per applicant unit to be availed as one-time assistance only.
2. Assistance/Relief Available from Government:
a) **Restructuring of existing loan account:** If the bank is willing to restructure the existing loan account and extend additional term loan/working capital loan based on the Revival Project recommendations of the Expert CommitteeRs. the unit is eligible for the following one-time Assistance. These assistances are also eligible for self-financed units availing term loan/working capital loan as part of the Revival Package recommended by the Expert Committee.

- **Margin Money Grant:** 50% of the margin insisted by the bank/Financial Institution towards additional working capital loan and term loanRs. will be payable as Grant Assistance limited to 2 lakhs. - **Interest Subvention Assistance:** To provide financial assistance in the form of interest subvention on a reimbursement basis for the additional term loan and additional working capital loan availed by the units based on the Revival Project Report recommended by the expert committee. The interest subvention is 6% per annum subject to a maximum amount of 1 lakh. The interest subvention is limited to one (first) year on the loan sanctioned by the financial institution/bank.
b) **Restart Expenses:** The following one-time assistance shall be payable as restart expenses based on the Revival Project recommendations of the Expert Committee.

- In cases where no term loan is availed for the purchase of brand new additional/balancing plant & machineryRs. 50% of the cost of Additional/Balancing Plant and Machinery limited to 1.50 lakhs will be payable as one-time assistance.
- 50% of the cost incurred for the inevitable repair and maintenance of the existing Plant and Machinery and Building limited to 1.00 lakh will be reimbursed.

c) **Clearance of Statutory Dues:** If there are statutory dues existing for the unit related to the agencies like KSEBRs. GST/Commercial TaxRs. ExciseRs. Pollution Control BoardRs. etc. 50% of the dues limited to 40Rs. shall be payable as one-time assistance based on the Revival Project recommendations of the Expert Committee.
d) **Cost of Revival Project Report:**

- Cost of preparation of RPR will be reimbursed @100%Rs. 10Rs./- per unit.
- The maximum assistance admissible for each unitRs. all reliefs and assistances put togetherRs. under the scheme will be limited to 5 Lakhs.
eligibility:
1. A MSME unit/enterprise which satisfies the following conditions is eligible for the scheme:

- MSME in the manufacturing category and set up in Kerala state.
- Does not come under the Negative List.
- Must have filed EM Part-II/UAM.
- Must come under the definition of Sick Unit and
- Must be Potentially Viable to be revived or restructured based on a definite Revival Project Report.

2. For the purpose of this schemeRs. an industrial unit eligible for the assistance shall be an independent legal entity.
> **Obligation of the applicant unit:**

1. The applicant unit shall provide all required details in time and declare such information as to be true.
2. The applicant unit shall provide clarification if any sought by vyavasaya mithra.
3. The applicant unit shall utilize the amount received as assistance only in the manner agreed upon.
4. The applicant units thus revived shall restart within one month of the date of receipt of financial assistance and shall be under obligation to function continuously for a further period of 5 years. OtherwiseRs. the assistance given shall be recovered under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act.
5. Units becoming sick on account of willful mismanagementRs. willful defaultRs. unauthorized diversion of fundsRs. dispute among Partners/PromotersRs. etc. should not be considered for rehabilitation.

name: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Reimbursement Scheme
brief_description: The scheme Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Reimbursement Scheme is a scheme by the Department of Information TechnologyRs. Electronics and CommunicationsRs. Government of GoaRs. for the Startups of Goa. The scheme is a part of the Start-up Policy 2017. The objective of the policy is to make Goa an aspirational geographical and human resource base for startups. The objective is to invite the best entrepreneurial minds and build a robust start-up ecosystem in the State. The policy contains various incentives for Start-ups and to avail the benefits of these incentivesRs. the government has proposed many schemes under the policy.
benefits:
1. For start-ups registering national and international IPRs. the Start-up Promotion Cell will **reimburse up to 50% of the cost incurred by the start-up in fees and all other costs associated with IP application**Rs. if the IP is registered successfullyRs. subject to a cap of 2Rs. for national IP and 5Rs. for international IP.1. This benefit can be availed by a maximum of 200 startups each year. 1. Once the application is approved by the SPCRs. the approved amount shall be disbursed within 60 days from the date of approval.
**NOTE 1:** Under no circumstance shall the benefits under this scheme be considered an entitlement. The SPC shall reserve the sole right to accept or reject applications. **NOTE 2:** The reimbursement amount will be released/ disbursed on the seniority basis/ SPC recommendation depending upon the budget allotment of the State Government. **NOTE 3:** The reimbursement will be in the nature of a **one-time payment** and the applicant cannot apply under this provision more than once for the same IP application.
eligibility:
1. All the Start-ups certified by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC) having a valid start-up certificate number are eligible.
1. IP created for a technology-based service or product or uses technology for enhancing functionality or reach of an existing product or service is eligible.
1. The applicant should have already filed or been granted an IP with the concerned authority.
1. The applicant should have paid the mandatory government fees and attorney fees in this regard.
1. Only expenditures incurred after notification of Goa Start-up Policy 2017 within the validity of this policy and paid for digitally would be considered.

**NOTE:** If the applicant has applied for the reimbursement benefits/ grant for the same IP in any other scheme of the Centre or other State GovernmentRs. then the application will be rejected.

name: Matching Grant Scheme
brief_description: The scheme Matching Grant Scheme is a scheme by the Department of Information TechnologyRs. Electronics and CommunicationsRs. Government of GoaRs. for the Startups of Goa. The scheme is a part of the Start-up Policy 2017. The Start-ups that raise funds from a registered/recognized funding source prior to the product launch phase will be provided 25% of the matching funds or a maximum benefit of 25Rs. at proportionate ownership of stockRs. subsequent to due diligence by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC).
benefits:
1. Start-ups that raise funds from a registered/recognized funding source prior to the product launch phase will be provided 25% of the matching funds or a maximum benefit of 25Rs. at proportionate ownership of stockRs. subsequent to due diligence by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC).
1. This benefit can be availed by 20 start-ups each year which shall be selected by the SPC as per its due diligence and guidelines.
1. Once the application is approved by the SPCRs. the approved amount shall be disbursed within 60 days from the date of approval.

**NOTE:** Under no circumstance shall the benefits under this scheme be considered an entitlement. The SPC shall reserve the sole right to accept or reject applications.
eligibility:
1. All the Start-ups certified by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC) having a valid start-up certificate number are eligible.
1. The product for which the benefit is being claimed should not have been made available in the market previously.

**NOTE:** Only expenditures incurred after notification of Goa Start-up Policy 2017Rs. being within the validity of this policy and paid for digitally will be considered for reimbursement under this scheme. If digital payments are not possible then it shall be up to the decision of SPC as per its due diligence to admit the expenditure.

name: PRISM (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs): Category-1: Proof of Concept/ Prototypes/ Models
brief_description:
The scheme "PRISM (Promoting Innovations in IndividualsRs. Start-ups and MSMEs)" by the Department of Scientific and Industrial ResearchRs. Ministry of Science and TechnologyRs. aims to support individual innovators which will enable them to achieve the agenda of inclusive development - one of the thrust areas of XIIth five year plan (2012-2017). Thrust Areas: The proposals shall preferably be considered in the following focus sectors: Green technologyRs. Clean energyRs. Industrially utilizable smart materialsRs. Waste to WealthRs. name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
brief_description: "Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu)Rs. Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region" by the Rubber BoardRs. Department of CommerceRs. Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Accelerated new planting/replanting would be achieved by giving proper technical guidance and financial assistance to growers.
benefits:
##### **Rate of Subsidy**
> **Traditional Region** 1. **General Category:** 20Rs./- ha + 5Rs. /ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. The assistance will be @ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha.1. **SC Category:** 35000/- ha + 5Rs. /ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. The assistance will be @ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha.
> **Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region** 1. 35Rs. per ha and 5Rs./ ha for planting material (Polybag/ Root trainer plants) of advanced growth. 1. The assistance will be @ 10/- per plant limited to 500 plants per ha. ##### **Mode of Payment** 1. Planting subsidy shall be paid in single instalments subject to the completion of the stipulated items of work to the satisfaction of the Board. 1. Payment of subsidy shall be only through bank by e-transfer. Beneficiaries should provide Aadhar-linked bank account details in the application for financial assistance.
eligibility:

The planting grant payable will be limited to an area of 1.00 ha. 1. The growers who undertake new planting/replanting rubber in a minimum area of 0.10 ha will be eligible for assistance. 1.
