name: Incentives to Encourage Consumption of Local Raw Material Scheme, 2008
brief_description: Launched in 2008Rs. the scheme "Incentives to Encourage Consumption of Local Raw Material SchemeRs. 2008" by the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and CommerceRs. Government of Goa aimed to encourage the consumption of local raw materialsRs. thereby supporting units manufacturing such materials and promoting the economies of villages supplying or producing these raw materialsRs. including those in horticultureRs. food processingRs. and cluster businesses. The scheme provided financial incentives such as reimbursement of up to 90% of Sales Tax paid and a 25% subsidy on power and water billsRs. subject to certain conditions. Eligible units included MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under the green and specified orange categoriesRs. which consumed a minimum of 50% local raw materials. The scheme was implemented by the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and CommerceRs. Government of Goa. The scheme remained in force until 31st MarchRs. 2011.
benefits:
- Reimbursement to the extent of a maximum of 90% of Sales Tax paid by such unitRs. subject to the quantum based on the proportion of local raw material consumed.
- Incentives in the form of a subsidy on power and water bills annually.
- 25% subsidy on the total expenditure incurred by the unit on power and water tariffsRs. subject to a maximum of 2Rs./- per annumRs. as per the proportion of local raw material consumed.
eligibility:
- The Scheme covered units that went into production on or after 6th August 2008.
- Only those units under green and specified orange categories were eligible under this Scheme.
- Only those units which were permanently registered with the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and Commerce or cleared by the High Powered Co-ordination Committee (HPCC) or any Committee or authority formed to grant such clearance for investment in the State were eligible under this Scheme.
- This Scheme was applicable only to Micro and Small Enterprises and Medium Scale Enterprises as defined under the MSMED Act.
- The unit consuming a minimum of 50% of its raw material (in value) from local sources was eligible for the benefit on pro-rata terms with those consuming 60% and aboveRs. which were considered for 100% benefit under this Scheme.


- For the purpose of this SchemeRs. the local raw material meant:

**(a)** MaterialRs. which was manufactured in an approved industrial unit (Micro and Small EnterprisesRs. MediumRs. Large Unit) in the State of Goa.
**(b)** MaterialRs. which was mined or produced in the State of Goa (for exampleRs. agricultural produceRs. marine produceRs. mineral and oreRs. etc.).

- The beneficiary had to proveRs. by submitting documentary evidenceRs. that the material had been locally produced or mined. In case of any dispute in interpreting the meaning of clauses (a) and (b) aboveRs. the decision/interpretation of the DirectorRs. Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and Commerce was final and binding.

name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
brief_description:
The "Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry" is a component under the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and PoultryRs. part of the National Livestock Mission (NLM). This initiative is introduced by the Department of Animal Husbandry and DairyingRs. under the Ministry of FisheriesRs. Animal Husbandry and DairyingRs. Government of India. Under this schemeRs. the Entrepreneurship will be developed by inviting the individualRs. Self Help Group (SHG)/Framers Producer Organizations (FPO)/Farmers Cooperatives (FCOs)/Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) and Section 8 companies for establishment of Parent FarmRs. Rural HatcheryRs. brooder cum mother unit for Production of Hatching EggsRs. and Chicks and rearing of the said chick upto four weeks in the mother unit. Emphasis will be given to those entrepreneurs who will be able to establish forward and backward linkage (Hub and Spoke). The scheme is implemented by State Implementing Agency and Department of Animal Husbandry and DairyingRs. Government of India.
**Objectives:**

- Bringing unorganized rural poultry farming into the organized sector.
- Promoting entrepreneurship in rural poultry farming sustainably.
- Establishing forward and backward linkages.
- Popularizing non-conventionalRs. low-cost feeding alternatives.
benefits:
***Financial Assistance:***

- One Time 50% capital subsidy of the total project cost will be provided with maximum subsidy up to 25 lakhs for each unit.

**Note 1:** The Central Government will provide 50% capital subsidy for the cost of the project for establishment of Parent FarmRs. Rural hatchery and Mother Unit with minimum 1000 parent layers.
**Note 2:** Subsidy will be the capital subsidy and provided in two equal instalments. First instalment will be released upfront to the scheduled bank or financial institutions like NCDC etc. by SIDBI to be credited to the Entrepreneur/ Eligible Entities account after the bank or financial institution releases First Instalment of loan to the beneficiary and its confirmation by State Implementing Agency.
**Note 3:** Beneficiaries will be eligible for release of the second instalment by SIDBI after completion of the project and certified so by the State Implementing Agency.
**Note 4:** In case of the self-financing projectRs. the project needs to be appraised by the bank where the Entrepreneurs/Eligible Entity have account. The first instalment of 50% subsidy will be provided into the lending bank by SIDBI where the beneficiary has account. The subsidy will be released only when the beneficiary has made expenditure of 25% cost for the project towards infrastructure and has been verified by the State Implementing Agency.
**Note 5:** Remaining amount of 50% subsidy will be provided y SIDBI after completion of the project and verified by State Implementing Agency.
**Note 6:** The Entrepreneurs / Eligible Entities interested in taking benefit under the entrepreneurship project in self-financing modeRs. need to provide Bank Guarantee from the scheduled bank valid for three years for the remaining cost of the project beyond the cost of subsidy sought for support. This Bank Guarantee shall be provided in the name of the Department of Animal Husbandry and DairyingRs. Ministry of FisheriesRs. Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
**Note 7:** The Entrepreneurs / Eligible Entities need to arrange the remaining amount through bank loan or from the financial institution or self-financing.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be an individualRs. Self Help Group (SHG)Rs. Farmers Producer Organization (FPO)Rs. Farmers Cooperative (FCO)Rs. Joint Liability Group (JLG)Rs. or a Section 8 company.
1. The applicant should establish a Parent FarmRs. Rural HatcheryRs. or Brooder cum Mother Unit with at least 1Rs. parent layers.
1. The applicant should arrange the remaining project cost through bank loansRs. financial institutionsRs. or self-financing.
1. The bird maintained in the parent farm should be of Low Input Technology Birds or any sustainable bird for free-range management.

**Note 1:** Central Poultry Development OrganizationsRs. Central Avian Research InstitutionsRs. Directorate of Poultry Research and State Veterinary Universities and other private organizations with certificates of guaranteed production will be eligible to supply birds to the entrepreneurs. Necessary Technical specifications for birds will be issued separately. A list of Low input technology birds is at [Annexure VI](https://www.dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-11/NLMGuidelinesFinalApprovedByEC.pdf).
**Note 2:** No subsidy will be provided for working capitalRs. personal vehicleRs. purchase of landRs. cost for rent and lease of land.
***Essential requirements of beneficiaries to avail benefit under the submission:***

1. Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities either have obtained training or have trained experts or have sufficient experience in the relevant field in managing and running the project or have technical experts with sufficient experience in the relevant field of managing and running the project.
1. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities have got the sanction loan for project by the bank or financial institutions furnished bank guarantee from scheduled bank along with appraisal of project for its validity by bank where it is holding the account.
1. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities should have own land or lease land where the project will be established.
1. The Entrepreneurs/ Eligible Entities have all the relevant documents for KYC.

name: Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the Industries, 2008
brief_description: Launched in 2008Rs. the scheme "Goa State Employment Subsidy Scheme for the IndustriesRs. 2008" by the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and CommerceRs. Government of Goa aimed to promote industrial growthRs. create a healthy environment for setting up new industrial unitsRs. revive sick industrial unitsRs. provide employment to local youthsRs. and create manpower suitable to the needs of the industry. The scheme offered additional benefits such as a 5% increase in local employment subsidyRs. preference in capital contributionRs. and increased interest subsidy limits. Eligibility was limited to manufacturing unitsRs. including new and existing microRs. smallRs. mediumRs. and large enterprisesRs. with a focus on units employing 80% local manpower. The scheme was implemented by the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and CommerceRs. with a Task Force Committee responsible for scrutinizing and recommending benefits. The scheme was in force until 31st March 2011.
benefits:
> **Additional Benefits**


- 5% additional benefit under the Local Employment Subsidy Scheme.
- Preference in Capital Contribution and under Special Capital Contribution Schemes.
- Increased interest subsidy limit from 1% to 2% of turnoverRs. with 35% of interest paid (up from 30%)Rs. subject to an overall ceiling of 8Rs./-.

> **Subsidy Quantum**


- For new units in developed talukas: 25% subsidy.
- For new units in less developed talukas: Additional 10% subsidy (total 35%).
- For existing micro and small units in developed talukas: 10% subsidy.
- For existing micro and small units in less developed talukas: Additional 5% subsidy (total 15%).
- For sick units under revival plan: Subsidy defined by the appropriate authorityRs. subject to a maximum of 25%.
- Total subsidy did not exceed 40% including all additional benefits.

> **Disbursement**


- 50% of the amount was paid upon signing the agreement.
- The remaining 50% was paid via bonds bearing 6% interestRs. payable after 5 yearsRs. subject to the unit being functional and employing 80% local youths at maturity.
- Disbursement was made within 15 days of claim finalization.
eligibility:
- Only manufacturing units were eligible.
- New and existing Micro and Small Enterprises registered with the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and Commerce.
- Medium and large units approved by the High-Powered Coordination Committee after 1st April 2008.
- Units had to employ 80% local manpower (contract/temporary/daily wage employees not considered).
- Units had to fall under "Green"Rs. "Orange"Rs. or specified "Orange" categories.

_*ProprietorRs. partnerRs. promotersRs. directorsRs. or their relatives (spouseRs. fatherRs. motherRs. son/daughterRs. grandparentRs. son-in-lawRs. daughter-in-lawRs. brotherRs. sisterRs. first cousin) were not considered employees for subsidy claims._
> **Preference/Priority**

Women-owned proprietary concerns (100% ownership) and partnership firms (51% ownership by womenRs. with at least one additional partner other than husbandRs. fatherRs. brotherRs. or son).

name: Incentives to Women Entrepreneurs Scheme, 2008
brief_description: Launched in 2008Rs. the scheme "Incentives to Women Entrepreneurs SchemeRs. 2008" by the Directorate of IndustriesRs. Trade and CommerceRs. Government of Goa aimed to encourage women entrepreneurship and promote self-employment by providing additional incentives to women-owned industrial units. The scheme offered benefits such as interest subsidiesRs. additional employment subsidiesRs. and preferential treatment under capital contribution schemes. Eligible units included those owned by womenRs. either as proprietary concerns or partnershipsRs. with specific ownership criteria. The scheme remained in force until 31st March 2011.
benefits:
**Interest Subsidy**

- The interest subsidy was applicable from the interest of the quarter preceding the quarter of the first commercial production date.
- The benefit under this scheme was for a period of 5 years (20 quarters) from the quarter of applicability.
- The subsidy was limited to 1% of the total net turnover or 30% of the interest paid by the unitsRs. whichever was lessRs. subject to a ceiling of 5Rs./- per annum.
- In case of the Interest Subsidy SchemeRs. the prescribed limit of 1% of turnover was increased to 2%Rs. and 30% of interest paid was increased to 35%Rs. subject to an overall ceiling of 8Rs./-.

**Additional Benefits**

- 5% additional benefit was provided under the Local Employment Subsidy SchemeRs. over and above what was eligible under the original scheme.
- Preference was given in Capital Contribution and under Special Capital Contribution Schemes.

_*The Task Force Committee disbursed the amount payable within 6 months from the date of receipt of the application._
eligibility:
- Only partnership and proprietary concerns were eligibleRs. provided the ownership was with women to the extent of 100% in case of proprietary concerns and 51% in case of partnership firms.
- In partnership firmsRs. the balance share of 49% should not be entirely held by the husbandRs. fatherRs. brotherRs. or sonRs. and there had to be at least one additional partner other than these relatives.
- Units that had gone into commercial production or service on or after the date of publication of this scheme were eligible.
- Women entrepreneurs were given preference under the Capital Contribution and Special Capital Contribution Schemes.

name: Market Development Assistance to MSMEs: Assistance to Organizers for Organizing Industrial Exhibitions in Gujarat

brief_description:
The "Gujarat Textile Policy" is an umbrella scheme introduced by the Industries and Mines DepartmentRs. Gujarat. name: Gujarat Textile Policy: Assistance for Saving in Consumption of Energy and Water
brief_description:

name: Schemes for welfare of School Children belonging to BPL and BC(A) families: Monthly Stipend for BC-A Students
brief_description: The scheme "Schemes for Welfare of School Children Belonging to BPL and BC(A) Families: Monthly Stipend for BC-A Students" was launched by the Government of Haryana during the financial year 2009-10. It aims to provide financial assistance to students from Backward Class Category (A) (BC-A) families to support their education. name: West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs: Reimbursement of Stamp Duty
brief_description: The scheme Reimbursement of Stamp Duty is a sub scheme under the West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs. It was launched on 16th SeptemberRs. 2020Rs. by the Department of MicroRs. Small & Medium Enterprises and TextilesRs. Government of West BengalRs. shall remain in force up to 5 years. > **Objective of the "West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs:** The objective of the Scheme is to provide state support in the form of fiscal and non fiscal incentives in order to encourage private sector to set up industrial parks on their own land with quality infrastructure so as to catalyze and promote growth of MSME units in the stateRs. boost employment generationRs. and lead to technology advancement and improved environmental compliance. > **Objective of the "Reimbursement of Stamp Duty" Sub-scheme:** Through this incentiveRs. an Approved Industrial Park shall be entitled to reimbursement of stamp duty paid by the SPV for registration of land documents within the State relating to purchase of land for development of the AIP.

name: Contribution to State Agriculture Marketing Board Development Fund (General)

name: Information, Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit (I-MESA): Central Smart Surveillance Unit (CSSU)
brief_description: The scheme "InformationRs. MonitoringRs. Evaluation and Social Audit (I-MESA)" was launched by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE)Rs. The component provides for the setting up of a central monitoring system either in the Ministry or at a convenient location for the continuous supervision of all Grant-in-aid institutions. The applicant (Grant-in-aid institution) must install Closed-Circuit Television cameras or electronic devices to cover the services provided in their campus and share login credentials with their respective State Coordinators.
benefits: **Total Financial Outlay:** The total financial outlay for setting up the Central Smart Surveillance Unit infrastructure over five years is 15Rs./- (Rupees fifteen crore). **Specific Annual Financial Requirements (Central Setup Costs):** - 2021-22: 2Rs./- for 1Rs. institutions. - 2022-23: 2Rs./- for 1Rs. institutions. - 2023-24: 3Rs./- for 1Rs. institutions. - 2024-25: 3Rs./- for 1Rs. institutions. - 2025-26: 3Rs./- for 1Rs. institutions. **Intended Use:** The funds are intended for setting up the Central Monitoring SystemRs. developing a dashboardRs. and covering maintenance costs. **Disbursement Conditions/Flow:** - Funds for installation of Closed-Circuit Television cameras or electronic devices in Grant-in-aid institutions will be incurred under their respective scheme. - Funds for the Central Monitoring SystemRs. dashboardRs. and maintenance will be contracted with an external agency selected through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) via a transparent mechanism. **Conditions** The Grant-in-aid organization must get the Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) of the Closed-Circuit Television system or electronic devicesRs. using their own resourcesRs. after the warranty period expires.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be one of the following: - A Grant-in-Aid Institution - A Training Centre - A Coaching Centre 2. The applicant must be funded by the Central Government. 3. The applicant must install Closed-Circuit Television cameras or electronic devices for covering the services provided in the campus of the institution. 4. The applicant must share the login credentials of their Closed-Circuit Television cameras with their respective State Coordinators for monitoring purposes. ***Post-Selection Conditions*** The applicant must secure the Annual Maintenance Contract of the Closed-Circuit Television system or electronic devices using their own resources after the warranty period expires.

name: Scheme for Construction of Multipurpose Community Halls in Areas Inhabited by Tribal Community (Sanskruti Bhavan)
brief_description: The scheme Scheme for Construction of Multipurpose Community Halls in Areas Inhabited by Tribal Community (Sanskruti Bhavan) was launched by the Department of Tribal WelfareRs. Government of Goa. The scheme aims to provide the most needed infrastructure of Multipurpose Community Halls to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) communityRs. who often reside in forested areas or remote interior villages lacking facilities like marriage halls. The scheme provides for the construction of a hallRs. named Sanskruti BhavanRs. which is intended to serve multiple functionsRs. including housing a special AnganwadiRs. a reading roomRs. a recreation roomRs. and a large hall capable of seating between 200 and 300 people. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Tribal WelfareRs. which may utilize an Executing Agency to carry out the construction work.
benefits: - Construction of a Multipurpose Community HallRs. designated as Sanskruti Bhavan. - The project provides funding for the entire cost of constructionRs. subject to a maximum limit of 50Rs./-Rs. which includes the cost of land. ##### ***Intended Use of the Benefits*** - The hall must be used by the local population as a Multipurpose Community Hall. - The facility must include a special Anganwadi. - The hall must include a reading room. - The hall must include a recreation room. - The main hall must have a seating capacity of 200 to 300 people. - The hall must serve as a marriage hall. - The facility must function as a facilitation point for organizing awareness programmesRs. conducting trainingsRs. seminarsRs. holding meetings of Forest Right Committees and other socio cultural events. ##### ***Disbursement*** - The entire cost of the project will be deposited with the Executing Agency. - The funds are released after the detailed estimateRs. drawing of the project is approved by the State Level Committee and the construction license is obtained for the project. ##### ***Conditions*** - A separate long term Maintenance Agreement will be entered into with the Executing Agency for the maintenance of the Sanskruti Bhavan/Multipurpose Community Hall. - The Panchayat may grant use of the facility at the rate fixed by the Government from time to time. - The amount collected from granting use of the facility will be credited into the maintenance fund of the hall.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must represent one of the following - - A Village Panchayat. - A group of tribals. - A Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) working for the betterment of tribals in the Village Panchayat area. 2. The applicant must propose the project in areas inhabited by the Tribal Community. 3. The applicant must ensure that the total cost of the projectRs. including the cost of landRs. must not exceed 50Rs./-. 4. The applicant must ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances. 5. The applicant must ensure that the application is made to the Tribal Welfare Department in the prescribed form. ##### ***The scheme classifies tribal habitations into three classes for sanctioning community halls.*** - For every five community halls sanctionedRs. the first two community halls must be sanctioned in "Class A areas". "Class A areas" are the tribal areas in the village(s) situated within the Forest areas where the Forest Right Act is implemented. - For every five community halls sanctionedRs. the next two community halls must be sanctioned in "Class B areas". "Class B areas" are the tribal areas in the village/hamlet which has the habitation of tribal population for more than 40% of the population in that village/hamlet. - For every five community halls sanctionedRs. the next one community hall must be sanctioned in "Class C area". "Class C areas" are the areas in the villages inhabited by the tribal population with density less than 40% of the population of the village. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must ensure that the Multipurpose Community Hall (Sanskruti Bhavan) will be used by the local population. - The applicant must agree that any land suitable for the purpose of building the infrastructure may be acquired by the Government in the public interest as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act. - The applicant must agree that land may also be transferred in favor of Government by Gift Deed by private persons.

name: Incentive Policy for Setting Up Community Radio Stations - Uttarakhand
brief_description: The scheme Incentive Policy for Setting Up Community Radio Stations is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority under the Department of Disaster ManagementRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote the establishment and operation of community radio stations across the stateRs. particularly in disaster-prone and remote areas.
benefits: Under this scheme: - The maximum grant for setting up new community radio stations will be 20 lakh or the actual cost incurred in establishing the radio stationRs. whichever is lower. - New community radio stations will be provided an operational grant of 4 lakh per year for three years.
eligibility: Priority will be given to setting up of community radio centres in areas or locations of the district that are not covered by existing community radio stationsRs. as well as in disaster-prone and remote areas. 1. The applicant organization must have at least three years of experience in Uttarakhand. 1. The benefits of this scheme are available only for setting up new community radio centres. 1. The concerned organization must also possess a valid license from the Ministry of Information and BroadcastingRs. Government of IndiaRs. for operating a community radio centre.

name: Construction of Minor Irrigation Projects for Scheduled Tribe Beneficiaries
brief_description: The scheme Construction of Minor Irrigation Projects for Scheduled Tribe Beneficiaries was launched by the Department of Minor IrrigationRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide Scheduled Tribe farmers with free and adequate irrigation by constructing small irrigation projects such as water tanks and pipelines in Scheduled Tribe-dominated areasRs. thereby helping them improve their farming. It is a 100% state government-funded scheme.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. farmers will be provided with free irrigation facilities. The following projects are constructed for collective irrigation in Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas: - Hauz (Water Storage Tank) - Construction of Pipelines / Water Channels (Gool)
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities. 1. The beneficiary must belong to the Scheduled Tribe category. 1. Collective irrigation projects will be constructed under the scheme. 1. The name of the proposed village must be included in the list of Scheduled Tribe-dominated villages issued by the Department of Social Welfare. 1. Sufficient irrigated area must be available for the project. 1. The cost of the project must not exceed 4.00 lakh per hectareRs. and the benefit-cost ratio must be greater than 1.0.

name: Water Connection for 100 to BPL/Poor Families Residing in Urban Areas of Uttarakhand
brief_description: The scheme Water Connection at 100 for BPL / Poor Families Residing in Urban Areas of Uttarakhand is implemented by the Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan under the Drinking Water DepartmentRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide affordable and accessible drinking water connections to BPL and economically weaker families residing in urban areas of UttarakhandRs. ensuring equitable access to safe water for eligible households.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. a water connection is provided for a nominal fee of 100/- to eligible beneficiaries.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a resident of an urban area in Uttarakhand. 1. The applicants family must belong to a BPL (Below Poverty Line) or economically weaker category. 1. The applicant must own a plot of land measuring up to 100 square meters and have constructedRs. be constructingRs. or plan to construct a building on the same plot; such applicants will be eligible for a water connection at 100/-.

name: Scheme for Campaign, Seminar and Sports under Disability Sector
brief_description: The "Scheme for CampaignRs. Seminar and Sports under Disability Sector" is a social welfare schemeRs. implemented by the Social Security and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (SSEPD) DepartmentRs. Government of Odisha. This scheme promotes sportsRs. cultural activitiesRs. and various events to highlight the rights and needs of PwDsRs. encouraging volunteer action and ensuring effective implementation of legal provisions and welfare schemes through extending financial support to the reputed organizations or an individual person with disabilities working for welfare of Persons with Disabilities.
benefits: - **State-Level Events:** Financial assistance limited to 1Rs./- per event. - **District-Level Events:** Financial assistance limited to 50Rs./- per event.
eligibility: - Institutions or an individual person with disabilities working for the welfare of Persons with Disabilities shall be eligible for financial support. - The events should be State and District level programs.

name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
brief_description:
The scheme Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swavalamban Yojana has been implemented by the Department of FinanceRs. Planning & InvestmentRs. Government of Arunachal PradeshRs. to promote entrepreneurship among unemployed youth by supporting viableRs. bankable self-employment projects. Through this schemeRs. loan support and capital subsidy are provided to eligible beneficiaries for establishing commercially viable enterprises. The scheme is implemented by the Department of FinanceRs. Planning & Investment through District Level Screening Committees (DLSCs) in coordination with banks. The Arunachal Pradesh Innovation & Investment Park (APIIP) functions as an institutional facilitation and incubation partner for DDUSY. From the current implementation cycle onwardsRs. the State Government has earmarked 50 (fifty) beneficiary quotas under DDUSY for APIIP. Under this arrangementRs. APIIP is authorised to identify and recommend 50 eligible startups that are selected under the Arunachal Pradesh Entrepreneurship Development Program (APEDP) for support under DDUSY.
> While DDUSY remains the financial support scheme providing subsidy and loan benefitsRs. APIIP acts as a structured selection and incubation channelRs. ensuring that beneficiaries recommended under its quota are entrepreneurially trainedRs. project-readyRs. and aligned with innovation and startup-led enterprises. Final financial assistance under DDUSY continues to be governed by DDUSY guidelinesRs. bank appraisalRs. and compliance with eligibility conditions.
benefits: 1. The applicant receives a 40% front-ended capital investment subsidy to eligible beneficiaries for setting up small and medium enterprises. 1. The applicant can avail of a loan ranging from 10Rs./- up to 50Rs./- for the project costRs. excluding the cost of land and building. 1. The applicant (specifically women entrepreneurs) is eligible for an additional 5% interest subsidy annuallyRs. provided the entrepreneur does not become a Non-Performing Asset (NPA). 1. The applicant is required to contribute at least 30% of the project cost as their own contribution. 1. The applicant receives a loan component amounting to 30% of the project cost.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must belong to Arunachal Pradesh. 1. The applicant must be an unemployed individual. 1. The applicant must be between 18 and 45 years of age. 1. The applicant must have a minimum educational qualification of Class XII passed or its equivalent (10+2). 1. The applicant must possess a bankable and viable project proposal in any of the following sectors: - Food-processing units in agricultureRs. horticulture and allied sectors include packagingRs. cold chainRs. cold storageRs. milk processingRs. etc. - Eco-tourismRs. including home stays and tour operators. - Traditional textile weaving forthe modernisation of traditional looms and purchase of new looms to start a new weaving unit. - To be set up Small-scale manufacturing units/bamboo processing units/service centres/ diagnostic > **Preference/Priority/Relaxation:** 1. The applicant will be given preference if they hold a Degree/Diploma in Tourism & HospitalityRs. Information Technology (IT)Rs. or from an Industrial Training Institute (ITI). 1. The applicant will be given preference if they contribute more than the minimum mandatory own contribution. 1. The applicant will be given preference for opening medical clinics or diagnostic centers in Border Community Development (CD) blocks. 1. The applicant will be given preference if the project is a manufacturing unit.

name: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)
brief_description:
The scheme "Scheme for Assistance to MicroRs. Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)" is an umbrella scheme launched by the Industries and Mines DepartmentRs. Gujarat. It aims to empower the state's dynamic MSME sectorRs. which significantly contributes to employmentRs. GDPRs. and exports. Effective from August 7thRs. 2020 to August 6thRs. 2025Rs. this initiative supports entrepreneurs and strengthens MSMEsRs. making them globally competitive.
The component "Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)" aims to support manufacturing enterprises by providing an interest subsidy on term loans. The subsidy percentage and duration vary based on the category of the taluka. Additional benefits are available for differently-abled entrepreneursRs. women entrepreneursRs. registered startupsRs. and young entrepreneurs below 35 years.
benefits: **Financial Assistance:** **Category of Taluka** **Quantum of Incentive** Category I7% on Term Loan with a maximum amount of 35Rs./- per annum for a period of 7 yearsCategory II6% on Term Loan with a maximum amount of 30Rs./- per annum for a period of 6 years Category III & Municipal Corporation Areas5% on Term Loan with a maximum amount of 25Rs./- per annum for a period of 5 years
eligibility:
1. The firm must be a Micro/Small/Medium enterprise.
1. The enterprise must be in the manufacturing sector.
1. The term loan must be sanctioned by a recognized Bank/Financial Institution (excluding NBFCs).
1. The enterprise must apply within one year of loan disbursement or before the commercial production starts.
1. The enterprise must remain operational for at least 7 years post-subsidy approval.
1. The enterprise must comply with pollution control measures.
1. Only one type of investment (Forward IntegrationRs. Backward IntegrationRs. DiversificationRs. or Expansion) will be eligible for subsidy.

name: Piggery Farming Scheme (HSFDC)
brief_description:
The "Piggery Farming Scheme" scheme is implemented by the Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (HSFDC) in collaboration with the bank tie-up schemes. The HSFDC is a company registered under the Companies ActRs. 1956 on 02.01.1971. It is a wholly Government-owned Corporation with a 51% share of the State Government and a 49% share of the Government of India.
Under this schemeRs. the Corporation provides loans/benefits to individuals from Below Poverty Line (BPL) familiesRs. whose annual family income does not exceed 1Rs./-Rs. in both rural and urban areas for self-employment income-generating activities such as piggery farming. The scheme provides a subsidy of 50% of the total project costRs. with a maximum subsidy amount of 10Rs./-.
benefits:
**Project Cost Ceiling:**

- Up to 1Rs. /-.

**Subsidy:**

- Subsidy @ 50% of the total project cost (Maximum amount of subsidy is 10Rs./-)

**Bank Loan:**

- Besides subsidyRs. the composite loan i.e. subsidyRs. and the balance amount of the bank loan is provided by the banks to the seller of the assets on behalf of the beneficiaries.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a resident of Haryana.
1. The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste Category.
1. The applicant should belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) family.
1. The applicant's annual family income should not exceed 1Rs./- in both rural and urban areas.
1. The applicant's annual family income should not exceed the BPL limit.
1. The applicant's name should be included in the BPL Survey List.

**Note:** The eligibility of the applicant is verified by the field staff before sponsoring the same to the bank for sanction.

name: Jhota Buggi/Camel/Mule Cart Scheme (HSFDC)

name: Raw Material Assistance Scheme

Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) to assist the MicroRs. Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in procuring the raw material(s). The Scheme aims to help MSMEs by way of financing the purchase of Raw Materials (Both indigenous & imported). This allows MSMEs to focus better on manufacturing quality products.
benefits: 1. Facilitating procurement of Raw Materials with credit support for up to 180 days. 2. MSMEs helped to avail Economics of Purchases like bulk purchasesRs. cash discountsRs. etc. 3. name: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure
brief_description:
The scheme envisages value addition and processing at farmers level so as to enhance their income by selling more marketable and processed produce in the market. For creation of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure including scientific Storage capacityRs. the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers WelfareRs. Govt. of India is implementing capital subsidy sub-scheme Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) of Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM) across the country and is continued till 31.03.2026
Projects for creation of storage infrastructure (50-5000 MT for Private &Cooperatives and 50-10Rs. MT for State agencies) and other marketing infrastructure projects (other than storage) are eligible for assistance under the scheme.
AMI is an open endedRs. demand drivenRs. credit linkedRs. back ended subsidy scheme. Beneficiaries vizRs. IndividualsRs. Agri-preneursRs. farmersRs. FPOsRs. CooperativesRs. and state agencies etc. are eligible for assistance. Under the schemeRs. the subsidy @ 25% for plain areas and 33.33% for NERRs. hilly areaRs. Women/SC/ST promoters & FPOs etc is available for development of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Projects including storage infrastructureRs. Infrastructure for development/Upgradation of Rural Haats as Grameen Agricultural Market (GrAMs)Rs. Common Facilitation Centre for FPOsRs. Marketing infrastructures in market yardsRs. Infrastructure for direct marketingRs. Mobile infrastructure for post-harvest operations including reefer vansRs. Stand-alone cold storages up to 1000 MTsRs. Integrated Value Chain (IVC) Projects up to primary processing stage etc. Assistance under the sub-scheme is inter-alia available to IndividualsRs. FarmersRs. Group of farmers/growersRs. Registered Farmer Produce Organizations (FPOs) / FPCsRs. firmsRs. companiesRs. corporationsRs. NGOsRs. SHGsRs. CooperativesRs. Cooperative Marketing FederationsRs. Autonomous Bodies of the GovernmentRs. Local BodiesRs. PanchayatsRs. State Agencies etc.
benefits:
The scheme envisages the following benefits:
1) Ensure remunerative prices to the farmers for their produce
2) Alternative &competitive marketing channels
3) Promotion of small size processing units
4) Reduce post-harvest & handling losses
5) Promote pledge financing and market access
6) Farmer-consumer market linkages and also to assist in integration GrAMs with e-NAM portal
eligibility: Anyone can apply for the scheme.

name: Sardar Patel National Unity Award
brief_description: The Sardar Patel National Unity Award scheme has been launched by the Ministry of Home AffairsRs. Government of India. The objective of the Award is to recognize the notable and inspiring contributions made by the citizens/ institutions/ organizations of India to promote the cause of national unity and integrity and to reinforce the value of a strong and united India.Z
benefits: **Tangible Benefits** - Conferment of the Sardar Patel National Unity Award. - A Sanad (Certificate) issued under the hand and seal of the President of India. - A specially designed medallion made of fine silver plated with gold. - National recognition and prestige. - Publication of the awardee details in an official commemorative brochure. **Number of Awardees** - Not more than 3 awards are conferred in a year. **Decoration Details** - The decoration is shaped like a lotus leaf measuring approximately 6 cm in length and 6.2 cm in breadth. - The medallion is made of fine silver and gold plating. - The obverse side features the portrait of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. - The reverse side displays the State Emblem of India and the national motto in Hindi. **Mode of Disbursement** - Physical medals and certificates are presented during the annually official ceremony. - Award announced on 31st October (National Unity Day) and presented at Rashtrapati Bhavan. - Lifetime honour unless withdrawn by the President of India.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a citizen of India; institutions or organizations based in India are also eligible. 1. The applicant should have made outstanding efforts to promote national unity and integrity. 1. The applicant should demonstrate inspiring contributions reinforcing the value of a united India. 1. The applicant should have achievements that serve as an example for others. 1. The applicant should have notable achievements in strengthening unity and harmony. 1. The applicant should have contributions that inspire others to promote national integration. 1. The applicant should not provide unverified or false claims regarding achievements.

name: Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Support for Development of Standards and Accreditation/Certification of Ayush Products and Materials in Collaboration With BIS, QCI and Other Relevant Scientific Institutions and Industrial R&D Centres
brief_description: The scheme-component "Support for Development of Standards and Accreditation/Certification of Ayush Products and Materials in Collaboration With BISRs. QCI and Other Relevant Scientific Institutions and Industrial R&D Centres" under the "Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana" implemented by the Ministry of AyushRs. Government of IndiaRs. focuses on strengthening the standardization ecosystem for AyurvedaRs. SiddhaRs. UnaniRs. HomoeopathyRs. and other Ayush products and raw materials. Financial assistance is provided to eligible organizations and institutions for researchRs. testingRs. and development of quality standardsRs. accreditation systemsRs. and certification mechanisms. The scheme also supports capacity buildingRs. training of technical staffRs. and associated activities required for the development of scientifically validated standards. Each supported organization is expected to develop standards for a specified number of Ayush materials annually.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** - Funding up to 20Rs./- per year per organization/institution for the development of standards and related activities. > **Reimbursable Expenditure:** - Salary of contractual manpower engaged in the project. - Collection and testing of samples. - Training of technical staff at PCIM&HRs. HPLRs. NABLRs. etc.Rs. as per approved norms. - Office expenses exclusively for the project. - Any other justified expenditure required to achieve project objectives. > **Expected Deliverables:** - Development of standards for at least 20 Ayush materials per year along with associated technical activities.
eligibility: > **Eligible Organisation:** - Organizations or institutes engaged in the development of standards for Ayush materials. - MedicalRs. scientificRs. and standards development institutionsRs. universitiesRs. or institutional departments in the government or the private sector. > **Eligibility Criteria:** - Institutions must have adequate infrastructure and technical expertise to undertake standard development activities.

name: Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Strengthening and Up-Gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to Achieve Higher Standards
brief_description: The scheme-component "Strengthening and Up-Gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to Achieve Higher Standards" under the "Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana" implemented by the Ministry of AyushRs. Government of IndiaRs. focuses on enhancing the quality and regulatory compliance of ASU&H pharmacies and drug testing laboratories. It provides financial assistance for infrastructure developmentRs. technology modernizationRs. and stability testing facilities to meet GMP and NABL requirements. The scheme also supports the establishment and strengthening of in-house testing laboratoriesRs. particularly for micro and small Ayush manufacturing unitsRs. to ensure consistent qualityRs. safetyRs. and efficacy of Ayush drugs.
benefits: > **For State Government/Union Territory ASU&H Pharmacies/ State Government ASU&H Cooperatives/ State Government ASU&H Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs):** - **Funding Support:** Up to 6Rs./- per unit. **1. Non-Recurring Expenditure (70% of Project Cost 4Rs./-):** - Funds are provided for infrastructure and technology upgradation and released in 30:40:30 instalments over five yearsRs. subject to submission of utilization certificates. **2. Recurring Expenditure (30% of Project Cost 1Rs./-):** - Released over 5 years with an annual ceiling of 36Rs./-. - Recurring funds are released only after completion of infrastructure and upgradation works. > **For State./U.T. Govt ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories Government and Research Councils Laboratories:** - **Funding Support:** Up to 3Rs./- per unit. **1. Non-Recurring Expenditure (70% of Project Cost 2Rs./-):** - Funds are provided for Addition of section in the existing building/renovation and Equipments for achieving higher standards/upgradation of technology. **2. Recurring Expenditure (30% of Project Cost 90Rs./-):** - Released over 5 years with an annual ceiling of 18Rs./-. - Recurring funds to units also availing non recurring fund under the present scheme will be eligible only on completion of infrastructure or up gradation related works. > **For Private ASU&H Pharmacies:** - **Funding Support:** Private manufacturing units will be supported with 50% of the project cost limited to 3Rs./- for equipmentRs. machinery and scientific instruments to achieve higher standards of GMP (like WHO-GMPRs. cGMPRs. EU-GMP). > **Private ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories/in house Quality Control Lab of GMP certified ASU&H Manufacturing Units:** - **Funding Support:** Private ASU&H Laboratories will be supported with50% of the project cost limited to 1Rs./- for acquiring scientific equipment and instruments for NABL accreditation. - Grants would be for Capital Expenditure for purchase of instruments and equipment only and not towards other laboratory infrastructure including furniture and fixtures.
eligibility: > **For State Government/Union Territory ASU&H Pharmacies/ State Government ASU&H Cooperatives/ State Government ASU&H Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs):** - The pharmacy must be licensed under the Drugs and Cosmetics ActRs. 1940 and RulesRs. 1945 and should be GMP certified. - Government Pharmacies that received partial funding earlier will be considered for additional funds up to the prescribed cap. - Pharmacies that availed grants under previous schemes are eligible for additional fundingRs. subject to full utilization of earlier grants and submission of work completion certificates with photographs. - Existing pharmacies must provide details of medicines manufactured during the last three yearsRs. including batch capacity and number of batches produced annually. - Applicant pharmacies must propose rational machineryRs. technologyRs. and infrastructure upgrades aligned with existing facilities. - **Note:** 1. Pharmacies without GMP certification can obtain certification through support under this scheme. 1. Priority will be given to Government Pharmacies that did not receive funding under earlier schemes due to fund constraints or technical reasons. 1. Application will be as per Format A1. > **For State./U.T. Govt ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories Government and Research Councils Laboratories:** - The Drug Testing Laboratory must be licensed under the Drugs and Cosmetics ActRs. 1940 and RulesRs. 1945. - ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories that availed grants under earlier schemes will be eligible for additional funds under the revised schemeRs. subject to full utilization of previous grants and submission of work completion certificates with photographs. - Existing ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories must provide details of ASU&H drug samples tested during the last three yearsRs. including the number of samples passed and failed. - The laboratory must have a Scientific Officer from the Ayush stream and a notified Government Analyst. - Funding will be provided only to Drug Testing Laboratories located in States/UTs with functional ASU&H Pharmacies. - Applicant laboratories must propose rational equipment and infrastructure aligned with existing facilities for strengthening and NABL accreditation. - Applications must include a Detailed Project Report (DPR)Rs. land recordsRs. and a commitment from the State Government for creation of regular posts to run the establishment. - **Note:** 1. Priority will be given to Government Drug Testing Laboratories that were not granted funds under earlier schemes due to non-availability of funds or technical reasonsRs. and such laboratories must apply afresh. 1. Laboratories that received partial funding under earlier schemes will be considered for additional funding up to the prescribed cap. 1. Equipment and instruments must be selected from the approved list (Annexure 2). 1. Applications must be submitted in the prescribed Format A2. > **For Private ASU&H Pharmacies:** - The Pharmacy should be licensed under Drugs and Cosmetics ActRs. 1940 and RulesRs. 1945 and holding valid manufacturing license and GMP certificates for last ten years. - The firm should have total turnover of minimum ten crores from the date of their inception to the date of application. - The premises and the available machinery and equipment and utility bills should be in the name of the applicant/firm. - **Note:** 1. Pharmacies having other ASU&H Pharmacies within the vicinity or at arms length will be given preference under this scheme. 1. Application will be as per [Format A3](https://ayush.gov.in/resources/pdf/schemes/aoushdhi.pdf). > **For Private ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories/in house Quality Control Lab of GMP certified ASU&H Manufacturing Units:** - The Laboratory having valid ASU&H drug testing license for last five years and not holding NABL. - The premises and the available machinery and equipments and utility bills should be in the name of the applicant/firm. - The laboratory should have an ASU&H stream scientific officer appointed on regular basis. - Existing ASU&H DTLs are required to provide number of ASU&H drug samples tested during last three years with number of samples passed/failed reports. - DTLs of only that State/UT will be funded where there is functional ASU&H Pharmacy. - Applicant Laboratories should demand rationale equipment and infrastructure which matches with their existing infrastructures to upgrade for NABL accreditation. - **Note:** - The equipment/instruments are allowed as per the list to purchase annexed as [Annexure 2](https://ayush.gov.in/resources/pdf/schemes/aoushdhi.pdf). - Application will be as per [FormatA4](https://ayush.gov.in/resources/pdf/schemes/aoushdhi.pdf).

name: Jute Raw Material Bank Scheme
brief_description:
Jute Raw Material Bank Scheme (JRMB) will be set up in the local clusters across the country in collaboration with bonafide Agencies who have adequate experience in similar activities and have the required storageRs. displayRs. and selling infrastructure. The JRMB will source the raw materials directly from the Jute Mills and Jute raw material manufacturers at economical rates. These JRMB will provide backward linkages to the Jute ArtisansRs. WSHGsRs. JDPs Micro & Small Units and beneficiaries of JRCPC to help them provide jute raw material in their locality to manufacture JDPs.
The objectives of the JRMB are:

- To set Up JRMBs in the jute-producing clusters/localities to help easy and uninterrupted supply and sale of jute raw materials to the beneficiaries of JRCPCRs. WSHGsRs. Jute ArtisansRs. Micro and Small Jute manufacturers below mill gate prices to make their JDPs cost competitive.
- To supply finer-count yarnRs. fabrics of 100% Jute / Union /BlendedRs. laminated fabricRs. Technical Textiles and other braidedRs. decorative yarns for diversified applications and value addition of Jute.
- To make jute raw materials available in the desired quantity and quality to the beneficiaries of JRCPCRs. WSHGsRs. Micro and Small Jute manufacturers for manufacturing Jute Diversified Products.
benefits:
- 30% Financial Support on Sales Value

- Up to 12Rs./- per year per JRMB
- Includes:
- 5% direct discount to beneficiaries on mill-gate price
- 25% support for transportation and operational costs

- Additional Freight Subsidy

- 1.50 per kg for JRMBs in hilly or high-transport-cost areas (e.g.Rs. J&KRs. Himachal PradeshRs. UttarakhandRs. NER states)

- 100% Reimbursement

- Financial support disbursed quarterly upon submission of valid documents (invoicesRs. GST returnsRs. certified bank statement)

- Affordable Raw Jute Access

- Jute ArtisansRs. Women Self-Help Groups (WSHGs)Rs. and small JDP units can purchase raw jute materials at subsidized rates

- Reliable Supply Chain Support

- Ensures regular and cost-effective access to jute fabricsRs. yarnsRs. and decorative materials from certified suppliers
eligibility:
1. The Agency and its functionaries should be bonafide Indian agencies and Indian Citizens.
1. Reputed Registered Jute Entrepreneurs/ ManufacturersRs. ExportersRs. Merchant TradersRs. NGOsRs. Cooperative SocietiesRs. FederationsRs. PSUs/ Organizations of the Central/ State Govt. and other firms / Agencies engaged in the Product identification and Marketing of Jute Diversified Products (JDPs) at least for the last three years.
1. Recognized agencies having at least three years of experience in Trading and promotion in the field of production and Marketing of Jute Diversified Products (JDPs) or similar schemes in the HandloomRs. HandicraftsRs. and Textiles sector will be preferred.
1. The CA / OA should have its own office with telephone/ mobile connectionRs. computer/ laptop with email facilitiesRs. etc. for running the Jute Raw Material Bank (JRMB) and at least 200 sq. ft space for running the JRMB.

name: Mizoram Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organisations and Individuals
brief_description: The Mizoram Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations and Individuals RulesRs. 2018 is implemented by the Social Welfare DepartmentRs. Government of Mizoram. The scheme is designed to strengthen social welfare initiatives by extending financial assistance to eligible voluntary organizationsRs. institutionsRs. and individuals engaged in welfare activities. The scheme supports a wide range of welfare servicesRs. including careRs. protectionRs. rehabilitationRs. skill developmentRs. health supportRs. and awareness programmes for vulnerable groups such as women in distressRs. childrenRs. persons with disabilitiesRs. elderly citizensRs. drug usersRs. and other socially disadvantaged individuals. Financial assistance is provided for both recurring and non-recurring expendituresRs. including project implementationRs. infrastructureRs. equipmentRs. and service delivery. The scheme encourages participation of NGOs and community-based organizations (CBOs) to supplement government efforts in addressing socio-economic challenges. Grants are provided based on project meritRs. subject to conditionsRs. and typically cover up to 75% of the project costRs. with the remaining contribution borne by the organization. The scheme also supports research and publications related to social welfare issues.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** - Up to 75% of project cost supported by Government. - Maximum recurring grant up to 5Rs./- per year. > **Support for Welfare Services:** - Funding for womenRs. childrenRs. disabledRs. elderlyRs. and vulnerable groups. - Support for rehabilitationRs. shelterRs. healthcareRs. and skill training. > **Infrastructure & Equipment:** - Grants for purchase of equipmentRs. furnitureRs. and infrastructure. - Up to 3Rs./- for non-recurring assets (over 3 years). > **Individual Assistance:** - Financial aid for destitute individuals. - Support for small self-employment ventures (up to 75Rs./-). > **Special Benefits:** - Disability pensionRs. stipendRs. and unemployment allowance. - Maintenance support for homes and institutions.
eligibility: > **For Organizations/Institutions:** - Must be a registered voluntary organizationRs. societyRs. trustRs. or institution. - Minimum 3 years of experience in welfare activities (relaxable). - Should have a proper management structure. - Must be financially sound. - Programmes must be non-discriminatory. > **For Individuals:** The applicant must be any of the following: - Senior citizens (65+ yearsRs. BPL). - Destitute women and children. - Persons with disabilities (40%). - Victims of domestic violence or trafficking. - OrphansRs. juvenile delinquents. - Drug usersRs. alcoholicsRs. HIV/AIDS affected persons.

name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
brief_description: The Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme (CITUS) is a component of the Coir Vikas YojanaRs. implemented by the Ministry of MicroRs. Small and Medium EnterprisesRs. Government of India. The scheme focuses on modernizing coir units by providing support for new machineryRs. infrastructureRs. and technology adoption to improve productivity and product quality. It also promotes setting up new coir processing unitsRs. expansion into new areasRs. and better utilization of raw materials. Special emphasis is given to generating employmentRs. especially for women in rural areasRs. and encouraging new entrepreneurs. The scheme supports eco-friendly production practices and aims to make the coir industry more competitive and technology-driven. It is implemented by the Coir Board with technical support from specialized institutes.
benefits: 1. **Financial Assistance:** 25% subsidy on the cost of eligible plant and machinery. 1. **Maximum Limit:** Financial assistance up to 2.50 crore per coir unit/project. 1. **Support for Modernization:** Assistance for upgrading existing units or setting up new coir processing units. 1. **Direct Benefit Transfer:** Subsidy is provided through DBT/PFMS as reimbursement after investment. 1. **Support to Entrepreneurs:** Available to SHGsRs. associationsRs. and small/medium/co-operative/public sector enterprises. 1. **Encouragement for New Units:** Promotes the establishment of new units and the expansion of existing capacity. > **Notes:** - A single unit/enterprise will not be allowed for the grant of assistance under this Scheme. - No applications from those units exceeding the investment limits prescribed for medium-scale enterprises in the MSME ActRs. from time to timeRs. shall be considered for grant of assistance under this component. - The amount will be released after the Coir Unit installs the appropriate/approved Plant and Machinery and commences its operation. - The applicant unit will be at liberty to procure the Plant and Machinery out of the loan amount from any financial institution/bank/leasing company or from its own resources.
eligibility:
1. All newly established coir production/processing units in the categories of individuals/partnership firmsRs. SHGsRs. AssociationsRs. and enterprises from small scale/medium / co-operative/ private sector / public sectorRs. interested in the production of value-added coir /coir blended itemsRs. where coir is the dominant fiber by setting up new coir unit or upgrading the existing unit will be eligible to apply for financial assistance.
1. All coir production/processing units registered with the Coir Board under Coir Industry (Registration) RulesRs. 2008Rs. and having Udyog Aadhar are eligible to apply for financial assistance for modernization under this scheme.
1. The units which have applied for assistance under this component will have to complete 5 years of successful operation before applying for assistance under modernization.
1. The financial assistance under this component will be available to entrepreneurs who have not availed of any Central Government subsidy under PMEGPRs. CUYRs. DPIRs. TUFRs. etc. for the same purpose.

**Note 01:** Financial assistance under this component will be extended to the entire coir sector of the country. The project cost of the units applying for financial assistance shall be within the investment limits prescribed for Small and Medium Enterprises under the MSME Act from time to time.
**Note 02:** The equipment and machinery/motors eligible for assistance under the scheme shall not be below the standards prescribed from time to time by BIS.
**Note 03:** The ceiling of prices of different items of machinery will be fixed and reviewed periodically by a five-member Technical Committee (TC).
**Note 04:** The machinery/equipment procured should be as per the standards prescribed by the BISRs. and can be sourced from the open market at the option/choice of entrepreneurs with valid receipts/invoices with GST number. Machinery can also be imported for setting up high-tech coir processing units for which the beneficiary unit shall substantiate the reason for the import of machinery.
**Note 05:** The machinery suppliers will have to give a 'performance guarantee' for a period of at least two years to the beneficiaries and a copy to be provided while availing the incentive under the scheme. In the case of imported machineryRs. the units shall produce the invoiceRs. shipping billRs. etc. certified by Customs Authorities/DGFT/Banks with a performance certificate from the supplier.
**Note 06:** With respect to projects for modernizationRs. the cost of new machinery/equipment/power generators/material handling equipment/conveyorsRs. etc. installed/procured will only be taken for arriving at the project cost for calculation of the amount of financial assistance.

name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
brief_description: With the objective to boost domestic manufacturingRs. investments and export in the telecom and networking products Department of Telecommunications (DoT) notified the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme on 24th February 2021.The PLI Scheme will be implemented within the overall financial limits of 12Rs. Crores only (Rupees Twelve Thousand One Hundred and Ninety-Five Crore only) for implementation of the Scheme over a period of 5 years. For MSME categoryRs. financial allocation will be 2500 Crores. Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has been appointed as the Project Management Agency (PMA) for the PLI scheme.The scheme is effective from 1st AprilRs. 2021. Investment made by successful applicants in India from 1 st AprilRs. 2021 onwards and up to Financial Year (FY) 2024-2025 shall be eligibleRs. subject to qualifying incremental annual thresholds. The support under the Scheme shall be provided for a period of five (5) yearsRs. i.e. between FY 2021-22 and FY 2026-27. Support under the Scheme will be provided to companies who will manufacture specified telecom and networking products in following 4 product categories in India : 1. Core transmission Equipment 2. 4G/5GRs. Next Generation RAN and Wireless Equipment 3. Access & CPERs. IoT Access Devices and Other Wireless Equipment 4. Enterprise Equipment: Switch and Router

eligibility: **Qualification and Eligibility** 1. Support under the Scheme shall be provided only to companies for manufacturing of goods in India as covered under Scheme Target Segments. Further any foreign (non-resident) investment in the Applicant company shall PLI Scheme Guidelines for Telecom and Networking Products be in compliance to the FDI Policy 2020Rs. as amended and effective from time to time. 2. There will not be any carryover of incentive for such years. HoweverRs. the Applicant will not be restricted from claiming incentive due in subsequent years during the tenure of the SchemeRs. provided eligibility criteria are met for such subsequent years. 4. name: Modified Market Development Assistance Scheme
brief_description: The scheme "Modified Market Development Assistance Scheme" was launched on 1st April 2010 by the Ministry of MicroRs. Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME)Rs. Government of India. The scheme aims to rationalize financial assistanceRs. promote market segmentationRs. strengthen marketing networksRs. and provide incentives to artisans and Karyakartas. The scheme provides financial assistanceRs. calculated at 35% on Prime Cost for Khadi (CottonRs. MuslinRs. Wool) and PolyvastraRs. and 20% on Prime Cost for Silk KhadiRs. distributed among producing institutionsRs. selling institutionsRs. artisansRs. and Karyakartas. This assistance supports technology upgradationRs. engaging design consultantsRs. value additionRs. modernization and computerization of sales outletsRs. and direct incentives to artisans and KaryakartasRs. thereby improving production and sales of Khadi. The scheme is implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)Rs. primarily through its Directorate of Khadi. The applications for this scheme are accepted online.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance on Prime Cost:** **Rate:** The Modified Market Development Assistance (MMDA) is calculated at 35% on Prime Cost for Khadi (CottonRs. MuslinRs. Wool) and Polyvastra. For Silk KhadiRs. the MMDA is calculated at 20% on Prime Cost. _*Definition of Prime Cost: Prime Cost includes the cost of raw material plus conversion charges up to grey cloth plus processing chargesRs. explicitly excluding establishment marginRs. trade marginRs. insuranceRs. and bank interest._ > **Distribution of MMDA (for CottonRs. WoolenRs. and Polyvastra Khadi)** **Producing Institutions:** - 34% of the total MMDA amount. - These funds are to be utilized for procuring tools and equipmentRs. upgrading technologyRs. engaging designers and consultants for new designsRs. value addition to post-fabric processesRs. and engaging technicians for maintenance of CharkhasRs. loomsRs. and other equipment. > **Selling Institutions:** - 17% of the total MMDA amount. - These funds are for sales promotional activities such as computerizationRs. bar-codingRs. billingRs. debit/credit card swiping machinesRs. accountsRs. renovation of sales outletsRs. introduction of mobile sales vansRs. participation in domestic and international exhibitionsRs. extension of sales discountsRs. and capacity building of sales personnel. > **Artisans (Spinners & Weavers):** 35% of the total MMDA amountRs. passed on as an incentive or bonus through their Aadhaar-seeded bank or post office accounts. > **Karyakartas:** - 14% of the total MMDA amountRs. passed on as an incentive or bonus through their Aadhaar-seeded bank or post office accounts. - Karyakartas include persons involved in production and post-production activities such as salesmenRs. saleswomenRs. cashiersRs. accountantsRs. marketing executivesRs. helpersRs. tailoring staffRs. store-keepersRs. and godown-keepers. - It also covers artisans engaged in pre-processing activities of spinning and weavingRs. and processing of Khadi and Polyvastra such as dyeingRs. who are workers of Khadi Institutions working in production centers. > **Composite Institutions:** Khadi institutions involved in both production and selling activities receive 51% of the MMDA amountRs. to be utilized for both product development and market development purposes. > **Distribution of MMDA (for Silk Khadi)** - **Producing Institutions:** 40% of the total MMDA amount.- **Selling Institutions:** 20% of the total MMDA amount.- **Artisans (ReelersRs. TwistersRs. Winders & Weavers):** 30% of the total MMDA amountRs. passed on as an incentive or bonus through their Aadhaar-seeded bank or post office accounts.- **Karyakartas:** 10% of the total MMDA amountRs. passed on as an incentive or bonusRs. with a maximum ceiling of 10Rs./- per quarter per KaryakarthaRs. whichever is less.- **Composite Institutions:** Khadi institutions involved in both production and selling activities receive 60% of the MMDA amount. > **Government Supplies (Rate Contract):** - Production of Khadi and Polyvastra products for Government supplies under Rate Contract (RC) of DGS&D is not eligible for the full MMDA. - HoweverRs. only artisans and Karyakartas of Khadi Institutions engaged in production and supply for Government supply/Rate Contract will be eligible for an MMDA incentive at 17.15% on prime cost (calculated as 35 100 49). > **Disbursement Conditions:** - MMDA is disbursed through an online portal via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). KVIC disburses the amount for artisans (spinnersRs. weaversRs. and Karyakartas) directly to their Aadhaar-linked bank or post office accounts. - Funds are released on a quarterly basis based on actual claims settled in the previous quarter. - Directorate of Khadi scrutinizes claims and recommends them to the Directorate of Accounts within 7 working daysRs. which then processes and releases funds to the respective institution and artisans' bank accounts within 5 working days. - Utilization of MMDA for specific purposes such as modernizationRs. renovationRs. and research and development may be allowed up to two years from the date of actual receiptRs. with specific sanction from KVIC. > **Conditions for Availing the Benefits:** - **Separate Bank Account:** Institutions must maintain a separate bank account for MMDA fundsRs. which will be subject to verification by KVIC.- **Utilization Certificates:** Khadi Institutions availing MMDA are bound to furnish utilization certificates annually as rendered by a registered Chartered Accountant (CA). Quarterly utilization certificates must also be furnished by KIs.- **Artisan Payments:** The portion of the total MMDA amount earmarked for artisans must be passed on to them in the form of incentive or 'bonus' through their bank or post office accountsRs. in addition to their normal earnings. Such additional incentives/bonus out of the MMDA grant should not be included in the cost of Khadi.- **Transfer to Selling Institutions:** Producing institutions transferring Khadi wholesale must pass on the relevant percentage (e.g.Rs. 17% for Cotton/Wool/Polyvastra or 20% for Silk Khadi) of the MMDA amount to purchasing/selling institutions through wholesale invoices.- **Timely Claims:** Claims not submitted within 15 days of the quarter's completion will be forfeited and returned to the institutions.- **Aadhaar Linkage:** KVIC must ensure that 100% Aadhaar-linked bank/post office accounts are opened for all artisans and that MMDA funds are routed through these accounts only.- **Target Achievement:** KVIC ensures that institution-wise specified targets fixed for increasing production and sales have been achieved and stock holding has been reduced.- **Recovery of Dues:** Recovery of dues out of MMDA claims shall not exceed 75% of the eligible amount for institutions having a combined production target (Khadi + Polyvastra) up to 1Rs./- per annum.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a Khadi Institution. - The applicant must be affiliated or registered with Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)Rs. State/Union Territory Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs)Rs. or State/Union Territory Khadi and Village Industries Board units. - The applicant must hold a valid Khadi/Polyvastra Certificate. - The applicant must hold a valid Khadi Mark Certificate. - The applicant's annual budget must be duly approved by Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). - The applicant must be engaged in the activity of production of Khadi to be considered a "Producing Institution" for the purpose of Market Development Assistance. - The applicant must be engaged in the activity of selling Khadi purchased from producing institutions to be considered a "Selling Institution" for the purpose of Market Development Assistance. - The applicant must be engaged in both production and selling of Khadi to be considered a "Composite Institution".

name: International Cooperation Scheme: Market Development Assistance
brief_description: The sub-scheme "Market Development Assistance" under the International Cooperation Scheme was launched by the Ministry of MicroRs. Small and Medium EnterprisesRs. Government of India with the aim to capacity build MSMEs for entering the export market by facilitating their participation in international exhibitions/fairs/conferences/seminars/buyer-seller meets abroad as well as providing them with actionable market-intelligence and reimbursement of various costs involved in the export of goods and services. The Scheme provides opportunities for MSMEs to continuously update themselves to meet the challenges emerging out of changes in technologyRs. changes in demandRs. the emergence of new marketsRs. etc. ThusRs. in totalityRs. all components of the scheme aimed at various aspects required to advance MSMEs' position as emerging export players. Under this componentRs. the following activities are covered: **Physical Medium:** 1. Participation (as exhibitors) of MSME delegations of industry associations and government organizationsRs. involved in the promotion of MSMEsRs. in international exhibitionsRs. trade fairs and buyer-seller meets in foreign countries for exploring potential markets for exportsRs. seeking joint venturesRs. awareness about latest technologiesRs. etc. 1. Organizing international conferences/summits/workshops/seminars in India on themes relevant to MSMEs by the Industry Associations and Government organizations. 1. Organizing Mega international exhibitions/fairs/buyer-seller meetsRs. conferences/summits/ workshops/ seminars abroad by the Ministry of MSMERs. its organizations solely or in partnership with industry associations for the promotion of the MSME sector. 1. Organizing Mega international conferences/ summits/ workshops/ seminarsRs. bilateral/multilateral Government to Government Events in India by the Ministry of MSMERs. its organizations solely or in partnership with industry associations for promotion of the MSME sector. 1. Participation of Ministry-led Industrial delegations to International Exhibitions/Fairs/Conferences in foreign countries. **Virtual Medium:** 1. Participation (as exhibitors) of MSME delegations of industry associations and government organizationsRs. involved in the promotion of MSMEsRs. in international exhibitionsRs. trade fairs and buyer-seller meets by foreign organizers for exploring potential markets for exportsRs. seeking joint venturesRs. awareness about latest technologiesRs. etc. 1. Organizing international conferences/ summits/ workshops/ seminars on themes relevant to MSMEs by the Industry Associations and Government organizations. 1. Organizing Mega international exhibitions/fairs/buyer-seller meetsRs. conferences/summits/seminars/ workshopsRs. bilateral/multilateral Government to Government Events by Ministry of MSMERs. its organizations solely or in partnership with industry associations for promotion of MSME sectors.
benefits: - **Financial Assistance for Participation & Promotion:** Reimbursement-based financial support for airfareRs. stall chargesRs. duty allowanceRs. freightRs. advertisement and publicityRs. entry/registration feesRs. and expenses for organizing or participating in international conferencesRs. summitsRs. workshopsRs. and seminars.
eligibility:
> **Eligible Organisations:**

**Events under the scheme can be organized by:**
a) Ministry of MSME and organizations under the Ministry;
b) State/Central Government Organisations/Institutions; and
c) Registered Industry/Enterprise Associations
> **Conditions:**


1. The applicant organization should be suitably registered under the relevant Act (i.e.Rs. companies under the Companies ActRs. Societies under the Societies ActRs. etc.) with the primary objective of promotion and development of MSMEs.
1. The applicant organization should have regular audited accounts for the past 3 years.
1. EventsRs. for which financial support under the Scheme is soughtRs. must be from the list of approved exhibitions/ events/ buyer-seller meets finalized by the Ministry of MSME in each financial year.
1. Financial assistance to one applicant organization would normally be restricted to three events in a financial year. The Screening Committee mayRs. howeverRs. recommend a relaxation of this condition for reasons to be recorded and allot more than 3 events.
1. The quantum of assistance shall only be supplemental in nature to the contribution of the organizer.
1. The Industry Associations/organizations are allowed to participate in a particular event continuously for 3 years. After participating in the particular event continuously for 3 yearsRs. they will be eligible to participate in the same event after a gap of 2 Years.
1. Selection of the participating units shall be based on the eligibility scorecard prescribed under the scheme (Annexure C) and in no case an MSME unit scoring less than 60 percent marks will be eligible for availing the benefits under the scheme. The applicant organization must satisfy itself in this regard before proposing the name of the MSME unit in the delegation and any discrepancyRs. if noticed laterRs. shall be the sole responsibility of the applicant organization.
1. While selecting entrepreneurs/participantsRs. the applicant organization should ensure that one MSME unit must not participate in more than 2 events in a financial year under the scheme.
1. The applicant organization should also ensure that the selection is done in a fair and transparent mannerRs. taking into consideration factors like the track recordRs. growth potentialRs. export potentialRs. etc.
1. In order to make representation in such events more inclusive and equitableRs. the following guidelines must be followed:


- Adequate representation would be given to SC/ST/Women/NER entrepreneurs in such events.
- While selecting entrepreneurs as well as representative(s) of the participating unitsRs. priority should be given to persons who have not participated in such events earlier with a Government grant.

name: AICTE-Training programs for Physical Education Trainers/Sport-Games Teachers/Director of Sports
brief_description:
Training programs for Physical Education Trainers/Sport-Games Teachers/Director of SportsRs. launched by All India Council for Technical EducationRs. aims to support institutions in conducting trainings to develop the skill of the participants to involve the masses in traditional sports/games and fun games for physical activity through recreation.
**Objective:**
The objectives of this program are:

- To orient the participants to develop physical fitness through mass participation in physical activities.
- To develop the skill of the participants to involve the masses in traditional sports/games and fun games for physical activity through recreation.
- To update the participants with modern rulesRs. regulations and techniques.
- To empower the participants to contribute to sports management and sports technology and to manage mass physical activities for fitness and recreation.

**Duration/Type/Participants:**
