name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
brief_description: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)" was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Department of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Government of India. The component "Development of Scheduled Caste dominated villages into Adarsh Gram" aims to achieve integrated development of selected villages primarily through implementation of existing Central and State Government schemes in a convergent mannerRs. ensuring access to quality services and infrastructure development in villages having Scheduled Caste population more than 40% and total population 500. The scheme provides Gap-filling funding of 20Rs./- per village for infrastructure development and administrative expenses of 1Rs./- per village for capacity buildingRs. awareness generationRs. need assessmentRs. and Village Development Plan preparation. The scheme focuses on saturating 50 socio-economic developmental monitorable indicators across 10 domains including drinking water and sanitationRs. educationRs. health and nutritionRs. social securityRs. rural roads and housingRs. electricity and clean fuelRs. agricultural practicesRs. financial inclusionRs. digitizationRs. and livelihood and skill development.
benefits: - **Gap-filling Fund:** 20Rs./- per newly selected village for carrying out infrastructure developmental requirements which cannot be carried out through convergence with other schemes.- **Administrative Expenses**: 1Rs./- per village for technical resource supportRs. training and capacity buildingRs. awareness generationRs. publicityRs. and Management Information System development and maintenance.- **Additional Round Funding:** 9Rs./- per village for Gap-filling component and 50Rs./- for administrative expenses after completion of 5 years for continuous development.- **Convergence Support:** Access to 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from existing Central and State Schemes or matching grants from State Governments.- **Infrastructure Development:** Development of adequate infrastructure necessary for socio-economic development including drinking waterRs. sanitationRs. educationRs. healthRs. rural roadsRs. housingRs. electricity facilities.- **Capacity Building:** Training and orientation programs for Village Level Convergence Committee members and other functionaries. ##### ***Disbursement*** - Direct transfer to State Governments and Union Territory AdministrationsRs. then to District Administrations. - Released in two installments - First installment (80Rs./- or 40Rs./- as applicable) immediately on selection of villages; Second installment (20Rs./- or 9Rs./- as applicable) after Village Development Plan finalization. - Administrative expenses released at beginning of financial year; Gap-filling funds released after Village Development Plan approval. - Gap-filling funds to be utilized within 2 years from date of release; convergent implementation continues for additional 3 years. ##### ***Conditions*** - _Villages must maintain Open Defecation Free status and achieve score of 70 or above on monitorable indicators for declaration as Adarsh Gram._ - _Village Level Convergence Committee must conduct Need AssessmentRs. data collectionRs. gap analysis and prepare Village Development Plan in online mode._ - _Village Development Plan must be approved by Gram Sabha and District Level Convergence Committee._ - _State Governments and Union Territory Administrations must ensure convergence of at least 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from other schemes._ - _Monthly progress reporting on fulfilling infrastructure and individual needs through prescribed formats._ - _Social audit by Gram Sabha at least once a year for transparency and better utilization._ - _Real-time updating of progress in centralized Management Information System portal._ - _Submission of utilization certificates in prescribed formats as per General Financial Rules 2017._
eligibility: - The village must have more than 40% Scheduled Caste population as per the latest available Census data. - The village must have total population 500 as per the latest available Census data. - The village must be willing to participate in convergence implementation with other Central and State Government schemes. - The village must constitute Village Level Convergence Committee headed by Sarpanch or Pradhan of the village. - The village must complete Need Assessment exercise for all 50 monitorable indicators across 10 developmental domains. - The village must prepare comprehensive Village Development Plan through online portal https://pmagy.gov.in. - The village must obtain approval of Village Development Plan from Gram Sabha. - The village must get Village Development Plan approved by District Level Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committee. - The village should commit to utilize Gap-filling funds within 2 years from date of release. - The village should agree to continue convergent implementation for additional 3 years after fund utilization period. ***Selection Process*** Villages will be selected in descending order of their Scheduled Caste population percentage. ***Priority*** Villages having less than or equal to 40% Scheduled Caste population but overall high number of persons belonging to Scheduled Castes shall be taken up after covering eligible villages with more than 40% Scheduled Caste population.

name: Scheme of Development Assistance to Colleges for the Construction of Buildings
brief_description: The scheme "Scheme of Development Assistance to Colleges for the Construction of Buildings" was launched by the University Grants CommissionRs. Ministry of EducationRs. Govt. of India. The scheme aims to help Colleges in the consolidation and expansion of infrastructure. The scheme provides financial assistance for the construction and renovation/extension of existing buildingsRs. including classroomsRs. libraryRs. laboratoriesRs. administrative blockRs. staff quartersRs. and hostels. The applications for this scheme are accepted after the College has constituted a Building CommitteeRs. finalized the plans and estimatesRs. and resolved to take up the building projects with University Grants Commission assistance.
benefits: ##### ***Financial Assistance*** - The scheme provides financial assistance for the construction and renovation/extension (of existing buildings) of various types of buildings (e.g.Rs. classroomsRs. libraryRs. laboratoriesRs. administrative blockRs. staff quartersRs. hostels). - The University Grants Commission provides financial assistance on a 100% basis within the approved ceiling. - Colleges may seek assistance up to 60% of the total grants allocated under General Development Assistance in a Plan period for the construction of buildings. ##### ***Disbursement*** The release of the approved grant is staggered based on progress and documentation: - 50% of the approved grant will be released while conveying the University Grants Commissions approval to the Plan and Estimates. - 40% of the approved grant will be released upon receipt of the audited Utilisation CertificateRs. audited Statement of ExpenditureRs. and progress report of the first installment indicating the stage of construction (Annexure-IV & V). - Remaining 10% of the grant will be released on receipt of the Completion documents (Annexure-IVRs. VIRs. VIIRs. revised estimatesRs. and photographs). ##### ***Conditions*** - The College must ensure that the expenditure exceeding the UGC grantRs. if anyRs. will be met by the College from its own resources. - The construction must not be delayed for want of funds. - The Project should be completed in a time-bound manner (in months). - The construction must be executed in accordance with the plan accepted by the Commission.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a College. - The applicant must be included in the list of Colleges maintained by the University Grants Commission. - The applicant must be included under Sections 2(f) and 12B of the University Grants Commission ActRs. 1956.

name: Uttarakhand State Science & Technology Congress (USSTC)
brief_description: The scheme Uttarakhand State Science & Technology Congress is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Department of Science and TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to foster scientific talent and encourage emerging scientists and researchers in the state. The congress is organized annually by UCOST and attracts significant participation from young researchers and scientists.
benefits: The Uttarakhand State Science and Technology Congress (USSTC) is organized annually by UCOST. The USSTC specifically aims to foster scientific talent and provide encouragement to emerging scientists and researchers in the state. The Science Congress attracts considerable attention from young researchers and scientists and has been a great success.
eligibility: 1. Individual researchers from research institutesRs. startup innovatorsRs. farmersRs. and NGOs from Uttarakhand are eligible to participate in the Science & Technology Congress.

name: Sagar Khedu Sarvangi Vikas Yojana
brief_description: The scheme Sagar Khedu Sarvangi Vikas Yojana was launched by the Energy and Petrochemicals DepartmentRs. Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to accelerate the process of development in 39 taluks of 15 districts of Sagar Kantha (Coastal Area). The scheme aims to resolve the problem of excessive tripping and faults in coastal areas due to corrosion and humidityRs. ensuring uninterrupted and quality power supply to consumers. The scheme provides improvement of distribution linesRs. construction of new 66 Kilovolt sub stationsRs. and repair and modernization of transmission linesRs. along with provisioning 12Rs. new agricultural electricity connections. The scheme is implemented by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL). The Government provides share capital contributions to the corporation for execution.
benefits: The scheme plans for several infrastructure improvements and resultant benefits for consumers in coastal areas: **Infrastructure Improvement:** Work is planned for the improvement of distribution linesRs. construction of new 66 Kilovolt sub stationsRs. and repair and modernization of transmission lines. **Voltage and Supply:** Industrial and residential customers located in the coastal areas will receive adequate voltage and continuous power supply. **Reduced Failures:** There will be a significant reduction in the rate of electric motor burnout and transformer failure. **Reduced Losses:** There will be a reduction in transmission loss and power interruption. **Crop Protection:** Provision of continuous power supply will prevent damage to crops. **Safety:** Accidents that occur due to the breaking of power lines can be largely avoided. **Development:** The all-round development of the villages of the taluks located in the Sagar Kantha area can be achieved. **New Connections:** New agricultural electricity connections are planned to be provided to coastal farmers (with a target of 12Rs. connections mentioned for the financial year 2016-2017). **Residential Coverage:** Electricity supply is planned for approximately 1Rs. housings.
eligibility: ***The guidelines of the scheme do not define any specific eligibility criteria. HoweverRs. the target groups benefiting from the infrastructure and connection provisions will be the following:*** - Electricity consumers living in the coastal area. - IndustrialRs. residentialRs. or agricultural customers located in the coastal areas. - Consumers residing within one of the 39 taluks of the 15 districts of the Sagar Kantha area. - Farmer seeking a new agricultural electricity connection in the areas of Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited (PGVCL) company.

name: Uttarakhand@25 Adarsh Champawat
brief_description: The scheme Uttarakhand@25 Adarsh Champawat is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Science and TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to develop Champawat district as a model district with the broader objective of positioning Uttarakhand as a model state for other Himalayan regions.
benefits: Uttarakhand@25 "Adarsh Champawat" aims to develop Champawat district as a model district under the vision of the Honorable Chief MinisterRs. with the broader goal of making Uttarakhand a model for other Himalayan states. The Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST)Rs. DehradunRs. has been designated as the nodal agency. In this contextRs. UCOST is working to develop the district as an ideal district by coordinating with NGOsRs. self-help groupsRs. various state and central government departmentsRs. and other institutions operating in Champawat district.
eligibility: 1. The beneficiaries must be farmersRs. entrepreneursRs. self-help groupsRs. studentsRs. researchersRs. and the general public of Champawat district of Uttarakhand.

name: Artificial Intelligence
brief_description: The scheme Artificial Intelligence is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Science and TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to promote awarenessRs. understandingRs. and practical learning of Artificial Intelligence among school students from classes 9 to 12 and provide them with opportunities to participate in AI coding camps and hands-on experiments.
benefits: UCOSTRs. Regional Science CenterRs. DehradunRs. in collaboration with IntelRs. has established an AI Skills Lab under the AI for Youth program. Students from classes 9 to 12 across the state can participate in AI coding camps and perform hands-on experiments.
eligibility: - The applicant must be a student of class 9 to 12 studying in a government or private school in Uttarakhand.

name: Policy for Establishment of Private Industrial Estates/Areas - 2023
brief_description: The Policy for Establishment of Private Industrial Estates/Areas - 2023 is implemented by the MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under the Department of IndustriesRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote and facilitate the development of private industrial estates and areas in Uttarakhand by providing financial incentivesRs. infrastructure supportRs. and a streamlined regulatory framework.
benefits: - **Capital Subsidy on Infrastructure:** 10 lakh per acre. - **Subsidy for Setting Up CETP:** 40% of the costRs. up to a maximum of 1 crore. - **Assistance for External Infrastructure Development:** 2% of the total fixed capital investment made by the private promoter on the fixed assets created for the industrial establishmentRs. per park/areaRs. will be payable.
eligibility: 1. Any individualRs. founderRs. developerRs. partnership firmRs. LLPRs. companyRs. or institution legally registered under the Companies ActRs. Societies ActRs. or Limited Liability Partnership ActRs. as well as entities operating in Joint Venture or Public-Private Partnership (PPP) modeRs. or as a Land Aggregator (with written consent of all concerned landowners)Rs. shall be eligible to apply for setting up a Private Industrial Estate/Area. 1. For establishing a private industrial estate/area/parkRs. it is mandatory to have at least 30 acres of land in plain areas and at least 2 acres in hilly areas. 1. The promoter/investor must arrange the required land from their own sources for setting up the industrial estate/area. 1. In cases where land is aggregated through land aggregatorsRs. SIDCUL will enter into an agreement with the promoter/land aggregator to ensure fulfillment of financial obligations under the policy. 1. If a minimum of 80% of the land is acquired or aggregated by the private industrial estate/park developerRs. and there is an obstacle in acquiring the remaining landRs. SIIDCUL (State Infrastructure and Industrial Development Corporation of Uttarakhand Limited) may acquire the remaining land through the District MagistrateRs. provided a bank guarantee from the developer equal to the acquisition price is submitted. 1. In cases where land is leased or aggregated by the developerRs. the minimum period of lease/agreement shall be 30 yearsRs. which may be renewed with the mutual consent of both parties. 1. The proposed land must be legally in the possession of the promoter and free from any encroachment.

name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
brief_description: The Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023 is implemented by the MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under the Department of IndustriesRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to support the growth of the startup ecosystem in Uttarakhand and create a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship by establishing a robust and sustainable startup environment in the state.
benefits: Under the policyRs. the following incentives are provided: - A monthly allowance of 15Rs./- per month for one year to entrepreneurial startupsRs. and 20Rs./- per month to women entrepreneursRs. person from Scheduled CasteRs. Scheduled TribesRs. DivyangRs. transgender startupsRs. or those based on grassroots innovations. - One-time seed funding of up to 10 lakh for recognized startupsRs. and up to 12.50 lakh for women entrepreneursRs. scheduled casteRs. scheduled tribesRs. DivyangRs. transgenderRs. or grassroots innovation-based startups. - Reimbursement assistance of 1 lakh per national patent and 5 lakh per international patent. - Reimbursement assistance of 10Rs./- for filing applications for trademarks and industrial designs. - Financial incentives under the MSME policyRs. such as special capital subsidyRs. interest subsidyRs. stamp duty exemptionRs. and SGST reimbursement assistance. - One-time free assistance for pre-incubation and incubation support. - Capital subsidy of up to 1 crore for setting up new incubation centres and up to 50 lakh for expanding existing incubation centres. - Provision of 200 crore for setting up a venture fund.
eligibility: ***For the purposes of this policyRs. an entity must be registered as a Private Limited CompanyRs. Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)Rs. or Registered Partnership Firm.*** Under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023Rs. an entity will be considered a Startup if it fulfills the following criteria: **Legal entities with their registered office in Uttarakhand:** 1. The period of formation and operation of the entity should not exceed ten years from the date of its incorporation. 1. The turnover of the entity should not have exceeded 100 crore in any financial year since incorporation or registration. 1. The entity should not be formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing businessRs. nor should it be a part of a family business or business group. 1. The entity should be engaged in innovationRs. developmentRs. or improvement of productsRs. processesRs. or servicesRs. or should have a scalable business model with high potential for employment or wealth generation; or should meet the startup criteria as defined by the Government of India from time to time. ***Legal entities having their registered office in other states of India (in addition to the criteria defined under this policy):*** 1. The entity must have an office in the State of UttarakhandRs. and its business operations should be conducted substantially through this office. During the entire period of recognitionRs. the entity must employ at least 70% of its total full-time workforce from among the domiciles of Uttarakhand.

name: IT Policy and Amendments-2020 - Information Technology Development Agency
brief_description: The policy IT Policy and Amendments-2020 is implemented by the Information Technology Development Agency (ITDA) under Department of Information TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote the growth of ITRs. ITESRs. Internet Service ProviderRs. and Telecom Service Provider industries in Uttarakhand by supporting startupsRs. and creating employment opportunities for local youth through policy incentives and initiatives.
benefits: Under the IT PolicyRs. the focus is on promoting the IT and IT Enabled Services (ITES) sectorsRs. as well as the Internet Service Provider and Telecom Service Provider industries in the stateRs. by encouraging investment through various beneficial schemes and policy incentives offered by the Industries Department.
eligibility: 1. ITRs. ITESRs. Internet Service ProvidersRs. Telecom Service ProvidersRs. IT-based industriesRs. investorsRs. startupsRs. and youth from Uttarakhand are eligible to avail of the benefits offered under the policy.

name: Construction of Minor Irrigation Projects for Scheduled Caste Beneficiaries
brief_description: The scheme Construction of Minor Irrigation Projects for Scheduled Caste Beneficiaries was launched by the Department of Minor IrrigationRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide Scheduled Caste farmers with free and adequate irrigation by constructing small irrigation projects such as water tanks and pipelines in Scheduled Caste-dominated areasRs. thereby helping them improve their farming. It is a 100% state government-funded scheme.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. farmers will be provided with free irrigation facilities. The following projects are constructed for collective irrigation in Scheduled Caste-dominated areas: - Hauz (Water Storage Tank) - Construction of Pipelines / Water Channels (Gool)
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities. 1. The beneficiary must belong to the Scheduled Caste category. 1. Collective irrigation projects will be constructed under the scheme. 1. The name of the proposed village must be included in the list of Scheduled Caste-dominated villages issued by the Department of Social Welfare. 1. Sufficient irrigated area must be available for the project. 1. The cost of the project must not exceed 4.00 lakh per hectareRs. and the benefit-cost ratio must be greater than 1.0.

name: Construction of Artesian Wells in Scheduled Tribe Areas
brief_description: The scheme Construction of Artesian Wells in Scheduled Tribe Areas was launched by the Department of Minor IrrigationRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide free irrigation facilities to farmers in Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas through the construction of artesian wellsRs. thereby enhancing agricultural productivity. It is a 100% state government-funded scheme.
benefits: - Under the schemeRs. free irrigation facilities will be made available to farmers. - Artesian wells are established in areas dominated by Scheduled Tribes.
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities. 1. Collective irrigation projects will be constructed under the scheme. 1. The name of the proposed village must be included in the list of Scheduled Tribe-dominated villages issued by the Department of Social Welfare. 1. The project site must be suitable for the construction of artesian wells. 1. A sufficient irrigated area must be available for the project. 1. The project cost must not exceed 4.00 lakh per hectareRs. and the benefit-cost ratio must be greater than 1.0.

name: Chief Ministers Special Rural Development Fund (CMSRDF)
brief_description: The Government of Meghalaya has been implementing the "Chief Minister's Special Rural Development Fund" since 2000 - 2001 as a component of the special Rural works program. The primary objective of the program is to generate wage employment and creation of socially and economically useful public assets by involving peoples participation at the grassroots level. The schemes undertaken in the program are varied in nature and are selected by the Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) and NGOs and are implemented through local durbars and beneficiaries organization under the supervision of respective Deputy Commissioners of the District. The works to be taken up under the chief Minister's special Rural Development Fund shall include construction of rural roadsRs. footpathsRs. footbridges' drainage' culverts with Hume pipesRs. improvements of water sourcesRs. community hallsRs. multi-purpose buildings' provision/improvement of rural electrificationRs. school buildingsRs. playground' schemes such as procurement of equipmentRs. new vehicles like mortuary vansRs. ambulanceRs. school buses and oxygenated vans for transporting live fishRs. etc. Eco-friendly innovative projects also will be considered under the scheme. The schemes/projects should not be highly technical in nature and the project cost should be minimized either through convergence or by ensuring peoples contribution. Benefits for Local Area Development The Chief Minister's Special Rural Development Fund will be applicable for the rural/semi-rural areas of the state.
benefits: 1. CMSRDF shall be through direct participation of the people and not through contractors. 1. The involvement of the people is through the village Dorbars/Local committees/ Beneficiary OrganizationsRs. etc. 1. The CMSRDF funds should be kept in savings Bank Accounts and the interest earned should be reported to the State Government periodically. 1. The implementing organizations should prominently display the scheme details ' on site/on equipment. 1. For Local Area Development.
eligibility: - Identified by Local MLAs - All implementing agencies' NGOsRs. etc.Rs. should open a Bank AccountRs. jointly operated by two members and funds should be released to their accounts only. - If the fund due to be released is above Rs. 50.000 the Block Development Officer concerned should release the same in 2 installments. - The fund shall not be allowed to be utilized for land compensation or for payment of salaries and office expenses. - A utilization certificate in respect of the amount drawn and utilized should be furnished by the Partner organizations to the Block Development officers concerned for record. - If the organization/beneficiaries fail to submit the UC(Utilization Certificate) for first installment and do not claim the second installment after a gap of three yearsRs. the particular work or project allotted or executed by them should be deemed as closed and the fund be returned back to the Directorate. - Citizens and SHGs in particular may seek the help of their local MLA to avail this scheme.

name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana - Har Khet Ko Pani (Surface Scheme) Uttarakhand
brief_description: The scheme Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana Har Khet Ko Pani (Surface Irrigation Scheme) is implemented by the Department of Minor IrrigationRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide every farmer with reliable surface irrigation facilities by developing sustainable irrigation infrastructureRs. ensuring that every field receives adequate water to improve agricultural productivity. This scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme with a funding pattern of 90% Central share and 10% State share.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. farmers are provided with free irrigation facilities. The following works are carried out to ensure irrigation support: - Pipelines / Gool (water channels) - Storage tanks / Geo-lined tanks - Solar pump sets - Small gated weirs
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities. 1. As per the guidelines issued by the Government of India: - For the construction of collective irrigation schemesRs. clusters will be formed within a radius of 5 km from the proposed villageRs. with a command area of 20 hectares or more. - In the case of an individual schemeRs. the command area should be 10 hectares or more. - The cost of the scheme must not exceed 4.00 lakh per hectare. - The benefit-cost ratio of the scheme must be greater than 1.0.

name: Post-Harvest Management
brief_description: The scheme Post-Harvest Management is implemented by the Department of HorticultureRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote the development of modern post-harvest infrastructure by supporting farmers and entrepreneurs in setting up facilities such as pack housesRs. pre-cooling unitsRs. cold roomsRs. cold storage unitsRs. and ripening chambersRs. thereby reducing post-harvest losses and improving the qualityRs. valueRs. and marketability of horticultural produce.
benefits: For setting up units such as Pack Houses (9 m / 6 m)Rs. Pre-Cooling Units (6 MT capacity)Rs. Mobile Pre-Cooling Units (5 MT capacity)Rs. Cold Rooms (30 MT capacity)Rs. Cold Storage UnitsRs. Refer Vans/Containers (6 MT capacity)Rs. and Ripening Chambers (300 MT capacity)Rs. a subsidy of 35% to 50% is provided through a bank-linkedRs. loan-based subsidy mechanism.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The applicant must be an interested entrepreneur or farmer. 1. The applicant must either own the land or have it on lease for a period of 25 to 30 years.

name: To Increase Fish Seed Production and Inland Fisheries Resources in Tribal Areas: Boat Net - Gujarat
brief_description: The scheme Boat Net is a component under the To Increase Fish Seed Production and Inland Fisheries Resources in Tribal Areas schemeRs. introduced by the AgricultureRs. Farmers Welfare and Co-operation DepartmentRs. Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to boost fish production and provide employment to people involved in inland fisheries activities. Under this schemeRs. financial assistance for boats and nets is provided to individualsRs. societiesRs. self-help groupsRs. associationsRs. reservoir monopoliesRs. private unitsRs. and particularly Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries engaged in inland fisheries. > **Objectives:** - To increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to people involved in inland fisheries activities. - To boost fish farming or fishing activities in fresh water bodies. - Fishing in reservoirsRs. aquaculture in ponds and catch from rivers increase fish production and boost inland fisheries. - The main objective is to provide employment opportunities to Scheduled Tribe fishermen in the state and increase fish production.
benefits: > ***Financial Assistance:*** ***Tin Boat with Net:*** **50% assistance of the unit costRs. amounting to 19Rs./-Rs. which includes:** - Tin Boat: 10Rs./- - Net: 5Rs./- - Lifesaving appliance: 4Rs./- ***F.R.P. Boat with Net:*** **50% assistance of the unit costRs. amounting to 34Rs./-Rs. which includes:** - FRP Boat: 25Rs./- - Net: 5Rs./- - Lifesaving appliance: 4Rs./- > **Frequency of Disbursement:** The benefits can be reclaimed after a minimum of 6 year.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be Individuals/societies/self-help groups/associations/reservoir monopolies/private unitsRs. etc.Rs. involved in inland fisheries activities can avail the benefits of inland schemes. 1. The applicant must be from the Scheduled Tribes. 1. The applicant must be above 18 years. 1. The beneficiary must have his/her own bank account. 1. The applicant must have an Aadhaar Card/Voter ID/Ration Card/Passport as proof of identity.

name: One Time Grant For Media Personality
brief_description: "One Time Grant for Media Personality" is a Financial Assistance Scheme by the Information and Public Relations DepartmentRs. Govt. of Assam. Through this schemeRs. the govt. provides a one-time grant to twenty journalists 50Rs./- each every year so that they can engage in their varied performances in a more productive and efficient manner. The assistance is intended to support journalists in their pursuit of outstanding achievements and also to support them in their time of need. The objectives of this scheme is to uphold the dignity of media persons and to inspire and motivate the media persons to excel in the field of journalism.
benefits: 1. A one-time grant of 5Rs./- to 20 Journalists in a year.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Assam. 1. The applicant must be an accredited/recognized journalist of Assam. 1. The scheme is open to all mainstream media journalists having accredited/recognized cards of DIPRRs. Assam including freelancers from PrintRs. ElectronicRs. and News Agencies. 1. The minimum age for journalists should be 40 years. There is no upper limit. 1. The applicant must have at least fifteen years of experience in the field of Journalism. 1. The applicant should not have been convicted for any criminal offense or punished by any Court of Law or reprimanded by the Press Council of India for misconduct or violation of ethics of journalism or for any other similar reason. 1. The Annual income of the applicant should be less than 5Rs..
**NOTE:** Canvasing for the grant in any form will disqualify the candidature. Anybody found canvassing in his/her favor shall be debarred from consideration for a grant.

name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
brief_description: The scheme-component "AYUSH for Sports Medicine" under the "Ayurswasthya Yojana" by the Ministry of AyushRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to provide AYUSH-based treatment and rehabilitation services to sports persons. AYUSH Sports medicine is a unique concept whereRs. the treatment will be provided on sports injuries and promote the health and fitness of sports persons through AYUSH intervention. Fit India Movement is a nation-wide movement in India to encourage people to remain healthy and fit by including physical activities and sports in their daily lives.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** - Maximum grant of 1Rs./- for one project for 18 months. - The funds will be released in two installments of 60% and 40% of the total amount sanctioned. The second installment will be released after receiving expenditure of at least 75% of the released amount and after acceptance of UC thereof.
eligibility: - The AYUSH teaching Institutions and AYUSH hospitals can apply for the scheme. - The Institutions/ Organisations should be having collaboration with only recognized National and International sports bodies such as the Sports Authority of IndiaRs. All India Football FederationRs. Indian Olympic AssociationRs. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)Rs. International Cricket Council (ICC)Rs. etc.

name: AICTE-PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
brief_description:
AICTE-Professional Development Scheme has been launched by the All India Council for Technical Education with an intention to provide financial assistance to regular faculty of the AICTE approved institutes and AICTE officers on regular and deputation basis in order to present research papers at international conferences abroad& within India.
**Objectives:**
To enable the meritorious faculties and officers of AICTE to interact at international level to update themselves to the global changes in the concerned field of specializations through paper presentation in conference abroad& within India.
benefits: - **Limit of Funding:** Up to 1Rs./- - **Disbursement of the Funds:** - The grant will be disbursed on reimbursement basis on receipt of claim form along with relevant documents. Total grant will be based on the recommended group of countries with fixed financial effect as follows:- - **Group A :** North AmericaRs. AustraliaRs. South AmericaRs. New Zealand : 1Rs./- - **Group B :** EuropeRs. Far-East AsiaRs. JapanRs. ChinaRs. Hong KongRs. TaiwanRs. KoreaRs.& Africa : 1Rs./- - **Group C:** Neighboring CountriesRs. Gulf Countries & SE Asia: 1Rs./- - **Group D :** Within India: 50Rs. - **Group E :** Conferences which are not covered under the above Groups (Group A-D) will be evaluated by the committee Amount recommended as per group of countries or Average of amount recommended by the expertsRs. **orRs.** - Actual expenditure incurredRs. whichever is lesser will be entitled. - Reimbursement of the following expenditures will be granted: 1. Registration fee for conference. 1. Per DayRs. allowance (Days of the conference plus actual journey period) asper the central government rules. 1. Total expenses towards travel from international airport to destination airport and back. **Note:** - In case a candidate has availed grant in Group DRs. individual is still eligible to avail this grant for international support (with in a period of three years) minus the amount utilized for with in India. - In case of the workshop/conference/seminar being held in online modeRs. AICTE will only be releasing the registration fee. **Terms and conditions:** - The applicant has to perform the journey by Air India onlyRs. unless Air India gives an official certificate that there is no flight on the concerned sector (either of Air India itself or in collaboration with some other airlines). In caseRs. journey is performed by any other airlineRs. the airfare approved will not be released. - Applicant should submit only one proposal at a time. - In case an application of a candidate for a particular event (for a Particular date as well as a particular venue) is rejectedRs. the same shall not be considered again and no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained by the Council. - The grant offered cannot be utilized for any other purpose other than the purpose for which granted. - Application should be submitted three months in advance.
eligibility:
1. Full time regular faculty from the AICTE approved Institute/AICTE approved University Department (with at least 5 years of existence).
1. The officers of Assistant Director and above on regular and deputation basis in AICTE.
1. The applicant must not have availed the grant under this scheme during the last three years.
1. Applicant must have received acceptance of paper from the organizer of conference abroad& within India.

name: Electronic Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme: Greenfield Electronic Manufacturing Clusters
brief_description: The scheme "Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information TechnologyRs. Government of India. It has two componentsRs. namely Greenfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) and Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters. The scheme aims to create basic infrastructure along with common facilities and amenities to enable domestic and global electronics manufacturing units to establish their operations within such clustersRs. and to develop a robust electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The establishment of these EMCs is expected to attract significant investment from electronics manufacturing unitsRs. generate large-scale employment opportunitiesRs. and contribute to government tax revenuesRs. thereby supporting overall economic growth.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** 1. **For Greenfield EMCs:** - Financial assistance up to 50% of the project cost. - Ceiling of 50Rs./- for every 100 acres (pro-rata for larger areas). 1. **Government grant in:** - Processing area: up to 50% of the project cost. - Non-processing area: up to 20% of project cost. > **Infrastructure Support:** 1. Basic infrastructure (boundary wallRs. internal roadsRs. drainageRs. lighting). 1. Essential services (water treatmentRs. electricityRs. waste managementRs. warehousing). 1. Support services (R&D centresRs. training facilitiesRs. IT infrastructure). > **Administrative Support:** 1. Administrative expenses up to 3% of assistance (only for SPV). > **Mode of Disbursement:** 1. Grant-in-aid is released in installments through escrow account. 1. Initial 20% released as advance; subsequent installments based on utilisation and contribution.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a legal entity such as an individualRs. companyRs. societyRs. industry associationRs. financial institutionRs. research and development (R&D) institutionRs. or government agency. 1. The applicant should form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for implementation. 1. The applicant should submit a preliminary application along with a feasibility study and project details. 1. The applicant should ensure that the committed investment is at least 4 times the assistance sought. 1. The applicant should ensure that at least 75% of the investment is in electronics manufacturing units. 1. The applicant should develop a new Electronics Manufacturing Cluster (EMC). 1. The applicant should procure land for the project. 1. The applicant should achieve financial closure before submitting the final application. 1. The applicant should submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR).

name: National Bamboo Mission
brief_description:
Resultant to this historic amendmentRs. bamboo grown in the non-forest area is out of the scope of regulations on the forest produces. During the year 2022-23Rs. the NBM has been merged with Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) scheme.
The restructured National Bamboo Mission primarily focuses on the development of complete value chain of bamboo sector to link growers with consumers starting from planting materialRs. plantationRs. creation of facilitiesRs. skilled manpower and brand processing marketingRs. microRs. small & medium enterprisesRs. skilled manpower and brand building initiative in a cluster approach mode. Presently the scheme is being implemented in 24 States/UTs. The NBM has provisions to raise bamboo plantations as well as to establish units for bio-energy extractionRs. activated carbon productRs. charcoal makingRs. pellet makingRs. Ethanol gasifierRs. etc for government agencies and private entrepreneurs.
NBM also envisaged to revitalise the bamboo industry through various innovations and policy support that would contribute by reducing the carbon emission and contribute to domestic manufacturing.
The key objectives of the Mission are as follows: To increase the area under bamboo plantation in non-forest Government and private lands to supplement farm income and contribute towards resilience to climate change as well as availability of quality raw material requirement of industries. The bamboo plantations will be promoted predominantly in farmers fieldsRs. homesteadsRs. community landsRs. arable wastelandsRs. and along irrigation canalsRs. water bodies etc. To improve post-harvest management through establishment of innovative primary processing units near the source of productionRs. primary treatment and seasoning plantsRs. preservation technologies and market infrastructure. To promote product development keeping in view market demandRs. by assisting R&DRs. entrepreneurship & business models at microRs. small and medium levels and feed bigger industry. To rejuvenate the underdeveloped bamboo industry in India To promote skill developmentRs. capacity buildingRs. awareness generation for development of bamboo sector from production to market demand. To realign efforts to reduce dependency on import of bamboo and bamboo products by way of improved productivity and suitability of domestic raw material for industryRs. so as to enhance income of the primary producers.
benefits:
The scheme targets to provide following benefits:
1) It would assist farmersRs. government agenciesRs. artisansRs. entrepreneursRs. private agenciesRs. Federated SHGsRs. FPOsRs. and other persons involved in bamboo industry
2) It will help in establishing bamboo nurseryRs. bamboo cultivationRs. post-harvest processingRs. product manufacturingRs. capacity buildingRs. entrepreneurshipRs. etc for the industry
3) It will help in creating self-dependency for fulfilling the demand of bamboo and bamboo products.
eligibility: The scheme is applicable to all farmers in India

name: Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Strengthening of Central and State Regulatory Frameworks Including Technical Human Resource and Capacity Building Programs for Ayush Drugs
brief_description: The scheme-component "Strengthening of Central and State Regulatory Frameworks Including Technical Human Resource and Capacity Building Programs for Ayush Drugs" under the "Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana" implemented by the Ministry of AyushRs. Government of IndiaRs. focuses on improving regulatory oversight of AyurvedaRs. SiddhaRs. Unani and Homoeopathy (ASU&H) drugs. At the Central levelRs. the scheme supports the Ayush vertical under the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) for professional servicesRs. training programsRs. documentationRs. dissemination of quality control materialsRs. and upgradation of drug regulatory portals and websites. At the State/UT levelRs. the scheme strengthens Ayush Drug Control systems by supporting regulatory and quality control activitiesRs. training of technical staffRs. testing of statutory and survey samplesRs. portal maintenanceRs. and awareness programs.
benefits: > **For Ayush vertical in CDSCO:** - **Training Support:** Training programs for capacity building are supported with a financial cap of 5Rs./- per program.- **Training Support Limit:** A maximum of three training programs can be supported under this component. > **For State Ayush Directorate / State Drug Controller of Ayush drugs:** - **Support for Regulatory and Quality Control Activities:** Financial assistance up to 15Rs./- per year per State/UT for regulatory and quality control activities.- **Reimbursable Expenditure Includes:** 1. Maintenance and development of online regulatory portals of Ayush Drug Controller/Licensing AuthorityRs. 1. Collection and testing of statutory and survey drug samplesRs. 1. Training of technical staff at PCIM&H / NABL as per approved normsRs. 1. Awareness and IEC activities related to Ayush drug regulation.
eligibility: > **For Ayush vertical in CDSCO:** - The Ayush vertical under the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) is eligible for financial assistance under this component. > **For State Ayush Directorate / State Drug Controller of Ayush drugs:** - State Ayush Directorate / State Drug Controller of Ayush drugs are eligible. - The state should have a functional Drug Testing Laboratory and a separate functional Enforcement Mechanism for ASU&H drugs. > **Note:** Preference is given to States/UTs maintaining a database of manufacturing units and productsRs. implementing dossier-based licensingRs. and conducting regular inspections as per the [Drugs and Cosmetics ActRs. 1940](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/15278/1/drug_cosmeticsa1940-23.pdf) and RulesRs. 1945.

name: Assistance for Digitization of Business Processes and Adoption of eCommerce
brief_description:
The scheme "Assistance for Digitization of Business Processes and Adoption of eCommerce" was introduced under the Rajasthan MSME Policy 2024 by the Department of Industries and CommerceRs. Government of RajasthanRs. aims to promote digital transformation and enhance the eCommerce capabilities of MSMEs in the state. This scheme will remain in force until 31st March 2029.
***Objective***
MSMEs are provided financial assistance for adopting softwareRs. equipment for digitizationRs. and for registering on eCommerce platforms.
***Scheme Implementation***
This scheme component will be implemented through the concerned DICC under the aegis of Department of Industries & Commerce. Office of the CommissionerRs. Industries & Commerce will be the nodal agency for the implementation and supervision of the scheme at the state level.
benefits:
**Financial Reimbursement for Digitization Equipment:**

- MSMEs are eligible for a one-time reimbursement of 75% of the cost incurred for purchasing software or equipment used in digitization of business process (such as POS systemsRs. barcode scanners machineRs. inventory management softwareRs. etc.).
- Maximum Limit: 50Rs./- per MSME.

**Financial Reimbursement for eCommerce Platform Fee:**

- Reimbursement of 75% of the total fee (excluding shipping fees) charged by eCommerce platform.
- Maximum Limit: 50Rs./- per MSME.

**Note:** Assistance would only be eligible for one eCommerce platform per MSME.
eligibility:
1. The enterprise should be a MicroRs. SmallRs. or Medium Enterprise (MSME) in production.
1. The enterprise should be located in Rajasthan.
1. The applicant should possess a valid Udyam Registration Certificate at the time of application.
1. The applicant should have incurred expenses on digitization (software/equipment) after notification of Rajasthan MSME Policy 2024.
1. The applicant should have registered on an eCommerce platform after the notification of Rajasthan MSME Policy 2024.
1. MSME enterprise will only be eligible for benefits once for each component.

name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Eco-certification of Coffee
brief_description: The scheme "Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Eco-certification of Coffee" is a Sub-Component of the Scheme "Integrated Coffee Development Project During the Medium Term Framework (MTF) Period: Development Support to Stakeholders" by the Coffee BoardRs. Department of CommerceRs. Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The objective of this scheme is to encourage coffee growers to access high-value specialty markets through production of eco-certified coffees so as to realize higher returns by adhering to a set of standards which help in communication of qualityRs. traceabilityRs. socialRs. environmental and financial conditions surrounding the production of coffee.
benefits:
> **Extent of Support/ Subsidy**

**Certification Support:** 50% of the certification costRs. subject to a maximum of 50Rs. (Rupees 50Rs.) per individual grower/grower groups. In the case of Organic certificationRs. spread over a period of 3 years or the conversion periodRs. whichever is less; in the case of other certificatesRs. one yearRs. during the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) period.
**Additional Support for SC/ST Community:** Individual coffee growers belonging to the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) community with a coffee holding size of up to 4.00 hectares are eligible for an additional 10% of the certification costRs. subject to a maximum of 55Rs. (Rupees 55Rs.) per grower during the MIDH period.
eligibility: 1. The individual grower should own up to 10 hectares of coffee holding. 1. The group of small growers such as SHGs or collectives should obtain certification for sustainability and quality standards. 1. The grower should not have availed subsidy for the same activity during the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture period unless new beneficiaries are covered. 1. The grower or group should obtain certification under recognized programs such as OrganicRs. Fair TradeRs. Rainforest AllianceRs. UTZ CertifiedRs. or Bird Friendly/Shade Grown coffee standards. 1. The grower claiming support for organic certification should be certified under the National Programme for Organic Production standards. 1. The grower or group should obtain certification only from agencies accredited by the respective certification programs. 1. The non-tribal grower in non-traditional areas should have a coffee holding of up to 10 hectares.

name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Promotion of Domestic Manufacturing of Critical Key Starting Materials (KSMs)/ Drug Intermediates (DIs) and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) in India
brief_description: The scheme "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Promotion of Domestic Manufacturing of Critical Key Starting Materials (KSMs)/ Drug Intermediates (DIs) and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) in India" by the Department of PharmaceuticalsRs. Ministry Of Chemicals And FertilizersRs. Government of India aims to boost domestic manufacturing of identified Key Starting Materials (KSMs)Rs. Drug Intermediates (DIs)Rs. and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) through providing financial incentives on incremental sales to manufacturers. The scheme focuses on 41 identified products covering critical APIs to reduce import dependence. It is applicable only for greenfield projects and encourages large investments in the pharmaceutical sector. - **Tenure of the Scheme:** The tenure of the scheme is from FY 2020-21 to FY 2029-30. - **Base Year:** Financial Year 2019-20. - **Financial Outlay:** Total financial outlay of the scheme is Rs. 6Rs. crore. - **Basis of Computation:** Assessment of threshold investment and sales of manufactured products shall be based on details furnished to the Departments/Ministries/Agencies and Statutory Auditor certificates. - **Project Management Agency:** The scheme is implemented through a Nodal AgencyRs. namely Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)Rs. which acts as the Project Management Agency (PMA).
benefits: > **Financial Incentive on Sales:** - Incentive is provided on sales of 41 identified products for 6 years. > **Target Segments:** - Four Target Segments covering 41 products are listed in [**Annexure B.**](https://plibulkdrugs.ifciltd.com/docs/Gazettee%20notification%20of%20bulk%20drug%20schemes.pdf) > **For Fermentation-Based Products:** - 20% incentive from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27. - 15% incentive in FY 2027-28. - 5% incentive in FY 2028-29. > **For Chemical Synthesis-Based Products:** - 10% incentive from FY 2022-23 to FY 2027-28. > **Coverage of Products:** - Incentives applicable for 41 products covering 53 critical APIs.
eligibility: - **Applicability:** The scheme is applicable only for greenfield projects. - **Eligibility** 1. Support under the scheme shall be provided only to manufacturers of critical KSMs/DIs and APIs registered in India. 1. Eligibility shall be subject to threshold investment in green field projects as given in the below-table. 1. Eligibility under the scheme shall not affect eligibility under any other scheme and vice-versa. > **Eligibility Threshold Criteria:** **S. No****Segment****Threshold Investment**1.Fermentation based 04 KSMs /Drug Intermediates400Rs./-2.Fermentation based 10 niche KSMs / Drug Intermediates / APIs50Rs./-3.Key Chemical Synthesis based 04 KSMs /Drug Intermediates50Rs./-4.Other 23 Chemical Synthesis based KSMs / Drug Intermediates / APIs20Rs./-

name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices
brief_description: The scheme Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices by the Department of PharmaceuticalsRs. Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers aims to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments through providing financial incentives to companies engaged in manufacturing medical devices in India. The scheme provides incentives based on incremental sales over the base year and subject to threshold investment conditions. The scheme is applicable only for greenfield projects and is implemented through a Project Management Agency. > **Target Segments:** Target Segment shall mean one of the four segmentsRs. viz.: 1. Cancer care / Radiotherapy medical devices 1. Radiology & Imaging medical devices (both ionizing & non-ionizing radiation products) and Nuclear Imaging devices 1. Anaesthetics & Cardio-Respiratory medical devicesRs. Oxygen ConcentratorsRs. including Catheters of Cardio-Respiratory Category & Renal Care medical devices 1. All implantsRs. including implantable electronic devices - **Tenure of the Scheme:** Financial Year 2020-21 to Financial Year 2027-28. - **Project Management Agency:** The scheme is implemented through a Nodal AgencyRs. namely Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)Rs. which acts as the Project Management Agency (PMA).
benefits: - **Financial Incentive:** 5% incentive on incremental sales of manufactured goods over the base year (FY 2019-20).
eligibility: > **General Eligibility:** - The applicant must be a company registered in India. - The applicant may also be registered as a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP). - The applicant must be engaged in manufacturing of medical devices covered under target segments. - The applicant must establish a greenfield project in India. - The applicant must meet the threshold investment and incremental sales criteria. - The applicant must fulfill all conditions specified for disbursement of incentives. > **Threshold Conditions:** - The applicant must achieve minimum cumulative investment of 1Rs. over 3 years. - The applicant must achieve incremental sales as specified for each year. > **Additional Conditions:** - The applicant must submit a complete application within the application window of 120 days. - The applicants eligibility under this scheme does not affect eligibility under other schemes. > **Target Segments of Medical Devices Eligible under the Scheme:** **Target Segment No.** **Description of Medical Devices covered under the Target Segment**Target Segment 1Cancer care/Radiotherapy medical devicesTarget Segment 2Radiology & Imaging medical devices (both ionizing & non-ionizing radiation products) and Nuclear Imaging DevicesTarget Segment 3Anaesthetics & Cardio-Respiratory medical devicesRs. including Catheters of Cardio Respiratory Category & Renal Care Medical DevicesTarget Segment 4All Implants including implantable electronic devices like Cochlear Implants and Pacemakers> **Note:** - A key component that constitutes a major part of a finished medical device (such as Rotating Anode TubeRs. Stationary Anode TubeRs. MRI MagnetRs. Flat Panel DetectorRs. and similar components)Rs. and has a distinct HS code for itselfRs. will be considered as included in the corresponding target segment. > **Eligibility Threshold Criteria:** **Segment****Incentive Rate (on Incremental Sales of Manufactured Goods)****Threshold Minimum Investment****Threshold Minimum Incremental Sales of Manufactured Goods**All four segments of medical devices (detailed in Annexure A)Year 1: 5%; Year 2: 5%; Year 3: 5%; Year 4: 5%; Year 5: 5%INR 180 Crore over 3 Years; Cumulative Minimum (Crore): Year 1: 60; Year 2: 120; Year 3: 180Year 1: INR 120 Crore; Year 2: INR 240 Crore; Year 3: INR 360 Crore; Year 4: INR 460 Crore; Year 5: INR 560 Crore

name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles Part 2
brief_description: The scheme "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles Part-2" has been launched by the Ministry of TextilesRs. Government of IndiaRs. and aims to promote the production of MMF ApparelRs. MMF FabricsRs. and Technical Textiles to achieve scaleRs. enhance global competitivenessRs. and generate employment. Through this schemeRs. financial incentives based on incremental turnover are provided to companies investing in the manufacturing of notified textile products under two componentsRs. Part-1 and Part-2. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles with support from a Project Management Agency (PMA) and monitored by the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). > **Objectives:** - To promote the production of MMF Apparel & Fabrics and Technical Textiles products in the country. - To enable the textile industry to achieve size and scale. - To become globally competitive and a creator of employment opportunities for people. - To support the creation of a viable enterprise and a competitive textile industry.
benefits: 1. **Financial Incentive:** - Incentive is provided to selected participants based on incremental turnover of notified products manufactured in India. - The incentive is available for a maximum period of 5 years from the first performance year. 1. **Incentive Structure:** - **Scheme Part-2** - Year 1: 11% on 200 crore turnover - Year 2: 10% on 250 crore - Year 3: 9% on 312.5 crore - Year 4: 8% on 390.63 crore - Year 5: 7% on 488.2 crore > **Conditions Linked to Benefits:** - The participant should achieve the minimum threshold investment and prescribed turnover to qualify for incentives. - The participant should achieve 25% incremental turnover over the previous year from Year 2 onwards. - Incentive is provided only when both turnover targets and incremental growth conditions are met. - Incremental turnover considered for incentive is capped at 35% growth. > **Mode of Disbursement:** Incentive is disbursed through Direct Bank Transfer to the participants account via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). > **Frequency of Disbursement:** Incentive claims are processed and disbursed on an annual basis. > **Time of Disbursement:** Claims are processed within 45 days of submission by the Project Management Agency (PMA). Disbursement is made within 15 days after approval by the competent authority. > **Validity of Benefits:** The scheme is operational till 31 March 2030. Incentives are available for 5 consecutive performance yearsRs. subject to meeting eligibility conditions.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should establish a new company under Companies ActRs. 2013. 1. The applicant should invest a minimum of 100 crore (excluding land and administrative building). 1. The applicant should achieve minimum 200 crore turnover in the first performance year. 1. The applicant should be a company/firm/LLP/trust incorporated in India. 1. The applicant should manufacture notified products only. 1. The applicant should maintain minimum value addition (60% or 30% for processing). 1. The applicant should have PANRs. GSTRs. and DIN. > **Preference / Priority:** > Preference is given based on investmentRs. employmentRs. technical capacityRs. and location (higher preference to aspirational districts and Category C cities).

name: Scheme Of Financial Assistance For The Preservation And Development Of Cultural Heritage Of The Himalayas
brief_description:
The scheme Scheme of Financial Assistance for the Preservation and Development of Cultural Heritage of the Himalayas was launched by the Ministry of CultureRs. Government of India. The objective of the scheme is to promoteRs. protect and preserve the cultural heritage of the Himalayan region spreading in UT of Jammu & KashmirRs. UT of LadakhRs. Himachal PradeshRs. UttrakhandRs. SikkimRs. and Arunachal Pradesh through researchRs. documentationRs. disseminationRs. etc.
**Mode of and Conditions for Release of Grants:**

- The grant shall be given based on the appraisal of applications and recommendations by the Expert Advisory Committee and thereafter administrative approval and financial concurrence of competent authorities in the Ministry of Culture.
- The grants will be paid in two equal installmentsRs. the first being normally released with the approval of the project. The second installment will be released on completion of the project and on receipt of duly audited statement of accounts showing the utilization of the entire amount of grant plus the share of the grantee/concerned State/U.T. Government and other documents. The release of the balance of the grant will be decided on the basis of the actual expenditure incurred on the project subject to the maximum limit.
- An organization in receipt of financial assistance under the scheme shall be open to inspection by an officer of the Ministry of CultureRs. Government of IndiaRs. or the State Government concerned.
- The accounts of the project shall be maintained properly and separately and submitted to the Government of India as and when required and will be subject to check by an officer of the Central Government or the State Government or by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India at his discretion.
- The organization shall maintain a record of all assets acquired wholly or substantially out of the Central Government grant and shall not dispose of or encumber or utilize for purposes other than those for which the grant was given without prior approval of the Government of India.
- If at any timeRs. the Government of India has reason to believe that the sanctioned money is not being utilized for approved purposesRs. the payment of the grant may be stopped and the earlier grants recovered.
- The organization must exercise reasonable economy in the working of the approved project.
- The grantee organization shall furnish to the Ministry of Culture a quarterly progress report of the project indicating in detail both the physical achievements and the expenditure incurred on each of the approved items separately.
- The grantee shall submit three copies of the Project Report duly bound/Audio-Video CDs/Photographs to the Ministry of Culture and one copy to the State Government where the project has been undertaken.
- Applications of the organizations against which the previous grant/ Utilisation certificate is pending will not be considered.

**Mode of Payment:** All payments will be made through electronic transfers.
**Special Provision:**
The Expert Advisory Committee (EAC) on the scheme is empowered to recommend or reject any proposal received without or with the recommendation of State Government/U.T. administration/ Local Administration and also to recommend the amount beyond the maximum limit but not exceeding 30.00 lacs from this schemeRs. in respect of any proposal which is of outstanding merit for which the EAC feels that the maximum limit would not be sufficient for undertaking the said projectRs. with the approval of Minister (Culture) and concurrence of AS & FARs. Ministry of Culture.
**Inspection & Monitoring:**
Inspection would be carried out by Ministry officials every year at least in 5% of the cases. The concerned State Govt.Rs. District Collector/Dy. Commissioner will also monitor.
**Penalties in case of Misutilisation of grants:**
The members of the executive body of the organization would be liable for the recovery of misused grants. The organization will also be blacklisted for misuse of fundsRs. fake registration certificateRs. etc. All immovable assets created from the Government grants would be taken over by local administration prescribed by the Ministry of Culture.
benefits:
The financial assistance is given for any of the items listed below up to a maximum of 10.00 lakhs to any single organization:
**Sl. No.****Items****Maximum amount per annum**1Study and research on cultural heritage 10.00 lakhs
2Preservation of old manuscriptsRs. literatureRs. art & craftsRs. and documentation of cultural activities/ events like musicRs. danceRs. etc. 10.00 lakhs
3Dissemination through audio-visual programmes of art and culture 10.00 lakhs
4Training in Traditional and Folk Art 10.00 lakhs
**Note 01:** The maximum grant admissible to an organization would be 75% of the total expenditure to be incurred on any item subject to the maximum ceiling fixed. The remaining 25% expenditure or more should be met by the State Govt./U.T.
**Note 02:** Administration failing which the grantee organization could contribute the amount from their own resources. HoweverRs. in the case of Arunachal Pradesh and SikkimRs. funding will be shared between the Government of India and the organization in the ratio of 90:10 respectively.
eligibility:
1. The voluntary organization should be registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act 1860 or as a public trust under Indian Trust ActRs. 1882Rs. and shall have been functioning for a period of three years.
1. Colleges and Universities are also eligible to apply.
1. The organization should have the capacity to undertake and promote research projects. It should have facilitiesRs. resourcesRs. and personnel to implement the scheme for which the grant is required.
1. A college applying for the grant should be affiliated with the University.
1. Grants from this scheme will be given only to those organizations which are not in receipt of grants from any other source for similar purposes.

**Note 01:** The Colleges and Universities should introduce in their curriculum or research course aspects of studies relating to the preservation of Himalayan art and cultureRs. in case not already done.
**Note 02:** The grants will be ad-hoc and of non-recurring nature.
**Note 03:** Organizations that are doing good work in the field and have resources for meeting matching funds will be given preference.

name: Seva Bhoj Yojna
brief_description:
The scheme Seva Bhoj Yojna was launched by the Ministry of CultureRs. Government of India and it has been made operational with effect from the 1st of AugustRs. 2018. The Scheme shall be applicable within the territorial jurisdiction of India. The Scheme will remain open from the 1st to the 15th of every month. ThereafterRs. the scrutiny of the applications received will be carried out by a duly constituted committee on a monthly basis.
**Objective:**
Under the Scheme of Seva Bhoj Yojna Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and Central Governments share of Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) paid on purchase of specific raw food items by Charitable/Religious Institutions like GurudwarasRs. TemplesRs. Dharmik AshramsRs. MosquesRs. DargahsRs. ChurchesRs. MathRs. MonasteriesRs. etc. for distributing free food to public shall be reimbursed as Financial Assistance by the Government of India.
**Scope:**
This is a Central Sector Scheme for providing reimbursement of CGST and the Central Governments share of IGST paid by charitable/religious institutions on the purchase of specific raw food items for serving free food to the public/devotees. The scheme shall be applicable only to such institutions which are eligible under the Scheme.
**Type of Activities Supported Under the Scheme:**
Free Prasad or free food or free Langar/Bhandara (community kitchen) offered by charitable/religious institutions like GurudwaraRs. TemplesRs. Dharmik AshramRs. MosquesRs. DargahRs. ChurchRs. MathRs. MonasteriesRs. etc. Financial assistance will be provided on First-cum-First Serve basis of registration linked to funds available for the purpose in a financial year.
**Outcome of the Scheme:**
A Performance-cum-Achievement Report on the activity undertaken will be submitted in triplicate by the beneficiary institutionsRs. at the beginning of the next financial yearRs. to the Ministry as per the following format:

- Location of Free Food Services:
- Cost of the Food items excluding GST:
- GST levied: Total GST paid (CGSTRs. SGST/UTGSTRs. IGSTRs. and amount of Financial Assistance released by the ministry:
- No. of days Free food was provided in a calendar month (month-wise)
- No. of persons who were provided Free Food in a calendar month (month-wise)
- At least 12 photographs (taken on a monthly basis) of Free Food Services:

**Release of Funds Under the Scheme:**
The funds will be released to the institutions as per the claims verified and passed by the GST authorities. The Refund Sanction Order will be issued by the GST Authority.
**Inspection And Monitoring:**
The inspection would be carried out by Ministry officials or its authorized representatives every year at least in 5% of the cases. The concerned State Govt./UTs AdministrationRs. District Collector/Dy. Commissioner and State GST authorities will also monitor the scheme. The Institutions /Organizations shall maintain separate accounts for the assistance received from the Ministry of Culture and these will be subject to inspection/audit by the officers of the Ministry or any other agency designated by the Ministry
**Penalties in Case of Misuse of Assistance/Grant:**
The members of the executive body of the entity /institution would be liable for the recovery of misused grants. The organization /institution will also be blacklisted for misuse of fundsRs. fake registration certificateRs. fake documentsRs. etc. All immovable and movable assets created from the Government grants would be taken over by local administration prescribed by the Ministry. The assistance provided by the Ministry of Culture shall be recovered with penal interestRs. apart from taking criminal action as per law.
benefits:
Financial assistance in the form of reimbursement shall be provided where the institution has already paid GST on all or any of the raw food items listed below:

1. Ghee
1. Edible oil
1. Sugar / Burra / Jaggery
1. Rice
1. Atta / Maida / Rava /Flour
1. Pulses
eligibility:
1. A Public Trust or society or body corporate or organizationRs. or institution covered under the provisions of section 10 (23BBA) of the Income Tax ActRs. 1961 (as amended from time to time) or registered under the provisions of section 12AA of the Income Tax ActRs. 1961Rs. for charitable/religious purposesRs. or a company formed and registered under the provisions of section 8 of the Companies ActRs. 2013 or section 25 of the Companies ActRs. 1956Rs. as the case may beRs. for charitable/ religious purposes or a Public Trust registered as such for charitable/religious purposes under any Law for the time being in forceRs. or a society registered under the Societies Registration ActRs. 1860Rs. for charitable/religious purposes.
1. The applicant Public Trust or society or body corporateRs. or organization or institutionRs. as the case may beRs. must be involved in charitable/religious activities by way of free and philanthropic distribution of food/prasad/langar (Community Kitchen)/ bhandara free of cost and without discrimination through the modus of publicRs. charitable/religious trusts or endowments including mathsRs. TemplesRs. GurdwarasRs. WakfsRs. ChurchesRs. SynagoguesRs. Agiaries or other places of public religious worship.
1. The institutions/organizations should have been in existence for the preceding three years before applying for assistance.
1. Only those institutions would be eligible for financial assistance which has been distributing free foodRs. LangarRs. and Prasad to the public for at least the past three years on the day of application. For this purposeRs. entities shall furnish a self-certificate.
1. Financial assistance under the scheme shall be given only to those institutions which are not in receipt of any financial assistance from the Central/State Government for the purpose of distributing free food.
1. The institutions shall serve free food to at least 5000 people in a calendar month.

name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries
brief_description: The Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) is an initiative of the Ministry of MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium EnterprisesRs. Government of IndiaRs. launched in 2005 to strengthen traditional industries by making them competitiveRs. market-drivenRs. and sustainable. The scheme focuses on organizing artisans and rural entrepreneurs into clusters to enhance productivityRs. incomeRs. and employment opportunities. It supports infrastructure developmentRs. technology upgradationRs. skill trainingRs. product designRs. and improved market access. The Coir Board acts as the nodal agency and implements the scheme through designated agencies for each cluster. The scheme also promotes innovationRs. brandingRs. e-commerceRs. and sustainable practices to improve the overall value chain of traditional industries.

name: Bank Loan Processing Fee Reimbursement Scheme
brief_description: The "Bank Loan Processing Fee Reimbursement Scheme" is implemented by the Ministry of MicroRs. SmallRs. and Medium Enterprises under the National SC-ST Hub programme. It provides financial support to SC/ST Micro and Small Enterprises by reimbursing a major portion of bank loan processing fees charged by financial institutions. The scheme covers both fund-based and non-fund-based loans. It reduces the initial financial burden on entrepreneurs and improves their access to institutional credit. The initiative promotes inclusive growth and supports the development of SC/ST-owned businesses.
benefits: - **Processing Fee Reimbursement:** Up to 80% of the processing fee or 1Rs./- (excluding GST and taxes)Rs. whichever is lower.
eligibility: - Applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe category. - He/she should represent/own any MSEs unit. - MSEs availing loans from any Scheduled Commercial BanksRs. Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs)Rs. and State Finance Corporations will be considered under the scheme.

Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED)Rs. Tribes IndiaRs. MSME MartRs. etc. to SC/ST Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs).

name: National Awards For Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities: National Awards For Institutions Engaged In Empowering Persons With Disabilities: Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan Ke Karyanvayan/badhamukta Vatavaran Ke Srijan Mein Sarvshrestha Rajya/ Ut/ Zila
brief_description:
The "National Awards for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities" are being awarded by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with DisabilitiesRs. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment every year since 1969 in recognition of the skills and contribution of persons with disabilitiesRs. individuals and institutions engaged in the empowerment of persons with disabilities.
> **Award Categories** 1. National Awards for Individual Excellence 2. National Awards for Institutions Engaged in Empowering Persons With Disabilities
The **"Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan Ke Karyanvayan/Badhamukta Vatavaran Ke Srijan Mein Sarvshrestha Rajya/ UT/ Zila"** award is given by DoEPwD for outstanding work in Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan and the creation of a barrier-free environment/working conditions for persons with disabilitiesRs. the working place with easy mobilityRs. toilet facilities and directions in the sign language and other indicatorsRs. which facilitate easy movements and integrate the persons with disabilities in its overall working milieu. The Department confers national awards to commemorate the 'International Day of Persons with Disabilities' which falls on 3rd December every year. The ceremony of the National Awards is held at Vigyan Bhawan. The National Awards are presented through the Hon'ble President or Hon'ble Vice President of India.
benefits: > **Decoration** 1. The Awardee is given a Certificate and a Shield > **Award Categories** 1. One Award for providing holistic comprehensive Rehabilitation Services. 1. One Award for promoting and imparting Inclusive Education or educational institutions that are preparing children with disabilities for inclusive education for higher studies. > **Presentation of Award (Ceremony Details)** 1. The ceremony of the National Awards is held at Vigyan BhawanRs. New Delhi on 3rd DecemberRs. every year which has been declared as the International Day of Persons with Disabilities. 2. The National Awards are presented through the Hon'ble President or Hon'ble Vice President of India. 2. The boarding and lodging expenses of the awardees and one escort shall be borne by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with DisabilitiesRs. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 3. To and fro travelling expenses and accommodation for up to one day prior to and after the day of the awards ceremony shall be arranged and the expenditure shall be reimbursed by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with DisabilitiesRs. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 4. The TA/DA admissibility of the awardees and their escorts shall be equivalent to a Class-I officer of the Central Government.
