Department also purchases the plants grown by women in these nurseries on a contract basis.
benefits: - Under this schemeRs. womens groups are enabled to establish nurseries. High-quality seeds are procured from Silvahill or SilvasalRs. and the resources required for nursery operations are provided through a fixed grant. Technical support and training are also provided. - Department purchases the plants grown by women in these nurseries on a contract basis.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a Women Self-Help GroupRs. Mahila Mangal DalRs. or a Local Womens Group from Uttarakhand.

name: Rural Sports and Health Promotion Scheme
brief_description: The scheme "Rural Sports and Health Promotion Scheme" was launched by the Department of Youth Welfare and prantiy rakshak dal (PRD)Rs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote physical fitness and well-being among rural youth by establishing open gyms in village communities.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. an amount of 17Rs./- is allocated to Mangal Dals for setting up community fitness equipment (open gym) in each Gram Panchayat to promote the health and fitness of the youth.
eligibility: 1. All Gram Panchayats in Uttarakhand are eligible.

name: Scheme of Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientists, companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act for their development
brief_description: The Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR)Rs. under the Ministry of EducationRs. Government of IndiaRs. provides Grants-in-Aid for supporting professional **associations/ organisations of social scientistsRs. companies and trusts** for their development. The grant sanctioned for supporting the association/organisationRs. companies and trusts duly registered under the Companies Act should only be used to incur expenditure for running of office i.e electricityRs.rentRs. telephone and other related expenditure and purchase of books/journals for libraryRs.postageRs.computerRs.furnitureRs.office stationery etc. The amount of ad-hoc grant shall ordinarily not exceed Rs. 8Rs./- annually. The ICSSR may also consider providing grant-in-aid to professional associations/organisations of social scientists of national importance for their development or for any other innovative idea which may help the social science community in general in their development. Ten percent (10%) of total grant-in-aid is paid as the last instalment at the end of the year after the Audited Statement of Accounts and Utilization Certificate in respect of the entire amount of the sanctioned grant are received.
benefits: 1) Grant-in-aid up to Rs. 8Rs. for supporting professional associations/ organisations of social scientistsRs. companies and trusts for their development. 2) Coverage of office maintenance costs like electricityRs. rentRs. and telephone. 3) Annual renewal for up to five years based on review. 4) Amount is disbursed in two instalmentsRs. first installment is 90% and second will be 10%Rs. which will be released after submitting Audited Statement of Accounts and Utilisation Certificate
eligibility: 1. Must be a national-level association or organisation. 2. Should have been in existence for at least 2 years. 3. Must be registered under the Societies Registration ActRs. 1860 if privately funded. 4. The professional associations/ organisations of social scientistsRs. companies and trusts should have been involved in national/regional/local socio-economic research objectives. 5. Must submit annual reportsRs. audited accountsRs. and member lists for the past three years.

name: Assistance to Scheduled Castes for Fisheries: Prawn Seed Stocking Gujarat
brief_description: The scheme Assistance to Scheduled Castes for Fisheries" with the component "Prawn Seed StockingRs. introduced by the AgricultureRs. Farmers Welfare and Co-operation DepartmentRs. Government of GujaratRs. aims to increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and to provide employment to Scheduled Caste (SC) individuals involved in inland fisheries activities. Through this schemeRs. 100% assistance is provided for the cost of prawn seed and its transportation to Scheduled Caste lessees of reservoirs. The scheme is implemented by the Commissioner of FisheriesRs. Government of Gujarat. **Objectives:** - To increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to scheduled caste (SC) people involved in inland fisheries activities. - To boost fish farming or fishing activities in freshwater bodies by scheduled caste (SC) fish farmers and fishermen. - Fishing in reservoirsRs. aquaculture in pondsRs. and catch from rivers increase fish production and boost inland fisheries through scheduled caste (SC) fish farmers and fishermen. - The main objective is to provide employment opportunities to Scheduled Caste fishermen in the state and increase fish production.
benefits:
100% assistance is given to the lessee of the reservoir of the Scheduled CasteRs. including the total cost of prawn seed and transportation cost.
> **Minimum Time Limit (in Years) for Reclaiming Benefits:** 1 Year
eligibility:
1. The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community. 1. The applicant should be above 18 years of age. 1. The applicant should be involved in inland fisheries activities. 1. The applicant can be an individualRs. a societyRs. a self-help groupRs. an associationRs. a reservoir monopolyRs. or a private unit. 1. The applicant must have a bank account in their own name. 1. The applicant must have an Aadhar Card/Voter ID/Ration Card/Passport as proof of identity.
> **Preference/Reservation:** The scheme specifically benefits Scheduled Caste fishermen under the inland fisheries scheme.

name: Grants Provisioned under Uttarakhand Tourism Policy, 2023
brief_description: The Grants Provisioned under Uttarakhand Tourism PolicyRs. 2023 was introduced by the Department of TourismRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to promote sustainable tourism development in the state by encouraging private and institutional investment in the tourism sector through targeted financial incentives and subsidies.
benefits: > **Under Uttarakhand Tourism PolicyRs. 2023Rs. the following grants are allowed to investors:-** The following capital subsidy is provided for tourism projects to be set up by making capital investment in the tourism sector in the state. Grants are admissible: **Maximum capital grant for housing projects:** - Category A up to 25% - Category B up to 35% - Category C up to 50% ***The grant will be given as per the following details:*** a) The maximum admissible capital subsidy shall be disbursed in 10 equal annual installments from the date of commencement of commercial operationsRs. i.e.Rs. 10% of the total capital subsidy per annum; OR b) The subsidy amount shall be equivalent to 75% of the net State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) paid by the unit during the preceding 12 monthsRs. + applicable additional incentivesRs. whichever is lower. ***Additional Annual Incentives for Residential Projects:*** i. Incentive for Marketing and Publicity Up to a maximum of 1% of the capital grant. ii. Incentive for Training and Skilling Up to a maximum of 0.5% of the capital grant. iii. Interest Subsidy Up to a maximum of 1% of the capital subsidy. iv. Incentive for Waste Treatment Up to a maximum of 0.25% of the capital subsidy. v. Incentive for Bookings through Online Travel Agencies/Platforms Developed by the State Up to a maximum of 0.25% of the capital grant. - Capital Grant for Development of Tourism Products and Services Grant of up to 100% of the capital asset ***Grant will be provided as per the following details:*** a) Capital subsidy shall be disbursed in 5 equal annual installments from the date of commercial operationRs. i.e.Rs. 20% of the capital subsidy per annumRs. or b) The subsidy shall be 75% of the net State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) paid by the unit for the last 12 monthsRs. + additional incentiveRs. whichever is lower. ***Additional Annual Incentives for Development of Tourism Products and Services*** i. Incentive for Marketing and Publicity Up to a maximum of 2% of the capital grant. ii. Incentive for Training and Skilling Up to a maximum of 2% of the capital grant. iii. Interest Subsidy Up to a maximum of 2% of the capital subsidy. iv. Booking through Online Travel Agency/Platform Developed by the State Up to a maximum of 1% of the capital grant. **Turnover Linked Incentive** A provision of turnover-based grants is available for tourism projects that are already operational and not receiving a capital grant. The following incentives are permissible: a) Premium Residential Units Up to a maximum of 1% of the eligible turnover. b) Incentive on Foreign Tourist Stay Up to a maximum of 1% of the eligible turnover. c) MICERs. Organization of ArtRs. Social and Cultural EventsRs. FairsRs. and Festivals Up to a maximum of 1% of the eligible turnover. **Incentive for Heli-Transport ** From SahastradharaRs. Jolly GrantRs. and Pantnagar helipads to the nearest residence or helipadRs. a subsidy of 500 per person per leg shall be provided to the unit for helicopter transport. **Reimbursement of Electricity Duty** 100% reimbursement of electricity duty shall be provided to new eligible tourism units for the duration of the policy period. **Reimbursement of Stamp Duty ** New eligible tourism units shall receive reimbursement of the applicable stamp duty in five equal installments. To qualify for grants under the Tourism Policy 2023Rs. the minimum investment requirement for new or expansion projects ranges from 1 crore to 5 croreRs. depending on the category and location of the project. Investors must also ensure the provision of minimum required infrastructureRs. compliance with prescribed conditionsRs. and adherence to other regulations specified in the guidelines. Detailed information is available in the Operational Guidelines.
eligibility: Minimum investment and infrastructure development requirements prescribed for tourism projectsRs. productsRs. and services identified under various NIC codes mentioned in the Tourism Policy. 1. Any legitimate entity or investor interested in investing in the tourism sectorRs. in accordance with applicable regulations and meeting the eligibility criteria specified in the Tourism Policy 2023 and its Operational GuidelinesRs. shall be eligible to receive the grants provided under the policy. 1. In cases where land is required for project implementationRs. the investor must either possess land in Uttarakhand or acquire it through purchase or lease within the state for the purpose of executing the project.

name: Entrepreneurship and Development Programme
brief_description: The scheme Entrepreneurship and Development Programme is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Science and TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to establish Technology Resource Centers (TRCs) that develop advanced technologies based on locally available natural resources and improve techniques for commercial applications.
benefits: Under the Entrepreneurship and Development ProgramRs. Technology Resource Centers (TRCs) are established. These centers work on the development of advanced technologies based on locally available natural resources and improve them for business needsRs. so that businesses can be created by adding value to the available natural resources.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be an interested Entrepreneur/NGO Scientist/Researcher/Teacher from Uttarakhand.

name: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Vigyaan Gram Sankul Pariyojana
brief_description: The scheme Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Vigyaan Gram Sankul Pariyojana is funded by the Department of Science and TechnologyRs. Government of IndiaRs. and implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Department of Science and TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The project aims to promote sustainable rural development through the application of science and technology to enhance livelihoods in selected villages throughout Uttarakhand.
benefits: - Under the projectRs. rural development work is carried out by forming clusters of villages across various districts of the state. - Based on the natural resources available in the selected villagesRs. various units are established to improve farmers' livelihoods through the application of science and technology.
eligibility: 1. The beneficiaries of the project include selected farmersRs. entrepreneursRs. self-help groupsRs. and general public residing in Uttarakhand.

name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Registered Organizations/Government Organization/Non-Government Organizations/Institutions for Running Residential Facilities/Half Way Homes for Persons with Disabilities
brief_description: The scheme Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Registered Organizations/Government Organizations/Non-Government Organizations/Institutions for Running Residential Facilities/Halfway Homes for Persons with Disabilities was launched by the Department for Empowerment of Persons with DisabilitiesRs. Government of Goa. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to registered organizationsRs. Government organizationsRs. and institutions for running residential facilities or halfway homes for Persons with Disabilities. The scheme provides financial support in the form of operational grants to offer shelterRs. basic foodRs. and medical facilitiesRs. thereby facilitating healthyRs. hygienicRs. and better living conditions for this section of society.
benefits:
##### ***Operational Grant*** - Maximum operational grant of 4Rs./- per month. - **Payment to Medical Officer/Councilor/Therapist:** 60Rs./- per month.- **Payment to team of Administrative Staff (ManagerRs. ClerkRs. and six Attendants/Care takers/Aayas/Drivers):** 1Rs./- per month.- **Administrative Expenses (Rent/Maintenance/Electricity/Water/TelephoneRs. MobileRs. NewspaperRs. etc.):** 46Rs./- per month.- **Food Expenses (200/- per 20 inmates):** 1Rs./- per month.- **Medical Expenses:** 40Rs./- per month. ##### ***One-time Grant*** An additional one-time grant of 50Rs./- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) shall be sanctioned for the purchase of furnitureRs. utensilsRs. etc.
##### ***Disbursement*** - **Mode of Grant:** The operational grant is provided on a reimbursement basis.- **Share of Cost:** Based on the claim made by the grantee organizationRs. 75% will be refunded by the department.- **Frequency:** The operational grant will be released in two installments in a year.- **Installment Period:** The six months period for calculating the installment will be reckoned from the month in which the sanction was issued.- **Documentation:** The maximum operational grant of 4Rs./- per month will be sanctioned only on the production of supporting documents such as billsRs. vouchersRs. and receipts.- **Second Installment Condition:** The second installment will be released only upon submission of a Utilization Certificate as per FORM-12A of General Financial Rules Rule 2017.- **One-time Grant Condition:** The one-time grant of 50Rs./- is sanctioned once in five years after following Codal formalities and Rules in force of the Government of Goa.
##### ***Conditions*** - _The grantee institution shall maintain separate accounts of the Grants received under the Scheme._ - _The accounts shall always be open to a system of internal audit or concurrent audit._ - _The accounts shall also be open to Audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India._ - _The grantee institution shall maintain the stock register of the expenditure incurred out of Government grants received under this scheme._ - _The grantee institution must maintain a separate register regarding the grants sanctionedRs. and an extract from this register shall be furnished to the Government annually with the Annual audited statements of accounts after the close of the financial year._ - _The account of the Grantee Institution/Government Bodies/Organization in respect of this grant should be audited by an approved Auditor/Chartered Accountant immediately after the end of the financial year for which the grant is sanctioned._ - _The accounts of the grants shall be maintained separately and properly from the institution's normal activities._ - _The Audited statement of accounts showing the expenditure incurred by the Grantee Institution/Organization from the grants should be furnished to the Government as soon as possible after the close of the financial year._ - _A certificate must be furnished from the Chartered Accountant/auditor confirming that the grant was utilized for the purpose for which it was sanctioned._ - _The Grantee Institution must exercise reasonable economy and observe all financial rules issued by the Government from time to time while incurring the expenditure._ - _No grant shall be allowed to be paid to any other institutions or voluntary organizations by the Grantee Institution/Organization out of this grant sanctioned by the Government._
eligibility:
- The applicant must be a registered voluntary organizationRs. Non-Governmental OrganizationRs. Government OrganizationRs. or Institution. - The applicant must be engaged in the Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. - The applying Organization must bear 25% of the cost proposed. - The grantee Institution should be capable of mobilizing the community towards the cause. - The grantee Institution should be capable of effective networking with other institutions for optimum utilization of allocated resources.
##### ***Conditions Applicable ONLY to Non-Government Organizations/Institutions (Government Organizations are exempted from these)*** - The grantee institution must be registered as per Section 50 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities ActRs. 2016 and its further amendments. - The Organization must have a minimum of 20 inmates at the time of applying for the scheme. - The grantee institution must have at least one year of field experience in the empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. - The grantee institution must maintain financial viability to independently sustain the operation of residential facilities or halfway homes for a minimum period of three months in the event of delays in the release of operational grants or scheme discontinuation. - The grantee institution must have a good reputation and credibility with no cases of criminal offence registered against the said organization/institution. - The grantee institution/organization must have accessible physical and digital infrastructure.

name: Drone Policy 2023 - Information Technology Development Agency
brief_description: The Drone Policy 2023 is implemented by the Information Technology Development Agency (ITDA) under Department of Information TechnologyRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to promote the useRs. innovationRs. and development of drone technology for improving service delivery and governance in UttarakhandRs. while strengthening the drone ecosystem through collaboration among industryRs. academiaRs. and government.
benefits: **The following measures have been initiated under the Drone Policy 2023 to boost the drone sector:** - Giving a major boost to service delivery and governance through the use of drones in the difficult terrains of the state. - Encouraging innovation and development in drone technology. - Strengthening the Drone System Design and Manufacturing (DSDM) and Drone-Based Services (DES) ecosystem. - Maximizing the benefits of drone technology for the state by promoting collaboration between industryRs. administrationRs. and academia. - Providing benefits under the policy to drone service providersRs. drone manufacturersRs. drone investorsRs. drone-related startupsRs. the youth of UttarakhandRs. universitiesRs. ITIsRs. and polytechnic colleges. - Developing a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework for the use of drones. - Rewarding startupsRs. companiesRs. and individuals excelling in drone manufacturing and drone-related services. - Establishing Drone Centers of Excellence. - Introducing various incentive schemes.
eligibility: 1. Drone service providersRs. drone manufacturersRs. drone industriesRs. drone investorsRs. drone startupsRs. the youth of UttarakhandRs. universitiesRs. ITIsRs. polytechnic collegesRs. and government institutions are eligible to avail benefits under the Drone Policy.

name: Jal Jeevan Mission (Har Ghar Jal Yojana) - Uttarakhand
brief_description: The Har Ghar Jal Yojana is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan under the Drinking Water DepartmentRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide every rural household in Uttarakhand with safe and adequate drinking water through household tap connectionsRs. ensuring the supply of 55 litres of potable water per person per day.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. each household will receive pure drinking water through a domestic tap connection at the rate of 55 litres per person per day.
eligibility: There is no eligibility criterion for providing connection/drinking water to rural drinking water consumers in Uttarakhand.

name: World Bank-funded Uttarakhand Drinking Water Programme (For Semi-Urban Areas)
brief_description: The "World Bank-funded Uttarakhand Drinking Water Programme (For Semi-Urban Areas)" is a World Bankfunded initiative implemented by the Uttarakhand Peyjal Sansadhan Vikas Evam Nirman Nigam under the Drinking Water DepartmentRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide affordable and reliable domestic drinking water connections to eligible households in selected semi-urban areas of UttarakhandRs. ensuring improved access to safe and adequate drinking water.
benefits: Under this schemeRs. domestic water connections are provided by depositing a nominal connection fee of 1.00 and an application fee of 25.00.
eligibility: 1. The World Bankfunded Uttarakhand Drinking Water Supply Programme for Semi-Urban Areas provides benefits to families residing in selected semi-urban regions of the state. 1. The programme is not applicable in urban areas.

name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen - Waste Management) - Uttarakhand
brief_description: The Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen - Waste Management) is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the State Water and Sanitation MissionRs. Uttarakhand Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Mission (Swajal) Project under the Drinking Water DepartmentRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote sustainable solid and liquid waste management in rural Uttarakhand by providing necessary infrastructure and facilities to ensure cleaner villagesRs. improved sanitationRs. and better public health.
benefits: Solid and liquid waste management facilitiesRs. such as public dustbinsRs. soak pitsRs. compost pitsRs. garbage collection centresRs. and community sanitation complexesRs. are constructed according to the requirements of Gram Panchayats through convergenceRs. addressing the needs of migrant and floating populationsRs. at a cost of 3.00 lakh (70% from the Swachh Bharat Mission and 30% from the 15th Finance Commission).
eligibility: 1. The Gram Panchayat can apply to the district level unit with a simple application form along with a Gram Panchayat resolution. There is no prescribed format for the application.

name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana - Har Khet Ko Pani (Groundwater Irrigation Scheme) Uttarakhand
brief_description: The scheme Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana Har Khet Ko Pani (Groundwater Irrigation Scheme) is implemented by the Department of Minor IrrigationRs. Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide assured and sustainable irrigation to every farm by developing groundwater-based irrigation facilities for farmers. This scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme with a funding pattern of 90% Central share and 10% State share.
benefits: Under the schemeRs. farmers are provided with free irrigation facilities. Collective irrigation projects or individual groundwater irrigation projects are constructed. The works carried out under the scheme include: - Solar-powered pumpsets - Electrically operated pumpsets
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 1. The beneficiary must be a farmer engaged in agricultural activities. 1. As per the guidelines issued by the Government of India: - For the construction of collective irrigation projectsRs. a command area of 5 hectares must be available. - According to the report of the Central Ground Water BoardRs. Government of IndiaRs. the command area must be classified under the safe category.

name: Establishment of Tea Factories - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
brief_description: The Establishment of Tea Factories is implemented by the Uttarakhand Tea Development BoardRs. almora under the Department of HorticultureRs. Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to promote the development of the tea industry in Uttarakhand by establishing tea factories for processing locally produced green leavesRs. generating local employmentRs. enhancing farmers income through fair procurementRs. and developing a sustainable tea value chain in the state.
benefits: In the fiscal year 2023-24Rs. the Uttarakhand Tea Development Board processed 5.92 lakh kilograms of green tea leaves and produced approximately 1.25 lakh cups of tea. At presentRs. the Board has established its own tea factories in the following districts: 1. Tea FactoryRs. Ghorakhal (Nainital) Organic 1. Tea FactoryRs. Champawat Organic 1. Tea FactoryRs. Bhatoli (Chamoli) Organic 1. Tea FactoryRs. Kausani (Bageshwar) Inorganic 1. Tea FactoryRs. Harinagari (Bageshwar) Inorganic In addition to the aboveRs. the Board is proposing to establish small tea factories in the following districts: - Tea FactoryRs. Dhauladevi (Almora) - Tea FactoryRs. Didihat (Pithoragarh)
eligibility: It is proposed to operate the above tea factories established by the Board in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode/private sector in the futureRs. for which the eligibility criteria and policy are being prepared.

name: To Increase Fish Seed Production and Inland Fisheries Resources in Tribal Areas: Prawn Seed Stocking - Gujarat
brief_description: The scheme Prawn Seed Stocking is a component under the To Increase Fish Seed Production and Inland Fisheries Resources in Tribal Areas schemeRs. introduced by the AgricultureRs. Farmers Welfare and Co-operation DepartmentRs. Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to people involved in inland fisheries activities. Under this schemeRs. 100% financial assistance is provided to Scheduled Tribe lessees of reservoirs for prawn seed and transportation costs. > **Objectives:** - To increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to people involved in inland fisheries activities. - To boost fish farming or fishing activities in fresh water bodies. - Fishing in reservoirsRs. aquaculture in ponds and catch from rivers increase fish production and boost inland fisheries. - The main objective is to provide employment opportunities to Scheduled Tribe fishermen in the state and increase fish production.
benefits: 100% financial assistance is given to Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries who are lessees of reservoirsRs. covering the total cost of prawn seed as well as transportation costs. > **Minimum Time Limit for Reclaiming Benefits:** 1 year from the date of availing benefit.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be Individuals/societies/self-help groups/associations/reservoir monopolies/private unitsRs. etc.Rs. involved in inland fisheries activities can avail the benefits of inland schemes. 1. The applicant must be from the Scheduled Tribes. 1. The applicant must be above 18 years. 1. The beneficiary must have his/her own bank account. 1. The applicant must have an Aadhaar Card/Voter ID/Ration Card/Passport as proof of identity.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland): Medium Biofloc Establishment - Gujarat
brief_description: The scheme Medium Biofloc Establishment (25 tanksRs. 4-meter diameter and 1-meter height) is a component under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland) schemeRs. implemented by the AgricultureRs. Farmers Welfare and Co-operation DepartmentRs. Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to increase fish production by rearing fish in reservoirs and provide employment to people involved in inland fisheries activities. Under this schemeRs. various components of inland fisheriesRs. including the establishment of Medium Biofloc and Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and freshwater hatcheriesRs. are supported to accelerate inland fish farming activities in freshwater bodies and boost inland fish production. The scheme is implemented by the Commissioner of Fisheries of the State GovernmentsRs. with 60% contribution from the Government of India and 40% from the Government of Gujarat. > **Objective:** - Assistance is provided for accelerating inland fish farming activities in freshwater bodiesRs. increasing inland fish production and boosting inland fisheries. - Except for water bodies or pondsRs. in less landRs. less waterRs. Biofloc with source as wellRs. Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS). By creating fish tanks with this methodRs. more fish production can be obtained in less land and less water. If more beneficiaries get the benefit of the subsidy of this schemeRs. more fish production can be achieved with less water sources and less land. - Inland fish production capacity can be increased by the establishment of freshwater hatcheries.
benefits: The scheme provides financial assistance for various inland fisheries activities. For Medium Biofloc Establishment (25 tanks 4 meter diameter and 1 meter height)Rs. the unit cost is 25Rs./- per unit. The scale of assistance is as follows: - **General Category:** 40% of the unit cost or 40% of the actual costRs. whichever is lessRs. is paid as subsidy.- **WomenRs. Scheduled Caste (SC)Rs. and Scheduled Tribe (ST) Categories:** 60% of the unit cost or 40% of the actual costRs. whichever is lessRs. is paid as subsidy. **Note 1:** The assistance is funded through a 60% contribution from the Government of India and a 40% contribution from the State Government. **Note 2:** The assistance is provided only once in a lifetime to the beneficiary.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be an individualRs. societyRs. self-help groupRs. associationRs. reservoir lease holderRs. or private entity involved in inland fisheries activities. 1. The applicant must be above 18 years of age. 1. The applicant must have their own bank account. 1. The applicant must have their own private land or a minimum 10-year lease agreement for land to avail construction-related assistance on land. In case of co-ownersRs. the consent form of co-owners must be submitted. 1. The applicant must have a Voter ID/Ration Card/Aadhaar Card/Passport as proof of identity. > **Preference/Priority/Reservation/Relaxation:** - All categories (GeneralRs. WomenRs. Scheduled CasteRs. and Scheduled Tribe) will receive benefits under the Inland Schemes. - Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries are required to have a Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe certificate to avail benefits under the inland components.

name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
brief_description: The scheme-component "AYUSH and Public Health" under the "Ayurswasthya Yojana" by the Ministry of AyushRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to promote AYUSH interventions through funding healthcare projects for public health issues affecting communities. It also aims to support for implementing Sustainable Development Goal-2 (SDG2) and Sustainable Development Goal -3 (SDG 3) through integrating AYUSH system.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** - Maximum grant of 1Rs./- for a project duration of 3 years. - Funds are released in installments of 40%Rs. 40%Rs. and 20%. > **Note:** The grant received under the scheme should be utilized as under:- - Not more than 30% of the total grant should be spent on Establishment / Project Management. - Not LESS than 50% of the total grant should be spent on MedicinesRs. laboratory testing or other investigations. - Remaining 20% of the total grant may be spent on AYUSH awarenessRs. minor Equipment etc.Rs. for the project.
eligibility: - The applicant organization must have credible project management expertise and core staff. - Applicant / organization (Other than AYUSH teaching institute registered under [IMCC ActRs. 1970](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19303/1/a1970-48_0.pdf) and [HCC Act 1973](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19294/1/homoeopathy_central_council_act%2C_1973.pdf)) should have track record of minimum 5 years of working in the field of community health. The organization should furnish the necessary evidence for implementing such programmes in the past. - Applicant / organization shall have to make information available regarding any assistance taken from any State/Central Agency in the last 5 years. - The organizations (other than the AYUSH teaching institutes recognized under [IMCC ActRs. 1970](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19303/1/a1970-48_0.pdf) and [HCC ActRs. 1973](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19294/1/homoeopathy_central_council_act%2C_1973.pdf) and the Central/ State Govt. institutes) must submit their application in the Proforma given at Annexure CRs. by the State Government officer of the respective State / UT concerned. Recommendations of the State / UT should clearly mention the following points:- 1. About the credibility of the organization and capability of applicant organization in 1. Implementing such public health initiatives projectRs. 1. Past experienceRs. 1. Relevance and usefulness of the project. - The State Government has to forward the proposal in the prescribed Proforma within 60 days of submission of the proposal by the applicant organization to the State. In caseRs. no response is received from State GovernmentRs. it shall be presumed that State Government has no specific comments against the applicant organization and Ministry of AYUSH will consider the proposal accordingly. > **Eligible Organisation:** - Directorates of Health/AYUSH of States / UTs. - Government Institutes dealing with public health. - Non-profit/Voluntary organizations working in the area of public health for at least five years and having a proven track record and a capable team comprising of public health specialists. - Government aided Institutions/ Undertaking/ Universities/ Research CouncilsRs. Autonomous Organizations and Non Profit Non-Governmental organizations engaged in one or more of the above fields listed in the introduction to the scheme. - Any reputed organization or stakeholders dealing with sports activities in India (only for proposals on AYUSH Sports medicine). - Collaboration of United Nations and International Organizations will be encouraged.

name: A Scheme to Provide Assistance for Building E-Market Facilities in Market Committees
brief_description: "A Scheme to Provide Assistance for Building E-Market Facilities in Market Committees" introduced by the AgricultureRs. Farmers Welfare and Cooperation DepartmentRs. GujaratRs. aims to support market committees to set up e-market facilitiesRs. enhancing transparency and efficiency in agricultural marketing across the state.
benefits: - **Financial Assistance:** 1Rs./- (One Lakh Rupees) per eligible market committee.
eligibility:
1. Co-operative Market Committees shall be eligible under this scheme.
1. The committee must operate within Gujarat.

name: Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation Societies M. N. R.-10 (General Area)
brief_description: The scheme "Assistance to Co-operative Irrigation SocietiesRs. M. N. R.-10 (General Area)" by the Agriculture and Co-operation DepartmentRs. Government of GujaratRs. aims to enhance agricultural yield in the state by offering assistance to irrigation cooperative societies formed by farmers of a common area. The support involves establishing water distribution systems using pumps and electric motors on wells and agar creeks to facilitate effective irrigation.
benefits: - **Monetary Benefit:** Financial assistance for setting up irrigation infrastructure (such as pumps and motors) for cooperative societies.
eligibility: - Cooperative irrigation societies formed by small and marginal farmersRs. or any other farmersRs. are eligible under this scheme. - The society should be located within the state of Gujarat. - The Scheme is applicable to the General category.

name: Assistance to Trusts/Institutions for Setting Up Cultural Centers/Auditoriums in the Municipal Area
brief_description: The scheme "Assistance to Trusts/Institutions for Setting Up Cultural Centers/Auditoriums in the Municipal Area" by the SportsRs. Youth and Cultural Activities DepartmentRs. Government of GujaratRs. aims to strengthen cultural development and encourage the preservation and promotion of arts and heritage by supporting the creation and improvement of cultural infrastructure in urban regions. Under this initiativeRs. eligible trusts and institutions are provided financial assistance either for constructing new cultural centres or for renovating existing ones. The scheme is implemented by the Sangeet Natak AcademyRs. Gujarat.
benefits: - **Assistance for New Construction:** 50% of the total cost or 30Rs./- whichever is lower. - **Assistance for Renovation:** Up to 15Rs./-.
eligibility: - A trust or institution operating within the municipal areas of Gujarat shall be eligible for this scheme.

name: India BPO Promotion Scheme
brief_description: The scheme India BPO Promotion Scheme (IBPS) has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information TechnologyRs. Government of India. It aims to create employment opportunities for youth and promote investment in the Information Technology (IT) and Information Technology Enabled Services (ITeS) sector by establishing BPO/ITeS operations in smaller cities and towns. Through this schemeRs. financial support in the form of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) is provided to eligible companies to establish and operate BPO/ITeS units. The scheme is implemented by Software Technology Parks of India as the nodal agency. The initiative operates under the Digital India Programme and supports the establishment of 48Rs. BPO/ITeS seats across the country (except the North-Eastern region).
benefits: 1. Financial support of up to 50% of expenditure [Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and/or Operational Expenditure (OPEX)] incurred on permissible itemsRs. with an upper ceiling of 1 lakh per BPO/ITeS seat. 1. Special incentives (Additional within the upper cap of 1 Lakh/Seat) - 5% incentive for employing 50% Women - 2% incentive for employing 4% differently abled persons - Up to 10% incentive for generating employment beyond the target - 5% incentive for local entrepreneurs - 5% incentive for setting up BPO at a location other than the State capital (only for IBPS) - Training incentive for regular employees
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a company or entrepreneur intending to establish and operate a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) or Information Technology Enabled Services (ITeS) unit. 1. The applicant must establish BPO/ITeS operations in eligible locations under the India BPO Promotion Scheme (IBPS). 1. The applicant must create the approved BPO/ITeS seats. 1. The applicant must create employment opportunitiesRs. particularly for youthRs. by establishing BPO/ITeS operations. > Note: Special consideration for Hilly states of HPRs. J&K and UK.

name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme- For Startups
brief_description:
The scheme Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) was launched by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) on 19th April 2021 with an outlay of INR 945 Crore to provide financial assistance to startups for Proof of ConceptRs. prototype developmentRs. product trialsRs. market-entryRs. and commercialization. Eligible startups can apply for the scheme on the Startup India portal. The Seed Fund will be disbursed to selected startups through eligible incubators across India.
> **Objective Of The Scheme:**

Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance to startups for proof of conceptRs. prototype developmentRs. product trialsRs. market-entryRs. and commercialization. This would enable these startups to graduate to a level where they will be able to raise investments from angel investors or venture capitalists or seek loans from commercial banks or financial institutions.
> **Features:**

Year-round Call for Applications for Incubators and Startups
Sector-agnostic
No mandatory physical incubation
PAN-India startup programme
Startups can apply to 3 incubators simultaneously
benefits:
**Seed Funds to an eligible startup by the incubator shall be disbursed as follows:**

1. Up to 20 Lakhs as a grant for validation of Proof of ConceptRs. prototype developmentRs. or product trials. The grant shall be disbursed in milestone-based installments. These milestones can be related to the development of prototypesRs. product testingRs. building a product ready for market launchRs. etc.
1. Up to 50 Lakhs of investment for market entryRs. commercializationRs. or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments.
1. Seed funds shall strictly not be used by startups for the creation of any facilities and shall be utilized for the purpose it has been granted for.

**Note 01:** Not more than 20% of the total grant to an incubator shall be given as grants to start-ups by the incubator. The rate of interest (as defined under GFR) on unutilized funds available with the incubator would also be taken into account and adjusted at the time of the next release by DPIIT.
**Note 02:** For startups being supported through convertible debentures or debtRs. or debt-linked instrumentsRs. funds shall be provided at a rate of interest of not more than the prevailing repo rate. The tenure should be fixed at the time of sanctioning the loan by the incubatorRs. which shall be not more than 60 months (5 years). A moratorium of up to 12 months may be provided for the startups. Because of the early stage of the startupsRs. this shall be unsecured and no guarantee from the promoter or third party will be required.
**Note 03:** The incubator shall execute a legal agreement with the selected startups before the release of the first installment. The incubators shall ensure that the necessary terms and conditionsRs. including milestonesRs. related to the Seed Fund are detailed in the agreement.
**Note 04:** Subsequent disbursement would be linked to the achievement of previously specified milestones as per agreement between the startup and incubator.
**Note 05:** Startups will receive the funds in their company bank accounts.
**Note 06:** For grantsRs. the first installment to any selected startup shall be released not more than 60 days from receipt of the application from the startup. The startup shall submit the interim progress update and utilization certificate to initiate the release of subsequent installments of the grant.
**Note 07:** Startup shall submit a final report and audited utilization certificate at the end of the project duration. For failed venturesRs. the entrepreneur will share his/her learnings and the reasons for failure in the report and submit this along with the utilization certificate for the fund amount.
**Note 08:** The incubator or any of its staff members shall not charge any fee in cash or in kind from applicants or beneficiaries under the scheme for any process of selectionRs. disbursementRs. incubationRs. or monitoring.
**Note 09:** A grievance cell shall be set up at DPIIT for the scheme to address issues of applicantsRs. such as delayed evaluation of applicationsRs. delayed disbursements by incubatorsRs. etc.
eligibility:
The eligibility criteria for a startup to apply under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme shall be as follows:

1. A startupRs. recognized by DPIITRs. incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application.
1. Startups must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with market fitRs. viable commercializationRs. and scope of scaling.
1. A startup should be using technology in its core product or serviceRs. or business modelRs. or distribution modelRs. or methodology to solve the problem being targeted.
1. Preference would be given to startups creating innovative solutions in sectors such as social impactRs. waste managementRs. water managementRs. financial inclusionRs. educationRs. agricultureRs. food processingRs. biotechnologyRs. healthcareRs. energyRs. mobilityRs. defenseRs. spaceRs. railwaysRs. oil and gasRs. textilesRs. etc.
1. The startup should not have received more than 10 lakhs of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme. This does not include prize money from competitions and grand challengesRs. subsidized working spaceRs. founder monthly allowanceRs. access to labsRs. or access to a prototyping facility.
1. Shareholding by Indian promoters in the startup should be at least 51% at the time of application to the incubator for the schemeRs. as per the Companies ActRs. 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) RegulationsRs. 2018.
1. A startup applicant can avail seed support in the form of grants and debt/convertible debentures each once as per the guidelines of the scheme.

name: Electronic Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme: Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters
brief_description: The scheme "Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information TechnologyRs. Government of India. It has two componentsRs. namely Greenfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) and Common Facility Centres/ Brownfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters. The upgradation of Brownfield aims to provide the common required technical facilities for various electronics manufacturing companies located in and around the regionRs. which in turn will reduce the lead time of productionRs. production cost (including transportation and logistics cost)Rs. increase export and revenue generationRs. etc. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) formed for the cluster.
benefits: > **Financial Assistance:** 1. **For Brownfield EMCs:** - Financial assistance up to 75% of the project cost. - Maximum limit of 50Rs./-. 1. **Government grant in:** - Processing area: up to 50% of the project cost - Non-processing area: up to 20% of project cost > **Infrastructure / CFC Support:** 1. Upgradation of existing infrastructureRs. such as roadsRs. powerRs. water supplyRs. and drainage. 1. Establishment of Common Facility Centres (CFCs)Rs. (Testing laboratoriesRs. Tool roomsRs. Design centresRs. Training centresRs. R&D facilities) 1. Support for logisticsRs. warehousingRs. and shared services > **Administrative Support:** - Administrative expenses up to 3% of assistance (for SPV) > **Mode of Disbursement:** - Grant-in-aid is released in instalments through an escrow account. - Initial 20% released as advance; subsequent releases based on utilisation.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a legal entity such as an individualRs. companyRs. societyRs. industry associationRs. financial institutionRs. research and development (R&D) institutionRs. or government agency. 1. The applicant should form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for implementation. 1. The applicant should submit a preliminary application along with a feasibility study and project details. 1. The applicant should ensure that the committed investment is at least 4 times the assistance sought. 1. The applicant should ensure that at least 75% of the investment is in electronics manufacturing units. 1. The applicant should propose the upgradation of an existing Electronics Manufacturing Cluster. 1. The applicant should ensure the presence of an existing industrial ecosystem/cluster. 1. The applicant should achieve financial closure before submitting the final application. 1. The applicant should submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR).

name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
brief_description: The scheme "Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) (Industrial Promotion Electronics Hardware Manufacturing (IPHW) Division)Rs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to help offset the disability for domestic manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the countryRs. in alignment with the National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019) and the Government's "Make in India" and "Digital India" programmes. Through this schemeRs. a financial incentive of 25% of capital expenditure (on a reimbursement basis) is provided to any legal entity registered in India investing in eligible electronic componentsRs. semiconductor/display fabrication unitsRs. AssemblyRs. TestingRs. Marking and Packaging (ATMP) unitsRs. specialised sub-assembliesRs. and capital goods for manufacture of the aforesaid goods covering both new units and expansion of capacity/modernisation and diversification of existing units. The scheme is implemented by MeitY through a Nodal Agency appointed as the Project Management Agency (PMA)Rs. which is responsible for receipt of applicationsRs. appraisalRs. issuance of acknowledgementsRs. verification of claimsRs. and disbursement of incentives; applications received under the scheme are appraised on an ongoing basis by the PMARs. which places eligible applications before the Executive Committee (EC) constituted by MeitYRs. chaired by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary.
benefits:
> **Financial Incentive:** A financial incentive of 25% of eligible capital expenditure is provided to approved units manufacturing goods as per the eligible list annexed to the Scheme. The total incentive under the Scheme is 25% of eligible capital expenditure for an approved application. The incentive is over and above any incentive offered by the State Government or any of its agencies or local bodies. Applicants shall also be eligible to take benefit under any other scheme(s) of the Government of India; howeverRs. investments committed under the Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme (M-SIPS) for which incentives have been claimed shall not qualify as eligible investments under SPECS. > **What Constitutes Eligible Capital Expenditure** Capital expenditure includes the following: Expenditure on plantRs. machineryRs. equipment and associated utilities including toolsRs. diesRs. mouldsRs. jigsRs. fixtures (including partsRs. accessoriesRs. componentsRs. and spares thereof); expenditure on packagingRs. freight/transportRs. insuranceRs. and erection and commissioning. Associated utilities include captive power and effluent treatment plants; clean rooms; air curtains; temperature and air quality control systems; compressed airRs. water and power supply; and IT/ITES infrastructure related to manufacturing including serversRs. software and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions. Expenditure on Research and Development (R&D) including in-house and captive R&DRs. test and measuring instrumentsRs. design toolsRs. software cost (directly for R&D)Rs. and expenditure on technologyRs. Intellectual Property Rights (IPR)Rs. patents and copyrights. Expenditure on Transfer of Technology (ToT) including cost of technology and initial technology purchase related to eligible goods. Expenditure on refurbished/used/second-hand plantRs. machinery and equipment (including associated utilities and R&D) whether imported or domestically procured not exceeding 20% of total eligible plantRs. machinery and equipment. Such equipment must have a minimum residual life of at least 5 (five) years at the time of transfer of assets. The following are NOT covered as eligible capital expenditure Expenditure on land and building (including factory building/construction). Expenditure on consumables and raw materials used for manufacturing. > **Sub-Limits within Eligible Capital Expenditure** Associated utilities expenditure: capped at not more than 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plantRs. machinery and equipment. Research and Development (R&D) expenditure: not exceeding 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plantRs. machineryRs. equipment and associated utilities. Transfer of Technology (ToT) expenditure: not exceeding 10% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plantRs. machineryRs. equipment and associated utilities. Refurbished/used/second-hand plantRs. machinery and equipment: not exceeding 20% of total eligible capital expenditure. > **Eligible Goods and Minimum Investment Thresholds**

eligibility: 1. The applicant should be a legal entity registered in India. The applicant may be a Private Limited CompanyRs. Public Limited CompanyRs. Sole ProprietorshipRs. PartnershipRs. or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India. 1. The applicant should be proposing to invest in a project/unit for the manufacturing of eligible goods as per the list in [Annexure-1](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/SPECS-Guidelines-01062020.pdf) of the SPECS Guidelines.1. Each application shall be treated as a new investment and as an independent application. The application shall be only for single-phase projects; phase-wise applications shall not be considered under the Scheme. 1. There is no restriction on any applicant from making multiple applications and/or for multiple locations. 1. The applicant should ensure that the proposed investment in capital expenditure is greater than or equal to the threshold value for the eligible goods under SPECS (as per [Annexure-1](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/SPECS-Guidelines-01062020.pdf) of the Guidelines). 1. The scheme is applicable for investments in new units as well as expansion of capacity/modernisation and/or diversification of existing units. 1. The minimum investment thresholds are the same for new units or expansion of capacity/modernisation/diversification of existing units. 1. A project/unit proposed under the Scheme may include multiple manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations. There is no limit on the number of applications for an applicant. 1. If an application covers more than one product categoryRs. the applicable minimum threshold of investment (capital expenditure) shall be the highest of the individual threshold investment for each of the product categories covered. 1. Eligibility under the SPECS Scheme shall not affect eligibility under any other schemeRs. and vice-versa. 1. The application shall contain the requisite land documents such as a registered sale deed and/or registered rent/lease agreement on the land for a period of not less than 10 years from the date of application in usual circumstances. 1. In case land has been taken on rent/lease for a period less than 10 yearsRs. such application shall be processed if there is a renewal clause for extension of the rent/lease agreement in the registered document. If the renewal clause is not presentRs. the application may be referred by the Project Management Agency (PMA) to the Governing Council (GC) for an appropriate decision. 1. In case the land has not been purchased or taken on rent/lease at the time of applicationRs. the applicant shall provide definite location/plot details and a suitable document confirming availability of the land; howeverRs. the final registered document shall be provided before the submission of the Appraisal Report by PMA for consideration of the Executive Committee (EC). 1. The application shall contain a Financial Closure for the investment required for the complete project. Financial Closure means: - Firm commitment from the applicant to invest in the project under SPECS in the form of a Board Resolution. - Sanction letter/Letter of Intent (LoI) from a Bank/Financial Institution (FI)/loan agreement with Bank/FI for the debt portion of the investment proposed. - Legally binding commitment from equity/unsecured loan providers to provide or mobilise fundsRs. in the form of an agreement backed by a Board Resolution (Board Resolution is not applicable in case of Banks and Financial Institutions; in that caseRs. a sanction letter and/or LoI from the Bank/Financial Institution may be provided). - Legally binding commitment of funding from internal accruals (applicable in case the applicant has any existing unit; shall be assessed from past performanceRs. including Profit and Loss AccountRs. Cash Flow StatementsRs. etc.). - Documents showing capability of fund providers in the form of unencumbered liquid funds (not applicable in case of Banks and Financial Institutions).

name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
brief_description: The scheme "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)Rs. Government of India. The aim is to promote domestic manufacturing of IT hardware products by providing production-linked incentives to eligible companies manufacturing target segment goods in India. Through this schemeRs. financial incentives on incremental sales of manufactured target segment goods covering LaptopsRs. TabletsRs. All-in-One Personal Computers (PCs)Rs. ServersRs. and Ultra Small Form Factor (USFF) devices are provided to Indian-registered companies across three categories: Global CompaniesRs. Hybrid (Global/Domestic) CompaniesRs. and Domestic CompaniesRs. that manufacture qualifying products in India. The scheme is implemented by a Project Management Agency (PMA). **Objectives:** - To boost domestic manufacturing of IT hardware products under the Target Segment (LaptopsRs. TabletsRs. All-in-One PCsRs. ServersRs. and Ultra Small Form Factor devices) in India. - To incentivise incremental investment in plantRs. machineryRs. equipmentRs. Research and Development (R&D)Rs. and Transfer of Technology (ToT) related to the Target Segment. - To promote localisation of components and sub-assemblies in the IT hardware value chain. - To encourage employment generation directly related to the manufacturing process. - To improve domestic value addition in the manufacturing of IT hardware.
benefits: > The scheme provides a financial incentive for the net incremental sales of goods manufactured in India and covered under the target segment. 1. Target Segment Products: The tangible benefits apply to the manufacturing of LaptopsRs. TabletsRs. All-in-One Personal Computers (PCs)Rs. ServersRs. and Ultra Small Form Factor (USSF) devices. 1. **Incentive Rates (Year 1 Year 6):** - Assembly of Laptops/Tablets/All-in-One PCs/USFF: 3% 0% - Assembly of Servers: 3% 0% - PCBA: 1.20% 0.90% - Display Panel: 1.49% 1.12% - Memory Modules: 0.95% 0.71% - SSD: 0.95% 0.71% - Cabinets/Chassis/Enclosures: 1.49% 1.12% - SoC Processors designed in India: 3.24% 2.43% (up to 3.78% 2.84% for Servers) - Additional incentives available for ATMP and IC manufacturing in India 1. **Investment Shortfall Relief** - If investment shortfall is 40% of the thresholdRs. incentive is still payable (with partial deduction of X/2%) - Withheld incentive is refunded without interest once the investment threshold is met in a later year. > **Duration:** Incentive given for 6 consecutive years within the scheme tenure > **Frequency:** Claims can be filed quarterlyRs. half-yearlyRs. or annually > **Filing Deadline:** Claims must be filed within 9 months from the end of the relevant financial year
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a company registered in India. 1. The applicant should propose to manufacture goods covered under the Target Segment. 1. The applicant must meet the threshold criteria of Incremental Investment. 1. The applicant must meet the threshold criteria of Net Incremental Sales of manufactured target segment goods over the base year. 1. The applicant should meet the qualification criteria based on Consolidated Global Manufacturing Revenue for Financial Year 2021-22. 1. The applicant under the Global Company category must have a Consolidated Global Manufacturing Revenue greater than 50Rs./- (5Rs. crore) for the target segment or greater than 100Rs./- (10Rs. crore) for electronics hardware. 1. The applicant under the Domestic Company category must have a Consolidated Global Manufacturing Revenue greater than 1Rs./- (10 crore) for the target segment or greater than 2Rs./- (20 crore) for electronics hardware. 1. The applicant must localise at least Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) and assembly of finished goods from the first year.

name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

It aims to provide financial incentives for the manufacturing of identified electronic components and capital goods in Bharat. The scheme is implemented by a Project Management Agency (PMA) appointed by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The scheme seeks to ensure the effective operation and smooth implementation of electronic system design and manufacturing (ESDM) through detailed industry consultations. It focuses on sub-assembliesRs. bare componentsRs. selected bare componentsRs. and the supply chain ecosystemRs. including capital equipment.
