- Skill upgradationRs. development of utilitarian products for increase in value market.
benefits:
**Activities to be undertaken under the Scheme:**
> **Market Intervention:** The various aspects of marketing intervention which will be supported under this scheme are:-


1. fixation of equitable prices for existing products both manmade and natural;
1. Actual procurement by State agencies as a safety net program and not monopoly/nationalization.
1. Support during seasons of harvest when prices tend to get depressed;
1. Sharing of information on prices so that people can make informed and conscious decisions and thereby markets become efficient;
1. Selling of products by the State Agencies in urban areas and areas away from where they are produced to increase the demand for the products.
1. Grading of productsRs.
1. StandardizationRs.
1. Source certification/Patent etc.
1. Other promotional activitiesRs.

> **Training and Skill upgradation:**


1. Training for improved production and higher-grade products
1. Training related to manmade products to improve quality
1. Diversion to high-value products
1. Development of improved quality and design.
1. Linkage with other departments such as agricultureRs. horticultureRs. khadi and village industriesRs. handloomsRs. and handicraftsRs. etc. for augmentation of trainingRs. skill upgradationRs. and technological support.

> **R&D/IPR Activity**


1. New product development through new usage
1. Development of new products per se
1. Development of new cost-effective processes for product development
1. Expansion of the market of the tribal products through R&D measures
1. The IPR regime would be to document traditional knowledge and craft for seeking benefits of royalty and protection against piracy
1. New technologies of harvestingRs. scientific harvesting practicesRs. etc. are other measures of R&D
1. Documentation and preservation of tangible and intangible heritage for promoting tourism etc.

> **Supply Chain Infrastructure Development:**


1. Setting up of efficient warehousing facilitiesRs. godownsRs. cold storagesRs. etc. wherever necessary
1. Establishing processing industries for value addition.
1. Sharing of information on inputs with the producers/gatherers
1. Develop product-specific efficient warehousing both at the IA level and also at the village level
1. Training related to product-specific warehousing.

> **Trade Information System:**


1. Capturing information about different tribal products related to the sourcesRs. typesRs. potentialRs. productionRs. collectionRs. etc.
1. Collection and dissemination of trade information about various aspects of tribal products/web-enabled service SMS etc.

> **In addition to the aboveRs. the following activities:**


1. Creating brands or brands for tribal produce/productsRs.
1. Developing product designs keeping in view the export market and support for exports.
eligibility:
**Support under the scheme will be made available to:**

1. Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation (TRIFED)Rs.
1. State Tribal Development Cooperative CorporationsRs.
1. State Forest Development Corporations (SDCs)Rs.
1. Minor Forest produce (Trading and Development) Federations (MFPTDFs)Rs.
1. Other institutions identified for product designRs. developmentRs. export processingRs. training of tribal producersRs. patenting and trademarkRs. researchRs. GI certificationRs. and activities ancillary to the above.

name: National Livestock Mission: Genetic Improvement of Pig Breeds - Import of Exotic Pig Germplasm
brief_description: The Import of Exotic Pig Germplasm is a component under the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry of the National Livestock Mission (NLM)Rs. implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and DairyingRs. Government of India. The scheme supports States in the need-based import of superior exotic pig germplasm for genetic improvement of indigenous and non-descript pig breeds. The imported germplasm is used to produce quality crossbred pigs with higher meat productivity. The superior exotic breeds are maintained as pure breeds in State nucleus farms. States are required to formulate and notify a pig breeding policy before submitting proposals under the scheme.
benefits: - **Funding Pattern:** Assistance will be provided on a cost-sharing basis of 60:40 for all States and 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan States.
eligibility:
***Eligible Beneficiaries:***

- State Livestock Agencies
- State Livestock Boards
- Animal Husbandry DepartmentRs. State Government

name: Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PMSETU) : Component I
brief_description: The scheme Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation (PM SETU) Component I: Upgradation of Industrial Training Institutes has been launched by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)Rs. Government of India. It aims to upgrade Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into industry-alignedRs. state-of-the-art skilling institutions to produce highly employable youth. Through this schemeRs. large-scale infrastructure upgradationRs. industry-led course designRs. and enhanced training and placement services are provided to studentsRs. traineesRs. and workforce participants. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) in collaboration with State Governments and industry partners through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) framework. > **Objectives:****** The schemes objective is to upgrade and reimagine ITIs through industryled governance into state-of-the-art skilling institutions that produce highly employable youth aligned with industry needs. The salient features include: 1. One thousand (1Rs.) Government ITIs (200 as hub ITIs and 800 as spoke ITIs) to be upgraded in a Hub-and-Spoke arrangement. A Hub ITI will haveRs. on averageRs. four (4) Spoke ITIsRs. with all upgraded ITIs equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructureRs. machineryRs. and equipment. 1. For upgradation of ITIs in Hub-and-Spoke arrangementsRs. the institutional structure of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) shall be established by bringing in a credible Anchor Industry Partner (AIP)Rs. along with other industry partners if requiredRs. to manage the Hub-and-Spoke cluster/s and deliver agreed outcome-based training and employment outcomes. 1. Introduction of new courses based on jobs/occupations and competencies required in the identified sector/industry segmentRs. with flexibility in duration and pedagogy. 1. Redesign of existing courses to align with industry needs and improve employability. High-demand traditional courses to be revamped with upgraded curricula and modern technology. 1. On averageRs. four (4) new courses would be introducedRs. and ten (10) existing courses would be upgraded at the Hub ITIs. On averageRs. two (2) new courses would be introducedRs. and eight (8) existing courses would be upgraded in Spoke ITIs. 1. Flexibility to introduce courses related to the service sectorRs. multi-skilled coursesRs. and livelihood promotion (where industry presence is low). 1. Other than the National Trade Certificate (NTC)Rs. which is the current course certification for ITI pass-outsRs. the options may include long-term courses (Diplomas)Rs. short-term courses (3-6 months)Rs. and Executive Education Programs for Graduates and working professionalsRs. leveraging the presence of advanced machinery and equipment and trainers at Hub ITIs. 1. Specialised short-term courses for both ITI and non-ITI (EngineeringRs. DiplomaRs. and working professionals) candidates. 1. Facility for Training of Trainers (ToT) at the Hub ITI. 1. Enhancement of student servicesRs. including those related to placement services and linkages to industriesRs. counsellingRs. remedial classes for addressing gaps in foundational learningRs. extra-curricular activitiesRs. life skills trainingRs. apprenticeshipsRs. and On-the-Job trainingRs. etc.Rs. in the Hub-and-Spoke cluster. 1. Hubs may offer services like production centresRs. incubation centresRs. and maker spacesRs. for which the ITI can charge fees as determined by them for ensuring financial sustainability. 1. Developing a digital interface and Learning Outcome Management System (LOMS) for mapping the entire network of Hub-and-Spoke ITI clustersRs. real-time data captureRs. digital learning avenues including artificial and virtual reality (AR/VR) capabilitiesRs. simulationRs. and linkages with the national datasets and Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH). 1. A human resource plan for managing the implementation of the upgradation plan for both Hub and Spoke ITIsRs. including a managerial layerRs. trainers and administrative staffRs. and adoption of better HR practicesRs. leading to improved training outcomes. 1. Mini-Hubs for North-East and Hilly region: To allow implementation of ITI upgradation in Hub-and-Spoke arrangements in North-Eastern and Hilly StatesRs. the indicative definition of Hubs and Spokes may be relaxed.
benefits: > **Financial Outlay and Financing Structure:** The total outlay of the scheme is 60Rs./- crore over five years. This cost is shared among the Central GovernmentRs. State GovernmentsRs. and IndustryRs. as shown below: **Particulars****Total ( Crore)****Central ( Crore)****State ( Crore)****Industry ( Crore)**Total Scheme Outlay (5 years)60Rs./-30Rs./-20Rs./-10Rs./-This corresponds to a funding pattern of approximately 50% Central: 33% State: 17% Industry. Each Hub-and-Spoke cluster will maintain this cost-sharing ratio in its funding plan as indicated in the Strategic Investment Plan (SIP). > **Indicative Investment per ITI and Cluster:** - Under the SchemeRs. support will be provided for the upgradation of Hub ITIs with an outlay not exceeding 81 crore (over five years) and for Spoke ITIs with an outlay not exceeding 40 crore. - In cases where the overall cost of upgradation exceeds the prescribed outlayRs. the contribution of the Central Government shall be capped at 50% of the above ceiling amounts and limited strictly to capital expenditure (exceptions apply for North-Eastern and Hilly States and Union Territories without legislature). > **Indicative Cost for Cluster:** - One Hub + Four Spokes (cluster total): 241 crore per cluster - Annual cost for one cluster (5-year average): ~48.2 crore per year > **Component-wise Outlay (1000 ITIs):** - Upgradation of 200 Hub ITIs: 20Rs. crore - Upgradation of 800 Spoke ITIs: 36Rs. crore - Subtotal ITI Upgradation (Component I): 56Rs. crore > **Central Support for Scheme Management:** - 1Rs. crore is earmarked for governanceRs. project managementRs. and capacity-building activities over five yearsRs. including: - Capacity building of central and state agencies: 200 crore - Office expenditure: 100 crore - IT and digital infrastructure (including LOMS): 600 crore - Technical assistance: 100 crore - MediaRs. awarenessRs. and advocacy: 100 crore - EvaluationsRs. studiesRs. and research: 100 crore - Project Management Unit (PMU) support: 400 crore > **Fund Flow Mechanism:** - Each approved cluster SPV will operate an escrow bank account to collect funds from all sources. All contributions CentralRs. StateRs. and Industry are deposited into this escrow accountRs. and funds become available only after all three parties have contributed their respective shares. > **Fund Disbursement:** - Initial Advance (Year 1): - An advance of up to 10% of the total project outlay shall be released upon approval of the Strategic Investment Plan (SIP). - Annual Instalments (Years 25): - The remaining funds are disbursed in annual instalments in two tranches of 50% eachRs. subject to: - Utilisation of at least 75% of previous funds - Approval of Annual Operational Plan (AOP) - Achievement of at least 80% of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) > **Validity:****** The scheme is implemented over a period of five years.
eligibility: > **For Government ITIs:** 1. The ITIs should be Government Industrial Training Institutes. 1. The selection of ITIs shall be carried out by the respective State or Union Territory. 1. The selection should be based on factors such as emerging skill requirementsRs. local industry demandRs. and potential for industry participation. > **For Anchor Industry Partner (AIP) / Industry Partner:** 1. The applicant should be a credible company or manufacturer with established operations in India. 1. The applicant may be an industry associationRs. consortiumRs. industry-led foundationRs. or an academic institution promoted by industry. 1. The applicant should have the capability to participate in governanceRs. curriculum designRs. and training delivery. > **Minimum Eligibility Conditions (As Defined by State/UT):** 1. The applicant should meet the minimum eligibility criteria such as turnoverRs. number of employeesRs. and sectoral experienceRs. as defined by the State or Union Territory. 1. The applicant should demonstrate the ability to ensure meaningful industry participation. 1. The applicant should not be a small or non-serious operator.

name: Vanchit Ikai Samooh aur Vargon ki Aarthik Sahayata Yojana (VISVAS) for Self-Help Groups
brief_description: The Vanchit Ikai Samooh aur Vargon ki Aarthik Sahayata (VISVAS) Yojana is an interest subvention scheme implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and EmpowermentRs. Government of India. The scheme aims to provide interest subvention to eligible Self-Help Groups (SHGs) belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs)Rs. Other Backward Classes (OBCs)Rs. and Safai KaramcharisRs. including identified Manual ScavengersRs. Waste PickersRs. and their dependents. The scheme covers loans obtained from Public Sector Banks (PSBs)Rs. Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)Rs. Private Sector BanksRs. Small Finance BanksRs. and other financial institutions.
benefits: > **Interest Subvention** - Interest subvention of up to 5% per annum on eligible loans. > **Loan Limits** - Self-Help Groups (SHGs): Loans/Cash Credit Limits up to 10Rs.. > **Mode of Payment** - The interest subvention amount is transferred directly into the beneficiary's bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
eligibility: 1. The SHG must have at least 70% members belonging to SCsRs. OBCsRs. or Safai Karamcharis (including identified Manual ScavengersRs. Waste PickersRs. and their dependents). 1. The SHG must have a standard loan account. 1. The SHG must not have received interest subvention on the same loan under any other scheme. 1. The annual family income of SC/OBC members should generally be up to 3Rs./-. > **NOTE:** No income ceiling for Safai KaramcharisRs. including identified Manual ScavengersRs. Waste PickersRs. and their dependents.

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups
brief_description: The scheme is the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)Rs. notified by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)Rs. Ministry of Commerce and IndustryRs. Government of India launched on 6th October 2022. The revised notification was issued on 8 May 2025 and comes into force from that dateRs. covering loan/debt facilities sanctioned to eligible startups on or after the notification. The scope of CGSS is to provide credit guarantees on a wide range of debt instrumentssuch as venture debtRs. working capitalRs. subordinated/mezzanine debtRs. debentures and other fund and nonfund-based facilities that crystallise into debtextended by eligible Member Institutions to DPIITrecognised startups. Its core objective is to offer guarantee cover up to specified limits against these credit instruments so as to enable collateralfree debt funding for eligible startups and improve their access to institutional finance. Salient features include transactionbased and umbrellabased guarantee structuresRs. maximum guarantee cover of 20 crore per borrowerRs. and differentiated Annual Guarantee Fee/Annual Commitment Charge slabsRs. with concessional rates for NorthEast unitsRs. women entrepreneurs and 27 identified Champion Sectors. Target beneficiaries are DPIITrecognised startups that are not in default or classified as NPAs and are certified as eligible by Member Institutions such as scheduled commercial banksRs. select NBFCsRs. financial institutions and SEBIregistered AIFs. Benefits include collateralfree debtRs. enhanced lender comfort through unconditional and irrevocable guaranteesRs. and improved flow of formal credit to innovative startups across sectors and stages. It offers 85% guarantee coverage for credit facilities up to 10 crore and 75% guarantee coverage for facilities up to 20 crore.
benefits: 1. Provides collateral free debt funding to eligible DPIIT recognised startups by backing their loans with a government guarantee. 2. Improves access to a wide range of instruments such as venture debtRs. working capital limitsRs. subordinated/mezzanine debtRs. debentures and other fund and non fund based facilities. 3. Offers high guarantee coverage of up to 85% of the amount in default for loans up to 10 croreRs. significantly reducing loss risk for lenders on smaller exposures. 4. Provides 75% guarantee coverage of the amount in default for loan amounts above 10 croreRs. up to an overall cap of 20 crore per borrower. 5. Lowers risk for Member Institutions (banksRs. NBFCsRs. FIsRs. AIF based venture debt funds)Rs. encouraging them to lend more actively to startups. 6. Supports both transaction based and umbrella based guaranteesRs. enabling individual startup loans as well as pooled venture debt portfolios to be covered. 7. Offers concessional guarantee fee/commitment charge for North East unitsRs. women led startups and entities in the 27 Champion SectorsRs. reducing their effective cost of borrowing. 8. Provides unconditional and irrevocable guarantee coverRs. increasing lender confidence and stability in credit flows to startups. 9. Permits restructuring and enhancement of existing CGSS covered credit facilities while retaining guarantee coverRs. subject to the overall limit. 10. Strengthens the startup ecosystem by improving formal credit availabilityRs. enabling innovative startups to scaleRs. invest in technology and create employment.
eligibility: 1. The Legal Status of the applicant should be: an entity recognised as a Startup by DPIIT as per the applicable Gazette Notifications. 2. The Credit History of the applicant should be: not in default to any lending or investing institution and not classified as a Non Performing Asset as per RBI guidelines. 3. The Certification requirement of the applicant should be: its eligibility must be certified by the concerned Member Institution for the purpose of obtaining guarantee cover. 4. The Nature of activity of the applicant should be: engaged in eligible startup business activities as per DPIIT recognitionRs. and continuing the activity for which the credit facility is being sought. 5. Any other: The applicant must comply with all other eligibility criteria and scheme conditions prescribed under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) from time to time.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0- Special Projects
brief_description: Launched in 2015Rs. with its 4.0 phase being implemented between Financial Year 2022 and Financial Year 2026Rs. the scheme "Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 Special Projects" by the Ministry of Skill Development and EntrepreneurshipRs. Government of IndiaRs. aims to meet the skilling needs of marginalized and vulnerable groupsRs. difficult geographiesRs. and specialized training courses that are likely to be offered outside of regular short-term skilling programmesRs. and can also focus on new-age job roles with future skills. Through this schemeRs. project-based short-term skilling initiatives which can be residential or non-residential and may avail certain exemptions granted with the approval of the Executive Committee are provided to marginalised and vulnerable groups and candidates in difficult geographies that require special attention. The scheme is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)Rs. which supports the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)Rs. and is delivered on the ground through Special Projects Implementing Agencies (SPIAs). > **Objectives of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0** - The scheme promotes an enabling ecosystem for the youth to get skilled and choose a career path aligned with their abilities and aspirations. - The scheme enables delivery of skill training in a market-oriented and demand-driven mannerRs. with emphasis on improving the employability of candidates. - The scheme simplifies processes of the skill ecosystem by leveraging technology and digitalisation. - The scheme enhances access to skilling by setting up skill development infrastructure in remote and difficult geographies such as hilly terrainRs. Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areasRs. and border areasRs. by designing special projects. - The scheme improves inclusivity by ensuring that Scheduled Caste (SC)Rs. Scheduled Tribe (ST)Rs. womenRs. and other marginalised communities can undertake skill training and access gainful wages and self-employment. - The scheme provides an opportunity for lifelong skilling through upskilling and reskilling to address the dynamic needs of the ever-changing market. - The scheme ensures quality training delivery through trained pedagogyRs. standardised assessmentsRs. and industry-relevant curriculum. - The scheme facilitates enhanced employability through training in transferable skills and incentives for employment generation. - The scheme provides candidate-centric training with emphasis on industry-relevant skills.
benefits: The following benefits are provided to candidates under Special Projects: 1. **Base Training Cost:** Provided as per the rationalised hourly base cost of 27.89 per hour.1. **Free Short-Term Skill Training:** On-the-Job Training (OJT) is provided in applicable job roles for practicalRs. live-work exposure.1. **UniformRs. Induction KitRs. and Participant Handbook:** Maximum up to 500 per candidate. The induction kit consists of a T-shirt (Male) or Jacket (Female) and a bag.1. **Assessment and Certification:** 600 per assessment per candidateRs. funded under the scheme. Every candidate is offered one free-of-charge chance of re-assessment.1. **BoardingRs. LodgingRs. and Transportation:** Provided to special groups (Women and Persons with Disability) and Special AreasRs. and may also be extended for training in AspirationalRs. BorderRs. Tribal-dominatedRs. and LWE-affected districts. Special Projects may also be taken up with fully residential training.1. **Conveyance / Transportation Cost:** Permissible for Women and Persons with Disability (PwD) in case of non-residential trainingRs. as per Common Norms.1. **Additional Support to Persons with Disability (PwD) Candidates:** 5Rs. towards assistive devicesRs. aidsRs. and appliances.1. **Accidental Insurance:** Every certified candidate is provided with 1-year accidental insuranceRs. as per prevailing rates (14.16).1. **Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS) Transaction Fees:** Up to 10 per userRs. borne under the scheme.1. **Post-Certification Tracking Support:** Information Technology (IT)-based tracking for up to 1 year from the date of certificationRs. with an allowance of up to 50 per certified candidate.1. **Certification:** A Quick Response (QR) code-based digital certificate is issued (on DigiLockerRs. on email/phone numberRs. and on the Skill India Digital profile)Rs. and one printed certificate is provided free of cost by the Training Provider.1. **Post-Certification Linkages:** Certified candidates are linked with Rojgar Melas (including virtual) and Apprenticeship Melas and gain access to jobsRs. apprenticeship opportunitiesRs. and loans for entrepreneurship through Skill India Digital.
eligibility: 1. The applicant should be of Indian nationality. 1. The applicant should possess a valid Aadhaar. 1. The applicant should fulfil the eligibility criteria of the respective job role. 1. The applicant should be in the age group of 15 to 45 years. 1. The applicant should belong to a marginalised or vulnerable groupRs. or another group requiring special attentionRs. or should be undertaking job roles with a focus on future skills.

name: State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme
brief_description:
The "State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme" is an Animal Husbandry scheme by the Animal Husbandry DepartmentRs. Government of ChhattisgarhRs. which aims to promote goat farming as a sustainable livelihood option. Goat rearing has been a traditional occupationRs. and with increasing demand for milk and meatRs. advanced goat farming presents a profitable self-employment opportunity in rural areas.
**Objectives** - To boost the supply of milk and meat through organized goat farming. - To provide an additional source of income for rural households. - To offer technical and financial support for setting up goat farming units.
**Key Features** - Low InvestmentRs. High Returns: Goat farming requires minimal investment but yields significant income. - **Nutritional Benefits:** Goat milk is highly nutritious and easily digestibleRs. making it ideal for children and patients.- **High-Quality Meat:** Goat meat is rich in protein and has high market demand.- **Fast Breeding Rate:** Goats have a short reproductive cycle and can produce multiple offspring.- **Drought Resilience:** Goats can survive in harsh conditionsRs. making them a reliable source of income even during droughts.
benefits: **Financial Assistance Under the State Goat Entrepreneurship Development Scheme** - **Total finance cost:** 1Rs./- per goat unit (30 goats + 2 improved breed goats).- **For general category beneficiaries:** 25% subsidy on the total costRs. up to a maximum of 25Rs./-- **For SC/ST beneficiaries:** 33.3% subsidy on the total costRs. up to a maximum of 33Rs./-.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a resident of Chhattisgarh for at least five years.
1. The applicant should be linked to a loan from a NationalizedRs. CooperativeRs. or Regional Rural Bank.
1. The applicant should be willing to sign a contract with the department to operate the unit for at least three years.
1. The applicant should be eligible for the grant only after obtaining the Unit Establishment Verification CertificateRs. a demand letter from the bankRs. and submitting necessary documents.

name: Sabooj Sathi
brief_description:
The Sabooj Sathi Scheme is a student welfare initiative launched by the government of West BengalRs. IndiaRs. to provide bicycles to students in the state. The scheme aims to promote education and empower studentsRs. particularly those from disadvantaged backgroundsRs. by providing them with a means of transportation to and from school. _Under the schemeRs. bicycles are distributed free of cost to students studying in government and government-aided schools from classes IX to XII. The scheme is implemented by the Department of School EducationRs. West BengalRs. in collaboration with the Department of Panchayats and Rural Development._
**Honble Finance MinisterRs. in his Budget Speech of 2015-2016Rs. announced a scheme for the distribution of bicycles to an estimated 40 lakh students studying in classes IX to XII in GovernmentRs. Government Aided SchoolsRs. and Madrasahs of the State. He announced that around 25 lakh students would be covered in 2015-16 and the remaining 15 lakhs in the next fiscal.**
By nowRs. this scheme is well-known as Sabooj Sathi as coined by Honble Chief Minister herself and it reflects her desire to see young students empowered to achieve new feats in the future through the bicycles provided under the scheme. She also created the scheme logo which is firmly attached in the basket in front of the bicycle. Honble CM flagged off the distribution in October 2015 from Paschim Medinipur. The scheme has been successful in achieving its objectivesRs. with over 80 lakh bicycles distributed to students across the state since its inception in 2015. The scheme has also received recognition from various national and international organizations for its impact on education and sustainable development.
**The scheme was conceived with the primary objective of enhancing student access to Secondary Education. The scheme is further expected-**
1. _To increase retention in schoolsRs._ 1. _To encourage students to take up higher studiesRs._ 1. _To inculcate sense of confidence among the girl students by promoting mobilityRs._ 1. _To promote environment-friendly and healthy means of transportation._ 1. _The objectives are aligned with four Sustainable Goals of agenda 2030. These are SDG3: Good Health & Well-beingRs. SDG4: Quality EducationRs. SDG5: Gender Equality and SDG13: Climate actions._
**The scheme has several objectivesRs. including:**
- _Enhancing the attendance and retention of students in schoolsRs. especially among girlsRs. who often face transportation-related challenges._ - _Encouraging students to pursue their education beyond the primary level and complete their higher studies._ - _Promoting social inclusion and reducing drop-out rates among disadvantaged students._ - _Supporting the government's efforts towards sustainable development by reducing the carbon footprint through the use of bicycles as a means of transportation._
benefits:
***Here are some of the benefits of the SABOOJ SATHI Scheme:***
**Encourages Education:** SABOOJ SATHI Scheme encourages education by providing bicycles to studentsRs. which helps them in attending school regularly. **Health Benefits:** Cycling is a form of exerciseRs. and the scheme encourages students to adopt a healthy lifestyle and remain physically fit. **Saves Time and Money:** The scheme saves the time and money of the students who have to otherwise walk long distances to reach school. **Environmental Benefits:** Encouraging cycling as a mode of transportation reduces the carbon footprintRs. making it an eco-friendly initiative. **Empowerment:** SABOOJ SATHI Scheme promotes the empowerment of girl students by providing them with bicyclesRs. making it easier for them to travel to school. **Enhanced Mobility:** The scheme provides enhanced mobility to students who live in remote areasRs. which makes it easier for them to attend school. **Reduces Dropout Rates:** By providing bicycles to studentsRs. the scheme reduces dropout ratesRs. as it becomes easier for students to attend school regularly. ***OverallRs. the SABOOJ SATHI Scheme has several benefits and has been successful in encouraging educationRs. improving healthRs. promoting empowermentRs. and reducing dropout rates.***
eligibility:
The SABOOJ SATHI Scheme is a government initiative launched by the West Bengal government to provide bicycles to students studying in government-run and government-aided schools from class IX to XII.
***The eligibility criteria for the SABOOJ SATHI Scheme are as follows:***
1. **Age Limit:** The student must be between 13 to 18 years of age.1. **Schooling:** The student must be studying in a government-run or government-aided school in West Bengal.1. **Residency:** The student must be a permanent resident of West Bengal.1. **Family Income:** The family income of the student should not exceed Rs. 2 lakh per annum.1. **Distance:** The student should live at least 2 km away from their school.1. **Attendance:** The student must have at least 60% attendance in the last academic year.1. **Ownership:** The student should not already own a bicycle.1. **Class:** The student must be studying in class IX to XII.
_It is important to note that the eligibility criteria may vary depending on the specific guidelines of the scheme in each state or region. AdditionallyRs. the application process and required documents may differ depending on the government's instructions._
